reason: A 60-patient pilot against silver sulfadiazine gives little power unless the healing effect is large; recruitment since 2022 has been slow and a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
rationale: Small phase 2 pilot (30 per arm) from a small sponsor, still recruiting 4.5 years after start. A hazard ratio for healing near 1.3 is plausible for a topical botanical against SSD, which is known to slow re-epithelialization, but the sample gives only modest power. Small sponsors often report late or not at all.
evidence: Cochrane review of dressings for superficial and partial thickness burns (Wasiak 2013)

assumptions.claim: Silver sulfadiazine heals partial-thickness burns more slowly than most modern dressings, over roughly 2-3 weeks.

reason: RAPID's CT density effect (p=0.03) was modest and likely overestimated; with about 115 per arm and a 3-year PD15 endpoint, a true effect somewhat below RAPID would leave power near 50-60%, helped by two active doses.
rationale: RAPID showed a slower annual decline in CT lung density with 60 mg/kg (-1.45 vs -2.19 g/L/yr, p=0.03), the basis for this confirmatory 3-year, 2-dose trial. Winner's curse suggests a smaller true effect. About 115 per arm and one-dose-suffices rule give roughly even odds. Hospitalised exacerbations showed no signal in RAPID.

assumptions.claim: In RAPID, 60 mg/kg weekly alpha1-proteinase inhibitor reduced the annual decline in CT lung density at TLC to -1.45 g/L/yr versus -2.19 g/L/yr on placebo (p=0.03).

reason: Adding a potent androgen receptor inhibitor to RT plus ADT in high-risk disease is likely to cut metastasis or death, but the long-delayed event-driven readout suggests few events and a possibly smaller effect than in metastatic or nmCRPC settings.
rationale: Apalutamide cut metastasis or death by about 70% in SPARTAN and darolutamide with RT/ADT reported a large MFS gain in DASL-HiCaP. Here 1503 patients and event-driven MFS give high power if HR is about 0.75. The 10-year run and low event rate temper confidence; timing of public readout by June 2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Apalutamide added to ADT in nmCRPC cut metastasis or death (HR about 0.30) in SPARTAN.

reason: Descriptive pediatric phase 2 already completed; Takeda normally posts results within the 12-month window after primary completion (July 2027), so posting by end of August 2027 is likely, and primary outcomes are unlikely to change.

SVR35 should be met easily versus physician's choice, but the co-primary TSS50 was not significant in PERSIST-2 (25% vs 14%, p=0.08); both must be met, and low-dose ruxolitinib in control could narrow the gap.
rationale: PERSIST-2 showed SVR35 18% vs 3% with pacritinib vs best available therapy, so SVR35 is likely met with about 400 patients. The symptom co-primary (TSS50) was a miss at p=0.08 there; a true 10-point gain would give roughly 70% power. Both co-primaries needed, giving roughly 0.6.

assumptions.claim: In PERSIST-2, SVR35 at week 24 was 18% with pacritinib vs 3% with best available therapy, while TSS50 was 25% vs 14% (p=0.08).
assumptions.source: PERSIST-2, Mascarenhas et al., JAMA Oncol 2018

reason: BPD-or-death at 36 weeks has repeatedly resisted drug prevention; with about 148 per arm and roughly 38% control incidence, an absolute reduction of about 11 points is needed for significance, above the modest effect likely.
rationale: Earlier phase 2 of IGF-1/IGFBP-3 in extremely preterm infants suggested lower severe BPD and ROP, but it was small. Open-label design, 295 infants, and a control event rate near 35-40% require an absolute reduction of about 11 points. Neonatal BPD prevention trials usually miss; moderate chance of a signal.
evidence: rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3 phase 2 in preterm infants 2019 (Ley, Lancet Respir Med)

assumptions.claim: In the earlier phase 2 in extremely preterm infants, rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3 numerically reduced severe BPD and severe ROP versus standard care.
assumptions.source: Ley et al., Lancet Respir Med 2019

reason: Mu-opioid agonism should firm stools, but a dose-ranging pediatric phase 2 splits 272 patients over several arms, enrolment was cut short in the older group, and placebo response is large; the study is labelled exploratory.
rationale: Eluxadoline improves stool consistency in adults, a pharmacologic effect that should carry over to children, and the stool endpoint is the most sensitive. But arms are split across doses, the older group closed early, and the objective is exploratory, so a clear significance statement is uncertain. Results likely appear only as CT.gov postings.
evidence: IBS-3001 and IBS-3002 adult phase 3 2016 (Lembo, NEJM)

assumptions.claim: In adult IBS-D phase 3 trials eluxadoline improved stool consistency and composite response versus placebo.

reason: An HDAC inhibitor added to pazopanib has only single-arm phase 1b/2 support, TKI add-on phase 3 trials mostly fail, and the combination adds toxicity; the sponsor is small and the trial is slow, so reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely.
rationale: Support comes from single-arm early data (abexinostat plus pazopanib, PFS about 16 months) that cannot be compared with controls. Add-on trials to VEGF TKIs have mostly failed, and the first-line setting has moved to immunotherapy combinations. The 2:1 design with about 413 patients is adequately powered for HR 0.7, but I expect a smaller true effect.
evidence: Abexinostat plus pazopanib phase 1b/2 in RCC (Aggarwal 2017)

assumptions.claim: Pazopanib first-line RCC median PFS was about 8-9 months in COMPARZ.

reason: Cariprazine has a robust adult schizophrenia effect (about 7 PANSS points), but adolescent trials run large placebo responses and sites in Eastern Europe and Latin America add noise; multiple doses help the chance of at least one hit.
rationale: Adult effect sizes of 6-8 PANSS points for cariprazine; adolescent antipsychotic trials (aripiprazole, lurasidone, paliperidone, asenapine) are mostly positive but sometimes fail on high placebo response. With 330 patients and possibly several doses, power is good for a 5-6 point effect. Positive results are likelier to be announced early.

assumptions.claim: In adult schizophrenia phase 3 trials, cariprazine separated from placebo on PANSS total by roughly 6-8 points.
assumptions.source: Durgam et al., Schizophr Res 2014; Kane et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2015

reason: Adding ipilimumab to nivolumab probably raises response and PFS, but both PFS and ORR must be significant, and the incremental benefit over nivolumab alone may be modest (cf. melanoma, where PFS HR was about 0.88).
rationale: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab achieved ORR about 42% in CheckMate 214 versus about 30% for nivolumab alone in earlier RCC studies, so an ORR gain of 10-12 points is plausible, with 218 per arm giving about 70% power. PFS is the second hurdle. Both co-primaries must be met; a phase 3b with modest incremental effect makes this roughly a coin flip.

assumptions.claim: In CheckMate 214 intermediate/poor-risk patients, nivolumab plus ipilimumab had ORR 42% and median PFS 11.6 months versus sunitinib.

reason: Fully enrolled phase 3 near its registered October 2026 primary completion; Sarepta tends to post results close to the 12-month deadline, so posting by August 2027 is possible but unlikely, and a small clean-up of the three primary outcomes is the main amendment risk.

Both arms are titrated to keep total Kt/V above 1.7, so a non-inferiority comparison should usually succeed; the main risk is a lower Kt/V in the glucose-sparing arm or a stricter margin than assumed, plus a small sponsor reporting selectively.
rationale: Both arms are prescribed to keep total weekly Kt/V above 1.7 and urea clearance depends mostly on residual renal function and prescribed volume, not the osmotic agent. With 85 per arm and an SD near 0.5, a typical non-inferiority margin of about 0.2 would usually be met. Residual risks are an unstated or tight margin and dropouts. The trial is still recruiting, so public results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Low-glucose-degradation-product PD solutions have not changed total Kt/V versus conventional solutions in randomized trials.

reason: Lilly paediatric study near completion with no efficacy hypothesis; Lilly usually posts results within about a year of primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is roughly a one-in-three event, and termination or primary-outcome changes are unlikely.

HPV vaccines are about 90 to 98% effective against persistent infection with vaccine types in HPV-naive people, so success is likely; the risk is that persistent oral infection is rare, leaving few events and a wide interval.
rationale: 9vHPV prevents persistent genital and anal infection with vaccine types at about 90 to 98% in per-protocol populations, and oral infection with the same types should respond similarly. 6000 men yield a limited number of oral persistent infections, but a near-complete effect needs only about a dozen cases to be significant. This is likely the post-marketing confirmatory trial for the oropharyngeal indication. Risks are low event counts and timing.
evidence: Costa Rica Vaccine Trial oral HPV (Beachler, 2016)

assumptions.claim: 9vHPV prevented persistent infection with types 31/33/45/52/58 with about 96% efficacy in young women.

reason: Adding PD-1 blockade to chemoradiation has repeatedly failed to improve disease control in other tumours, and chemoradiation in bladder cancer already controls disease well; a hazard ratio near 0.65 is needed for the trial design to succeed.
rationale: Bladder-preserving chemoradiation already gives about 65% two-year event-free rates, leaving limited room. PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitors added to chemoradiation failed in head and neck (KEYNOTE-412, JAVELIN H&N 100), and the atezolizumab bladder chemoradiation trial (S1806) is, to my recollection, also negative. Phase 2 hints exist, so success is plausible but below one in four. Event-driven timing could slip the final analysis.

assumptions.claim: Chemoradiation alone gave 2-year locoregional disease-free survival of about 67% in BC2001.
Adding PD-(L)1 blockade to chemoradiation did not improve outcomes in locally advanced head and neck cancer.

reason: Four MRI and X-ray structural outcomes must all be significant with only 64 patients per arm, and diacerein's structure-modifying effect is small at best, so meeting all four is very unlikely.
rationale: The round requires all four co-primary structural outcomes (cartilage volume, bone marrow lesions, synovitis, joint space width) to be met. Diacerein only modestly slowed joint space narrowing in hip osteoarthritis (ECHODIAH), and 2-year MRI cartilage differences in knee osteoarthritis are small relative to variability with 64 patients per arm. Success on one outcome is plausible; success on all four is not. Single-site Thai trial, slow publication.

assumptions.claim: In hip osteoarthritis, diacerein only modestly slowed joint space narrowing over 3 years.

reason: Mite subcutaneous immunotherapy usually beats placebo on combined symptom-medication score and two doses give two chances, but 50 per arm leaves a noisy score and a large placebo response.
rationale: Subcutaneous mite allergoid immunotherapy usually reduces the combined symptom and medication score versus placebo, and one of two active doses meeting the objective is enough. Counterweights are 50 per arm, a noisy composite score and unknown scoring details. Conditional on a public result the sponsor most likely reports a positive outcome. The trial is still recruiting a year-long treatment, so a result by mid-2027 is very unlikely.
evidence: Cochrane review of SCIT in allergic rhinitis (Calderon, 2007)

assumptions.claim: Subcutaneous allergen immunotherapy lowers combined symptom and medication scores versus placebo in allergic rhinitis.
assumptions.source: Calderon et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2007

reason: BTK inhibitor added to R-CHOP in non-GCB DLBCL; ibrutinib in PHOENIX missed in the overall non-GCB group and only helped younger patients, and the ABC enrichment here is incomplete (unclassified included), so the effect may be diluted.
rationale: PHOENIX (ibrutinib + R-CHOP) did not improve EFS in non-GCB DLBCL overall (HR about 0.93), with benefit only under 60 years and added toxicity in older patients. Acalabrutinib is more selective and better tolerated, and the age limit is 75, but the population is not restricted to MCD/N1 or pure ABC. With about 150 events a true HR near 0.8 gives low power. I expect a miss more likely than not.

assumptions.claim: Ibrutinib plus R-CHOP did not significantly improve EFS in non-GCB DLBCL overall (HR about 0.93).
assumptions.source: PHOENIX, Younes et al., J Clin Oncol 2019

assumptions.claim: R-CHOP control arms in untreated DLBCL with IPI 2-5 have a 2-year PFS of about 70%.

reason: Only about 54 patients were randomized instead of the planned 120, so even a true HR near the SOLAR-1 value of 0.65 gives roughly one-in-three power for a significant PFS result.
rationale: SOLAR-1 showed PFS 11.0 vs 5.7 months (HR 0.65) in PIK3CA-mutant disease, and a Chinese bridging study should see a similar effect. But the randomized cohort is only about 54 patients with perhaps 40 events, so power is around 30-45% and a non-significant HR is likely to be reported. Public disclosure is probably only a CT.gov posting or a Chinese congress later in 2027.

assumptions.claim: In PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- ABC after AI, alpelisib plus fulvestrant gave median PFS 11.0 vs 5.7 months (HR 0.65).
Alpelisib led to treatment discontinuation for adverse events in about 25% of patients versus about 4% on placebo.

reason: ADI-PEG 20 has no established efficacy in GBM, and a 100-patient phase 2 with an OS endpoint in Stupp-treated patients has low power for any realistic effect; most such add-ons fail.
rationale: Arginine deprivation is biologically reasonable in ASS1-low GBM, but no add-on to Stupp chemoradiation has improved OS in unselected newly diagnosed GBM since bevacizumab and TTFields. With about 75 deaths a realistic HR of 0.8 is far from detectable. A small Taiwanese sponsor may announce positive results sooner, so conditional on release I raise the success chance a little.

assumptions.claim: Radiotherapy plus temozolomide gives median OS of about 14.6 months in newly diagnosed GBM.

reason: The primary test is limited to the baseline-CNS-metastases subgroup of 217 patients, perhaps 80-110 patients and about 55 events, so a true HR near 0.65 reaches significance only about half the time.
rationale: Entrectinib has better CNS penetration than crizotinib, with intracranial ORR around 80% in pooled trials and CNS-metastasis PFS about 13.6 months versus roughly 9-10 for crizotinib in historical cohorts. A true HR near 0.6-0.7 is plausible, but the primary analysis is restricted to a subgroup with perhaps 50-60 events, so power is only moderate. Roche may report this confirmatory study late (conference or CT.gov) with little press.
evidence: STARTRK-1/2 and ALKA-372-001 integrated analysis (Drilon, Lancet Oncol 2020)

assumptions.claim: Entrectinib showed median PFS of about 13.6 months in ROS1+ NSCLC with baseline CNS metastases.
assumptions.source: Dziadziuszko et al., J Clin Oncol 2021

assumptions.claim: Crizotinib gave a median PFS of about 19.3 months in ROS1+ NSCLC overall.
assumptions.source: PROFILE 1001, Shaw et al., Lancet Oncol 2019

reason: Adjuvant immunotherapy in HCC has a mixed record (IMbrave050 interim positive then eroded, CheckMate-9DX and EMERALD-2 negative), but a PD-1 plus anti-angiogenic TKI in a high-risk Chinese population versus open-label surveillance has a good chance on BIRC-assessed RFS.
rationale: Large trial (687 patients, about 300 events) in high-risk resected or ablated HCC, mostly HBV, where the control RFS is poor (median under 2 years), leaving room for a clear effect. Camrelizumab plus apatinib is already approved first-line in China and phase 2 adjuvant data were encouraging. Risks: toxicity-driven early discontinuation, and adjuvant HCC trials that look positive at interim often fade. Hengrui tends to disclose positive results fast, so earlier release favors success.
evidence: Camrelizumab + apatinib adjuvant HCC with MVI, phase 2

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant atezolizumab plus bevacizumab improved RFS versus surveillance in the IMbrave050 interim analysis (HR 0.72).
Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib is approved in China as first-line treatment of unresectable HCC.
assumptions.source: NMPA approval of camrelizumab plus apatinib in HCC, 2023

reason: Roche phase 3b in active-not-recruiting status with a firm 2027-02 primary completion; schedule comparison with no hypothesis, so the main uncertainty is slippage of the date and CT.gov posting timing.

Racetam-class SV2A ligands, including levetiracetam, have shown little efficacy against human absence seizures, so brivaracetam may fail to beat placebo on EEG seizure freedom despite its higher SV2A affinity.
rationale: Absence seizures respond to ethosuximide, valproate and lamotrigine, not to levetiracetam, which shares the SV2A mechanism with brivaracetam. The trial likely exists partly for regulatory pediatric requirements, and the adaptive design completed to full size. If the drug works at all, a 24-hour EEG freedom endpoint against a placebo near 10% is easy to separate with 76 per arm. UCB posts results promptly and reports in annual results.
evidence: Levetiracetam in absence epilepsy small studies (Berkovic 2007)

assumptions.claim: Ethosuximide gave freedom from treatment failure in 53% of children with CAE versus 29% with lamotrigine.
Levetiracetam showed little efficacy in human absence epilepsy in a small placebo-controlled study.

reason: Small safety-focused phase 2 by a Korean sponsor, active-not-recruiting with a past primary completion and study completion in April 2027, so results posting by August 2027 is unlikely and primary outcome changes are rare.

About 37 patients per arm in an open-label randomized phase 2 of a small sponsor; an OS hazard ratio needs roughly 0.5 to reach significance, and the trial is slow and likely to slip or report quietly.
rationale: Third-line MSS mCRC with liver metastases: standard TAS-102 or regorafenib gives median OS of about 6.5-7 months. Beating it needs a hazard ratio near 0.5 with only about 55 deaths, which is unlikely for TATE plus pembrolizumab in MSS disease. Pembrolizumab alone is inactive in MSS CRC; any signal would come from liver-directed embolization. Trial began in 2021 and is still recruiting at 3 sites, so a result by mid-2027 is improbable.

assumptions.claim: Median OS with TAS-102 in refractory mCRC is about 7 months and with regorafenib about 6.4 months.
Pembrolizumab monotherapy has essentially no activity in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer.

reason: Non-inferiority against monthly ranibizumab with an assumed margin of about 4.5 letters; one-time gene therapy with rescue injections should be close, but a 1-2 letter deficit with a 12-letter SD leaves the lower bound near the margin.
rationale: Pivotal subretinal AAV8 anti-VEGF gene therapy tested for non-inferiority of week 54 BCVA against ranibizumab, with protocol rescue injections allowed. Phase 1/2a showed stable vision with a large cut in injections. Expected difference is about -1.5 letters; with 210 per arm and SD about 12, the confidence bound sits near a 4.5-letter margin, so success is a coin flip. Two doses give a second chance. Topline expected around Q1 2027.

assumptions.claim: In phase 1/2a, subretinal RGX-314 kept BCVA broadly stable while substantially reducing anti-VEGF injection burden.
Non-inferiority margins in nAMD BCVA trials are typically 4-5 ETDRS letters.

reason: Pediatric bipolar depression trials have high placebo response and mixed outcomes (lurasidone positive, quetiapine negative); a true effect near 3 CDRS-R points gives only about 50-55 percent power with 190 per arm.
rationale: Cariprazine works in adult bipolar depression with a modest effect (about 2.5 MADRS points). In youths, lurasidone beat placebo by 5.7 CDRS-R points, while quetiapine and others failed on high placebo response. Expected cariprazine effect near 3 points with SD about 13 and 190 per arm gives roughly 50% power. Recruitment has been slow (Russia sites), so reporting before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Lurasidone beat placebo by about 5.7 points on CDRS-R at week 6 in pediatric bipolar depression, with placebo change about -15.
assumptions.source: Findling et al, Am J Psychiatry 2017 (NCT01914393)

assumptions.claim: Cariprazine 1.5 mg improved MADRS by about 2.5 points vs placebo in adult bipolar I depression.
assumptions.source: Durgam et al 2016; Earley et al 2019

reason: Only 40 patients per arm for a 6-month patency endpoint where sham patency is already high; an absolute gain of 10-15 points would be needed for significance, and recruitment still seems ongoing.
rationale: Small phase 2 device-drug study of perivenous dexamethasone after DVT recanalization. Sham-arm patency at 6 months is probably around 80%, leaving little headroom; with 40 per arm a significant difference requires about 15-20 points. Biological rationale (reducing venous wall inflammation) is plausible but unproven. Status is still recruiting with a 6-month endpoint, so primary completion will likely slip and results are unlikely by mid-2027.
evidence: Bullfrog perivascular dexamethasone EVOLVE/DANCE feasibility studies 2019

assumptions.claim: After successful venous recanalization, 6-month primary patency is commonly around 75-90%.

reason: Adding a PD-L1 inhibitor to an already effective T-DM1 backbone has little precedent in HER2-positive disease; neoadjuvant IMpassion050 showed no pCR gain and adjuvant atezolizumab failed in TNBC (IMpassion030).
rationale: T-DM1 control after residual disease gives 3-year IDFS about 88% in KATHERINE. Checkpoint inhibitors have not improved outcomes in HER2-positive early breast cancer (IMpassion050 no pCR benefit) and adjuvant atezolizumab failed in IMpassion030. Event-driven trial with about 200 events; true HR is probably 0.9-1.0. Chance of success mainly from a modest benefit in PD-L1 positive tumours.

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant T-DM1 yields 3-year invasive DFS of about 88% in HER2-positive residual disease.
assumptions.source: KATHERINE, von Minckwitz et al, NEJM 2019 (NCT01772472)

assumptions.claim: Adding atezolizumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus HER2 blockade did not improve pCR in HER2-positive early breast cancer.
assumptions.source: IMpassion050, Huober et al, Ann Oncol 2022 (NCT03726879)

reason: SLE phase 3 trials fail often on SRI-4 at week 52 because of high placebo response; litifilimab had supportive phase 2 data but an effect of about 10 points is needed with roughly 183 per arm for reliable significance.
rationale: Anti-BDCA2 litifilimab showed activity on joints and SRI-4 in the LILAC phase 2 SLE cohort. SRI-4 phase 3s in SLE have a roughly 40-50% success rate (anifrolumab TULIP-2 positive, TULIP-1 negative on SRI-4; belimumab positive). Placebo response about 40%, effect about 10 points; 183 per arm gives roughly 60% power, plus a second dose. Topline expected in the first half of 2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo SRI-4 response at week 52 in SLE phase 3 trials is about 35-45%.
Litifilimab improved SLE disease activity vs placebo in the LILAC phase 2 study.

reason: Small two-site drug-vaccine interaction study, active not recruiting with a 59-day follow-up; completion date likely accurate or already past, with slow results posting by a small sponsor.
rationale: Enrollment appears complete and follow-up is short, so a further slip beyond April 2027 is unlikely; SIGA tends to post results late.

reason: JAK inhibitors consistently beat placebo on ACR20 at week 24 in PsA by 25-35 points; with about 139 per arm failure would require an unusually high placebo response or a weak dose.
rationale: SHR0302 (ivarmacitinib) is a JAK1 inhibitor already positive in RA, AS and atopic dermatitis. In PsA, JAK inhibitors reach ACR20 of 55-70% vs about 30-36% placebo (SELECT-PsA 1, OPAL Broaden). With 139 patients per arm a 25+ point gap is overwhelmingly significant. The main uncertainty is whether Hengrui publicly reports it by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Upadacitinib 15 mg gave ACR20 of 70.6% vs 36.2% placebo at week 12 in PsA.
Tofacitinib gave ACR20 of about 50% vs 33% placebo at month 3 in PsA.
assumptions.source: OPAL Broaden, Mease et al, NEJM 2017 (NCT01877668)

reason: SLE phase 3s often fail on a placebo SRI-4 response of 35-45%; litifilimab had a clear phase 2 joint and skin signal, but about a 10 point difference is needed for significance at roughly 187 per arm.
rationale: Anti-BDCA2 litifilimab met its LILAC phase 2 primary (joint count, SLE cohort) at 450 mg. SRI-4 at week 52 has a mixed record: TULIP-2 positive, TULIP-1 negative, placebo near 37-40%. About 187 per arm needs roughly a 10 point difference. One dose meeting the goal is enough, but the two TOPAZ trials share risk. I put success near a coin flip.

assumptions.claim: Placebo SRI-4 response at week 52 was about 37% in TULIP-2 and about 40% in TULIP-1.
Litifilimab 450 mg met the LILAC phase 2 primary endpoint in SLE (change in active joint count at week 24).

reason: Adolescent migraine trials show large placebo responses and pediatric CGRP antibody trials have been mixed; the adult effect of about 2 days could shrink with only 95 per arm.
rationale: Eptinezumab 300 mg beat placebo by about 2.6 migraine days in adult chronic migraine (PROMISE-2). Adolescent placebo responses are large and pediatric CGRP antibody trials have been mixed, so I expect a smaller effect near 1.5 days. With about 95 per arm and SD near 5.5, power is modest. Dosing is PK-matched to adults and one dose suffices.
evidence: Pediatric erenumab episodic migraine trial OASIS 2024

assumptions.claim: In adult chronic migraine, eptinezumab 300 mg reduced monthly migraine days by about 8.2 versus about 5.6 on placebo over weeks 1-12.

reason: CIK-cell add-on to adjuvant gemcitabine has a prior HCC phase 3 signal but no proven pancreatic effect, and delays make a 2027 read unlikely.
rationale: Immuncell-LC cut recurrence in adjuvant HCC in a Korean phase 3, but cell-therapy effects in pancreatic cancer are unproven and Asian CIK trials often overstate benefit. Gemcitabine-alone median RFS is about 12-19 months. The trial is still recruiting and its analysis is tied to 36 months after last patient in, so a result before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Lee 2015 Gastroenterology adjuvant Immuncell-LC in HCC phase 3

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant gemcitabine alone gave a median disease-free survival of about 18.8 months by independent review in APACT.

reason: Active, not recruiting phase 2 with no formal hypothesis; Merck keeps registered dates fairly stable but may close a multi-cohort exploratory study early, and results are unlikely to be posted before the registered March 2027 completion plus several months.

BET inhibitor plus enzalutamide in post-abiraterone poor responders has only single-arm support; the open-label randomized phase 2b is still recruiting and the small sponsor faces funding and timing risk.
rationale: ZEN003694 plus enzalutamide gave rPFS of about 9 months in the single-arm phase 1b/2a post-abiraterone cohort versus 3-5 months historically, but BET inhibitors add thrombocytopenia and randomized confirmation is uncertain. Poor responders on enzalutamide progress fast (about 4 months). With roughly 90 events, an HR near 0.65 is needed. I expect slow enrolment and no early read.
evidence: NCT02711956 ZEN-3694 plus enzalutamide phase 1b/2a, Aggarwal 2020

assumptions.claim: ZEN-3694 plus enzalutamide gave a median rPFS of about 9 months in the single-arm phase 1b/2a study in post-abiraterone mCRPC.

reason: A higher-exposure octreotide depot beating standard SSAs on PFS is plausible but the likely hazard ratio is modest; the active control is slow to progress in a mostly grade 1-2 population.
rationale: CAM2029 gives higher octreotide exposure than octreotide LAR, and dose-escalated SSAs show some activity, but first-line SSA PFS is already long (CLARINET lanreotide over 30 months in extension; PROMID octreotide about 14 months). A superiority gain on blinded-review PFS needs an HR near 0.7. I expect a modest hazard ratio and about a one in five chance of significance.

assumptions.claim: Lanreotide Autogel gave a median PFS of over 30 months in the CLARINET open-label extension in non-progressing GEP-NET.
Octreotide LAR gave a median time to progression of 14.3 months versus 6.0 on placebo in midgut NET.

reason: Clemizole is a repurposed serotonergic antihistamine with no randomized LGS efficacy data; many LGS candidates fail, and the registered completion date is likely optimistic for a rare-disease trial.
rationale: Clemizole is a serotonergic antihistamine repurposed from zebrafish screens, with only small early clinical support and no randomized LGS efficacy data. LGS trials of fenfluramine and cannabidiol showed about 15-20 point placebo-adjusted gains, but many other LGS candidates failed. With 130 per arm and heavy-tailed seizure counts, success needs a true effect near 20 points. A read by mid-2027 is also unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the fenfluramine LGS phase 3, the placebo arm's median change in drop seizures was about -8% versus about -26% on 0.7 mg/kg.

reason: Inhaled alprazolam should stop prolonged seizures faster than placebo, but both co-primaries must be met and a slow, event-driven outpatient trial adds noise and timing risk.
rationale: Inhaled alprazolam acts within minutes, and the qualifying episodes normally last 3-5 minutes or longer, so spontaneous stops within 90 seconds should be uncommon and the drug should separate from placebo. Risks are the second co-primary (no recurrence or rescue to 2 hours), caregiver-administered outpatient noise, and a long slow-enrolling event-driven trial. I put success moderately high but the read probably lands after mid-2027.
evidence: Staccato alprazolam phase 2 photosensitive epilepsy model 2019

assumptions.claim: Qualifying episodes in the record last at least 3 to 5 minutes, so termination within 90 seconds of dosing without treatment should be uncommon.

reason: Fixed-schedule vaccine study already past enrolment, so the final visits are set by the dosing calendar; GSK usually posts results within about a year of completion and rarely changes primary outcomes late.

Perioperative PD-1 plus chemotherapy has repeatedly won on EFS in resectable stage III NSCLC; the uncertainty is the timing of an interim read and that a second primary (ITT EFS at 3 years) may be reported later.
rationale: Perioperative PD-1 plus chemotherapy has repeatedly beaten chemotherapy on EFS in resectable stage III NSCLC (Neotorch HR 0.40, KEYNOTE-671 0.58, AEGEAN 0.68, RATIONALE-315 0.56), so a positive result is likely if one is reported. The uncertainty is timing: an interim EFS read may come in 2027, and two primaries (stage III at 2 years, ITT at 3 years) could leave one unreported.

assumptions.claim: In Neotorch, toripalimab plus chemotherapy gave an EFS hazard ratio of about 0.40 in stage III disease, with control median EFS about 15 months.

reason: Small phase 2a safety study from a small private sponsor; enrolment is closed, so it most likely just finishes, with results posted slowly or only after a later publication.
A realistic hazard ratio of 0.75-0.85 with roughly 250-300 relapse events puts the significance threshold near HR 0.79, so the result is close to a coin flip with a lean to missing.
rationale: Vidofludimus calcium is a DHODH inhibitor (teriflunomide-like mechanism, TEMSO relapse HR about 0.72) with a Nurr1 effect and a positive MRI signal in phase 2 EMPhASIS. The phase 3 primary is time to first relapse in about 1100 patients, with modest event counts (placebo ARR about 0.2-0.3 and Eastern European sites). I expect a true HR near 0.8, so significance is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Vidofludimus calcium showed fewer active MRI lesions than placebo in the phase 2 RRMS trial EMPhASIS.
Teriflunomide 14 mg, another DHODH inhibitor, reduced the relapse hazard by roughly 28% vs placebo in RMS.

reason: The phase 2 TULIP-LN missed its primary endpoint, and add-on effects on top of MMF and steroids in lupus nephritis have been about 10 points; with 180 per arm this is borderline powered.
rationale: Anifrolumab has type I interferon biology and works in SLE, but in phase 2 TULIP-LN the primary missed, with numerically better complete renal response only on the secondary. Benchmarks for add-on therapy at 1 year are belimumab (CRR about +10 points), voclosporin (+18) and obinutuzumab (+13). With 182 per arm and 29% placebo response, significance needs a difference of about 9-10 points. If results are public by June, they are more likely to be positive.

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-LN the primary endpoint (UPCR change) was not significant, but week-52 CRR was numerically higher on anifrolumab than on placebo.
assumptions.source: Jayne et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2022 (TULIP-LN)

assumptions.claim: Placebo complete renal response with MMF and steroids at about one year is roughly 20-35% in recent lupus nephritis trials.

reason: A 24-week FVC endpoint with about 37 per arm and SD near 160 mL has a standard error near 37 mL, so only an effect above about 75 mL reaches significance, and the dose B arm may be the lower dose.
rationale: Phase 2b with two doses against placebo and 24-week FVC change, 110 patients, so power is modest unless the drug acts like nerandomilast or nintedanib (about 50-100 mL benefit at 52 weeks). The record still shows recruiting in October 2026, so primary completion will slip well beyond the registered 2026-12 and data are unlikely before mid-2027. Any dose meeting the primary counts, which helps slightly.

assumptions.claim: In PF-ILD trials placebo patients lose roughly 80-190 mL of FVC over 24-52 weeks.
assumptions.source: INBUILD, Flaherty et al., NEJM 2019; FIBRONEER-ILD 2025

reason: Co-primary HbA1c and triglycerides must both be significant with only 69 patients; the HbA1c effect is diluted in patients who enrolled on triglycerides alone, and benefit in partial lipodystrophy is milder than in generalised disease.
rationale: Metreleptin is approved for generalised lipodystrophy; in partial lipodystrophy open-label data show smaller, variable HbA1c and triglyceride improvement, mostly in patients with poor baseline control. With 35 vs 34 patients and both co-primaries required, power is limited, though the triglyceride effect is likely stronger than HbA1c. A public result by June is more likely if positive.
evidence: Diker-Cohen et al., JCEM 2015 (metreleptin in partial lipodystrophy)
Brown et al., JCEM 2016 (metreleptin in lipodystrophy)

assumptions.claim: Metreleptin improved HbA1c and triglycerides in open-label partial lipodystrophy cohorts with poor baseline control, with smaller effects than in generalised lipodystrophy.

reason: A small sequential phase 2 light-dose study with an unclear primary hypothesis; hemoporfin PDT works, but the arms are small and the Stage Two efficacy test may not be formally powered.
rationale: Hemoporfin PDT was clearly effective against vehicle in Chinese phase 3 trials of port-wine stain, so a high-fluence arm should beat vehicle on PWB-IGA if the scale is sensitive. This is a US dose-finding phase 2 with sequential stages and about 40 per arm, still recruiting, with a safety first primary that may not count as met. Public reporting before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Hemoporfin PDT phase 3 in China (Gu et al., 2019)

assumptions.claim: Hemoporfin PDT gave a clinically meaningful response rate vs placebo PDT in Chinese phase 3 trials in port-wine stain.

reason: Recruitment is closed and the primary safety outcome covers only 24 hours after dosing, so the trial is expected to finish roughly on time; a small Taiwan-based sponsor is unlikely to post results by August 2027.
Same design as ENSURE-1: a true HR near 0.8 with about 250-300 relapse events puts the significance threshold near HR 0.79, so success is roughly a coin flip with a lean to missing.
rationale: Twin of ENSURE-1, with the same vidofludimus calcium DHODH-inhibitor biology and the same primary of time to first relapse over 72 weeks in about 1100 patients. The phase 2 MRI signal supports activity, but relapse events are limited and Eastern European sites usually mean low event rates. Results of the two trials are strongly correlated and likely announced together.

assumptions.claim: Vidofludimus calcium showed fewer active MRI lesions than placebo in the phase 2 RRMS trial EMPhASIS.
Teriflunomide 14 mg, another DHODH inhibitor, reduced the relapse hazard by roughly 28% vs placebo in RMS.

reason: LGS drop-seizure trials succeed about half the time; carisbamate has a mixed history in focal epilepsy and a sodium-channel-like profile, so an effect over a 15-20% placebo response may fall short of significance.
rationale: Large 252-patient placebo-controlled LGS trial gives good power for a 15-20 point difference in median drop-seizure change. Carisbamate showed dose-dependent efficacy in some focal-seizure trials but others were mixed, and LGS placebo-controlled trials of other agents (ganaxolone, soticlestat) have failed. Roughly even odds, with the usual 10-20% placebo reduction as the bar.

assumptions.claim: In the cannabidiol LGS trial GWPCARE3 the placebo arm had a median 17.2% reduction in drop seizures.
The record lists the percent change in drop-seizure frequency per 28 days as the single primary outcome.

reason: Add-on checkpoint combinations after chemoradiation on top of durvalumab have mostly failed, and the strong phase 2 COAST signal (HR 0.44, small and randomized in a modest sample) usually shrinks sharply in phase 3.
rationale: COAST (phase 2, n=189 per arm) gave PFS HR about 0.44 for durvalumab plus oleclumab versus durvalumab, but phase 2 effects shrink and add-ons to durvalumab (PACIFIC-2, SKYSCRAPER-03, KEYLYNK-012) have failed in this setting. Anti-CD73 has weak late-stage precedent, monalizumab failed INTERLINK-1. With about 350 per arm and a durvalumab median near 17 months, an HR near 0.8 would be roughly even power.

assumptions.claim: In COAST, durvalumab plus oleclumab improved PFS versus durvalumab alone with HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.26 to 0.75).
assumptions.source: Herbst et al., Cancer Discovery 2022 / NCT03822351

assumptions.claim: In PACIFIC the durvalumab arm had median PFS by BICR of about 16.9 months.
assumptions.source: PACIFIC, NCT02125461, Spigel et al., JCO 2022

reason: Proof-of-concept with about 70-80 per arm in a slowly progressing disease; oral factor B inhibition may only modestly slow conversion to iRORA, and the conversion rate in placebo eyes may be too low for 24-month power.
rationale: Complement inhibition in geographic atrophy gives only modest lesion-growth slowing, and preventing conversion from intermediate AMD to iRORA is a harder, slower endpoint. The trial is a small phase 2 proof of concept with perhaps 40-50 total events, so even a true 25-30% hazard reduction would reach significance only about 30% of the time. Novartis tends to post results on ClinicalTrials.gov near the 12-month deadline.

assumptions.claim: The record states that about 146 participants, 73 per arm, would be treated worldwide, with a 1:1 allocation.
The single primary outcome is conversion to new iRORA or late AMD in the study eye through month 24.

reason: About 20 men per arm, two co-primaries (IIEF and EHS) that must both be met by the same dose, and a large placebo response in erectile dysfunction make a clean double win unlikely despite company-friendly priors.
rationale: Small industry-supported nutraceutical trial of a fenugreek extract with 64 men over three arms (about 21 each). Earlier Testofen studies reported benefits in libido and some in testosterone-related symptoms, and sponsor-run supplement trials are usually published with positive claims. But ED trials have large placebo responses, IIEF change SD is about 9, so n of 21 per arm has weak power, and two co-primaries plus two doses add hurdles.
evidence: Steels et al. 2011 Testofen libido RCT (Phytother Res)
Maheshwari et al. 2017 fenugreek extract in men (Int J Med Sci)

assumptions.claim: The record lists enrollment of 64 across a placebo group and two Testofen dose groups (300 mg and 600 mg).
Both IIEF and Erection Hardness Score changes are registered as primary outcomes.

reason: Non-inferiority with about 80 per arm and a roughly 30% remission rate gives a wide interval; passing depends on how generous the unstated margin is, though depemokimab's potency makes a true gap near zero likely.
rationale: Depemokimab has higher IL-5 affinity and a longer half-life than mepolizumab, and eosinophil depletion is equivalent in asthma, so true remission rates should be close. Mepolizumab remission at both timepoints was 32% in MIRRA. With about 81 per arm, SE of the difference is near 7.4 points, so non-inferiority needs a margin of 15-20 points or a favourable estimate; GSK likely powered the design with a wide margin. Risk is wide CI.

assumptions.claim: In MIRRA, 32% of mepolizumab 300 mg patients versus 3% on placebo were in remission at both week 36 and week 48.
The record states a non-inferiority design with remission (BVAS=0 and OCS <=4 mg/day) at both week 36 and week 52 as the primary outcome.

reason: Completed pediatric AstraZeneca study run with FDA input; AstraZeneca normally posts results near the 12-month deadline (August 2027) and the primary outcome is simple and unlikely to be edited.

Sputum neutrophil counts are highly skewed and variable; a 56-patient crossover may miss a modest PDE4-mediated anti-inflammatory effect of nebulized ensifentrine on top of maintenance bronchodilators.
rationale: Ensifentrine inhibits PDE4 as well as PDE3, and roflumilast reduced sputum neutrophils by about 36% in a small study, so an anti-inflammatory signal is plausible. But PDE4 inhibition by ensifentrine is weaker, the endpoint is an absolute induced-sputum cell count with large between-subject variance, and a crossover of 56 gives moderate power. Primary completion in March 2027 makes a result by June unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Roflumilast reduced sputum neutrophil counts by about 36% in COPD patients versus placebo.
The record gives March 2027 as the registered primary completion for this crossover with 56 patients.

reason: Phase 2 VIRO-15 was a small single-arm study (n=27); in heavily pretreated platinum-resistant disease control PFS is about 4 months, and open-label randomization with BICR PFS makes a modest oncolytic effect hard to confirm.
rationale: VIRO-15 showed ORR 54% and median PFS 11 months with Olvi-Vec then platinum-bevacizumab, but it was a 27-patient single-arm study compared with historical data. Phase 3 control (non-platinum chemo plus bev, 3+ prior lines) should have median PFS around 4 months; to win, Olvi-Vec must truly reverse platinum resistance. Prior for such phase 2 to phase 3 transitions is about 30%; sponsor discloses promptly if positive.
evidence: AURELIA bevacizumab plus chemotherapy in PROC 2014 (NCT00976911)

assumptions.claim: In AURELIA, chemotherapy plus bevacizumab in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer had median PFS of 6.7 months versus 3.4 months with chemotherapy alone.
The record shows OnPrime enrolling 186 patients, still recruiting, with registered primary completion December 2026.

reason: Small NINDS-funded device feasibility study with 24-month safety follow-up; the registered December 2026 completion may be extended as final visits are confirmed, and device-study results posting is unlikely before late 2027.

Inclisiran lowers LDL-C about 50% on top of statins, and PCSK9 imaging trials (GLAGOV, PACMAN-AMI) showed plaque benefit, but CCTA volume change is noisy and plaque burden in non-obstructive disease is low, so the 24-month difference may not reach significance.
rationale: Inclisiran cuts LDL-C roughly 50% in statin-treated patients with LDL-C 55 or higher. PCSK9 imaging trials (GLAGOV, PACMAN-AMI, HUYGENS) showed plaque regression or slowed progression. 610 patients over 24 months is adequately sized, but CCTA percent-change volumes are highly variable (SD about 30 points) and the statin background slows progression in the placebo arm. Novartis phase 3b readout likely comes at ESC or AHA 2027, after June.

assumptions.claim: Evolocumab added to statin reduced percent atheroma volume versus placebo over 76 weeks on IVUS.
Alirocumab added to high-intensity statin reduced coronary plaque burden versus placebo at 52 weeks after myocardial infarction.

reason: Small open-label phase 2 (42 vs 21) with a four-part composite that requires Breg induction, no de novo DSA, no rejection and minimal immunosuppression; the cell product plausibly moves Breg but the composite is demanding and recruitment is still running, so a result is unlikely before late 2027.
rationale: The trial is still recruiting although primary completion is registered for December 2026 and the primary needs 12 months of follow-up per patient, so results by mid-2027 are very unlikely. If reported, a sponsor-designed composite centred on MIC-induced Breg should favour MIC; controls will rarely meet all four criteria (Breg 3% or more, no steroids, no DSA). Small numbers limit significance.
evidence: TOL-1 MIC phase 1 kidney transplant, Sawitzki 2020

assumptions.claim: Donor-derived modified immune cells allowed reduction of immunosuppression to low-dose tacrolimus monotherapy in a small phase 1 living-donor kidney transplant cohort.

reason: Surgical revascularisation already gives about 90% amputation-free at 30 days in Rutherford I-IIb, leaving little room for superiority with 85 per arm; a sponsor report of non-inferiority is the likelier positive route.
rationale: Limb salvage after surgery for early acute limb ischemia is high, so a 30-day amputation difference is small and 170 patients are underpowered for superiority. Catheter-directed thrombolysis has historically matched surgery (STILE, TOPAS, Rochester). A Russian sponsor with prior positive staphylokinase trials may frame the result as non-inferior or equally effective, which is why the probability is not lower.

assumptions.claim: In randomised comparisons, catheter-directed thrombolysis and surgery for acute limb ischemia gave similar amputation-free survival at 30 days to 6 months.
assumptions.source: STILE (Ann Surg 1994) and Rochester trial (J Vasc Surg 1994)

reason: Agitation-in-Alzheimer's trials have large placebo responses, and an earlier masupirdine phase 3 did not meet its primary; this repeat rests on a subgroup-driven rationale and a 5-HT6 antagonist with modest activity.
rationale: Placebo response in CMAI-based agitation trials is typically 10 or more points and variable. An earlier masupirdine phase 3 missed its primary, and this study was designed around post hoc findings, which often fail to replicate. Either dose meeting significance counts, which helps a little. A 5-HT6 antagonist has no strong precedent for agitation efficacy. Suven usually announces results via exchange filings.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in agitation trials in Alzheimer's dementia improve substantially on CMAI over 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: Brexpiprazole agitation phase 3 (NCT01862640) and AVP-786 phase 3 programmes

reason: Non-inferiority needs the gene therapy to stay within the margin (likely 4.5 letters) of aflibercept at week 54; supplemental-injection rescue keeps vision stable, but variable expression or a slow start could widen the gap.
rationale: Phase 1/2a and phase 2 data showed stable vision and large cuts in injection burden, and protocol-defined rescue aflibercept injections protect BCVA in the gene-therapy arms, making non-inferiority likely if the margin is about 4.5 letters. Two dose arms give two chances. Risks are early BCVA dips before expression, patient variability and a tight margin. Sponsors guided to topline data around the turn of 2026-27.

assumptions.claim: Subretinal RGX-314 in a phase 1/2a study maintained vision with a large reduction in anti-VEGF injections over 2 years.
Aflibercept arms in pre-treated nAMD patients show small BCVA changes (about 0 to +3 letters) at one year.

reason: Ascending-dose phase 2 with only 64 patients, so cohorts are small; the RV/LV effect of an alpha2-antiplasmin inactivator at 48 hours must beat heparin-alone improvement, and a small private sponsor may report late or only numerically.
rationale: TS23 enhances endogenous fibrinolysis by neutralising alpha2-antiplasmin and may improve clot lysis safely. RV/LV on CT at 48 hours typically improves only about 0.1 on heparin, so a thrombolytic-sized effect of 0.2 to 0.3 would clearly separate; a weaker effect with SD about 0.2 and 32 per arm would not. Dose splitting reduces power further. Small private sponsor, so reporting is slow.

assumptions.claim: Heparin alone lowers RV/LV by only about 0.03 to 0.1 at 24-48 hours in intermediate-risk PE.

reason: Two co-primary cognitive and functional endpoints must both be met in a single-site phase 2 of 120 patients over 28 weeks; add-on to cholinesterase inhibitors with unproven mechanism and a slow-progressing mild population make this unlikely.
rationale: Both ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB must be significant at week 28 with 60 per arm. Placebo decline over 28 weeks in mild AD on cholinesterase inhibitors is small (about 1 to 2 ADAS-Cog points), so detecting a 2-point difference needs SD below 5. Most add-on symptomatic phase 2 trials in AD are negative. The trial is still recruiting, so results are unlikely before late 2027.

assumptions.claim: Add-on symptomatic agents tested on top of cholinesterase inhibitors in mild-to-moderate AD (idalopirdine, intepirdine) failed to separate from placebo.

reason: Three-year event-driven outcomes trial in compensated cirrhosis; resmetirom's fibrosis effect may be too modest to move a composite driven by MELD rise and decompensation, and earlier cirrhosis outcome trials of other agents failed.
rationale: Resmetirom improved fibrosis and liver stiffness in F2-F3 and in open-label F4c cohorts, but cirrhosis outcomes trials of simtuzumab, selonsertib and belapectin failed. Event rates in Child-Pugh A are low and 3:1 allocation costs power for a modest hazard ratio. Madrigal has guided to 2027 data, so a readout by June is unlikely and may slip to H2.

assumptions.claim: Resmetirom 80 mg gave fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without NASH worsening in about 24% vs 14% on placebo in F2-F3 NASH.
Selonsertib did not reduce fibrosis or events in compensated NASH cirrhosis.
assumptions.source: STELLAR-4, Harrison et al, J Hepatol 2020

reason: Small cohorts with a high placebo response from background first-line immunotherapy; both cohort primaries (NMDAR at wk 24, LGI1 at wk 52) must be met, and an IL-6R blocker's added effect over steroids/IVIG is unproven.
rationale: About 30 patients per arm per cohort gives power only for a large responder difference. Most NMDAR patients improve on first-line therapy and rescue use counts as failure, so placebo response is sizable. Joint success in both cohorts is unlikely; LGI1 responds slowly. Roche tends to disclose readouts via pipeline updates and congresses, so some statement by mid-2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: Satralizumab is an anti-IL-6 receptor antibody already approved for NMOSD.

reason: Twenty infants per arm with a 24-month composite endpoint: only a very large difference reaches significance, and the trial is still recruiting so any 24-month result is unlikely before 2028.
rationale: Control death or disability is likely 50-65% in this setting; with 20 per arm a significant result needs roughly 25-30 points of absolute benefit. Sponsor has reported positive small trials of sovateltide before, which raises the chance of a favorable framing, but the 24-month follow-up of a still-recruiting trial makes a public result before late 2027 improbable.

assumptions.claim: The registry description cites death or disability in about 55% of infants receiving therapeutic hypothermia.

reason: Mezigdomide is a more potent CELMoD than pomalidomide with encouraging phase 1/2 MeziVd data; failure would most likely come from a PVd arm doing better than historical and toxicity limiting dose intensity.
rationale: Phase 1/2 MeziVd showed high response rates and long PFS in heavily pretreated RRMM, while PVd median PFS was 11.2 months in OPTIMISMM. This population (1-3 prior lines, PI-sensitive, pomalidomide-naive) favors the experimental arm. Expect HR near 0.65. Event-driven analysis timing is uncertain because the trial is still enrolling, so reporting by June is about a coin flip.

assumptions.claim: PVd median PFS was 11.2 months vs 7.1 months for Pd in OPTIMISMM.

reason: Tirzepatide's large weight loss should reduce renal sinus fat, but MRI fat percent change is noisy and the arms are modest (about 67 each), so a smaller-than-expected effect could miss significance.
rationale: Tirzepatide produces roughly 15-20% weight loss in obesity and ectopic fat falls with weight loss. Assuming a 15-25% relative reduction in renal sinus fat versus placebo and a between-patient SD near 30%, 60+ per arm gives good power. Lilly usually posts results about a year after primary completion (July 2026), so a public result by June 2027 is about even odds.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide produced 15-21% mean weight loss at 72 weeks in adults with obesity.

reason: With 11 vs 6 patients, significance needs a very large response difference; spontaneous partial regression in the placebo arm further limits power.
rationale: Fisher exact testing with 11 vs 6 needs roughly 80% vs 17% responders to reach p<0.05. Earlier artesunate work in HPV-related high-grade lesions suggests activity, but partial histologic response in placebo is common. A small private sponsor with two sites may report slowly or as exploratory.

assumptions.claim: The trial randomizes 2:1 with 17 participants and a single response endpoint at week 18.

reason: Percent change in ALT at Day 3 is extremely skewed and noisy in 12 vs 12 patients who all receive standard IV NAC, which already prevents most liver injury.
rationale: Early-treated acetaminophen overdose patients on IV NAC often have small ALT changes, so there is little room to show benefit, and percent change from a low baseline is heavy-tailed. One Taiwan site recruiting 24 patients over several years suggests slippage. Exploratory phase 2 with a small sponsor makes timely public reporting unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Both arms receive standard IV NAC, with 12 patients per arm planned.

reason: Four co-primary outcomes must all be met, including CV death, which will have only a handful of events at 52 weeks in a 150-patient phase 2, so a formal win on all of them is very unlikely.
rationale: The registry lists CV death, NYHA class, LVEF and 6MWT as separate primaries; under the round rules all must be met by the same arm. With about 50 per arm and annual CV mortality of a few percent, the death comparison cannot reach significance. Gene therapy signals from phase 1 are encouraging but a phase 2 is more likely reported as exploratory or positive without a formal win.

assumptions.claim: The trial randomizes 1:1:1 to two AB-1002 doses or placebo with a 52-week primary analysis after all patients complete follow-up.

reason: Adding anti-LAG-3 to PD-1 has not beaten a PD-1 backbone in adjuvant melanoma (RELATIVITY-098 failed) and pembrolizumab is a strong comparator, so a significant RFS gain is unlikely.
rationale: Relatlimab plus nivolumab failed to beat nivolumab alone for RFS in the adjuvant setting (RELATIVITY-098), and LAG-3 add-ons have shown little over PD-1 in melanoma outside RELATIVITY-047. Pembrolizumab already cuts recurrence strongly in stage II-III, leaving little room. The record still shows the trial active and the registered primary completion date unchanged, so timing is uncertain. I expect a modest or null hazard ratio with wide chance variation.

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant nivolumab plus relatlimab did not significantly improve RFS over nivolumab alone in resected stage III-IV melanoma.
Adjuvant pembrolizumab in resected stage II melanoma gave 12-month RFS of roughly 90%.

reason: SRI-4 at week 52 carries a large placebo response (about 35-45%) and SLE phase 3 trials fail often, so the 24-point phase 2 gap may shrink to an unconvincing 8-12 points.
rationale: Phase 2 PAISLEY showed a large SRI-4 gain for deucravacitinib 3 mg BID (58% vs 34% at week 32), and TYK2 inhibition has a solid rationale in SLE. Phase 3 effects usually shrink, placebo SRI-4 at week 52 is around 40%, and SLE trials have a mixed record (TULIP-1, SLE-BRAVE-II failed). With about 258 per arm I expect roughly 75% power at a 12-point gap, so near even odds. SLE-2 is a near-identical twin, so outcomes are correlated.

assumptions.claim: In PAISLEY, SRI-4 response at week 32 was about 58% for deucravacitinib 3 mg BID versus about 34% for placebo.
assumptions.source: PAISLEY, NCT03252587 (Morand et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2023)

assumptions.claim: Placebo SRI-4 response at week 52 in belimumab BLISS-52 was about 44%.

reason: SRI-4 at week 52 carries a large placebo response (about 35-45%) and SLE phase 3 trials fail often, so the 24-point phase 2 gap may shrink to an unconvincing 8-12 points.
rationale: Same design as POETYK SLE-1 (twin trial, same dates). Phase 2 PAISLEY showed a large SRI-4 gain for deucravacitinib 3 mg BID (58% vs 34% at week 32), and TYK2 inhibition has a solid rationale in SLE. Phase 3 effects usually shrink, placebo SRI-4 at week 52 is around 40%, and SLE phase 3 trials fail often. With about 257 per arm I expect roughly 75% power at a 12-point gap. Outcome strongly correlated with SLE-1.

assumptions.claim: In PAISLEY, SRI-4 response at week 32 was about 58% for deucravacitinib 3 mg BID versus about 34% for placebo.
assumptions.source: PAISLEY, NCT03252587 (Morand et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2023)

assumptions.claim: Placebo SRI-4 response at week 52 in belimumab BLISS-52 was about 44%.

reason: With 31 patients per arm and a subjective, noisy patient-reported VHI-10 percent change, a real but moderate effect often misses significance, and placebo injections carry a large response.
rationale: Small Japanese confirmatory trial of a recombinant HGF injection for vocal fold scar, 31 per arm, with a patient-reported primary (VHI-10 percent improvement at week 24). Percent-change SD is large (about 35-40 points), so a 15-20 point true gap gives only about 50% power. Earlier Japanese studies suggested a benefit, but placebo injection responses in voice outcomes are sizeable. I put success a bit below even.

assumptions.claim: The trial enrolls 62 patients in Japan with a 24-week VHI-10 improvement rate as the primary outcome.

reason: SRI-4 placebo response of around 40% at week 60 narrows the gap; a depleting anti-BAFF-R antibody should give a belimumab-sized or larger effect, but SLE phase 3 trials fail often.
rationale: Ianalumab deeply depletes B cells and cut disease activity in Sjögren's phase 3 trials, so monthly dosing should beat placebo on SRI-4 by roughly 12-16 points, similar to or above belimumab. With about 145 per arm and 40% placebo response, power is near 80%. Risks are a high steroid-taper-adjusted placebo response and the usual SLE phase 3 failure rate. The registered primary completion (March 2027) leaves little time for a public result by June 2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo SRI-4 response at week 52 in belimumab BLISS-52 was about 44%.
The trial's registered primary completion date is 26 March 2027 with SRI-4 at week 60 as primary.

reason: Small pediatric phase 2a of 48 patients in rare serious infections across 8 countries and 4 age cohorts; registered primary completion of March 2027 while still recruiting in October 2026 makes a slip past June 2027 likely, and results are unlikely to be posted by August 2027.
About 60 per arm and a high adolescent pain placebo response mean a roughly 10-15 point responder gap, as seen in adults, would only just reach significance.
rationale: Adult T3MPO-1 and T3MPO-2 showed 6/12-week APS responder gaps of 8 and 13 points for tenapanor 50 mg BID. Adolescent IBS has a high placebo response for pain, and the combined endpoint needs both pain and SBM response. With about 60 per arm, a 12-point gap gives only about 45-55% power. Tenapanor's bowel effect is robust, which helps; two active doses add a small multiplicity cost but one dose passing counts.

assumptions.claim: In adult T3MPO-2, the 6/12-week APS responder rate was 36.5% with tenapanor 50 mg BID versus 23.7% with placebo.
assumptions.source: T3MPO-2, NCT02686138 (Chey et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2021)

assumptions.claim: The study is completed per the registry, with primary completion on 20 August 2026.

reason: Inavolisib may only modestly out-last alpelisib in a post-CDK4/6 population; the gain likely comes mostly from better tolerability, so the hazard ratio could land near 0.8 and miss.
rationale: Inavolisib is more PI3K-alpha-selective and better tolerated than alpelisib; INAVO120 showed HR 0.43 against placebo, and alpelisib post-CDK4/6 gives median PFS around 6-7 months (BYLieve 7.3). Alpelisib's hyperglycaemia and rash cause many dose reductions and discontinuations, which should favour inavolisib. About 420 patients and around 300 events give good power for HR near 0.7. Uncertainty comes from the lack of any head-to-head phase 2 data and open-label BICR variance.

assumptions.claim: Alpelisib plus fulvestrant after CDK4/6 inhibitor gave median PFS of 7.3 months in BYLieve cohort A.
assumptions.source: BYLieve, NCT03056755 (Rugo et al., Lancet Oncol 2021)

assumptions.claim: Inavolisib plus palbociclib-fulvestrant had a PFS hazard ratio of 0.43 versus placebo in INAVO120.

reason: Cenerimod missed its primary endpoint in phase 2 CARE, with benefit seen mainly post hoc in high-interferon patients, so an all-comer SRI-4 gain over a ~40% placebo response is likely small.
rationale: Phase 2 CARE did not meet its primary endpoint (mSLEDAI-2K change at month 6); signals at 4 mg were concentrated in a high type-I interferon subgroup and in post hoc analyses. S1P1 modulation reduces circulating lymphocytes but is a mild immunomodulator. With about 235 per arm and a 40% placebo SRI-4 rate, a true 6-8 point gap gives under 40% power. Registered primary completion is March 2027, so a result before June is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 CARE study the primary endpoint (mSLEDAI-2K change at month 6) was not met for any cenerimod dose.
assumptions.source: CARE, NCT03742037 (Hermann et al., Lancet Rheumatol 2022)

assumptions.claim: The trial's registered primary completion date is 31 March 2027 with SRI-4 at month 12 as primary.

reason: Patients must already respond to steroids, so many placebo patients keep a stable response off treatment; a 12-month off-treatment endpoint also carries more dropout and rescue noise with about 75 per arm.
rationale: Rituximab added to dexamethasone roughly raised sustained response in newly diagnosed ITP from about 36% to 60%, and ianalumab depletes B cells more deeply and also blocks BAFF-R survival signalling. Entry requires steroid response, which lifts control response to about 30-35%. With about 75 per arm and a 15-point gap, power is about 65-70%. The primary was switched to SROT-12 in May 2026, likely before unblinding, which adds some uncertainty but little bias.
evidence: Zaja et al., Blood 2010 (dexamethasone with or without rituximab in newly diagnosed ITP)

assumptions.claim: Adding rituximab to dexamethasone in newly diagnosed ITP raised sustained response at 6 months from about 36% to about 63%.
The primary endpoint was changed to SROT-12 in May 2026, with time to treatment failure now a key secondary.

reason: Chinese PANOVA-3 replication in locally advanced pancreatic cancer with a modest expected OS gain (PANOVA-3 HR 0.82, p=0.039); open-label device trial, 5 sites, still recruiting, so result unlikely before mid-2027 and effect likely near the significance edge.
rationale: Design mirrors PANOVA-3, which gave HR 0.82 and a borderline p of 0.039 for TTFields plus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel. With 512 patients and about 360 deaths this trial has fair power for HR 0.80, but the true effect may be smaller, the trial is open-label, and a Chinese device sponsor may report favourably. Reporting before June 2027 is unlikely because it is still recruiting.

assumptions.claim: PANOVA-3 reported median OS 16.2 vs 14.2 months, HR 0.82, for TTFields plus GnP vs GnP in locally advanced pancreatic cancer.
Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel control arms in locally advanced pancreatic cancer have median OS of about 13-15 months from randomization.

reason: Bevacizumab biosimilar equivalence trial on week-18 ORR; such trials usually succeed and the main risk is a chance miss of the ORR margin. Russian sponsor with little public disclosure, and enrolment still recruiting so completion likely slips.
rationale: Bevacizumab biosimilars in non-squamous NSCLC with paclitaxel-carboplatin have almost always shown ORR equivalence with Avastin (e.g. ABP 215, MIL60, BAT1706), with 620 patients giving ample power at usual margins. The residual risk is a chance miss on the ORR ratio or difference. Public disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely because the sponsor is Russian and still recruiting.

assumptions.claim: Approved bevacizumab biosimilars demonstrated ORR equivalence to Avastin with paclitaxel-carboplatin in non-squamous NSCLC.

reason: Oral NLRP3 inhibitor with modest phase 2 signal in gout flare; placebo response on the 72-hour VAS is large with rescue medication available, so a 7-10 mm difference is needed and may not materialize. Private sponsor, slow recruiting.
rationale: Dapansutrile showed a dose-related pain reduction in phase 2 gout flare work, but placebo patients improve a lot by 72 hours and rescue medication is allowed in both arms. With SD around 27 mm and 200 vs 100 patients, a 8 mm difference gives about 70 percent power, and the true effect is uncertain. Private sponsor, so reporting before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Placebo patients with acute gout flare improve by roughly 35-45 mm on a 100-mm pain VAS by 72 hours.

reason: S1P1 modulator whose phase 2 CARE study missed the overall SRI-4 endpoint and showed benefit only in a high-IFN, low-steroid subgroup. SLE trials with 12-month SRI-4 and a 40-45 percent placebo response fail often.
rationale: Phase 2 CARE did not meet its primary endpoint overall; cenerimod 4 mg looked better only in patients with high interferon signature and low steroid dose. OPUS enrols a broad moderate-to-severe population on background therapy, and SLE trials commonly have placebo SRI-4 rates of 40-45 percent, which blunts differences. Viatris will announce topline for both OPUS studies around the first half of 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 CARE study cenerimod 4 mg did not significantly improve mSRI-4 at month 6 vs placebo in the overall population.
Placebo SRI-4 response in recent SLE phase 3 trials is typically around 35-45 percent at week 52.

reason: Remibrutinib clearly beat placebo in adult CSU (REMIX-1/2, UAS7 difference about 7-8), but this adolescent study has only about 100 patients and needs UAS7, ISS7 and HSS7 all significant; a high adolescent placebo response is the main risk.
rationale: In adult REMIX-1/2 remibrutinib improved week-12 UAS7 by about 7-8 points over placebo with p<0.001. Adolescent disease behaves similarly, but with 67 vs 33 patients and SD about 12.5 the power for a 7-8 point difference is around 80 percent per endpoint, and all three correlated co-primaries must win. Novartis typically posts or presents pediatric data within a year.

assumptions.claim: In REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, remibrutinib 25 mg bid improved week-12 UAS7 versus placebo by roughly 7-8 points (p<0.001).

reason: Strong phase 1b/2 evidence for cabozantinib/zanzalintinib plus nivolumab in non-clear cell RCC against a weak sunitinib control (mPFS 6-8 months); risk is that both PFS and ORR must be significant with split alpha, and event-driven timing may slip.
rationale: Non-clear cell RCC has few active drugs; sunitinib median PFS is about 6-8 months while cabozantinib plus nivolumab reached 12.5 months with ORR 48 percent in phase 2, and zanzalintinib plus nivolumab showed similar activity in STELLAR-002. With 317 patients and about 190 events, an HR near 0.6 is comfortably significant for PFS and ORR; modest risk from alpha splitting between two primaries.
evidence: Lee et al. cabozantinib+nivolumab nccRCC phase 2, Lancet Oncol 2022

assumptions.claim: Cabozantinib plus nivolumab in non-clear cell RCC produced ORR 48 percent and median PFS 12.5 months in a phase 2 trial.
Sunitinib median PFS in first-line non-clear cell RCC is roughly 6-8 months.

reason: Benralizumab cuts exacerbations 30-50 percent in adults, but this paediatric event-driven trial has only 94 patients and perhaps 40-50 events, giving limited power unless the HR is below about 0.5.
rationale: Benralizumab reduced annual exacerbation rates by about 28-51 percent in SIROCCO/CALIMA and is already approved in adolescents and recently in children by extrapolation. A time-to-first-exacerbation design with 94 patients has few events, so even a true HR of 0.6 gives only around 40 percent power. Placebo exacerbation risk in treated paediatric patients on high-dose ICS may also be lower than in adults.
evidence: TATE benralizumab paediatric PK study NCT04305405

assumptions.claim: Benralizumab reduced annual asthma exacerbation rate by 28-51 percent versus placebo in adults and adolescents with severe eosinophilic asthma.

reason: Factor XIa inhibition just reduced recurrent ischemic stroke in OCEANIC-STROKE (asundexian HR 0.74), supporting the class; risk is that milvexian's dose or the antiplatelet background gives a smaller effect, as in the stopped ACS trial.
rationale: OCEANIC-STROKE showed asundexian lowers ischemic stroke after non-cardioembolic stroke with HR 0.74 and no major bleeding excess, supporting factor XIa inhibition in this setting. AXIOMATIC-SSP suggested milvexian 25 mg bid was the best dose. With roughly 12,500 patients and about 950 events, an HR of 0.82 is significant; risk is a smaller effect or dose issues, as seen when the ACS trial stopped for futility.

assumptions.claim: OCEANIC-STROKE met its primary endpoint of ischemic stroke with HR about 0.74 for asundexian vs placebo on top of antiplatelet therapy.
In AXIOMATIC-SSP milvexian reduced symptomatic ischemic stroke and covert infarcts, with the 25 mg bid dose showing the largest effect.

reason: Rare FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma phase 2 still recruiting 120 patients; registered primary completion of December 2026 is unlikely to hold, and the ORR primary is generally unchanged.

Non-inferiority to apixaban should be met if milvexian 100 mg BID inhibits factor XIa adequately; the main failure path is under-inhibition as seen with asundexian 50 mg in OCEANIC-AF, or a tight margin with few events.
rationale: About 20,000 patients make non-inferiority well powered if the true HR is near 1. Asundexian 50 mg failed in OCEANIC-AF through weak factor XIa inhibition, but milvexian 100 mg BID gives fuller inhibition and showed less bleeding than apixaban in PACIFIC-AF. The AF trial continued after the sister ACS trial stopped in 2025. Margin unknown; I allow about a 1 in 3 chance of inferiority or a missed margin.

assumptions.claim: Asundexian 50 mg once daily was inferior to apixaban for stroke or systemic embolism in OCEANIC-AF, with a low apixaban event rate (about 26 events in roughly 7,400 patients).
Milvexian 100 mg twice daily had less bleeding than apixaban in the phase 2 AF study.

reason: Phase 2a crossover with three doses where any dose may win; the drug augments counter-regulatory glucagon, but nocturnal CGM events are noisy and the effect could be modest. Recruitment was still open in late 2026, so reporting before mid-2027 is unlikely.
rationale: Crossover design gives each patient their own placebo period, which boosts power; about 62 patients per dose can detect a rate ratio near 0.7. Any dose meeting the objective counts, which helps. The mechanism (enhanced glucagon response during hypoglycaemia) is plausible, but nocturnal hypoglycaemia counts are overdispersed and a phase 2a effect may be modest. A private sponsor tends to announce positive results.

assumptions.claim: Enrolment requires at least 1% time below 54 mg/dL over 4 weeks, which implies several nocturnal events per 28 days in the placebo period.

reason: An overall survival gain from a microbiome product at 12 months after reduced-intensity transplant is a high bar: deaths are driven by relapse, infection and GvHD, and the trial has only about 100 expected events.
rationale: Phase 2b with 387 patients and an all-cause survival endpoint at 12 months. Earlier open-label MaaT033 data and gut-microbiome associations suggest benefit, but overall survival is a distal endpoint with roughly 100 deaths, so only a large effect (HR below about 0.65) would reach two-sided 0.05. Prior microbiome-in-transplant evidence is observational. The sponsor is listed and will announce topline early in 2027.
evidence: Peled et al, JCO 2020 (microbiota diversity and survival after alloHCT)

assumptions.claim: Higher gut microbiota diversity after alloHCT is associated with better overall survival in observational cohorts.
assumptions.source: Peled et al, J Clin Oncol 2020 (PMID 32040086)

reason: Invasive-injection placebo responses in fecal incontinence are large and the OASI-restricted population looks like a post hoc enrichment; the sponsor is private and rarely issues press releases, so public results by mid-2027 are unlikely.
rationale: Single injection of autologous muscle-derived cells vs placebo with 12-month change in incontinence episodes. Fecal incontinence trials show high sham or placebo responses (often 30-50% reduction), and the restriction to women with obstetric sphincter injury suggests enrichment after an earlier less clear result. A two-stage design with 200 patients gives moderate power for a modest treatment difference.
evidence: Cook MyoSite iltamiocel phase 2/3 fecal incontinence programme (2017-2022)

assumptions.claim: Placebo or sham injection arms in fecal incontinence trials typically show large reductions in weekly episodes.
assumptions.source: Pooled FI trial literature (e.g. NASHA Dx/Solesta 2010 sham response)

reason: Adjuvant CDK inhibitor benefit is real in monarchE and NATALEE but PALLAS and PENELOPE-B failed; with an early analysis and few IDFS events the HR may not reach significance, and a Chinese sponsor may not report by mid-2027.
rationale: TQB3616 is a CDK2/4/6 inhibitor with positive metastatic phase 3 data; adjuvant CDK4/6 trials split (monarchE and NATALEE positive, PALLAS and PENELOPE-B negative). With 1,946 patients and roughly 2.5 years median follow-up at an interim, events may be limited; a true HR near 0.75 would be significant only with enough events. Sponsor tends to disclose positive interim results.

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy improved IDFS (HR about 0.75) in high-risk HR+/HER2- early breast cancer.
Adjuvant palbociclib added to endocrine therapy did not improve invasive disease-free survival.

reason: SLE phase 3 trials fail often because of high placebo BICLA response and background therapy effects; upadacitinib has phase 2 support, but two replicate studies must both show benefit and results are unlikely before July 2027.
rationale: Upadacitinib 30 mg showed BICLA and SRI-4 benefit over placebo in phase 2 SLE (alone and with elsubrutinib), and JAK inhibition has partial support from baricitinib (BRAVE-I positive, BRAVE-II not). Placebo BICLA at week 52 is typically 30-47%. About 500 patients per study give adequate power for a 10-point difference, but SLE phase 3 history has about 50% failure and the program needs both studies to succeed.

assumptions.claim: Placebo BICLA response at week 52 in the anifrolumab TULIP-2 trial was about 30% vs 47% with anifrolumab.
Baricitinib met its SRI-4 primary in SLE-BRAVE-I but not in SLE-BRAVE-II.

reason: Small (49 patients) non-comparative Novartis phase 2, enrolment closed; primary completion should be met or updated to an actual date near Dec 2026, with results posting more likely after the August 2027 read date.

An oral JAK1 inhibitor in an unselected exacerbation-prone asthma population with about 62 per arm needs roughly a 125 mL FEV1 gain over placebo to reach significance, which is a large effect for this mechanism.
rationale: Dose-ranging phase 2 with about 62 patients per arm and a pre-BD FEV1 SD near 330 mL gives a standard error of about 60 mL, so the top dose needs about +125 mL over placebo. JAK1 inhibition in non-biomarker-selected asthma is unproven and the effect is likely modest. Any one dose or a dose-response test can count, which helps. Incyte tends to disclose positive readouts quickly, which raises the conditional chance.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-arm pre-BD FEV1 improvement in moderate-to-severe asthma trials is typically about 80 to 150 mL by weeks 12 to 24.
The trial compares three povorcitinib regimens with placebo on change in pre-BD FEV1 from baseline to week 24, with 247 patients randomized.

reason: A PD-1/LAG-3 bispecific against pembrolizumab on the same chemotherapy backbone needs an implausibly large PFS gain to be significant in 83 patients, and the program appears deprioritized.
rationale: Head-to-head against a pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy standard in PD-L1-positive TNBC. With 83 patients and about 60 events, a significant PFS result needs a hazard ratio near 0.55 or better. Adding LAG-3 blockade to PD-1 has rarely beaten PD-1 alone, and Roche has not advanced tobemstomig to phase 3 in this setting. A randomized phase 2 with a small sample is very unlikely to show superiority.

assumptions.claim: In KEYNOTE-355 median PFS was 9.7 months with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in CPS 10 or higher and about 7.6 months in CPS 1 or higher.
The trial randomizes 83 patients to tobemstomig or pembrolizumab, each with nab-paclitaxel, with PFS as the primary outcome.

reason: Descriptive dose-regimen comparison with data collection essentially complete at registered primary completion; BMS usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline, so posting by the August 2027 read date is unlikely to be more than a minority outcome.
Bacterial lysate effects on wheezing are modest and inconsistent; with about 150 per arm a rate ratio around 0.8 to 0.85 would not reach significance.
rationale: Earlier small trials and meta-analyses suggest OM-85 cuts wheezing attacks by about 30 to 40 percent, but those were small and often open to bias, and a large NIH-funded infant trial did not show a clear benefit. With 148 per arm and a placebo rate near 1.4 episodes per 6 months, power for a rate ratio of 0.8 is only about 30 percent. A true effect of 0.7 or better is needed for a likely win.
evidence: Cochrane review of OM-85 for respiratory infections, 2012

assumptions.claim: Small earlier randomized trials of OM-85 in preschool children reported roughly 30 to 40 percent fewer wheezing attacks than placebo.
