The trial randomizes 296 children 1:1 and compares the 6-month rate of wheezing episodes on OM-85 versus placebo.

reason: Both ORR and PFS are listed as primaries and must both be met; ORR after prior CDK4/6 inhibitor is low in both arms, so a significant ORR gap is hard to show, and PFS data are likely not mature by mid-2027.
rationale: Co-primary ORR and PFS must both be met. Rechallenge with a CDK4/6 inhibitor plus fulvestrant after progression gives a modest PFS gain (postMONARCH HR 0.73) or none (PACE), and ORR is low (about 5 to 17 percent) so ORR significance with 127 per arm is uncertain. Still recruiting in Oct 2026, so any early public result would be a phase 2 stage readout.

assumptions.claim: In postMONARCH abemaciclib plus fulvestrant after CDK4/6 inhibitor progression improved PFS versus placebo plus fulvestrant (6.0 vs 5.3 months, HR 0.73).
In PACE palbociclib plus fulvestrant after CDK4/6 inhibitor progression did not significantly improve PFS over fulvestrant alone.

reason: A small phase 2 of a novel peptide on a hard endpoint (any KDIGO AKI incl. urine output) in an enriched population; the incidence in placebo is high and the drug needs about a 40 percent relative reduction to be significant.
rationale: With 120 per arm and a placebo AKI rate near 40 percent (KDIGO including urine output, high-risk CKD patients), a significant result needs roughly 40 versus 24 percent. Prior AKI-prevention drugs in cardiac surgery have mostly failed and earlier LSALT data were not clearly positive. A small sponsor with 9 sites also risks slow enrolment.
evidence: Cardiac surgery AKI prevention trials, e.g. amino acid infusion PROTECTION (NCT03709264), 2021

assumptions.claim: Cardiac surgery-associated AKI affects roughly 20 to 30 percent of patients by creatinine criteria and more when urine output criteria are added.
The trial enrols CKD stage 2 or 3 patients with an additional AKI risk factor, randomized 120 per arm to LSALT 10 mg twice daily for 5 days or placebo.

reason: Both primaries must be met: rPFS non-inferiority within an unknown margin and a hot-flash benefit; the hot-flash benefit is near-certain, but non-inferiority on rPFS with few events and an unstated margin carries real risk.
rationale: Patients have PSA below 0.2 after 6 months of apalutamide plus ADT, a favourable group, so rPFS over the next 18 months should be around 85 percent in both arms and events few (about 60). Apalutamide continues in the intermittent arm, which should preserve disease control. Hot flash improvement off ADT is near-certain. Risk is the non-inferiority margin versus event noise, and SWOG 9346 failed to show non-inferiority for intermittent ADT.

assumptions.claim: In SWOG 9346 intermittent ADT did not meet the non-inferiority criterion for overall survival (HR 1.10, upper bound above the 1.20 margin).

LIBERTAS randomizes about 420 patients with mCSPC and PSA below 0.2 ng/mL after 6 months of apalutamide plus ADT to continued versus intermittent ADT, with 18-month rPFS and hot flash score as co-primaries.

reason: The 0.01 significance level and the placebo response in hair counts make a small true effect hard to confirm; the non-inferiority comparison to topical 2% minoxidil may also be required and has no stated margin.
rationale: Oral minoxidil is an established hair-growth agent. A 24-week 1 mg trial in women (Ramos 2020) showed gains over placebo, and topical 2% minoxidil adds about 10 hairs/cm2 over placebo. With 208 versus 104 patients and an SD near 18, a 10 hair difference gives z above 4, so the 0.01 level should be met. Risks are a smaller true effect, the extra topical non-inferiority requirement, and the unusual wording that calls the analysis descriptive.
evidence: Ramos 2020 JAMA Dermatol, minoxidil 1 mg oral vs placebo
DeVillez 1994 Arch Dermatol, topical minoxidil in women

assumptions.claim: Oral minoxidil 1 mg for 24 weeks increased hair density versus placebo in women with non-scarring hair loss in a randomized trial.
Topical 2% minoxidil produces an increase in non-vellus hair count of about 20 hairs/cm2 versus about 12 with placebo in women at 32 weeks.

reason: Inavolisib has proven PFS benefit in PIK3CA-mutated HR+ disease, but PI3K inhibition with HER2 therapy is unproven (alpelisib EPIK-B2 was stopped), and PIK3CA-mutant HER2+ maintenance PFS may only be modestly improved.
rationale: Still recruiting in Oct 2026, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely; if it comes early it would be an interim that crossed the boundary. Inavolisib cut progression by more than half in INAVO120, and PIK3CA-mutant HER2+ disease has poor outcomes on anti-HER2 alone, so a real effect is plausible. EPIK-B2 with alpelisib and tolerability remain risks. Small trial of 230.

assumptions.claim: Inavolisib plus palbociclib-fulvestrant reduced the risk of progression or death by about 57 percent (HR 0.43) in PIK3CA-mutated HR+ endocrine-resistant breast cancer.
assumptions.source: INAVO120, NCT04191499, Turner et al NEJM 2024

assumptions.claim: In PATINA the control arm of anti-HER2 therapy plus endocrine therapy had median PFS of about 15 months after induction.

reason: The trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026 against a Feb 2027 registered completion, so the date will probably slip and topline is more likely H2 2027; Celltrion biosimilar equivalence trials almost always succeed.
rationale: Celltrion biosimilar programmes (CT-P41, CT-P42, CT-P43, CT-P47 and others) have met their equivalence primaries in phase 3 with high reliability. Ocrelizumab PK is well characterised and new GdE lesion counts are a sensitive, established equivalence endpoint at week 24. The main uncertainty is that both PK and efficacy must be shown within the protocol margins, and the timing of the readout.
evidence: Sandoz natalizumab biosimilar Antelope trial in RRMS

assumptions.claim: Celltrion phase 3 biosimilar comparative trials have generally met their equivalence primary endpoints.
assumptions.source: Celltrion CT-P41 and CT-P43 phase 3 publications 2022-2024

reason: Small Roche phase 2 (21 patients) with a safety primary and a registered end of 2026; Roche usually keeps or updates dates promptly, and results posting typically comes closer to the one-year deadline.
rationale: Active, not recruiting with only 21 participants; the registered completion of 31 Dec 2026 is close, with some chance of a slip past March 2027. Roche generally posts results within about a year of completion, so posting by Aug 2027 is less likely than not.

reason: Strong precedent for an ADC plus PD-1 over platinum chemo, but OS is a co-primary and may be immature at the first analysis, and HER2 IHC 1+ patients may benefit less.
rationale: The Chinese RC48-C016 trial of disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab versus chemotherapy in HER2-expressing urothelial cancer reported PFS HR 0.36 and OS HR 0.54, and EV-302 shows ADC plus pembrolizumab beats platinum chemo by wide margins. The global trial uses pembrolizumab and includes IHC 1+. Main risk is the co-primary OS not being significant at the first analysis.

assumptions.claim: In RC48-C016, disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab versus chemotherapy gave PFS HR about 0.36 and OS HR about 0.54 in HER2-expressing locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer.
In EV-302 the platinum chemotherapy control arm had median PFS of about 6.3 months.
assumptions.source: EV-302 NCT04223856, Powles et al NEJM 2024

reason: Adjunctive MDD trials have large placebo responses and Alto's biomarker-enriched programme has missed before (ALTO-100 phase 2b); the subgroup is small, so power is limited.
rationale: Phase 2b in a pre-defined biomarker subgroup, which shrinks the analysed sample. Adjunctive depression trials succeed perhaps a third of the time and placebo change is typically 10 to 12 MADRS points. Alto's earlier ALTO-100 phase 2b in MDD failed despite biomarker enrichment, though ALTO-300 had a positive phase 2a signal. A public company will announce topline either way.

assumptions.claim: Alto Neuroscience reported that ALTO-100 did not meet its primary endpoint in its phase 2b MDD trial.

reason: Systemic sclerosis phase 3 trials have a poor record and anifrolumab's phase 2 did not clearly separate on skin score; placebo CRISS response is also substantial.
rationale: Type I interferon signature is present in a subset of SSc, and the trial enriches for diffuse early disease, but SSc trials of immunomodulators (tocilizumab, abatacept, rituximab) have mostly missed their primaries. Anifrolumab's phase 2 was not clearly positive on mRSS. A responder endpoint needing two improved components with 157 per arm is demanding. AstraZeneca will disclose by pipeline update even if negative.

assumptions.claim: Tocilizumab missed its primary mRSS endpoint in the phase 3 focuSSced trial in early diffuse SSc.
assumptions.source: focuSSced NCT02453256, Khanna et al Lancet Respir Med 2020

reason: A naked EGFR x HER3 bispecific added to docetaxel must beat docetaxel on both OS and PFS (co-primary); post-IO NSCLC docetaxel add-on and replacement strategies have mostly failed to improve OS.
rationale: Both OS and BICR PFS must succeed. Second-line NSCLC after chemo-immunotherapy has seen many failures against docetaxel (EVOKE-01, TROPION-Lung01 OS), and a naked bispecific plus docetaxel is a modest-effect strategy. Registered completion of July 2026 has passed without an update, suggesting analysis is delayed. A Chinese sponsor typically discloses when positive.

assumptions.claim: The docetaxel control arm in EVOKE-01 had median OS of about 11 months in post-chemo-immunotherapy NSCLC.

reason: ESSDAI trials in Sjogren's carry large placebo improvement in recently diagnosed, highly active patients, leaving only a modest placebo-adjusted effect to detect.
rationale: TYK2 inhibition targets the interferon axis central to Sjogren's, and the trial has two doses and 258 per arm, with one dose enough. Recent ESSDAI trials (ianalumab NEPTUNUS-2) reached significance with placebo-adjusted differences of about 1.5 to 2 points, so a realistic effect is near the detection limit. Placebo response in early, active disease is the main risk.

assumptions.claim: Ianalumab reached statistical significance on ESSDAI change in the phase 3 NEPTUNUS-2 trial in Sjogren's disease with a placebo-adjusted difference of under 2 points.

reason: Part B is small and event-driven; a true effect is likely against poor chemotherapy outcomes after FGFR inhibitor failure, but few events and an uncertain dose selection add variance.
rationale: After chemotherapy and an FGFR inhibitor, cholangiocarcinoma has few options and control PFS is about 2 to 3 months. Phase 2 data for tinengotinib in this refractory setting showed meaningful response rates and disease control, so a large HR is plausible and a small trial can still win. Risks are the small size, dose-selection design and a small sponsor's timing.

assumptions.claim: Median PFS on chemotherapy after progression on an FGFR inhibitor in FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma is only a few months.
assumptions.source: Retrospective series after FGFR inhibitor failure, 2021-2023 (e.g. Silverman et al)

reason: Both stent non-inferiority on target lesion failure and superiority of 1-month DAPT on bleeding are primaries; the second is the more fragile, and the margin is unknown.
rationale: Modern thin-strut sirolimus-eluting stents are usually non-inferior to Xience on 1-year TLF, and 2312 patients give adequate power for a typical margin. Abbreviated DAPT reliably cuts BARC 2/3/5 bleeding (MASTER DAPT, TWILIGHT, STOPDAPT-2), but superiority must be shown in about 1156 per arm. Both primaries must succeed under round rules. Timing depends on the congress slot, likely ESC or TCT 2027.

assumptions.claim: In MASTER DAPT, abbreviated DAPT after PCI in high-bleeding-risk patients reduced major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding compared with standard DAPT.
assumptions.source: MASTER DAPT NCT03023020, Valgimigli et al NEJM 2021

reason: A saline intradermal active control that also gets three injection sessions can produce a sizeable 1-grade response on both cheeks, which could narrow the margin versus a filler-like gel in 118 vs 39 patients.
rationale: AbbVie advanced to a Phase 3 pivotal with a space-filling gel, which gives an immediate visible effect that investigators can see, and the 3:1 design with blinded evaluator rating on a 5-grade scale. I expect roughly 55-60% responders vs 20-30% on saline, so a difference of about 30 points would be strongly significant with 118 vs 39. Risk is saline response and the both-cheeks requirement.

assumptions.claim: Filler-type products for acne scars achieve roughly 50-65% responders vs 20-35% with saline or no-treatment control in pivotal trials.
assumptions.source: Karnik et al. 2014, Dermatol Surg (Bellafill acne scar pivotal)

assumptions.claim: The trial is a 3:1 randomization (1 in 4 chance of saline) with an evaluating investigator blinded to treatment.

reason: Placebo ASAS20 response at week 8 after NSAID washout can be 30% or higher; a TCM tablet needs a 12+ point margin with 204 per arm, though such domestic phase 3 trials are usually reported as positive.
rationale: With 204 per arm, a 12-point ASAS20 difference gives about 80% power and a 17-point difference near certainty. Phase 3 TCM trials from large Chinese sponsors are rarely reported as failures and the endpoint is soft and patient-reported, but placebo response after NSAID washout in active AS is high. Recruitment was still open in October 2026, so a public result before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Placebo ASAS20 in AS NSAID-free trials (e.g., secukinumab MEASURE 1, 2015)

assumptions.claim: Placebo ASAS20 response in active ankylosing spondylitis is typically 20-35% at 12-16 weeks.
The record lists a single primary endpoint, ASAS20 at week 8, with 408 patients and 10 sites in China.

reason: A 103-patient phase IIb with roughly 75-80 PFS events needs an HR near 0.6 to reach p<0.05; the likely true effect of durvalumab plus tremelimumab over pembrolizumab with chemotherapy is HR 0.7-0.85.
rationale: POSEIDON showed PFS HR 0.72 for durvalumab plus tremelimumab plus chemo vs chemo, with signals in STK11/KEAP1 subgroups, but this trial compares against pembrolizumab plus chemo, a stronger control, in 103 patients. Around 78 events give about 25% power for HR 0.75. A formal hypothesis is not stated, so it may be reported descriptively. AZ may present at a congress after June.

assumptions.claim: In POSEIDON, durvalumab plus tremelimumab plus chemotherapy improved PFS vs chemotherapy with HR about 0.72.
assumptions.source: Johnson et al. 2023, J Clin Oncol (POSEIDON)

assumptions.claim: Patients with STK11 or KEAP1 mutations have median PFS around 4-6 months on pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy.
assumptions.source: Skoulidis et al. 2022, KEYNOTE-189 biomarker analysis

reason: A FAK inhibitor added to PLD in a double-blind randomized phase 2 with about 130 BICR PFS events needs HR near 0.7 or better; the earlier single-arm signal may overstate the benefit over PLD alone.
rationale: IN10018 (ifebemtinib) plus PLD showed encouraging response and PFS in early platinum-resistant ovarian trials against PLD alone with median PFS of about 3.5 months, and the Chinese designation as breakthrough therapy suggests this randomized phase 2 is registrational. With 168 patients 2:1 and about 130 events an HR of 0.62 is highly significant, but early single-arm data often overstate. Still recruiting in late 2026, so reporting is probably after mid-2027.
evidence: IN10018 plus PLD phase 1b/2 platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (InxMed, 2023)
PLD control arm PFS in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (AURELIA 2014)

assumptions.claim: PLD monotherapy in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer yields median PFS of roughly 3-4 months.
The trial randomizes 2:1 (about 112 vs 56) and the primary endpoint is BICR-assessed PFS per RECIST 1.1.

reason: Chronic discoid CLE is less interferon-driven than SLE skin disease, so the CLASI-70 gap at week 24 could be smaller than the 15-25 points seen with CLASI-50 in SLE; with 170 per arm a gap under 10 points would be borderline.
rationale: Type I interferon blockade strongly improves cutaneous lupus: anifrolumab doubled CLASI response in SLE (TULIP-2), and litifilimab was positive in CLE phase 2. With about 170 per arm and a plausible CLASI-70 rate of 30-35% vs 14%, power is high. Risks are the discoid-predominant population and the stringent CLASI-70 threshold. AZ announces phase 3 topline by press release, likely in H1 2027.

assumptions.claim: In TULIP, anifrolumab gave a CLASI response (at least 50% reduction) of about 49% vs 25% on placebo among SLE patients with baseline CLASI of 10 or more.
Litifilimab improved CLASI-A response vs placebo in cutaneous lupus in a randomized phase 2 trial.

reason: A novel TPL2/COT mechanism in advanced-therapy-experienced UC, with only about 55-60 patients in the top-dose arm, needs a 15+ point gap in clinical response versus a placebo rate near 25-30%.
rationale: Clinical response at week 12 is a forgiving endpoint, but this is an unproven mechanism, many patients have failed advanced therapy, and the highest-dose arm is probably 55-60 patients, so significance needs a gap of about 15-18 points over a 25-30% placebo response. Phase 2 UC trials of new mechanisms succeed about 40-50% of the time. Gilead rarely announces phase 2 UC results quickly; a congress or earnings disclosure likely falls in H2 2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo clinical response rates in moderately to severely active UC phase 2 trials are typically 20-35%.
assumptions.source: Obefazimod phase 2b (Vermeire 2022, Lancet) and etrasimod OASIS (Sandborn 2020, Gastroenterology)

assumptions.claim: The study randomizes 176 patients across several tilpisertib fosmecarbil doses and placebo with a primary endpoint of clinical response at week 12.

reason: Small 15-patient pediatric heart transplant study in only 3 German centres; pediatric heart transplants are rare, enrolment has been slow since 2023, and a safety-only primary outcome from a small German sponsor makes late completion likely and CT.gov results unlikely.

A single-site pilot with perhaps 15-30 PTSD patients per arm, SD of CAPS-5 change near 14, and primary outcomes that are mostly feasibility and safety, so significance on CAPS-5 is uncertain and the 'primary objective met' wording is ambiguous.
rationale: Phase 3 MDMA-assisted therapy trials showed CAPS-5 gaps of 10-14 points vs therapy with placebo, but here the control is active CBCT, which itself lowers CAPS-5 by roughly 15 points, and the pilot has 15-30 per arm. Primary outcomes are feasibility and safety, so a 'met' call depends on how labellers read a descriptive pilot. Recruiting into 2027, so results by June 2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In MAPP1 and MAPP2, MDMA-assisted therapy reduced CAPS-5 by about 10-14 points more than therapy with placebo.
assumptions.source: Mitchell et al. 2021 Nat Med (MAPP1); Mitchell et al. 2023 Nat Med (MAPP2)

assumptions.claim: The study is a single-site Toronto trial of 60 participants where feasibility, safety and appropriateness measures are listed ahead of CAPS-5 among the primary outcomes.

reason: About 22 patients per arm and a strict endpoint (BVAS 0 with prednisolone 4 mg or less) mean NS-229 needs roughly a 35-point gain to reach p<0.05; a phase 2 novel oral agent in EGPA on top of steroids and biologics will probably fall short.
rationale: Phase 2, n=45, week-28 remission (BVAS 0, OGC 4 mg or less) in patients on 7.5 mg or more steroid, some on mepolizumab/benralizumab. Placebo remission is low (MIRRA placebo 3%). Fisher significance at 22 per arm needs a very large gap (for example 40% vs 9%). Novel mechanism, unproven in EGPA; a modest true effect is likely.

assumptions.claim: Placebo remission (BVAS 0 and prednisolone 4 mg/day or less) was about 3% at weeks 36 and 48 in MIRRA.
Benralizumab and mepolizumab remission rates were 59% and 56% in MANDARA.

reason: The earlier phase 3 of patidegib 2% gel in Gorlin syndrome missed its primary endpoint, and this trial rests on a post-hoc high-burden subgroup; topical hedgehog inhibition may be too weak to cut new BCC counts significantly at 12 months.
rationale: The prior PellePharm phase 3 (NCT03703310) missed its primary endpoint; the sponsor's rationale is a post-hoc benefit in patients with high BCC burden, which this trial enriches for (10 or more facial BCCs, PTCH1 confirmed, photo-review counts). A real but modest effect is plausible; n=113 is small for a count outcome with high variance. Sol-Gel is likely to report promptly.

assumptions.claim: The earlier phase 3 of patidegib gel 2% in Gorlin syndrome did not meet its primary endpoint in the overall population.
Patients with higher baseline facial BCC burden showed a larger post-hoc treatment effect, motivating the 10-or-more BCC entry criterion here.

reason: As-needed ICS plus albuterol rescue has cut severe exacerbations by about 25-30% in MANDALA and BATURA; a fluticasone/albuterol analogue at high dose in a large event-driven trial should replicate, with some risk from a different ICS or a pediatric mix.
rationale: Strong class precedent: MANDALA budesonide/albuterol high dose gave HR about 0.74 for time to first severe exacerbation vs albuterol, and BATURA confirmed in mild-moderate asthma. Event-driven design with 924 per arm and a long follow-up gives high power for HR 0.75. Residual risks: fluticasone as-needed dosing, low event rate, children dilution.

assumptions.claim: Budesonide/albuterol 180/160 reduced risk of first severe exacerbation vs albuterol by about 26% (HR 0.74) in MANDALA.
About a third of albuterol-only patients had at least one severe exacerbation in MANDALA.

reason: With only 18 vs 9 patients, a significant difference needs about 50% histologic complete response against near 0% on placebo; the topical artesunate effect from earlier small studies is likely smaller and placebo response in vulvar HSIL is non-zero.
rationale: Phase 2, 27 patients randomized 2:1, still recruiting in Oct 2026 so results by mid-2027 are unlikely. Earlier open-label artesunate data in vulvar HSIL showed response in a sizeable fraction, but Fisher testing at 18 vs 9 needs a very large gap. Placebo complete response in vulvar HSIL is around 0-15%.
evidence: Imiquimod vs placebo vulvar HSIL trials (van Seters 2008)

assumptions.claim: Placebo complete response in vulvar HSIL is low, typically 0-15%.
The trial is randomized 2:1 with 27 planned patients.

reason: Phase 2a in Acinetobacter HABP/VABP started May 2026 with sequential cohorts; this rare, critically ill population is slow to enrol, so the March 2027 primary completion likely slips past June 2027; a small company will not post results by Aug 2027.

Zibotentan adds a UACR reduction of about 30-35% over dapagliflozin, but an endothelin antagonist's acute eGFR dip offsets the chronic slope benefit at month 24, so the net eGFR difference may be about 1 mL/min, near the edge of detectability.
rationale: Phase 2b ZENITH-CKD showed zibotentan/dapagliflozin cut UACR a further 30%+ vs dapagliflozin. Primary is eGFR change at month 24 (includes the haemodynamic dip), with SD about 9 and about 900 per arm, SE about 0.4; a net gain of 0.8-1.0 gives roughly even power. Sparsentan PROTECT shows how marginal eGFR effects can be with ERAs.

assumptions.claim: Zibotentan/dapagliflozin lowered UACR by about 34% more than dapagliflozin alone in the phase 2b.
Dapagliflozin on top of RAAS inhibition gives a total eGFR slope of about -2.9 mL/min/1.73m2 per year in DAPA-CKD.

reason: Anti-IL-6 acts mainly on inflammation (CAS) rather than proptosis; a 2 mm proptosis response at week 20 may be modest vs IGF-1R drugs, and with about 26 per arm the effect must reach about 30 points over placebo to be significant.
rationale: Tocilizumab RCT in TED showed benefit on activity and some on proptosis; IGF-1R drugs reach 70-80% proptosis response but IL-6 and FcRn approaches reach about 30-50%. Placebo around 10%. Phase 2b with about 26 per arm and two doses: either dose meeting p<0.05 is plausible with a roughly 35% vs 8% split. Novartis ownership favours disclosure of success.

assumptions.claim: Placebo proptosis responders (2 mm or more) are about 5-15% in TED trials at week 24.
Tocilizumab reduced CAS and improved proptosis in a placebo-controlled TED trial.

reason: Gilead PrEP phase 2 with primary completion July 2026 is already fully enrolled; Gilead usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline (July 2027), so posting by Aug 2027 is more likely than not, and the PK, safety and acceptability outcomes are unlikely to change.

Gilead-sponsored phase 2 PK/safety study with primary completion registered July 2026; the record is in follow-up with no efficacy goal. Gilead usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline (about July 2027), so posting by 31 Aug 2027 is roughly a coin flip.

If an early readout exists it is most likely an event-driven interim; the risk is too few PFS events in patients who are stable on a BTK inhibitor, so the hazard ratio is imprecise even if the combination works.
rationale: Adding a BCL-2 inhibitor to continued BTK inhibitor in patients with persistent disease after at least 12 months of BTKi should deepen responses and cut progression. Control patients are stable on BTKi, so few events occur at 12 months. Registry still shows recruiting, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely; if it comes early it is probably a positive interim.
evidence: Lisaftoclax China approval in R/R CLL/SLL 2025

assumptions.claim: Patients in GLORA must have received BTK inhibitor monotherapy for at least 12 months before randomization.
Lisaftoclax is a BCL-2 inhibitor developed by Ascentage Pharma and approved in China for relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL.

reason: Small phase 2a with an unproven oral mechanism in alopecia areata and only 12 weeks of treatment, short for hair regrowth; the placebo arm is noisy, so a significant difference needs a large effect.
rationale: About 37 per arm, 12-week % SALT change. JAK inhibitors need 24 weeks to separate clearly from placebo, and this agent has no established activity in alopecia areata. Placebo change is near zero with SD around 30 points, so only a large effect gets p below 0.05. Record still says recruiting past the registered completion, so reporting by mid-2027 is uncertain, and a Korean-only phase 2a is unlikely to be heavily publicized.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in alopecia areata trials show little mean change in SALT over the first 12-24 weeks.
NXC736 phase 2a is run at 2 sites in South Korea with 73 planned participants.

reason: The primary counts the share losing 15 or more letters, a rare event in both arms over 36 weeks, so superiority of eye drops over aflibercept injection is very unlikely and any statement would probably be descriptive.
rationale: Loss of 15 or more letters occurs in only a few percent of patients treated with aflibercept, so the two arms will be close to zero and no significant difference favouring a topical drop is realistic. A topical VEGFR inhibitor is unlikely to match intravitreal aflibercept. Kyowa Kirin may report the outcome only in pipeline tables, and the record gives no non-inferiority hypothesis.

assumptions.claim: Losing 15 or more ETDRS letters on intravitreal aflibercept in DME is rare, a few percent at 1 year.
KHK4951 is a topical eye-drop VEGFR inhibitor compared with intravitreal aflibercept.

reason: An IL-6 inhibitor needs roughly a 12 percent or larger relative risk reduction to reach significance with about 850 events; CANTOS-size effects (HR 0.85) give only marginal power while colchicine post-MI trials were mixed.
rationale: 10,000 high-risk post-MI patients, event-driven 3P-MACE. IL-6 blockade lowers CRP by about 90 percent and CANTOS showed HR 0.85 with IL-1 blockade, so a true HR near 0.80-0.88 is plausible, which gives roughly even odds of statistical significance with about 850 events. Colchicine was positive in COLCOT but null in CLEAR SYNERGY, so anti-inflammatory benefit post-MI is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Canakinumab reduced 3-point MACE with HR 0.85 (150 mg) in post-MI patients with elevated hsCRP.
Colchicine after MI was neutral on the primary composite in CLEAR SYNERGY (HR about 0.99).

reason: BMS phase 2a safety/PK study that is active and not recruiting with primary completion December 2026. BMS tends to keep dates or update them modestly, and results are usually posted near the 12-month deadline, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

About 100 patients per arm gives a standard error near 35 mL/year for the FVC slope difference, so a pirfenidone-like effect of 70-100 mL/year is borderline, and dose selection at an interim adds uncertainty.
rationale: Sufenidone is a pirfenidone-like antifibrotic. Approved antifibrotics reduce annual FVC decline by about 100 mL versus placebo in large trials, but this phase 2/3 has 210 patients, possibly split across doses. Standard deviation of annual slope is around 250 mL, so power for a 70 mL difference is near 50 percent. The registry still shows recruiting with 52-week treatment, so reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Pirfenidone reduced annual FVC decline by roughly 100-120 mL versus placebo at 52 weeks in IPF.
Nintedanib reduced adjusted annual FVC decline by about 110 mL/year versus placebo.

reason: Placebo response on NPI-C hallucinations and delusions is large in dementia psychosis, and tolerability (nausea, vomiting, falls) in frail elderly may drive dropouts; the 250 per arm design is otherwise well powered for a 2-point difference.
rationale: Xanomeline reduced psychosis and agitation in an older Alzheimer's trial and KarXT was robustly positive in schizophrenia (EMERGENT-2). Antipsychotic class effects in Alzheimer's psychosis are modest against a high placebo response. With 250 per arm and SD about 8.5, a 2-point difference is detectable. Still recruiting in Oct 2026, so the readout likely lands mid-2027.
evidence: Bodick xanomeline in Alzheimer's disease, Arch Neurol 1997

assumptions.claim: KarXT lowered PANSS total by about 9.6 points more than placebo in EMERGENT-2.
The 6-month xanomeline trial in Alzheimer's disease reduced hallucinations, delusions and agitation versus placebo.

reason: Placebo cure of hookworm is near zero, so a working anthelmintic wins easily; the risk is that the primary covers three species and only hookworm is sized (114 evaluable), so Ascaris or Trichuris comparisons could be underpowered.
rationale: Single-dose anthelmintic (apparently a benzimidazole-class chewable) against placebo: spontaneous cure by day 14 is a few percent, while albendazole-like agents cure 70-80% of hookworm. The trial is sized for hookworm only, so per-species significance for Ascaris or Trichuris is the main uncertainty. Private sponsor with one site; slow recruitment and sparse disclosure make a public result by mid-2027 unlikely.
evidence: Moser et al., BMJ 2017 network meta-analysis of STH drugs

assumptions.claim: Single-dose albendazole cures roughly 70% of hookworm infections in controlled trials.
Spontaneous clearance of hookworm within 14 days without treatment is low, in the single digits.
assumptions.source: Moser et al., BMJ 2017 (placebo arms in STH trials)

reason: With 80 patients, a single site and a large natural recovery in the placebo arm, only a sizeable Barthel gain would reach significance; co-primary mRS and multiple time points add chance and reporting-bias noise.
rationale: Small single-centre trial of umbilical cord MSCs after stroke. Large phase 3 MSC stroke trials (MASTERS-2) were negative, but small regional trials often report positive Barthel or mRS signals. With 40 per arm and SD about 25, an 8-point difference gives z about 1.5. Co-primary mRS must also be met. Still recruiting as of Oct 2026 with 12-month follow-up, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Law ZK et al. 2021 (phase 2 MSC in subacute MCA infarct)

assumptions.claim: Intravenous MultiStem cells did not improve mRS in the phase 3 MASTERS-2 trial in ischemic stroke.
A phase 2 trial of bone-marrow MSCs in subacute MCA infarct showed safety and reduced infarct volume.
assumptions.source: Law et al. 2021, cited in the record

reason: TRIDENT-1 median PFS in TKI-naive ROS1+ NSCLC was 35.7 months against about 16-20 months for crizotinib; a crizotinib arm that outperforms history or immature follow-up are the only realistic threats.
rationale: Repotrectinib is a next-generation, CNS-active ROS1 inhibitor with ORR 79% and mPFS 35.7 months in TKI-naive patients (TRIDENT-1) versus crizotinib mPFS 15.9-20 months in PROFILE 1001, EUCROSS and OxOnc. Cross-trial HR about 0.5. 190 patients with event-driven analysis give adequate power for HR below 0.6. Main uncertainty is timing and maturity.

assumptions.claim: Repotrectinib median PFS was 35.7 months in TKI-naive ROS1+ NSCLC in TRIDENT-1.
Crizotinib median PFS in ROS1+ NSCLC was about 19 months in PROFILE 1001.

reason: Zongertinib has about 75% ORR in HER2-mutant NSCLC against chemo-immunotherapy PFS near 6 months; failure would need a surprisingly durable control arm or immature data.
rationale: Selective HER2 TKD inhibitor with high response rates and approval in pretreated disease; HER2-mutant NSCLC responds poorly to chemo-immunotherapy (real-world PFS about 5.5-7 months). Oral targeted therapy versus pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy resembles other oncogene-driven first-line wins (HR 0.3-0.5). 428 patients give ample power. Main uncertainty is timing and disclosure by a private sponsor.

assumptions.claim: Zongertinib produced a confirmed ORR of about 75% in pretreated HER2-mutant NSCLC, supporting FDA accelerated approval in 2025.
Chemo-immunotherapy yields median PFS of roughly 6 months in HER2-mutant NSCLC.
assumptions.source: Retrospective series of HER2-mutant NSCLC on chemo-IO (e.g. Wang 2022)

reason: LAG-3 add-on to PD-1 plus chemotherapy has a poor track record in lung cancer, and a 98 versus 97 phase 2 can only show a significant pCR gap if the true effect is large, which is unlikely.
rationale: Phase 2 with about 98 versus 97 patients: to be significant the pCR gap would need roughly 15-18 points over a control of about 21%. Neoadjuvant PD-1 plus chemotherapy gives pCR 17-24% (CheckMate 816, AEGEAN, KEYNOTE-671). Adding LAG-3 inhibition has not clearly helped in NSCLC, so a small non-significant gain is most likely. Regeneron often reveals such results in earnings updates or congress abstracts.

assumptions.claim: Neoadjuvant PD-1 plus platinum chemotherapy gives pCR rates of about 17-24% in resectable NSCLC.
A phase 2 randomized trial with fewer than 100 patients per arm has low power for pCR differences below about 15 points.

reason: Pfizer-run 52-week extension that is fully enrolled with a registered primary completion of Mar 2027; slippage of more than 90 days is uncommon and results usually post closer to 12 months after completion.
rationale: Safety-only primaries in a long-term extension of the Tranquillo vitiligo parent study; enrollment is closed (active, not recruiting). Pfizer rarely changes such records, tends to post results near the 12-month deadline, and extension studies are seldom stopped unless a program-wide safety issue arises.

reason: Naked CLDN18.2 antibodies add roughly 25-30% PFS risk reduction to chemotherapy (zolbetuximab HR 0.69-0.75), so an unproven antibody of this class could land on either side of significance; the CPS<5 restriction is helpful.
rationale: Class precedent is positive: zolbetuximab plus chemotherapy gave PFS HR 0.75 (SPOTLIGHT) and 0.69 (GLOW), and other Chinese CLDN18.2 antibodies have shown benefit. M108 potency is unproven and the sponsor is small. With 486 patients and about 330 events, HR 0.75 would be detected. Trial is still recruiting, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Zolbetuximab plus CAPOX improved PFS with HR 0.687 (median 8.2 vs 6.8 months) in CLDN18.2-positive HER2-negative gastric cancer.
assumptions.source: GLOW, Shah et al., Nat Med 2023 (NCT03653507)

assumptions.claim: Placebo plus chemotherapy median PFS is about 7-9 months in first-line CLDN18.2-positive gastric cancer.

reason: Adding the LAG-3 antibody fianlimab to cemiplimab may raise pCR, but with about 75 patients per arm a gain under roughly 15 points will not reach p<0.05, and LAG-3 add-on benefit over anti-PD1 has been inconsistent.
rationale: Neoadjuvant anti-PD1 alone gives pCR of about 20-30% in clinically detectable stage III/IV melanoma; dual checkpoint blockade reaches about 47% (NADINA). A LAG-3 add-on plausibly adds 10-15 points, but n=76 vs 75 gives power near 50% for that gap. BIPR tends to give lower pCR than local review. Phase 2 sponsor reporting may also use looser thresholds.
evidence: NADINA 2024 (neoadjuvant ipilimumab+nivolumab in stage III melanoma)

assumptions.claim: Neoadjuvant anti-PD1 monotherapy yields pCR in roughly 20-30% of patients with resectable stage III melanoma.
Neoadjuvant ipilimumab plus nivolumab produced a pathologic complete response in about 47% of patients in NADINA.
The trial enrolled 151 patients, randomized to the combination or cemiplimab plus placebo.

reason: An oral multi-target kinase inhibitor in post-PD-1, 2+ line ESCC must show an OS benefit over irinotecan/docetaxel/S-1; earlier TKIs in this setting showed modest, often non-significant OS gains. Results are also unlikely to be public by mid-2027.
rationale: Third-line ESCC chemotherapy gives median OS near 6 months, a low bar, and an angiogenesis-type TKI with a reasonable phase 2 signal can reach HR 0.7-0.8 with 490 patients. But anlotinib's ESCC phase 2 missed OS significance, open-label designs favour chemo dropouts, and a single-site-listed Chinese sponsor may report late. Success needs about 380 deaths.

assumptions.claim: Chemotherapy control arms in second-line-and-later ESCC have median OS of roughly 5 to 6 months.
Anlotinib versus placebo in 2nd+ line ESCC gave PFS 3.0 vs 1.4 months and OS 6.1 vs 4.6 months.
assumptions.source: ALTER1102, Huang et al., J Thorac Oncol 2021

assumptions.claim: The trial randomizes 490 patients 1:1 to KC1036 or investigator's choice of irinotecan, docetaxel or S-1 with OS as the primary outcome.

reason: A small single-site proof-of-concept study by a private biotech with sequential dose cohorts, a 6-month registered primary window and a recent start; the dates will probably slip, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
With 32 vs 16 patients, a true gap near 25 points gives under 50% power, and placebo response in biopsy-defined anal HSIL (spontaneous regression) is substantial.
rationale: Topical artesunate has antiviral and anti-proliferative activity, and oral artesunate showed histologic regression signals in cervical HSIL. But anal HSIL placebo response is often 20-30% and the trial has 32 vs 16 patients, so the gap must be around 25-30 points to reach p<0.05. Small private sponsors tend to publicise only favourable results, which lifts the conditional estimate.
evidence: Trimble 2018 (oral artesunate in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, phase 2)

assumptions.claim: Participants are randomized 2:1 to artesunate or placebo ointment, 48 in total.
Oral artesunate showed dose-related histologic regression of cervical HSIL (CIN2/3) in a phase 2 trial.
assumptions.source: Trimble et al. 2018 phase 2 oral artesunate CIN2/3

reason: Anti-CLDN18.2 antibodies add PFS benefit to chemotherapy (zolbetuximab HR about 0.69-0.75), but the PD-1 backbone raises the control arm and may shrink the incremental gain; 780 patients still give good power for HR near 0.75.
rationale: Zolbetuximab added to chemotherapy gave PFS HR 0.75 (SPOTLIGHT) and 0.69 (GLOW) in CLDN18.2-positive gastric cancer. ASKB589 with CAPOX and PD-1 had a strong phase 1b/2 signal. 780 patients give high power for HR 0.75; the risk is that the PD-1 backbone lessens the add-on effect. Early public results would likely be positive interim analyses.

assumptions.claim: Zolbetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 improved PFS in CLDN18.2-positive gastric cancer with HR about 0.75.
Zolbetuximab plus CAPOX improved PFS with HR about 0.69 (median 8.2 vs 6.8 months).
assumptions.source: GLOW, Shah et al., Nat Med 2023 (NCT03653507)

assumptions.claim: Tislelizumab plus chemotherapy gave median PFS of about 7 months in first-line gastric cancer.

reason: About 33 patients on atovaquone plus azithromycin, which already works in low-risk hospitalized babesiosis, leave little room for tafenoquine to speed symptom resolution measurably, and the sample is far too small to detect a modest hazard ratio.
rationale: Standard atovaquone plus azithromycin resolves most low-risk babesiosis; tafenoquine's long half-life matters mainly for relapsing or immunocompromised disease. The primary needs all 11 symptoms, including fatigue, absent for 7 days, which is noisy. With about 33 patients, only a large HR (above about 2) would reach p<0.05. Seasonal enrolment makes timing uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Atovaquone plus azithromycin is the guideline standard regimen for babesiosis in both arms.
The trial plans only 33 participants across both arms.

reason: A large Incyte long-term extension with enrolment complete and a registered end of December 2026; sponsor-managed record, modest chance the end date is extended, and results are likely posted only near the 12-month deadline.
A completed GSK phase 2 vaccine study; GSK normally posts results close to the 12-month deadline after primary completion (August 2026), and a completed trial rarely changes primary outcomes.

Add-on factorial design against matched placebo, where the component's known blood-pressure or HbA1c effect should easily win at n about 92 per arm; the main risks are the second co-primary (HbA1c) and a low placebo-arm baseline.
rationale: Korean fixed-dose combination trials remove one component against a matched placebo, so each comparison tests a drug with an established effect: an ARB-type agent lowers SBP by roughly 8-12 mmHg, and an antidiabetic component lowers HbA1c by 0.5-0.8 points. With about 90 per arm, both co-primaries should succeed. Public reporting is likely via Korean press or approval filings, later in 2027.
evidence: Typical Korean add-on factorial phase 3 programs for hypertension-diabetes fixed-dose combinations

assumptions.claim: Each primary comparison removes one component against its matching placebo (the -1 suffix), keeping the other drugs in both arms.
The trial enrolls 276 patients across three or more arms with co-primary SBP and HbA1c outcomes at week 12.

reason: A HER2 ADC plus a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific should out-respond second-line paclitaxel (ORR about 15%), but 30 patients per arm give wide uncertainty and the HER2 IHC 1+ cases may respond poorly.
rationale: Disitamab vedotin alone gave ORR near 25% in heavily pretreated HER2-expressing gastric cancer, and adding an immunotherapy bispecific plausibly lifts ORR to 40-50% against paclitaxel's 15-20%. With 30 per arm, a gap of about 22 points reaches p<0.05. Publication bias toward favourable phase 2 readouts, and the phase 3 co-primaries (PFS/OS) not being reported, add scoring uncertainty.
evidence: Peng 2021 (RC48 in HER2-overexpressing gastric cancer, phase 2)

assumptions.claim: Second-line paclitaxel alone in gastric cancer had an ORR of about 16% in RAINBOW.
assumptions.source: RAINBOW, Wilke et al., Lancet Oncol 2014

assumptions.claim: Disitamab vedotin monotherapy showed an ORR of about 25% in HER2-expressing gastric cancer after two or more prior lines.
The phase II part compares the combination, disitamab vedotin alone and paclitaxel, with about 30 patients per arm.

reason: A selective TYK2 inhibitor in Crohn's disease with 67 per arm; the class has so far shown weak IL-23-pathway efficacy in CD, so the top dose may not separate from placebo on endoscopic response.
rationale: Phase 2b dose-ranging with any-dose-wins rule helps, and zasocitinib is more potent than deucravacitinib, whose Crohn's phase 2 missed. TYK2 blockade is a weaker IL-23 surrogate than biologics. With 67 per arm and placebo around 12%, a true 10-15 point gain gives only about 50-60% power. Ileal-disease definition inflates placebo response slightly.

assumptions.claim: Placebo endoscopic response at week 12 in biologic-experienced Crohn's trials is roughly 10-15%.
Deucravacitinib did not show a significant endoscopic benefit over placebo in its phase 2 Crohn's study.

reason: Small private-sponsor phase 1/2 mRNA study with several sequential parts; completion dates often slip as later parts run, results posting by a private company within 10 months is unlikely, and a new part could alter the primary list.
Placebo-controlled MTX in adult AD should beat placebo on EASI75, but the dose is unknown and a high placebo response or early dropouts on tolerability could narrow the gap.
rationale: MTX is an established conventional systemic in AD with prior RCTs showing meaningful EASI improvement; placebo monotherapy EASI75 at week 16 is usually 10-15%, and MTX likely reaches 30-40%. With about 138 per arm a 20 point difference is detectable with good power. Risks are a low MTX dose, a high placebo response and dropouts. Sponsor medac is the MTX owner and designed this as a registrational phase 3.
evidence: Schram 2011 MTX vs azathioprine in AD
TREAT trial MTX vs ciclosporin in paediatric AD 2020

assumptions.claim: Placebo EASI75 at week 16 in adult AD monotherapy trials is about 8-15%.
Methotrexate in adult AD produced EASI improvements clearly above placebo-level in randomized comparisons.
assumptions.source: Schram et al., JACI 2011 (PMID 21777996 area, MTX vs azathioprine)

reason: TIL cell therapy against single-agent gemcitabine in previously treated cervical cancer should clear a low PFS bar, but 83 patients, manufacturing delays and open-label assessment add noise and dropout risk.
rationale: Gemcitabine is a weak comparator with PFS around 2-3 months, while TIL in pretreated cervical cancer gave 44% ORR and durable responses in the Iovance C-145-04 study. PFS is counted from first study treatment, which favours the cell-therapy arm by excluding the manufacturing wait. About 60 events give roughly 85% power at HR 0.5. Risks: patients lost before infusion, small sample, open-label bias reversal.
evidence: gemcitabine second-line cervical cancer phase 2 series

assumptions.claim: TIL therapy (LN-145) gave about 44% objective response in previously treated cervical cancer.
assumptions.source: Jazaeri et al., ASCO 2019 / C-145-04 interim

assumptions.claim: Single-agent chemotherapy in second-line cervical cancer yields median PFS of about 2-3 months.

reason: Symptom-only Sjogren's trials carry large placebo improvements on patient-reported scores, and both ESSPRI and DASPRI must be met at week 48 while the earlier symptom-state phase 2 gave a modest signal.
rationale: Two co-primary patient-reported endpoints must both succeed at week 48. Placebo improvement on ESSPRI in Sjogren's trials is typically around 1 point, and the dazodalibep phase 2 in the symptom-dominant population showed at best a modest separation. A 0.4 point treatment difference with an SD near 2 and 217 per arm gives about 45% power per endpoint, lower jointly.

assumptions.claim: Dazodalibep's phase 2 in symptom-predominant Sjogren's did not clearly beat placebo on ESSPRI.
Placebo ESSPRI improvement at 24-48 weeks in Sjogren's trials is about 1 point on the 0-10 scale.

reason: Superiority on ORR over an already active LAG-3 plus PD-1 combination needs about an 8-point gain at roughly 43% control; fianlimab's phase 3 record against anti-PD-1 has been underwhelming, so a clear ORR win is unlikely.
rationale: The comparator, relatlimab plus nivolumab, gave 43% ORR in RELATIVITY-047. Fianlimab plus cemiplimab showed about 57% ORR in single-arm phase 2, but cross-trial gaps shrink in randomized comparisons, and the larger phase 3 against pembrolizumab has not delivered a clear win. With 280 per arm, an 8-point gap is needed for significance; a true gap of 4-5 points gives low power.

assumptions.claim: Relatlimab plus nivolumab achieved an objective response rate of about 43% in first-line melanoma.
Fianlimab plus cemiplimab showed roughly 57-61% ORR in the single-arm first-line melanoma phase 2 cohort.

reason: A novel-mechanism oral antidepressant in a 4-week US phase 2b faces the typical large placebo response and a short window, and no top-line release has appeared in the months since completion.
rationale: Phase 2b MDD trials of novel mechanisms mostly fail, with US placebo MADRS improvements of 9-11 points by week 4 and true drug effects of 1-3 points. With about 248 per arm and SD near 9, a 2 point difference is needed. The trial finished in July 2026 and no top-line had surfaced by late October, mildly negative for a small private sponsor.

assumptions.claim: Placebo MADRS improvement in short US MDD trials is typically 8-11 points.
assumptions.source: Meta-analysis of antidepressant placebo response, Rutherford/Roose reviews

assumptions.claim: Most phase 2b trials of novel-mechanism antidepressants fail to separate from placebo on the primary MADRS endpoint.

reason: Chinese weekly GLP-1 head-to-head against dulaglutide is probably non-inferiority first, which JY09 should meet; a strict superiority test would be closer, with the gap near 0.3 points.
rationale: Weekly exendin-4 Fc fusion at 2.4 mg should lower HbA1c about as much as dulaglutide or slightly more; Chinese head-to-head phase 3s (ecnoglutide, mazdutide) showed modest superiority over dulaglutide. If the primary is non-inferiority it is almost certain to be met. With 200 per arm and SD near 1.0, a 0.3 point difference gives about 75% power for superiority. Open-label and a single site registered add little risk.
evidence: ecnoglutide vs dulaglutide phase 3 T2D China 2024

assumptions.claim: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg lowers HbA1c by about 1.4-1.6 points at week 26 in Chinese metformin-treated patients.
In Chinese phase 3 head-to-head trials, newer weekly GLP-1 agents beat dulaglutide on HbA1c by a few tenths of a percentage point.

reason: Active, not recruiting Janssen paediatric study with an accurate registered completion date; big-company registries are kept current, results posting normally comes about a year after primary completion, and the primary outcome is unlikely to change.

An anti-MTBR tau antibody must slow tau PET accumulation significantly over 76 weeks in 155 vs 155 patients; earlier tau-directed antibodies mostly failed to move tau PET, and readout likely falls after mid-2027.
rationale: Single biomarker primary (tau PET) in a proof-of-concept phase 2 with 155 per arm. MTBR-directed antibodies target seed-competent tau and early signals (CSF MTBR-tau243, E2814 tau PET data) are encouraging, but N-terminal antibodies (semorinemab) did not change tau PET. A significant slowing is plausible but far from assured; variability of tau PET change is moderate.

assumptions.claim: Semorinemab (N-terminal tau antibody) did not slow clinical decline or tau PET accumulation in early AD phase 2 trials.
Primary completion is registered as 2027-03-18, so topline is unlikely before July 2027.

reason: 150 patients at 2:1 gives modest power for the expected 0.8-1.0 point difference on a pain scale where saline injections produce a large placebo response.
rationale: Zilretta knee phase 3 beat saline by about 0.9 points on average daily pain at week 12 with a large saline response. Shoulder OA is harder to inject accurately and 100 vs 50 patients with SD about 2.4 gives roughly 55-60% power for a 0.9 difference. Pacira ran this phase 3 after a supportive earlier shoulder study, and a single-injection design limits dropout.

assumptions.claim: In the knee OA phase 3, Zilretta 32 mg improved average daily pain at week 12 by about 0.9 NRS points more than saline.
assumptions.source: Conaghan et al., J Bone Joint Surg Am 2018 (NCT02357459)

assumptions.claim: Registry lists 150 participants randomized 2:1 to Zilretta 32 mg or saline, primary at week 12.

reason: Small open-label phase 2 (30 per arm) framed as effect-size estimation by a private company; a significant difference in wound closure is unlikely and results may not appear publicly in time.
rationale: Wound closure at 8 weeks after flap surgery for pressure ulcer with osteomyelitis has a substantial control rate, so a significant gain with only 30 per arm needs a 25-point difference. The record frames the aim as estimating effect size, and the sponsor is a private device-drug company with slow recruitment (still recruiting, 9 sites), making delay and no early public result likely.

assumptions.claim: The trial is open-label, randomized 1:1, 60 patients, primary completion registered as 2026-12-01 while still recruiting.

reason: Retatrutide lowers HbA1c far more than placebo; the only realistic risk is a smaller effect from advanced renal impairment or dropouts from GI adverse events.
rationale: Retatrutide phase 2 in T2D reduced HbA1c by up to 2 points at 24 weeks, and tirzepatide on basal insulin beat placebo by about 1.5 points at 52 weeks (SURPASS-5). Even with eGFR below 60 and lower efficacy, a placebo-adjusted difference near 1.4 points in 160 per arm is overwhelmingly significant. Lilly routinely announces such phase 3 readouts.

assumptions.claim: In SURPASS-5, tirzepatide 15 mg added to insulin glargine reduced HbA1c by about 2.4 points versus about 0.9 with placebo at 40 weeks.
Retatrutide reduced HbA1c by up to about 2.0 points at 24 weeks in T2D phase 2.

reason: Still recruiting in October 2026 at 5 Chinese sites with 24-week treatment, so the registered December 2026 primary completion cannot hold; the record may also go stale, and a small Chinese sponsor is unlikely to post results.

A single-site Chinese phase 2 of 63 lower-risk MDS patients with 24-week endpoints, still recruiting in October 2026, will almost certainly run past the registered December 2026 completion; results posting is unlikely.

Phase 1/2 dose-escalation plus expansion in second-line HCC with ORR measured through study completion, still recruiting across 9 sites, so completion slippage is likely; primary outcomes may be revised to add safety or dose-finding measures.

Kv7 openers (azetukalner, ezogabine) have beaten placebo in focal epilepsy, but a short 8-week double-blind phase with titration and a high placebo response can shrink the 75 mg effect below significance.
rationale: Same mechanism as azetukalner, which separated from placebo by about 30 points of median seizure reduction in X-TOLE. BHV-7000 is a potent Kv7.2/7.3 opener with 130 per arm and a 75 mg dose chosen for efficacy. Risks are the short 8-week treatment phase, placebo response of 15-25% and the sponsor's earlier non-epilepsy failures, so a roughly 60% chance of a significant primary is reasonable.

assumptions.claim: In X-TOLE, azetukalner 25 mg reduced median monthly focal seizure frequency by about 53% versus about 18% with placebo.
Registry lists a 75 mg BHV-7000 vs placebo primary comparison with an 8-week observation phase and 8-week double-blind phase.

reason: Anti-Sema3A in NPDR has no proven DRSS effect; with about 35 eyes per arm a significant 2-step responder gap needs roughly 20+ points over a sham rate of about 10-15%.
rationale: Phase 2 dose-ranging with 35 per arm and a novel Sema3A mechanism, not VEGF. Anti-VEGF raises 2-step DRSS responders strongly (PANORAMA), but Sema3A blockade is less certain to move DRSS in 52 weeks. Sham responder rate is about 10-15%. A significant gap needs about 20+ points, so success is possible but under even odds. Sponsor tends to disclose at congresses, late.

assumptions.claim: Sham-treated NPDR eyes show roughly 10-15% with a 2-step DRSS improvement at about one year
The trial has 5 groups and 175 patients, about 35 per group

reason: Two histology co-primaries must both be met with 24 per arm over 52 weeks; HSD17B13 knockdown has human-genetic support but no proven fibrosis benefit on this timescale.
rationale: HSD17B13 loss-of-function protects against inflammation and fibrosis in cohorts, but 52 weeks of siRNA may not move fibrosis much. With 24 per arm a significant fibrosis gap needs about 22 points over a placebo rate of about 20%. Both co-primaries must be met, which lowers the odds. Small sample makes a false negative likely even with a real effect.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in 52-week MASH biopsy trials show about 14-25% with at least 1-stage fibrosis improvement without NASH worsening
Enrollment is 48, split about 24 per arm at a single site

reason: An anti-IL-5 type antibody in eosinophilic asthma should cut exacerbations by 40-55%; the main risk is a low Chinese placebo exacerbation rate cutting power, though 480 patients is ample.
rationale: 610 is most likely an anti-IL-5 pathway antibody; mepolizumab, reslizumab and benralizumab all cut severe exacerbations 40-55% in eosinophilic asthma. With 480 patients and about 350 events, a rate ratio near 0.55 is easily significant. Risk is a low placebo rate in China. The record says still recruiting, so a readout before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Anti-IL-5 antibodies reduced annualized severe exacerbations by about 47-51% vs placebo in severe eosinophilic asthma
Placebo annualized exacerbation rates were about 0.9-1.8 per year in these trials

reason: With 100 patients and about 18 expected dropouts by 24 weeks, a retention hazard ratio would need to be around 0.3 to reach significance; both primaries must also be met.
rationale: Retention in methadone care over 24 weeks is fairly high in control, so few events occur (about 18). A significant hazard ratio would need a very large effect, and there is no strong prior that video-observed take-homes lengthen retention. The take-home count primary likely favors Sonara by design, but retention must also be met. Results are unlikely before mid-2027.
evidence: Methadone take-home flexibilities and retention studies (Krawczyk 2022)

assumptions.claim: Sample is 100 patients across two arms, with 24-week retention and take-home primaries

reason: IL-13 blockade added to standard nasal steroid in perennial allergic rhinitis is unproven; a placebo-corrected TNSS gain near 0.6 of 12 points is borderline with a high placebo response.
rationale: Lilly commits to a phase 3 only with some signal, and IL-13 is central in allergic inflammation. But anti-IgE and IL-4/13 biologics give modest nasal symptom gains over placebo in allergic rhinitis, and the placebo response with background nasal steroid is large. With n=225 per arm and an SD near 3, a gap of 0.6 to 0.8 is borderline to significant. Lilly reports via earnings and congresses.

assumptions.claim: Biologics for allergic rhinitis typically improve nasal symptom scores by a modest amount (about 0.3-0.5 on a 0-3 scale) over placebo
The trial plans 450 adults split between lebrikizumab and placebo with TNSS at week 16 as primary

reason: Small phase 2 safety study whose start (2026-12) and primary completion (2026-12) are placeholders; 12-month TEAE follow-up means completion will fall well after the registered date. A small sponsor, so a funding-driven delay or stop is possible and results posting is unlikely by late 2027.

PFS should be positive (anti-VEGFR2 plus paclitaxel alone gave HR 0.64), but PFS and OS are co-primaries, and an early statement may report only PFS or leave OS immature, which would count as not met.
rationale: Adding an anti-VEGFR2 antibody to paclitaxel in second-line gastric cancer is validated (RAINBOW PFS HR 0.64), and a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific adds more, so PFS success is likely. OS as co-primary after prior immunochemotherapy is the harder bar and may be immature at an interim. Akeso announces readouts publicly and quickly.

assumptions.claim: Paclitaxel plus placebo gave median PFS about 2.9 months and ramucirumab added reduced progression or death by 36% (HR 0.64)
PFS by BICR and OS are dual primary outcomes with 506 patients

reason: Anti-TIGIT add-ons have failed in larger trials and this phase 2 has about 39 per arm; a significant ORR gain over about 26% would need roughly 25 points.
rationale: Anti-TIGIT combinations failed to improve outcomes in lung and liver phase 3 programs (SKYSCRAPER). Control PD-1 plus bevacizumab biosimilar already gives ORR near 25-30% in first-line HCC. With about 39 per arm, a significant ORR difference needs more than 20 points, and PFS is a co-primary. Dose-exploration design also dilutes power. Disclosure likely only at later congresses.

assumptions.claim: PD-1 plus bevacizumab-type regimens give IRRC-assessed ORR of about 21-30% in first-line HCC
The trial randomizes 117 patients across HLX53 1000 mg, HLX53 2000 mg and placebo arms

reason: OGA inhibition is an unproven mechanism in PSP and every earlier disease-modifying PSP trial on PSPRS failed; 241 patients over 52 weeks give modest power against a plausible small effect.
rationale: Phase 2 of an O-GlcNAcase inhibitor aimed at slowing tau pathology in PSP-RS. All prior disease-modifying PSP trials (davunetide, tideglusib, gosuranemab, tilavonemab, zagotenemab-class antibodies) showed no PSPRS benefit, and the OGA inhibitor ceperognastat failed in Alzheimer's. With about 120 per arm and a PSPRS change SD near 7, only a true benefit of 2 or more points is detectable.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-arm PSPRS worsening over 52 weeks in PSP-RS trials is roughly 9 to 11 points.
assumptions.source: Davunetide phase 2/3, Boxer et al, Lancet Neurol 2014

assumptions.claim: No disease-modifying therapy has shown a significant PSPRS benefit versus placebo in a randomized trial.
assumptions.source: Tilavonemab phase 2, Hoglinger et al, Brain 2021

reason: A TROP2 ADC unselected for expression in 3L+ gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma needs a clear OS gain over weak chemotherapy; plausible but uncertain, with TROP2 ADCs having mixed OS results elsewhere.
rationale: Control TPC (trifluridine-tipiracil, irinotecan, taxanes) gives median OS about 5 to 6 months (TAGS 5.7 months). Sac-TMT shows meaningful activity in gastric cancer, and with roughly 400 deaths an HR near 0.78 is detectable. But TROP2 ADCs vs docetaxel in NSCLC (TROPION-Lung01, EVOKE-01) missed OS, and gastric TROP2 expression is heterogeneous. Merck usually announces topline results promptly.

assumptions.claim: Trifluridine-tipiracil in 3L+ metastatic gastric cancer gave median OS of 5.7 months versus 3.6 months for placebo.
assumptions.source: TAGS, Shitara et al, Lancet Oncol 2018 (NCT02500043)

assumptions.claim: Sacituzumab govitecan and datopotamab deruxtecan did not significantly improve OS versus docetaxel in previously treated NSCLC.

reason: Plasma-derived IV C1-INH is a proven acute HAE therapy; the main risks are a high placebo response inside a 4-hour window with about 60 per arm, and a slow, late-running recruitment.
rationale: IV plasma C1-INH at 20 U/kg beat placebo on time to onset of relief in IMPACT-1 (median 0.5 vs 1.5 h) and other C1-INH products showed clear separation from placebo. A same-class Octapharma concentrate should separate on time to unequivocal relief, but placebo relief rates within 4 hours are not trivial and the sample is small. The record is still recruiting, so reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In IMPACT-1, C1-INH 20 U/kg gave a median time to onset of relief of 0.5 h versus 1.5 h for placebo.
assumptions.source: Craig et al, J Allergy Clin Immunol 2009 (IMPACT-1)

assumptions.claim: In FAST-3, median time to symptom relief with placebo was about 19.8 hours, showing a modest placebo rate early on.
assumptions.source: Cicardi et al, N Engl J Med 2010 (FAST-3)

reason: Randomized phase 2 of ocular-prophylaxis strategies for mirvetuximab, all patients already enrolled and primary completion due Feb 2027; expect on-time completion, a safety-style primary outcome unlikely to change, and AbbVie posting results only near the 12-month deadline.
The EGFRxHER3 bispecific ADC has shown high response rates in EGFR wild-type NSCLC, but ADCs versus docetaxel have missed OS elsewhere and toxicity may blunt survival benefit.
rationale: BL-B01D1 had ORR near 40% in pretreated EGFR wild-type NSCLC in phase 1/2 and several Chinese phase 3 trials of the drug met OS or PFS at interim. Docetaxel median OS about 9 to 10 months. Counterweights: TROPION-Lung01 and EVOKE-01 ADCs did not significantly improve OS versus docetaxel, and haematologic toxicity is heavy. With about 400 deaths, an HR near 0.76 would be significant.

assumptions.claim: Docetaxel median OS after platinum and PD-(L)1 therapy in NSCLC is about 9 to 10 months.
Dato-DXd versus docetaxel in previously treated NSCLC had OS HR 0.94, not significant.
assumptions.source: TROPION-Lung01, Ahn et al, J Clin Oncol 2024

reason: A 120-patient (80 vs 40) phase 2 with OS as primary has little power; cusatuzumab would need a very large survival effect on top of venetoclax-azacitidine to reach p<0.05.
rationale: With about 60 to 70 deaths and a 2:1 split, only an HR below roughly 0.55 reaches significance. Venetoclax-azacitidine already gives median OS of about 14 months, and anti-CD70 added value on top is unproven (earlier CULMINATE data were with azacitidine alone and small). Added toxicity is likely. Results from a private sponsor are likely to appear only at a congress such as ASH 2027.

assumptions.claim: Venetoclax plus azacitidine gave median OS of 14.7 months in unfit newly diagnosed AML.
assumptions.source: VIALE-A, DiNardo et al, N Engl J Med 2020 (NCT02993523)

assumptions.claim: Real-world venetoclax-azacitidine median OS is often 10 to 13 months.

reason: Open-ish comparison versus untreated eyes on a sponsor-specific maze test; phase 2 showed large effects in small groups, but a variable, learning-prone functional endpoint may not reach significance in the pooled analysis.
rationale: Phase 1/2 of OCU400 reported stabilization or improvement on LLVA and LDNA in treated versus untreated eyes, and Ocugen aligned the LDNA endpoint with regulators. But the phase 2 groups were small, controls are untreated (no sham), the test is subject to learning and motivation effects, and gene therapy RP trials have mixed records. Ocugen is a listed company and will announce topline results promptly, likely framing them as positive if significant.

assumptions.claim: In the OCU400 phase 1/2, treated eyes showed improved or stabilized LLVA and LDNA compared with untreated eyes.
LDNA is the pre-specified primary endpoint of the phase 3 liMeliGhT study.

reason: A 65-per-arm open-label phase 2 designed to estimate the contribution of axatilimab; a difference of about 16 points would be needed for significance and the study may carry no formal hypothesis test.
rationale: Ruxolitinib plus steroids already yields high response rates in newly diagnosed cGVHD (ORR near 60%), leaving limited headroom. Axatilimab has activity in refractory cGVHD (AGAVE-201 ORR about 74% at any time) but the add-on benefit over ruxolitinib is likely modest, and with 65 per arm the standard error is about 8 points. Phase 2 of this kind may be reported descriptively, which counts as not met.

assumptions.claim: Ruxolitinib in steroid-refractory or dependent cGVHD gave ORR of 49.7% at week 24 versus 25.6% for best available therapy.
assumptions.source: REACH3, Zeiser et al, N Engl J Med 2021

assumptions.claim: Axatilimab 0.3 mg/kg every 2 weeks gave ORR of 74% in refractory cGVHD.

reason: Dupilumab inadequate responders staying on dupilumab rarely reach EASI 90 by week 8, while a JAK inhibitor switch gives large, fast responses; the trial is well powered, so failure would need an unexpectedly strong control arm.
rationale: Patients already failing dupilumab and continuing it have very low odds of a 90% EASI reduction from an on-treatment baseline (about 5%). Upadacitinib 15 mg with escalation to 30 mg gave EASI 90 around 40-60% by week 16 in Heads Up and Measure Up, and switch data suggest roughly a third by week 8. With 92 per arm the difference is large and highly significant.
evidence: Heads Up (NCT03738397) 2021: upadacitinib 30 mg vs dupilumab, EASI 90 at week 16 61% vs 39%

assumptions.claim: Upadacitinib 30 mg gave EASI 90 at week 16 in 61% vs 39% for dupilumab in a head-to-head AD trial.
Patients with inadequate response on dupilumab rarely reach EASI 90 from their on-treatment baseline when staying on dupilumab.
assumptions.source: Clinical pattern; Level Up NCT05601882 dupilumab arm response rates

reason: Descriptive dose-optimisation phase 2 with no efficacy hypothesis; the registered primary completion looks near-term but the sponsor (now inside AstraZeneca) updates records infrequently, and results posting normally lags until close to the 12-month deadline.
rationale: No efficacy hypothesis, so only operations are forecast. Active not recruiting with primary completion Dec 2026; the primary safety outcome runs to 5 years of follow-up, which creates some risk of a date edit. Large-company posting usually comes close to the 12-month deadline, after Aug 2027.

reason: A phase 2a oral amyloid-lowering drug over 72 weeks may only slow plaque accumulation by a few centiloids, and the study has no formal efficacy hypothesis, so a clear statement that the PET objective was met is uncertain.
rationale: Oral Abeta-lowering agent in amyloid-positive early AD; placebo patients accumulate roughly 3-5 CL over 72 weeks. Production-lowering drugs (BACE inhibitors) slowed accumulation modestly. With 128 per arm and SD about 7 CL a 3 CL difference is detectable, but the effect size is unknown and a phase 2a safety/biomarker study may not declare success.
evidence: A4 / AHEAD placebo amyloid PET accumulation rates

assumptions.claim: Amyloid-positive older adults on placebo accumulate roughly 3-5 centiloids per year on amyloid PET.
assumptions.source: A4 Study, Sperling NEJM 2023 and ADNI cohort analyses

reason: Neuroprotectants given on top of thrombolysis have a poor track record in acute stroke, and the adaptive design makes an early futility stop at least as likely as a clear win.
rationale: Single-dose neuroprotectant in stroke patients receiving thrombolysis, with an mRS shift primary and an open-label PROBE control. Prior neuroprotection trials (ESCAPE-NA1, ESCAPE-NEXT, FRONTIER) were largely negative or confined to subgroups. An adaptive phase 2b can stop early for futility or enrichment, which would mostly be reported as not met.

assumptions.claim: Nerinetide, a related PSD-95 inhibitor, did not improve mRS shift in patients treated with alteplase in ESCAPE-NA1.

reason: BED trials carry high placebo response (about a 3 episode/week fall), so a drug effect of about 1 episode/week at 12 weeks is needed for significance; the phase 2 signal and the dopaminergic/noradrenergic mechanism are supportive.
rationale: Solriamfetol (DNRI plus TAAR1 agonism) showed a reduction in binge eating days at 300 mg in an earlier phase 2, and lisdexamfetamine proved the stimulant mechanism works in BED. Placebo response is large and Axsome's phase 3 record is mixed (ADHD positive, MDD negative). Two doses against placebo with 150 per arm gives decent power for a 0.3-0.4 SD effect.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in BED phase 3 trials typically reduce binge episodes or days by about 2.5-3.5 per week at 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: McElroy lisdexamfetamine BED trials, JAMA Psychiatry 2015

assumptions.claim: Solriamfetol is an approved dopamine/norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor with TAAR1 agonist activity.
assumptions.source: Sunosi FDA label; Axsome ENGAGE description

reason: Only 45 children and young adults with heterogeneous high-grade glioma; a CDK4/6 add-on to temozolomide has no proven benefit here, so even a real effect would struggle to reach p<0.05 with about 28 events.
rationale: Pediatric HGG has poor outcomes with temozolomide-based therapy and no drug has beaten it in randomized trials. Abemaciclib has CNS penetration and CDKN2A/B-loss rationale, but the population mixes H3-altered and other subtypes. A 45-patient randomized phase 2 needs a hazard ratio near 0.4 to be significant.
evidence: Abemaciclib recurrent GBM / DIPG phase 1-2 studies

assumptions.claim: Median event-free survival with temozolomide-based therapy in pediatric HGG after radiotherapy is well under 12 months.

reason: With only 21 patients per arm and a QMG change SD near 3.8, a real benefit of about 2.5 points is detected only about 60% of the time; the phase 2a signal supports a real effect.
rationale: NMD670 (ClC-1 chloride channel inhibitor) improved QMG in the phase 2a MG study with clinically meaningful changes. Phase 2b adds three doses at 21 days. SE of the difference is about 1.1 points, so an effect of 2-3 points gives roughly 50-65% power; any of three doses can win, and a small biotech will report significant results promptly.

assumptions.claim: NMD670 improved QMG total score versus placebo in a phase 2 proof-of-concept study in myasthenia gravis.

reason: Platinum doublet after osimertinib gives only about 4-5 months PFS and an EGFR-directed ADC with strong ORR in this setting should beat it clearly; the main risk is a hazard ratio closer to 0.8 than 0.6.
rationale: Chemotherapy after osimertinib progression gave PFS of about 4.2 months in MARIPOSA-2. Dato-DXd showed ORR about 43% and PFS about 5.8 months in EGFR-mutant NSCLC (TROPION-Lung05 / Lung01) and secured accelerated approval. With 256 per arm and about 330 events, an HR near 0.6 is highly significant. Sponsor AstraZeneca reports topline promptly.

assumptions.claim: Platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy after osimertinib progression gives a median PFS of about 4.2 months.
Dato-DXd monotherapy had a 43% ORR and median PFS of 5.8 months in pretreated EGFR-mutated NSCLC.

reason: Only 19 patients and a slow-moving liver iron endpoint at 24 weeks: raising hepcidin cuts iron absorption but a 2-3 mg Fe/g fall with SD about 3 is borderline significant at 10 vs 9 patients.
rationale: TMPRSS6 inhibition raises hepcidin and limits iron absorption, which should lower liver iron in NTDT, but LIC changes slowly and R2* MRI has measurement noise. Placebo LIC is flat to slightly rising. SE of the difference is about 1.4 mg Fe/g, so a true 2.5 mg fall gives roughly 50% power. Regeneron discloses small phase 2s mainly at congresses.

assumptions.claim: In non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia, hepcidin deficiency drives iron overload through excess absorption.
assumptions.source: Taher et al., Blood 2013 NTDT review

reason: Biosimilar PK similarity studies by experienced sponsors usually pass the 80-125% margin; residual risk is the steady-state AUC with about 80 patients per arm and between-subject variability around 30%.
rationale: Amgen designs PK similarity trials with adequate power and ABP 234 is made to match Keytruda; pembrolizumab PK has moderate variability, and 163 patients provide a narrow 90% CI for AUC ratios. Both single-dose and steady-state AUC must fall within the margin, which trims the probability slightly. Amgen rarely issues press releases on PK similarity results.
evidence: Amgen ABP 938 and ABP 654 biosimilar programs

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab has linear PK with moderate between-subject variability in AUC (CV around 30%).

reason: Small phase 2 (about 60 PFS events) needs a large effect (HR below about 0.65) to reach significance, and B013 has no published efficacy signal; weekly paclitaxel control PFS is only about 4 months.
rationale: Placebo-controlled phase 2 of an unpublished agent added to weekly paclitaxel in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, 90 patients, roughly 60 PFS events. Paclitaxel control PFS is about 3.5-4 months (AURELIA 3.4). Only a strong effect (HR under about 0.65) reaches p<0.05; B013 mechanism and prior signal are unknown, so the effect prior is modest. Still recruiting, so an early readout is unlikely.
evidence: AURELIA 2014 (bevacizumab plus weekly paclitaxel in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer)

assumptions.claim: Weekly paclitaxel alone in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer gives a median PFS of about 3.4 months.

reason: Chinese phase 3 and phase 2 showed large MG-ADL gains over placebo; with 191 patients a 1.2-point difference is enough, so the main risk is a larger global placebo response.
rationale: Telitacicept (BLyS/APRIL TACI-Fc) gave a large MG-ADL benefit over placebo at week 24 in RemeGen's China phase 3 (about -5.7 vs -2.3). With 191 patients and SD near 3.8, a difference of 1.2 points suffices. Global placebo response is the main uncertainty. Enrolment is complete and primary completion is 2027-03, so topline around mid-2027 is plausible.
evidence: RemeGen China phase 3 telitacicept gMG NCT05737160

assumptions.claim: Telitacicept beat placebo on MG-ADL change at week 24 in the Chinese phase 3 gMG trial.
Placebo MG-ADL change at week 24-26 in gMG phase 3 trials is typically about -2 to -3 points.

reason: Obefazimod worked in ulcerative colitis but Crohn's efficacy is unproven; CDAI is noisy with a large placebo response, and the many week-52 primaries may be judged as not all met.
rationale: Obefazimod (miR-124 enhancer) reached its phase 3 UC endpoints, but Crohn's efficacy is untested. CDAI week-12 change has SD near 105 and placebo about -55, so with about 106 per arm one needs roughly -27 points for significance. Prior chance the drug works in CD is about 55%. The many week-52 co-primaries add labelling risk. Induction topline likely Q2 2027.

assumptions.claim: Obefazimod met induction clinical remission in the ABTECT phase 3 ulcerative colitis trials.
Placebo CDAI change at week 12 in Crohn's induction trials is about -40 to -70 points.
assumptions.source: U-EXCEL and U-EXCEED upadacitinib CD trials, Loftus 2023

reason: Open-label phase 2 with 142 patients; docetaxel is a weak control (PFS about 3.5-4 months) so a platinum-doublet-plus-ICI regimen could win, but the oncolytic virus contribution is unproven and the readout is likely late.
rationale: Experimental arm gives platinum-doublet plus ICI after Olvi-Vec versus docetaxel, a weak post-ICI comparator (PFS about 3.5-4 months). About 100 events give 80% power near HR 0.62. Olvi-Vec showed HR about 0.7 in its ovarian phase 2. The regimen change alone may deliver much of the benefit, but recruitment is slow with 15 US sites and a small sponsor.
evidence: SAPPHIRE sitravatinib plus nivolumab vs docetaxel 2023

assumptions.claim: Docetaxel after chemo-immunotherapy in NSCLC gives a median PFS of about 3.5-4 months.

reason: Efinopegdutide cut liver fat about 70% in phase 2a NAFLD; the main uncertainty is smaller absolute PDFF change in cirrhosis, and whether and when Merck reports at all.
rationale: GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist efinopegdutide reduced MRI-PDFF liver fat by about 72% at 24 weeks in earlier NAFLD phase 2a, more than semaglutide. Cirrhotic livers have lower baseline fat, so absolute change shrinks, but 43 vs 42 patients and a placebo change near zero still give a large effect size. The safety primaries are descriptive. Merck results posting is due by August 2027.
evidence: MK-6024-001 efinopegdutide NAFLD phase 2a (Romero-Gomez, J Hepatol 2023)

assumptions.claim: Efinopegdutide reduced liver fat content by about 72% from baseline at 24 weeks in phase 2a NAFLD.
