reason: Adaptive phase 2 across five glomerular diseases with 36 weeks of safety follow-up per patient; recruitment of 96 patients is likely to run past mid-2027, and the sponsor is a private biotech with funding risk.
B007 (probably anti-CD20) tends to beat cyclosporine only at later time points (MENTOR: 60% vs 20% at 24 months, similar at 12), so the unspecified assessment time decides the outcome.
rationale: Open-label phase 2/3 vs cyclosporine, 108 per arm. In MENTOR rituximab beat cyclosporine at 24 months (60% vs 20% remission) but not at 12 months (39.8% vs 34.8%). The time frame here is about 2 years, which favours the anti-CD20 type antibody, and a 20-point gap gives about 80% power. Uncertainty about the actual measurement time and a not-yet-proven agent temper this.
evidence: MENTOR rituximab vs cyclosporine membranous nephropathy (Fervenza NEJM 2019)

assumptions.claim: In primary membranous nephropathy, cyclosporine achieved CR+PR in 34.8% at 12 months and 20% at 24 months versus 39.8% and 60% for rituximab.

reason: Only 20 per arm, and the registered primary spans day 70 and day 112 (both may need to be met); a 30-point gap is roughly the minimum for significance by Fisher test.
rationale: First-in-class CRISPR lentiviral-particle therapy against HSV-1 for stromal keratitis, tested add-on to triple-drug therapy. Cure requires clinical resolution plus viral genome clearance, which the gene editor targets directly. Early exploratory cases looked promising. With 20 vs 20 patients, 80% vs 50% gives Fisher p near 0.05, and both day 70 and day 112 appear in the primary.
evidence: BDgene BD111 / HELP investigator-initiated HSK study 2025

reason: SVR35 is likely to separate with 400 vs 200 patients, but TSS50 must also be met and symptom co-primaries have often failed in ruxolitinib add-on trials; the readout is also unlikely before mid-2027.
rationale: Both SVR35 and TSS50 must be met. Navtemadlin showed SVR35 15% vs 5% and TSS50 25% vs 12.5% in BOREAS (monotherapy, relapsed). Add-on to ruxolitinib in suboptimal responders should give a modest SVR35 gain over a low placebo rate. Pelabresib (MANIFEST-2) met SVR35 but missed TSS50, a pattern I expect to recur. Run-in design and 600 enrolment push the readout late.

assumptions.claim: In BOREAS navtemadlin gave SVR35 about 15% vs 5% for best available therapy and TSS50 about 25% vs 12.5%.
In MANIFEST-2 pelabresib plus ruxolitinib met SVR35 (65.9% vs 35.2%) but not TSS50 (52.3% vs 46.3%, p=0.216).

reason: Adjunctive GAD trials carry large placebo responses (about 10 HAM-A points); an expected 2-point drug advantage gives roughly even odds in a dose-ranging phase 2 with two doses and multiplicity.
rationale: Phase 2, 235 per arm, SD about 8.5 gives SE near 0.8 points, so a 2-point drug-placebo difference is borderline significant. Placebo response in adjunctive anxiety trials is high. Lumateperone-class mechanism had a sizeable adjunctive MDD effect, which supports a real but moderate anxiolytic signal. Two doses give some chance that either wins, offset by multiplicity.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in adjunctive or monotherapy GAD trials typically improve by about 9 to 12 HAM-A points at 6 to 8 weeks.
assumptions.source: Quetiapine XR GAD phase 3 trials, Khan 2011 / Merideth 2012

reason: SGLT2-class effects on KCCQ-CSS in related heart failure populations are 1.5 to 4 points against a placebo response of 5 or more; with 250 per arm and SD near 17 the trial has roughly even-to-lower power.
rationale: SGLT2 inhibitors improve KCCQ by about 1.5 to 4 points in HFpEF; ODYSSEY-HCM (mavacamten, non-obstructive HCM) failed on KCCQ-CSS despite a strong mechanism, and HCM placebo response is large. SE is about 1.5 points with 250 per arm, so power against a likely 2 to 3 point effect is about 40 percent. Sponsor is small and will report quickly after the January 2027 last visit.

assumptions.claim: In DELIVER dapagliflozin improved KCCQ total symptom score by about 2.4 points over placebo at 8 months.
assumptions.source: DELIVER, Nassif et al. Nat Med 2022

assumptions.claim: In ODYSSEY-HCM mavacamten did not significantly improve KCCQ-CSS versus placebo in non-obstructive HCM.

reason: Two-site Taiwanese cell-therapy phase 2 that was still recruiting only two months before its registered primary completion, so a later date is likely if the record is updated; results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is unlikely for a Taiwan-only study.

Non-inferiority of a 6-monthly axitinib implant against aflibercept 2 mg needs near-equal week-48 vision; durable agents have usually met the margin, but a small loss in a 4 to 5 letter margin is the main risk.
rationale: A Phase 3 active-controlled nAMD trial of a sustained-release TKI implant, with fully enrolled arms and week-48 completion in January 2027. Aflibercept 2 mg q8w typically gains about 6 to 8 letters; sustained-release and high-dose agents (faricimab, aflibercept 8 mg) have met non-inferiority, while some durable agents (KSI-301 in DAZZLE) missed. Early phase data showed stable vision with few rescue injections.

assumptions.claim: Aflibercept 2 mg every 8 weeks gains roughly 6 to 8 ETDRS letters at week 48 in treatment-naive nAMD.
Non-inferiority margins in nAMD BCVA trials are typically 4 to 4.5 letters.

reason: A biologic that blocks the upstream cytokine pathway should cut blood eosinophils sharply even in 36 per arm; the main risk is a press release that gives no statement on the primary comparison.
rationale: The primary endpoint is a pharmacodynamic biomarker with a large expected effect: anti-TSLP-type antibodies lower blood eosinophils by about 50 to 60 percent against flat placebo, so even 36 per arm gives very high power. Failure would mostly come from reporting only as encouraging, or no statistical test published for this private sponsor.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab reduces blood eosinophils by about 50 to 60 percent from baseline in asthma.

reason: Eosinophil lowering in an eosinophil-enriched COPD population should be large and significant at the high dose; the risk is the report form (percent change, or no formal statement) rather than the biology.
rationale: Primary is eosinophil change, a direct pharmacodynamic effect of the antibody, in patients selected for elevated eosinophils, so baseline is high and the absolute reduction large with about 60 per arm. FEV1 is a small, exploratory secondary in a 12-week phase 2, so it is unlikely to reach significance.

assumptions.claim: Anti-TSLP antibody tezepelumab lowered blood eosinophils substantially in COPD patients with higher baseline eosinophils in COURSE.
assumptions.source: COURSE phase 2a, Singh et al. Lancet Respir Med 2022

reason: Only 16 patients per arm: PFS-6 would need a difference of roughly 40 points to reach p<0.05, and the study is still recruiting, so it is unlikely to report by mid-2027.
rationale: A Phase 3 label with 32 patients; PFS-6 with bevacizumab alone is about 25 to 40 percent in recurrent GBM. Focused-ultrasound blood-brain-barrier opening could add benefit, but proportion tests at n=16 per arm need a very large gap. Early NaviFUS studies were tiny and safety-focused. Still recruiting in October 2026 so reporting by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Bevacizumab alone gives 6-month PFS of roughly 25 to 40 percent in recurrent glioblastoma.
assumptions.source: BELOB 2014; EORTC 26101 Wick et al. NEJM 2017

reason: EGFRxHER3 bispecific ADC against topotecan in second-line SCLC after PD-1 and platinum has shown high response rates in phase 2 and topotecan control survival is short; with 722 patients the OS comparison is well powered.
rationale: Second-line SCLC after chemo-immunotherapy is a setting where effective agents beat topotecan clearly (tarlatamab DeLLphi-304 OS HR 0.60). Iza-bren (BL-B01D1) showed roughly 40 to 50 percent response in phase 2 SCLC. With 722 patients and open-label design, an interim or final OS win is likely; risk is toxicity-driven early deaths or a weaker-than-phase-2 effect.

assumptions.claim: Tarlatamab beat topotecan, lurbinectedin or amrubicin in second-line SCLC with OS HR 0.60 (13.6 vs 8.3 months).
Topotecan control arms in second-line SCLC have median OS of about 6 to 8 months.

reason: About 14 patients per arm with highly variable percent UPCR change gives low power; an anti-CD40L effect in steroid-responsive MCD/FSGS is plausible but placebo also drifts down, and slow rare-disease recruitment pushes any readout past mid-2027.
rationale: Phase 2a umbrella with roughly 14 patients per arm and a noisy percent-UPCR endpoint, so even a real effect often fails a 0.05 test. Entry requires prior steroid responsiveness, so placebo patients can remit spontaneously. Anti-CD40L has a plausible rationale (B-cell/T-cell help in podocytopathy; rituximab works in MCD) but no human data in FSGS/MCD. Sanofi would likely only publicise a clear win; readout probably after June 2027.
evidence: Rituximab in steroid-dependent minimal change disease case series and trials

assumptions.claim: Entry requires a documented prior UPCR reduction of more than 40 percent on corticosteroid or immunosuppressant therapy, so spontaneous placebo improvement is likely.
The study is a 6-arm umbrella with 84 planned participants, i.e. about 14 per arm.
assumptions.source: NCT06500702 ClinicalTrials.gov record, enrollment and summary

reason: Open-label single-arm biomarker study, fully enrolled (active, not recruiting); the week-48 biopsy readout is date-driven so little slippage, but UCB usually posts results only many months after primary completion and study completion is March 2028.
Thrombopoietin receptor agonists reliably beat placebo on pre-procedure platelet response in this setting; the main uncertainty is whether and when Hengrui publishes, not efficacy.
rationale: Avatrombopag (ADAPT-1/2) and lusutrombopag (L-PLUS 1/2) beat placebo by 40-60 points on pre-procedure platelet response in chronic liver disease; hetrombopag is a potent TPO-RA, Part A fixed the dose, and 60+ patients per arm gives ample power. Placebo response with the no-rescue requirement is about 15-25%. The trial is complete; risk lies in publication timing by Hengrui.
evidence: ADAPT-1 and ADAPT-2 avatrombopag, Terrault 2018 Gastroenterology

assumptions.claim: In ADAPT-1 the low-baseline-platelet group had 65.6 percent responders on avatrombopag 60 mg versus 22.9 percent on placebo.
The record's Part B primary is the share with platelets at least 50 and a rise of at least 20 within 24 hours before surgery without transfusion.

reason: Adding an anti-CD38-type antibody to pomalidomide-dexamethasone has repeatedly cut progression risk by about 40 percent; the larger risk is timing, since a recruiting trial from a small sponsor is unlikely to read out PFS by mid-2027.
rationale: SG301 appears to be a CD38-directed antibody (CD38-refractory patients are excluded). CD38 antibody plus Pd versus Pd gave PFS HR about 0.6 in ICARIA-MM and APOLLO with control PFS 6.5-7 months. A 360-patient placebo-controlled design is well powered if SG301 is active. Main uncertainty is whether PFS is analysed and made public by mid-2027; the registry still shows recruiting.
evidence: ICARIA-MM isatuximab plus Pd, Attal 2019 Lancet
APOLLO daratumumab plus Pd, Dimopoulos 2021 Lancet Oncology

assumptions.claim: In ICARIA-MM, isatuximab plus Pd had median PFS 11.5 versus 6.5 months with Pd alone, HR 0.596.
The record excludes patients primary refractory to a prior CD38 antibody, consistent with SG301 being anti-CD38.

reason: A daily GLP-2 analog should beat placebo on PN reduction as teduglutide did, but with 36 per arm and a 20 percent responder threshold the margin for a significant result is modest.
rationale: PJ009 is a GLP-2 analog; teduglutide STEPS gave 63 percent versus 30 percent responders at weeks 20-24 and apraglutide had similar separation. With about 36 per arm, a 30-point difference gives roughly 80 percent power. Chinese phase 3 sponsors usually carry forward a validated mechanism and a phase 2 signal. Primary completion has passed, so data exist; publication timing by a private sponsor is the unknown.

assumptions.claim: In STEPS, 63 percent of teduglutide patients versus 30 percent of placebo patients had at least 20 percent PN volume reduction at weeks 20 and 24.
The registered primary completion (2026-09-28) has passed and the status is active, not recruiting.

reason: The composite of itch NRS4 plus IGA success at week 24 is strict and the phase 2 itch effect was modest, but about 115-175 patients per arm gives good power if the JAK1 inhibitor effect holds.
rationale: JAK1 inhibition gives fast itch relief and povorcitinib showed dose-related itch and nodule effects in phase 2 PN. The composite requires both itch and lesion response, which lowers rates (placebo about 5-10 percent, drug about 20-25 percent), but 349 patients still give strong power for a 10+ point gap. Primary completion Oct 2026 means topline likely in Q1 2027 from Incyte.
evidence: PRIME and PRIME2 dupilumab PN, Yosipovitch 2023 Nature Medicine

assumptions.claim: In PRIME, 60.0 percent of dupilumab versus 18.4 percent of placebo patients reached at least 4-point itch improvement at week 24.
The registered primary is the composite of Itch NRS4 and IGA CPG-S 0/1 with at least 2-grade improvement at week 24.

reason: Twin of STOP-PN1: the strict itch-plus-lesion composite at week 24 and a modest phase 2 itch effect are the main risks, but the trial is well powered if the JAK1 inhibitor effect holds.
rationale: Replicate pivotal with the same design as STOP-PN1 and the same primary completion date, so Incyte will likely report both together. JAK1 inhibition gives fast itch relief; the composite endpoint lowers response rates (placebo about 5-10 percent, drug about 20-25 percent), but 346 patients give strong power. Outcomes of the two twins are highly correlated.
evidence: PRIME and PRIME2 dupilumab PN, Yosipovitch 2023 Nature Medicine

assumptions.claim: In PRIME2, 37.2 percent of dupilumab versus 22.0 percent of placebo patients reached at least 4-point itch improvement at week 12.
STOP-PN2 shares the identical primary outcome and registered dates with STOP-PN1.

reason: A TROP2 ADC should clearly beat single-agent chemotherapy on PFS, but the OS co-primary must also be met and may be immature at the first announcement.
rationale: FDA018-ADC is a TROP2-directed SN-38 ADC, a class that gave PFS HR 0.41 (ASCENT) and 0.32 (OptiTROP-Breast01) against chemotherapy in pre-treated TNBC, with chemotherapy PFS of 1.7-2.5 months. PFS success is very likely. Because OS is a co-primary that must also be met, the overall probability is discounted; a sponsor announcement may report PFS only.

assumptions.claim: In ASCENT, sacituzumab govitecan had median PFS 5.6 versus 1.7 months with chemotherapy, HR 0.41.
In OptiTROP-Breast01, sacituzumab tirumotecan had median PFS 5.7 versus 2.3 months with chemotherapy, HR 0.32.

reason: Norovirus VLP efficacy in young children is unproven (a bivalent infant vaccine failed in phase 2b), and the primary depends on enough PCR-confirmed cases of four specific genotypes over two years.
rationale: Large 1:1 placebo-controlled efficacy trial in 6600 children with a tetravalent VLP vaccine targeting GI.1, GII.3, GII.4 and GII.17. Challenge and adult data support VLP protection, but the HilleVax HIL-214 infant phase 2b missed its endpoint and genotype mismatch or low case counts can sink the analysis. Observation ends March 2027, so a public result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Atmar 2011 NEJM norovirus VLP vaccine challenge study

assumptions.claim: The HIL-214 bivalent VLP vaccine did not meet its primary endpoint in the infant phase 2b NEST-IN1 trial.
The trial randomises 6600 children 1:1 with primary observation ending around March 2027.

reason: A dose-finding phase 2 with about 24 patients per arm and an active bupivacaine control makes superiority on 72-hour pain AUC uncertain, though the longer duration of liposomal bupivacaine favours it.
rationale: Liposomal bupivacaine extends analgesia to 48-72 hours versus roughly 8-12 hours for plain bupivacaine, supporting lower 72-hour pain AUC at the highest dose. But the trial is a small multi-arm dose-finding study at one site, nerve-block studies of liposomal bupivacaine are mixed, and no formal superiority hypothesis is stated. Results are unlikely to be public by mid-2027.
evidence: Exparel (liposomal bupivacaine) nerve block trials, mixed results

assumptions.claim: The trial enrolls 96 patients with a plain bupivacaine hydrochloride active control and a dose-finding design.
The trial started on 2026-03-03 with primary completion registered as 2026-11.

reason: Small-company phase 2 with a safety run-in, enrichment and an optional randomized part; 178 patients and a registered end of Dec 2026 will not be reached, so the trial will still be recruiting after March 2027 and will not have posted results.

Rare-disease phase 2 with a 17-week safety primary, enrollment closed, and registered primary completion Dec 2026; small biotech is unlikely to post results by Aug 2027 and a modest chance the date slips.
AMOR-1 gets half the elemental calcium, so serum calcium may drift out of 8.0-10.0 mg/dL at week 14, but the control arm cannot reach a 50% dose cut, so even a modest responder rate beats it.
rationale: The composite needs a 50% calcium dose cut plus calcium 8.0-10.0 and no vitamin D increase. Control patients keep their dose, so they almost never qualify; AMOR-1 patients have the cut by design. With 41 vs 21, about 20-25% responders vs 0% is already significant. Risk is that half the calcium fails to hold serum calcium in range. A press release is likelier if results are positive.
evidence: PaTH Forward / rhPTH(1-84) composite responder trial (Mannstadt 2013)

assumptions.claim: Control patients keep their initial elemental calcium intake, so the 50% dose-reduction component is rarely met in that arm.

reason: The phase 1 hazard ratio near 0.4 came from small numbers and is likely optimistic, and a pooled control that includes docetaxel is somewhat stronger than enzalutamide alone, but a 600-patient trial still has high power at a realistic HR near 0.65.
rationale: Phase 1b mevrometostat plus enzalutamide gave median rPFS about 14 months vs about 5 months for enzalutamide in a randomized expansion (HR about 0.4), in post-abiraterone mCRPC with an EZH2 rationale. Expect a smaller phase 3 effect (HR 0.6-0.7) against physician's choice with median rPFS of about 6 months. With about 360 events the trial is well powered, and BICR rPFS is the only primary.
evidence: Pfizer phase 1 mevrometostat + enzalutamide post-abiraterone mCRPC, ASCO GU 2025
CARD 2019 (ARPI switch control rPFS about 2.7 months)

assumptions.claim: Mevrometostat plus enzalutamide showed median rPFS of roughly 14 months in post-abiraterone mCRPC in phase 1 data, versus about 5 months for enzalutamide alone.
assumptions.source: Pfizer phase 1 data presented at ASCO GU 2025

assumptions.claim: Control arm median rPFS on second-line enzalutamide after abiraterone is short, about 3-6 months, and on docetaxel about 5-7 months.

reason: The top-dose cohort has about 10 children against 12 pooled placebo, and this is a dose-ranging safety study without a formal hypothesis, so a descriptive report or a non-significant test is the likely outcome even with a real effect.
rationale: Tenapanor raises SBM frequency in adults (about 1-1.5 SBM/week over placebo), but here about 10 children per top dose and 12 placebo with SD near 2.5 SBM/week gives a standard error near 1.1, so a true difference of 1.2-1.5 is not clearly significant. The design is dose-escalating and pediatric; results may appear only as a registry post or label update without a formal win claim.

assumptions.claim: Tenapanor in adult IBS-C raised weekly SBM frequency by roughly 1.5-2.5 above placebo in phase 3 trials.

reason: OX40L blockade has no proven mucosal effect in celiac disease; it must blunt the gluten-induced fall in Vh:Cd against a noisy biopsy endpoint with about 38 patients per arm, and most celiac phase 2 programs have failed.
rationale: Gluten challenge models are sensitive: the TG2 inhibitor ZED1227 held Vh:Cd about 0.4 above placebo at 100 mg. Amlitelimab is a T-cell costimulation blocker without celiac precedent, atopic dermatitis phase 3 effects were modest, and six arms with about 38 each leave the highest-dose comparison noisy. Sanofi tends to disclose phase 2 readouts in earnings pipeline updates.

assumptions.claim: In the ZED1227 gluten-challenge trial, placebo Vh:Cd fell by about 0.4 while the 100 mg dose held it near baseline.

reason: SLE placebo BICLA response runs high at 30-45% and the effect of a non-depleting CD19/FcgRIIb antibody is unproven in lupus, so a difference under about 15 points would miss significance with 95 per arm.
rationale: Obexelimab dampens B cells and reduced IgG4-RD flares, but SLE phase 2 trials often fail on BICLA/SRI because placebo response is 35-45%. With 95 per arm, a significant result needs a difference of about 15-18 points. Obexelimab may reach that if B-cell inhibition works, but the typical phase 2 success rate in SLE is about 35-40%.

assumptions.claim: Placebo BICLA response at week 24 in SLE trials is typically 30-45%.

reason: The expected 2-3 point MADRS advantage is small relative to a placebo change near 10 points, earlier phase 3 results were not uniformly significant, and the second primary (relapse in Part 2) must also be met.
rationale: MDD3001 showed seltorexant 20 mg at about 2.6 MADRS points over placebo at Day 43 (p=0.007); other phase 3 data were less consistent. With about 300+ per arm the Part 1 test is well powered for a true effect of 2.5 but not for 1.5. Co-primary Part 2 relapse prevention adds risk, and J&J rarely announces phase 3 psychiatry toplines separately.

assumptions.claim: Seltorexant 20 mg beat placebo by about 2.6 MADRS points at Day 43 in the first phase 3 trial MDD3001.

reason: Adjunctive MDD trials carry large placebo response with psychological support; the psychedelic effect (partial unblinding helps) must still exceed about 2.7 MADRS points with 110 per arm, which phase 2 and psilocybin phase 3 data suggest is likely.
rationale: CYB003 phase 2 showed a very large MADRS advantage (about 14 points at 3 weeks) in small groups; psilocybin phase 3 (COMP005) gave -3.6 points at week 6 with 258 patients, and LSD phase 3 was positive. Functional unblinding favours detection. With 110 per arm and SD near 10, a difference of 2.7 suffices; expect about 5. Cybin has guided topline for Q4 2026.

assumptions.claim: COMP360 psilocybin 25 mg beat placebo by 3.6 MADRS points at Week 6 in the phase 3 COMP005 trial.
Cybin guided APPROACH topline data for Q4 2026.

reason: A novel anti-NETosis antibody tested for only 6 weeks in about 24 patients per arm needs a difference of roughly 0.6 DAS28 points to reach significance, and placebo response in csDMARD-background RA is sizeable.
rationale: CIT-013 targets NET formation, a mechanism not yet shown to work in RA. With 24 patients per arm, a 6-week DAS28-CRP change has SD near 1.0, so the trial needs about a 0.6-point gain over placebo. Any one of three doses counts, which helps, and private sponsors tend to publicise positive readouts, but efficacy here is uncertain.
evidence: Citryll CIT-013 phase 1 healthy volunteer study 2022

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in csDMARD-background RA trials typically improve DAS28-CRP by about 0.8 to 1.1 points by week 12.
The trial randomises about 96 patients across three CIT-013 doses and placebo, about 24 per arm.

reason: PD-1 blockade adds modest activity to chemotherapy in MSS colon cancer, and with 60 patients per arm only a difference near 20 points would reach p<0.05.
rationale: Dostarlimab alone is inactive in MSS colon cancer, and the benefit of adding it to CAPEOX is probably modest. A 60 versus 60 randomised phase 2 reaches significance only with a gain of about 18-20 points over a control mPR near 15%. The trial is still recruiting, so a readout before mid-2027 is unlikely, and results may be descriptive.

assumptions.claim: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone produces major pathological response in only a low share of MSS colon tumours, from single digits to about 15-20% with longer regimens.
The trial planned 120 patients, 60 per arm, and was still recruiting at launch.

reason: Solriamfetol robustly lifts MWT latency in other sleepiness disorders, so the MWT should win, but both MWT and CGI-S must be met and placebo response or night-shift measurement noise could sink one.
rationale: Solriamfetol 300 mg raised MWT sleep latency by roughly 8-12 minutes over placebo in narcolepsy and OSA, and modafinil/armodafinil, weaker drugs, worked in shift work disorder. With about 173 per arm the MWT is well powered. The risk is the co-primary CGI-S and placebo response. Axsome reports toplines quickly once the last visit is done.
evidence: Czeisler modafinil shift work disorder NEJM 2005

assumptions.claim: Solriamfetol 300 mg improved MWT sleep latency by roughly 8-12 minutes over placebo in narcolepsy and OSA phase 3 trials.
Modafinil improved night-shift sleep latency and clinical global impression in shift work disorder versus placebo.

reason: Complete debridement should be met given phase 2 data, but wound closure is a co-primary that a product applied for only up to 8 days may not move enough, and both must succeed.
rationale: The phase 2 VLU study showed about 63% versus 30% complete debridement, so the first co-primary is likely met. The second, time to wound closure within 12 weeks, is the real risk: phase 2 showed only a trend in area reduction, and a short debridement course may not translate into closure. Adaptive sample size helps power but both co-primaries must pass.

assumptions.claim: In the EscharEx phase 2 VLU study, complete debridement was about 63% with EscharEx versus about 30% with gel vehicle.
The phase 3 has two co-primary endpoints: complete debridement and time to wound closure.

reason: A new siderophore-type cephalosporin versus imipenem in cUTI usually clears a 10-point non-inferiority margin, so the main risk is a strong imipenem arm or resistant isolates in China.
rationale: Non-inferiority against imipenem-cilastatin in cUTI at test of cure is a low bar: cefiderocol, cefepime-taniborbactam and others met or beat it with margins of 10 points. With about 290 per arm and a mostly susceptible Enterobacterales population the noninferiority bound should be cleared. The uncertainty is mainly whether and when Hengrui discloses the result.

assumptions.claim: Cefiderocol reached a composite response of 72.5% versus 54.6% for imipenem-cilastatin in cUTI at test of cure.
assumptions.source: APEKS-cUTI, Portsmouth et al, Lancet Infect Dis 2018

assumptions.claim: The usual non-inferiority margin for the cUTI composite endpoint is 10 percentage points.

reason: Prophylaxis with an anti-TFPI agent versus on-demand treatment cuts treated bleeds by 70-90% in earlier trials, so success is near certain; the open question is when Alphamab discloses it.
rationale: Anti-TFPI prophylaxis versus on-demand therapy gives very large ABR reductions: concizumab in explorer7 and marstacimab in BASIS cut treated bleeds by roughly 80-90%. With 42 versus 21 patients who bled at least 6 times in the prior 26 weeks, significance is almost guaranteed. The main uncertainty is disclosure timing, not the result.

assumptions.claim: Anti-TFPI prophylaxis reduced treated bleeding rates by roughly 80-90% versus on-demand in phase 3.
Part A randomises on-demand patients 2:1 to KN057 prophylaxis or continued on-demand treatment for 26 weeks.

reason: FGF21 analogs have shown large histologic effects, but about 40 patients per arm with a biopsy endpoint is small and the trial is slow, so a readout before mid-2027 is very unlikely.
rationale: FGF21 analogs (pegozafermin, efruxifermin) lifted NASH resolution by roughly 25-30 points over placebo in phase 2, so a class effect is likely and the OR-composite primary is lenient. With about 40 per arm and biopsy read variability, power is moderate. Public status is the issue: the trial was still recruiting, so data are unlikely by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: FGF21 analogs raised NASH resolution without fibrosis worsening by roughly 25-35 points over placebo in phase 2b.
The trial was still recruiting in late 2026 with a 48-week biopsy endpoint.

reason: Both WOMAC at 48 weeks and MRI cartilage must be met; the cartilage co-primary and a sizeable hyaluronate response are the main hurdles, and no readout is likely before mid-2027.
rationale: Allogeneic adipose MSC injections versus hyaluronate in knee OA: pain scores often favour MSCs at 48 weeks because the hyaluronate effect fades, so WOMAC may be met. But MRI cartilage volume is a harder co-primary, and the trial was still recruiting with two sites, so results are unlikely before mid-2027.
evidence: Lee 2019 adipose stem cells knee OA phase 2b

assumptions.claim: Intra-articular hyaluronate gives clinically relevant WOMAC improvement early on, but its effect wanes by about 6-12 months.
assumptions.source: Meta-analyses of viscosupplementation in knee OA, 2012-2020

assumptions.claim: The trial has two primary outcomes, WOMAC at 48 weeks and MRI cartilage at 24 weeks, and enrolls 520 patients at 2 sites.

reason: A single-site Chinese phase 2 with ORR as the only primary, still recruiting past its registered completion; it will probably run on quietly, with little chance of posted results or a stop by August 2027.
A dual sclerostin/DKK1 bispecific at its highest regimen should raise lumbar spine BMD far above placebo; the main uncertainty is the dose actually tested and whether and when Angitia reports.
rationale: AGA2118 blocks sclerostin and DKK1; osteoanabolics like romosozumab raise lumbar spine BMD by about 13% at 12 months versus about 0.4% for placebo. With roughly 54 per arm and an SD near 4.5, even a 5% effect is significant, so the highest regimen is very likely to beat placebo. Risk is mainly low dose selection or a nonstandard analysis.

assumptions.claim: Placebo lumbar spine BMD change at 12 months is about +0.4% in postmenopausal women.
Romosozumab raised lumbar spine BMD by about 13% at 12 months.

reason: The comparator is active atropine, which already slows myopia, and a 140-patient exploratory phase 2 is unlikely to show a significant superiority difference in spherical equivalent against it.
rationale: SHJ002 is an anti-miRNA antisense oligonucleotide being compared with atropine, not placebo. Atropine has a solid effect on spherical equivalent progression, and with 70 per arm and SD near 0.45 D a significant superiority difference would need about 0.22 D. An exploratory design makes a 'met' statement unlikely, and a small private sponsor may report slowly.

assumptions.claim: Low-dose atropine 0.05% slows myopia progression to about -0.4 to -0.5 D per year in children.
The record lists atropine as the only comparator, with no placebo arm.

reason: Shingrix already produces a near-ceiling gE-specific CD4+ response rate, so superiority of an srRNA vaccine on this responder rate is very unlikely; a comparability message is the realistic best case.
rationale: Seven of the eight primaries are safety counts with no formal hypothesis; the only efficacy-like one is the CD4+ response rate versus Shingrix, which gives about 90% responders. An srRNA vaccine would need to exceed that ceiling for superiority, which is improbable. A vague statement of 'met primary objectives' on safety could count, so I allow a little probability.

assumptions.claim: Shingrix induces gE-specific CD4+ T-cell responses in roughly 90% or more of adults aged 50+ after two doses.
The registry lists seven safety primaries and one CD4+ response-rate primary with no stated hypothesis.

reason: Placebo response in Alzheimer's psychosis trials is large, and the elderly tolerate the cholinergic side effects of KarXT worse, so a mean difference of about 1.5 points may fall just short of significance.
rationale: KarXT (xanomeline-trospium) was strongly effective in schizophrenia, and muscarinic agonism has early signals in AD psychosis. But dementia psychosis trials have high placebo response and mixed success (pimavanserin, brexpiprazole). With 203 per arm and SD about 6.5, significance needs about 1.3 points. I put the chance near a coin flip. The trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026, so reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: KarXT cut PANSS total by about 9 points more than placebo in EMERGENT-2.
The record shows the trial still recruiting with primary completion registered for 2026-11-24.

reason: Anti-TL1A antibodies showed large clinical remission gains over placebo in phase 2 UC, so the week-12 induction primary should be met; residual risk is a higher placebo rate or a lower effective dose.
rationale: Anti-TL1A antibodies produced clinical remission of about 26% versus 1% placebo (tulisokibart ARTEMIS-UC), and afimkibart's own phase 2 (TUSCANY-2) was also strongly positive. With 175 per arm, a 15+ point gap is significant at p<0.001. Class and mechanism are validated in UC, so the phase 3 induction success rate is high. Risk is a higher placebo rate or dose-related shrinkage.

assumptions.claim: Tulisokibart gave about 26% clinical remission versus about 1% placebo at week 12 in UC.
The registry lists week-12 clinical remission by modified Mayo score as the primary outcome.

reason: Both co-primaries (week 12 and week 52 remission) must be met; week 12 is very likely, and week 52 in the treat-through design adds some risk, but anti-TL1A effects look durable.
rationale: Anti-TL1A antibodies showed about 25 points over placebo for week-12 remission in phase 2 UC, and maintenance data in phase 2 extensions held up. With 200 per arm, week 12 is very likely significant (about 93%), and week 52 treat-through is likely too (about 91% given week 12). Both are needed, so the joint probability is about 0.85. Roche will likely announce combined results.

assumptions.claim: Tulisokibart gave about 26% clinical remission versus about 1% placebo at week 12 in UC.
The registry lists clinical remission at week 12 and at week 52 as two primary outcomes in a treat-through design.

reason: Same total daily dose given once rather than twice may slightly lower mucosal contact; non-inferiority succeeds unless the once-daily regimen loses more than the unstated margin, with remission rates near 90% leaving little room.
rationale: Budesonide orodispersible tablet 1 mg BID gave about 93% histological remission at 6 weeks in EOS-1. A 2 mg once-daily regimen at the same dose is likely to perform similarly. With 154 per arm and rates near 90%, the SE of the difference is about 3.4 points, so non-inferiority with a 10-15 point margin is likely unless QD is truly worse by 4+ points. Margin is unstated, which adds uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: Budesonide orodispersible tablet 1 mg BID for 6 weeks gave histological remission in about 93% of patients.
The title states a non-inferiority design comparing 2 mg once daily with 1 mg twice daily.

reason: An anti-ELR+ chemokine antibody given alone has uncertain efficacy in UC and the dose-ranging arms are small, so a significant monotherapy-versus-placebo remission difference is unlikely.
rationale: Eltrekibart neutralises neutrophil-attracting chemokines; evidence of monotherapy efficacy in UC is limited and Lilly is testing it alongside mirikizumab, which suggests the combination is the main hope. Only about 30-48 patients per arm, a placebo remission rate near 6%, and a modest likely effect make significance at week 12 unlikely. Lilly usually posts phase 2 results on ClinicalTrials.gov around 12 months after primary completion.

assumptions.claim: Placebo clinical remission at week 12 in moderate-to-severe UC trials is typically 5-15%.
The record includes a mirikizumab combination arm alongside eltrekibart monotherapy and placebo.

reason: Pembrolizumab in CPS>=1 first-line HNSCC is a strong control (median OS about 12-14 months), and an OS primary needs many events; a report by mid-2027 would likely be an interim that Akeso only announces if positive.
rationale: Ivonescimab plus ligufalimab showed very high response rates in earlier first-line HNSCC data and PD-1/VEGF bispecifics have beaten pembrolizumab in PFS in lung. OS against pembrolizumab in CPS>=1 is a harder bar. If a result is public by June 2027 it is probably an early interim, which Akeso reports mainly when positive, so I lean to met.

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab monotherapy in CPS>=1 R/M HNSCC had median OS of about 12.3 months.
Akeso reported high ORR for AK112 plus AK117 in first-line PD-L1-positive HNSCC in phase 2.

reason: Small 12-week safety and pharmacodynamic phase 2a, already fully enrolled with an OLE; primary completion in March 2027 should hold, and Denali/Biogen rarely post results within five months of completion.
rationale: Enrolment is complete (active, not recruiting) and the double-blind period is only 12 weeks, so a delay beyond late June is unlikely. A sponsor-led safety study with a stable record is unlikely to change its primary outcome or stop.

reason: A target-engagement biomarker should move clearly with the highest E2814 dose, so the main risk is a small sample with several dose arms and assay variance, or a dose-response test that is not strictly significant.
rationale: E2814 binds the MTBR region of tau and earlier data (DIAN-TU, phase 1) showed lower CSF MTBR-tau243 on E2814. The primary is a biomarker mechanism readout, so success is likely if it reports. Eisai tends to present at AAIC (July) or CTAD (December), so a public result by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: E2814 lowers CSF MTBR-tau243, a tangle-associated tau species, in earlier studies.
assumptions.source: Eisai E2814 phase 1/2 and DIAN-TU data (AAIC/CTAD 2024)

reason: MEDI0618 (PAR2 antibody) has a novel, unproven migraine mechanism, tested in patients who have failed two or more preventives, where effects over placebo are small and placebo response is sizeable.
rationale: There is no clinical proof of concept for PAR2 blockade in migraine, and the population is treatment-resistant (at least two failed preventives), which lowers effect sizes even for CGRP drugs. A phase 2 with about 150 per arm is powered for roughly 1 day, so a modest true effect could miss. AbbVie rarely announces phase 2 outcomes quickly, and public results lean positive.

assumptions.claim: In difficult-to-treat migraine (LIBERTY), the placebo MMD change was about -0.2 and erenumab was about -1.6.
Placebo change in episodic migraine prevention trials is typically 1.5 to 3 monthly migraine days.

reason: Only about 90 patients with a 2:1 split and few hepatic progression events, so a real local-control benefit may still miss significance; the 6-month hepatic PFS of the control is also uncertain.
rationale: Hepatic delivery of melphalan in liver-dominant refractory colorectal cancer plausibly delays hepatic progression, and hepatic PFS in an open-label, non-crossover trial favours the liver-directed arm. Control TAS-102 plus bevacizumab has PFS near 5.6 months (SUNLIGHT). Small numbers make significance uncertain; the trial is still recruiting, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely and mostly a company update.
evidence: FOCUS/PHP colorectal liver metastases (Delcath earlier study)

assumptions.claim: Trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab gave median PFS of 5.6 months in refractory colorectal cancer.

reason: A patient-reported two-domain composite at week 24 in just 98 patients is noisy, and standard repair also recovers well; a PEG-fusion benefit on function may not separate from control at 24 weeks.
rationale: PEG fusion has mechanistic and earlier clinical rationale for faster functional return, but the primary is a subjective questionnaire at one time point with a small sample. The trial is still recruiting, so topline by June 2027 is unlikely; a private sponsor would announce mainly if positive.

assumptions.claim: NTX-001 is applied once at surgery alongside standard suture neurorrhaphy.

reason: The primary analysis is limited to the combined pre- and post-capillary subgroup, roughly 30 to 40 per arm, so only a sizeable PVR reduction would reach significance; the relaxin mechanism has not been proven in this population.
rationale: A relaxin-receptor agonist should vasodilate and lower PVR, but there is no prior patient proof. The CpcPH subgroup has perhaps 30 to 40 patients per arm; with SD near 1.6 Wood units, an effect of about 1 would give roughly 60 percent power. Two dose regimens help a little. Tectonic is a small public company and should report topline soon after database lock in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: Primary completion is registered for 24 November 2026, so topline falls in the first half of 2027.
PVR in CpcPH baseline is roughly 4 Wood units with SD of change of about 1.5.

reason: Sugemalimab is itself an effective consolidation drug (median PFS about 10 months by investigator), so showing superiority needs a clear added benefit from CTLA-4 co-blockade; the hazard ratio may land near 0.8.
rationale: Head-to-head against an active PD-L1 consolidation drug is a high bar, but Akeso chose the design and usually reports interim analyses promptly when they are positive, while a silent negative is not public. Cadonilimab adds CTLA-4 activity, which may help in PD-L1-low disease. Conditional on a public statement by June 2027, a positive claim is more likely than not.

assumptions.claim: Sugemalimab consolidation gave median investigator-assessed PFS of about 10.5 months after chemoradiotherapy.

reason: VX-993 missed efficacy in its acute pain phase 2, and beating pregabalin on NPRS (rather than just placebo) is a stringent test for a NaV1.8 inhibitor in a noisy phase 2 of about 100 per arm.
rationale: VX-993 did not separate from placebo in post-surgical pain phase 2, which lowers confidence in the NaV1.8 mechanism at this dose range. Pregabalin is an active comparator reducing NPRS by about 2 points at week 12, so superiority over it is unlikely. If the study hypothesis is vs placebo rather than pregabalin, the chance is somewhat higher, but still low.

assumptions.claim: Pregabalin reduces weekly average pain by roughly 2 NPRS points in painful DPN trials.
VX-993 did not show efficacy over placebo in acute pain phase 2.

reason: Enzalutamide in ARSi-naive mCRPC is a strong control (rPFS about 20 months or more), so the EZH2 add-on must deliver a hazard ratio near 0.75 or better to reach significance.
rationale: Mevrometostat plus enzalutamide gave rPFS of about 14 months versus about 4 to 6 in post-abiraterone phase 1b, a strong signal that supports an AR-pathway plus EZH2 combination. In ARSi-naive disease enzalutamide alone is strong, so the effect shrinks; with 900 patients and about 450 events the trial can detect HR 0.75. Reading by June 2027 would likely be driven by a positive event-driven analysis.

assumptions.claim: Placebo plus enzalutamide had median rPFS of about 22 months in first-line mCRPC (TALAPRO-2).
Mevrometostat plus enzalutamide reached rPFS of roughly 14 months in post-abiraterone mCRPC in phase 1b.

reason: About 100 patients and perhaps 20 to 25 DFS events leave little power for a personalised vaccine effect, and enrolment is still open, so a report by mid-2027 is unlikely and would probably be an interim.
rationale: Small adaptive phase 2 by a small sponsor. DFS includes PSA recurrence, so events accrue, but 100 patients give perhaps 22 events; a hazard ratio near 0.7 will not be significant. The record is still recruiting with 22-month follow-up, so a primary completion of Feb 2027 is not credible. Any early public result is likely selected for positivity.

assumptions.claim: The trial enrols about 100 men randomised 1:1 and follows them for about 22 months for DFS.
Biochemical recurrence within about 2 years after prostatectomy for high-risk disease is roughly 25 to 35% without adjuvant therapy.
assumptions.source: Published adjuvant radiotherapy series after radical prostatectomy (e.g. RADICALS-RT, 2020)

reason: Month-16 IRC-assessed CR/CRi may be too early for the combination to separate fully, but BTK-inhibitor monotherapy gives few CRs by then and Bcl-2 plus BTK combinations clearly raise CR/CRi.
rationale: Adding a Bcl-2 inhibitor to a BTK inhibitor roughly multiplies the CR/CRi rate: zanubrutinib alone gives about 5 to 10% CR/CRi, while venetoclax-BTKi combinations give 40 to 55% and sonrotoclax plus zanubrutinib phase 1/2 data were similar. A gap of 30 points or more with 47 per arm is very likely significant.
evidence: BGB-11417-101 sonrotoclax + zanubrutinib TN CLL cohort (ASH 2024)

assumptions.claim: Zanubrutinib monotherapy in untreated CLL gives a CR/CRi rate of only about 6 to 7% after about 2 years.
Fixed-duration BTK inhibitor plus Bcl-2 inhibitor combinations reach CR/CRi rates of about 40 to 55% in untreated CLL.

reason: IL-17A/F nanobody has strong ARGO phase 2 PsA data; the main risk is a lower effect in TNF-IR patients or an unusually strong placebo response, neither likely to erase a 25+ point gap.
rationale: IL-17A/F inhibition is validated in PsA, including after TNF failure (bimekizumab BE COMPLETE ACR50 43% vs 7% at week 16). Sonelokimab showed ACR50 around 50% vs about 10% placebo in ARGO phase 2. With 150 per arm in phase 3, success at 120 mg is nearly certain even if the effect is somewhat smaller in TNF-IR patients.

assumptions.claim: In TNF-inhibitor-inadequate-responder psoriatic arthritis, week-16 ACR50 was 43.4% with bimekizumab vs 6.8% with placebo.
Sonelokimab showed clearly higher ACR50 than placebo at week 12 in the ARGO phase 2 trial.

reason: Gepant prevention effects are modest and placebo response in a 5-day window is large; 241 per arm and averaging over five cycles give good power only if the effect is at least about 0.25 migraine days.
rationale: Rimegepant every other day was effective for episodic migraine prevention (about 0.8 fewer migraine days per month vs placebo), and perimenstrual migraine responds to short-term prophylaxis (frovatriptan, CGRP agents in post hoc data). With 241 per arm and a five-cycle average the trial is reasonably powered. The record still recruits, so primary completion will slip and a public result before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Croop 2021 Lancet (rimegepant every other day prevention, NCT03732638)

assumptions.claim: Rimegepant 75 mg every other day reduced monthly migraine days by about 4.3 vs 3.5 with placebo over weeks 9 to 12.
The record lists the trial as still recruiting with a registered primary completion of 2026-11-29.

reason: With 45 per arm a 20-point gap in response is borderline significant, and a cyclosporine arm held to week 76 could respond better than expected.
rationale: Anti-CD20 therapy beats cyclosporine in membranous nephropathy at long follow-up (MENTOR: remission 60% vs 20% at 24 months) because cyclosporine responses relapse after withdrawal. Zuberitamab is a glycoengineered anti-CD20 expected to behave like rituximab. At week 76 a response rate near 62% vs 38% is plausible, but 45 per arm makes significance only moderately likely. Reporting by June 2027 is unlikely for a single-site-listed Chinese phase 2.

assumptions.claim: Rituximab produced complete or partial remission in 60% vs 20% for cyclosporine at 24 months in membranous nephropathy.
The primary endpoint is the share with overall UPCR response at week 76 with about 45 patients per arm.

reason: Orforglipron produces about 10% weight loss at one year and AHI falls with weight, so a placebo-adjusted reduction near 10 events/hour with 178 per arm is very likely significant.
rationale: Tirzepatide at 17-18% weight loss cut AHI by about 20 events/hour vs placebo (SURMOUNT-OSA). Orforglipron gives about 10-12% placebo-adjusted weight loss at one year in ATTAIN-1, implying roughly 10 events/hour AHI difference. With about 178 per arm and SD about 22, that is z near 4. Lilly is a prompt reporter and the trial is already complete.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide reduced AHI by about 25 events/hour vs about 5 with placebo in adults with obesity and OSA not using PAP.
Orforglipron 36 mg produced mean weight loss of about 12% vs about 1% with placebo at 72 weeks.

reason: FcRn blockade removes IgG but the causal role of autoantibodies in skin fibrosis is unproven; a 58 vs 29 trial with a large placebo response in early disease detects only a sizeable effect on mRSS.
rationale: Proof-of-concept phase 2 in early SSc with no strong biological rationale that IgG depletion reduces skin thickening. Placebo mRSS change at 24 weeks in early diffuse disease is about -3, SD about 5.5, so significance needs a placebo-adjusted drop of about 2.7 points with 58 vs 29 patients. Readout is likely only after unblinding near week 48, so reporting by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: SENSCIS and other mRSS placebo response data

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated patients with early diffuse SSc improve by roughly 3 to 4 mRSS points over 24 to 48 weeks.
The trial randomises 2:1 with about 87 patients and mRSS change at week 24 as primary.

reason: An eye-drop with indirect anti-amyloid mechanism must slow GA growth by about 20% in only 55 per arm; even approved injectable complement inhibitors achieve 15 to 20% reductions.
rationale: Small phase 2 with 55 per arm and annual GA growth SD about 1 mm2, so a 20% slowing (about 0.35 mm2) is needed for significance. Topical delivery to the posterior retina is a concern and GA programmes mostly fail. The record is still recruiting with a 12 to 24 month treatment period, so the March 2027 primary completion will slip and results are unlikely before 2028.

assumptions.claim: Intravitreal complement inhibitors slowed GA lesion growth by roughly 14 to 28% over 12 months in phase 3.
assumptions.source: OAKS/DERBY, Heier et al., Lancet 2023; GATHER2, Khanna et al., Lancet 2023

assumptions.claim: Patients must have at least 12 months of treatment and the trial is still recruiting.

reason: 5-HT2C agonism (like fenfluramine) is validated in Dravet and bexicaserin gave about 50% median seizure reduction in phase 1b/2, but 48 per arm and a placebo response near -10 to -15% leave some chance of a miss.
rationale: Selective 5-HT2C agonist; fenfluramine in Dravet gave about 60% placebo-adjusted median reduction, and bexicaserin showed about 50% median reduction in the PACIFIC DEE study. With 48 per arm, a 30-point median difference is likely significant, but Dravet placebo variance is high and some DEE phase 3s have underperformed. The sponsor (Lundbeck) reports by company announcement, likely in Q1 to Q2 2027.

assumptions.claim: Fenfluramine 0.7 mg/kg/day reduced median monthly convulsive seizure frequency by about 62% vs about 1% with placebo in Dravet syndrome.
Cannabidiol in Dravet syndrome reduced convulsive seizures by 39% vs 17% on placebo.

reason: A multipotent MMP-inhibiting neuroprotectant added to thrombolysis in a trial sized for a roughly 10-point mRS 0-1 gain; neuroprotectants have almost always failed phase 3, and enrolment of 852 in Korea will probably run past March 2027.
rationale: Otaplimastat's earlier phase 2 in thrombolysed stroke was not clearly positive on its primary measure, and the NIHSS 8 or higher signal was exploratory. Neuroprotectant add-ons to thrombolysis (NXY-059, nerinetide ESCAPE-NEXT) have failed repeatedly. The 852-patient size implies an optimistic effect of about 10 points; a true effect of 3 to 5 points would be borderline. Reporting before mid-2027 is unlikely given the recruitment burden.
evidence: Otaplimastat (SP-8203) phase 2 RCT with rt-PA, Korea, 2023

assumptions.claim: Nerinetide, a neuroprotectant given with thrombolysis, did not improve 90-day mRS in ESCAPE-NEXT.
The phase 2 otaplimastat trial in thrombolysed stroke saw its benefit signal mainly in an exploratory NIHSS 8 or higher subgroup.

reason: DPP1 inhibition is validated by brensocatib, but its exacerbation benefit was modest (rate ratio about 0.8), so a 669-patient trial has only moderate power if HSK31858 is similar or a bit weaker, or the Chinese placebo rate is low.
rationale: Brensocatib (DPP1) cut exacerbations about 20% in ASPEN against a placebo rate near 1.3 per year, and HSK31858 is a second DPP1 inhibitor with positive earlier data. With 669 patients and 52-week follow-up, a rate ratio near 0.8 gives roughly 60 to 70% power. The registry still showed recruiting in October 2026, which suggests delay, so reporting by mid-2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In ASPEN, brensocatib 10 mg and 25 mg reduced the annualized exacerbation rate by about 19-21% against a placebo rate near 1.3 per year.
Entry requires at least 2 exacerbations in the previous 12 months, which enriches for a placebo rate above 1 per patient-year.

reason: Retatrutide has shown about 28% weight loss at 68 weeks against roughly 21% for tirzepatide at similar duration, so superiority is very likely; the risk is high retatrutide dropout from adverse events, or a lower retatrutide dose, narrowing the gap.
rationale: Retatrutide 12 mg produced 24% weight loss at 48 weeks in phase 2 and about 28.7% at 68 weeks in TRIUMPH-4, whereas tirzepatide reaches about 20-22% at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-5. With 400 per arm and a standard deviation near 8.5 points, a gap of 4 to 7 points is detected with very high power. Lilly reports retatrutide toplines quickly.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide 15 mg gave about 20.9% weight loss at 72 weeks (treatment-regimen estimand) in SURMOUNT-1.
Retatrutide 12 mg gave about 24.2% weight loss at 48 weeks in phase 2.

reason: Both co-primaries must be met: albuterol's 6-hour bronchodilation is near certain to show, but trough FEV1 after only 4 weeks depends on the inhaled steroid effect against the albuterol-only arm and is the weaker comparison.
rationale: A SABA/ICS combination trial built to show each component contributes. The albuterol effect on FEV1 AUEC0-6h is large (about 200 mL or more) and robust at 160 patients per arm. The trough FEV1 comparison needs a 4-week fluticasone effect over albuterol alone, probably around 80 to 150 mL, which is likely but not certain to be significant. Teva rarely press-releases such studies, so public timing is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Albuterol MDPI raises FEV1 AUEC0-6h by roughly 200 mL or more over placebo in asthma trials.
The record lists co-primaries of AUEC0-6h and week-4 trough FEV1 in four arms.

reason: Only 58 per arm and an open-label design; a fibrin-coated patch should achieve faster hemostasis than oxidized cellulose, but a smaller true gap or a strong Surgicel arm at 3 minutes would leave the trial short of significance.
rationale: TachoSil provides active fibrin sealing and tends to give faster hemostasis than passive oxidized regenerated cellulose, which is slow at 3 minutes. A true gap of about 20 points would be significant with 58 per arm (about 85% power), but the gap is uncertain and the surgeon is unblinded. The sponsor is private and the trial is still recruiting, so early public reporting is unlikely.
evidence: Surgicel Original oxidized cellulose hemostasis studies

assumptions.claim: Oxidized regenerated cellulose is a passive hemostat that often needs more than 3 minutes to control mild to moderate bleeding.
assumptions.source: Surgicel Original prescribing information and hemostat reviews

assumptions.claim: The record gives 3-minute hemostatic success as the single primary outcome with 116 participants.

reason: A bridging non-inferiority comparison with latanoprost; omidenepag was non-inferior to latanoprost in Japanese phase 3 (AYAME), so success is likely, but a 115-per-arm study could miss the margin if the Chinese effect is smaller, and results may not be made public soon.
rationale: Omidenepag isopropyl 0.002% met non-inferiority to latanoprost 0.005% on diurnal IOP at week 4 in the Japanese AYAME study, with a difference well inside 1.5 mmHg. A Chinese bridging cohort of about 115 per arm and a standard deviation near 2.8 mmHg gives high power for non-inferiority if the true gap is about 0.5 mmHg. Public reporting depends on Santen's disclosure habits.

assumptions.claim: Omidenepag isopropyl 0.002% was non-inferior to latanoprost 0.005% for diurnal IOP change at week 4 with a 1.5 mmHg margin.
The record has a randomized evaluator-masked latanoprost-controlled bridging cohort with week-4 mean diurnal IOP change as primary.

reason: Relugolix with add-back gave about 72% responders against 15 to 19% on placebo in LIBERTY, so a 2:1 trial of 120 should be clearly positive; the main uncertainty is whether Qilu makes the result public by mid-2027.
rationale: LIBERTY 1 and 2 showed relugolix combination therapy with 73% and 71% responders against 19% and 15% on placebo for the same MBL responder endpoint. Even a smaller effect of 40 points gives over 95% power with 80 versus 40 patients. Amenorrhea was also frequent on active treatment and rare on placebo, so the key secondary should follow. Qilu is private and seldom issues early press releases.

assumptions.claim: In LIBERTY 1 and 2, MBL responder rates were 73.4% and 71.2% with relugolix combination versus 18.9% and 14.7% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Al-Hendy et al., NEJM 2021, NCT03049735 and NCT03103087

assumptions.claim: The record randomizes 80 to relugolix with progestin add-back and 40 to placebo for 12 weeks.

reason: Anti-IL-5 antibodies raise FEV1 by only about 100 mL, and with roughly 75 patients per arm the 52-week FEV1 comparison is underpowered; two dose groups give some extra chance that one reaches significance.
rationale: Mepolizumab, reslizumab and benralizumab raise pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by around 100 to 160 mL against placebo, with FEV1 the weaker efficacy signal for anti-IL-5. With about 75 per arm and an FEV1 standard deviation near 380 to 450 mL, power per dose is only about 30 to 40%. Two dose arms and positive-result publication bias raise the chance of a reported success.

assumptions.claim: Mepolizumab 100 mg SC raised pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by about 98 mL over placebo in MENSA.
The record has two 610 dose groups plus placebo with about 75 per arm and FEV1 change at week 52 as primary.

reason: Small AstraZeneca phase 2 (24 of about 30 planned) with safety-only primaries and a 40-week open-label extension; primary completion Aug 2026 puts the 12-month results deadline just before the read date, so posting by 31 Aug 2027 is possible but not likely.
rationale: Enrollment closed at 24 patients, status active not recruiting. Results are due about 12 months after the Aug 2026 primary completion, and AstraZeneca usually posts near the deadline, so a posting by the read date is uncertain. The 12 safety primaries are stable, so changes are unlikely. Termination is unlikely for a fully enrolled study.

reason: Phase 2 showed a very large effect on AMR resolution, so failure would most likely come from a heavier chronic-active, scarred late-AMR mix and a higher placebo resolution rate than in the small phase 2.
rationale: Phase 2 (Mayer, NEJM 2024) in late AMR gave about 82% vs 20% histologic resolution at week 24, with clear effects on MVI, DSA and dd-cfDNA. The phase 3 has 66 per arm and the same week-24 biopsy endpoint, so even a halved effect (about 45 points) is highly powered. Residual risk is a regression in effect and placebo resolution higher than 20%.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial in late AMR, AMR resolved at week 24 in about 82% of felzartamab patients vs about 20% on placebo.
The phase 3 enrolls kidney transplant recipients at least 6 months post-transplant with biopsy-proven active or chronic active AMR and DSA, the same type of population as phase 2.

reason: Biosimilar pembrolizumab trials usually meet PK and ORR equivalence at n=726, but two primaries and a three-way PK comparison against EU and US reference leave some risk of missing a margin.
rationale: Two-primary biosimilar design (AUC bioequivalence vs EU and US Keytruda, and ORR equivalence at week 24). Pembrolizumab with pemetrexed-platinum gives an ORR of about 48% (KEYNOTE-189), and the sample is large enough for typical margins. The sponsor's earlier bevacizumab biosimilar succeeded. Risk is mainly PK variability across two comparators and an unclear public statement.

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum gives an ORR of about 48% in non-squamous NSCLC.

reason: The record still said recruiting in Oct 2026 although the registered completion (Nov 2026) is 181 days after the last dose, so the last vaccination and the date must move later; GSK posts results typically within about a year of completion.
rationale: Primary completion is the Day 181 visit of the last child. A recruiting status in late Oct 2026 means that visit falls in 2027, probably after Feb 2027, so the registered date is likely to slip. Results posting by Aug 2027 is unlikely if completion moves to mid-2027. Eight safety primaries, so a rewrite is uncommon.

reason: Functional dyspepsia placebo response is high and the stringent weekly 50% reduction in two symptoms may narrow the gap, but Chinese TCM phase 3 trials with 171 per arm usually report a positive primary.
rationale: Placebo-controlled TCM phase 3 in Rome IV PDS with 171 per arm; a 14-point gap (for example 42% vs 28%) gives roughly 80% power, and Chinese TCM pivotal trials are mostly reported positive. The registered completion looks unrealistic given recruiting in Oct 2026, and public reporting before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Chinese placebo-controlled TCM functional dyspepsia phase 3 trials, 2018-2023

assumptions.claim: Placebo responder rates in functional dyspepsia symptom-response trials are typically 25-40%.
assumptions.source: Pinto-Sanchez et al., Cochrane review of FD therapies, 2017

reason: The responder threshold is not defined in the record; with an untreated control that declines slowly, a gene therapy effect is likely to be large, but a strict threshold or n=45 could dilute it.
rationale: AAV-CYP4V2 gene therapy against an untreated control, 30 vs 15, with BCVA responders at week 52. Early AAV-CYP4V2 studies in China reported BCVA gains in a good share of treated eyes while untreated BCD eyes drift down slowly, so even a 30-40% responder gap is significant at this size. Risks are an undefined threshold and a small single-site sample.
evidence: AAV-CYP4V2 phase 1/2 studies in Bietti crystalline dystrophy, China 2022-2023

assumptions.claim: Untreated Bietti crystalline dystrophy eyes show slow BCVA decline, so few untreated eyes gain letters.
assumptions.source: Natural history studies of BCD, Ophthalmology 2019-2022

reason: Upadacitinib has a very large EASI 75 effect with TCS in adolescents and adults; only a small sample (about 50 per arm) or an unexpectedly strong placebo+TCS response could threaten significance.
rationale: In AD Up, EASI 75 at week 16 was about 65-77% on upadacitinib+TCS vs 26% on placebo+TCS, and pediatric dupilumab+TCS gave 70% vs 27%. A gap of about 40 points with 50 vs 49 patients is very well powered. Public reporting before mid-2027 is unlikely because primary completion is Jan 2027 and AbbVie usually posts about a year later.

assumptions.claim: In AD Up, EASI 75 at week 16 was about 65% (15 mg) and 77% (30 mg) with TCS vs about 26% for placebo+TCS.
assumptions.source: AD Up, Reich et al., Lancet 2021; NCT03568318

reason: Venous leg ulcer drug trials often fail to beat compression-based standard care; a 10-point gain is needed with 156 per arm, and standard care alone is not truly blinded.
rationale: Complete closure at week 16 vs standard care alone; 156 per arm gives about 70% power for 35% vs 22%. VLU adjunctive drug trials have a poor track record (for example HP802-247), and compression standard care heals 25-40%. The registered Dec 2026 completion is unrealistic for a study still recruiting in Oct 2026, so a mid-2027 readout is unlikely.
evidence: HP802-247 phase 3 venous leg ulcer trials, 2018
Cochrane review of compression for venous ulcers, 2012

assumptions.claim: Standard-care arms in 12-16 week venous leg ulcer trials show about 25-40% complete closure.
assumptions.source: O'Meara et al., Cochrane review of compression for venous leg ulcers, 2012

reason: A 24-week exacerbation endpoint with 129 per arm yields only about 50 events per arm, so a plausible 25-35% reduction from an anti-TSLP type antibody is unlikely to reach significance.
rationale: Phase 2 anti-TSLP-type antibody in COPD (tezepelumab COURSE showed about 37% fewer exacerbations overall, larger with eosinophils) tested over only 24 weeks. With a placebo rate near 1 per year, about 50-60 events per placebo arm leave power at 25% or lower for a rate ratio near 0.7. Phase 2 sponsor reporting is selective, so I allow some upward selection.

assumptions.claim: Placebo moderate or severe exacerbation rates in recent COPD biologic trials with an exacerbation history are about 1.0-1.3 per year.
assumptions.source: BOREAS and NOTUS dupilumab COPD trials, NEJM 2023-2024

reason: Completed two-dose phase 2 from a Chinese sponsor with a single stable primary outcome; no US registration obligation makes results posting unlikely.
rationale: Status is already completed. The sponsor is Chinese with 9 sites in China, so a CT.gov results posting is unlikely. The single primary (CRT change at week 12) has little reason to change.

reason: Only about 24 patients per arm and six doses; an unexpectedly weak gut-restricted phosphate transporter inhibitor effect or a large placebo response could leave the top dose short of significance.
rationale: Pan-phosphate transporter inhibition in the gut is a validated route (tenapanor lowered phosphate by about 1.5 mg/dL vs placebo). The top total daily dose of 375 mg should give a clear reduction, and with 24 per arm and SD near 1.7 a 1.4 mg/dL difference is about 2.8 SE. One of six regimens succeeding is enough. Small arms and private sponsors reporting late are the main caveats.

assumptions.claim: Tenapanor lowered serum phosphate by roughly 1.5 mg/dL more than placebo over 8 weeks in dialysis patients.
Placebo-treated dialysis patients show small phosphate changes of a few tenths of mg/dL over several weeks.

reason: A GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist against placebo in drug-naive type 2 diabetes with baseline HbA1c 7.5-11% should win by a wide margin; the only real risk is an unexpectedly weak molecule or odd handling of the analysis.
rationale: BGM0504 is a tirzepatide-like GLP-1/GIP dual agonist. Tirzepatide 10 mg cut HbA1c by about 1.9 points versus placebo in SURPASS-1 monotherapy. Even with a weaker molecule and Chinese baseline HbA1c near 8.5%, a 1.2+ point advantage over placebo is likely, and 69 patients per arm gives huge power at that size. Main uncertainty is only whether and when the sponsor reports.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide 10 mg lowered HbA1c by about 1.9 percentage points versus placebo at 40 weeks in diet-and-exercise-only type 2 diabetes.
Placebo arms in diet-and-exercise-only Chinese diabetes trials show small HbA1c falls (about 0.1 to 0.4 points).
assumptions.source: Ecnoglutide and mazdutide phase 3 monotherapy trials, 2023-2024

reason: Non-inferiority against semaglutide is likely if BGM0504 10 mg behaves like tirzepatide; failure would need the molecule to fall clearly short of semaglutide, which the margin of probably 0.3 points would catch.
rationale: Tirzepatide 10 mg beat semaglutide 1 mg by about 0.4 HbA1c points in SURPASS-2. BGM0504 is a similar dual agonist, and 179 per arm gives ample power for non-inferiority at a usual 0.3-0.4 margin. Open-label design adds little bias to a lab endpoint. Residual risk is a weaker-than-expected molecule in Chinese patients or a tighter margin.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide 10 mg lowered HbA1c about 0.4 points more than semaglutide 1 mg at 40 weeks.
Semaglutide 1 mg lowers HbA1c by roughly 1.7-1.9 points over about 30 weeks in Chinese patients on background metformin.

reason: A broad mixed DEE population with LGS and other syndromes, plus an unknown dose, could dilute the large effect seen in the small phase 2; otherwise the sample is large and the mechanism clinically precedented.
rationale: Bexicaserin (selective 5-HT2C agonist) showed a median seizure reduction of about 55% versus about 12% on placebo in the small PACIFIC phase 1b/2a. Serotonergic fenfluramine gave about 20 points placebo-adjusted in LGS. With 367 patients a 20-point median difference is well powered. Risk is shrinkage from phase 2 and heterogeneous DEE syndromes.

assumptions.claim: Bexicaserin showed a median countable motor seizure reduction of over 50% versus a small reduction on placebo in the PACIFIC study.
Fenfluramine 0.7 mg/kg gave about a 20-point greater median drop in drop seizures than placebo in LGS.

reason: Single-site, 40-participant phase 2 single-dose safety/PK study with safety primaries; still recruiting at its registered primary completion date, so dates likely slip, results are unlikely to be posted soon, and the vague primary outcomes could be tidied.

Six-patient ultra-rare pediatric study with safety primaries, run by a small cash-constrained sponsor; recruitment is closed but follow-up and the extension phase may push the registry date, and results posting within the window is unlikely.
Pegcetacoplan already slows GA growth by about 20%; with about 67 per arm, a new complement inhibitor would need to be clearly better than it to reach significance on a 56-week slope.
rationale: Active-controlled phase 2 against pegcetacoplan, the approved complement inhibitor that cuts square-root GA growth by about 20% at one year. Superiority over an active comparator in about 67 patients per arm with noisy two-point slopes is a low bar to clear unless BI 771716 is far more potent. No sponsor expectations are public, and BI rarely announces phase 2 toplines.

assumptions.claim: Monthly pegcetacoplan reduced GA lesion growth by roughly 20% versus sham at 12 to 24 months.
Square-root GA growth in untreated eyes is about 0.35-0.40 mm per year.

reason: Anti-TIGIT add-ons have failed to beat anti-PD-1 alone repeatedly (including gastric STAR-221); with 39 patients and two co-primaries that both must favour domvanalimab, a clear win is very unlikely.
rationale: Small randomized phase 2 with ORR and PFS as co-primaries and no stated formal test. TIGIT blockade added to PD-1 plus chemo has not improved outcomes in several phase 3 trials, and domvanalimab's gastric phase 3 was stopped for futility. With about 20 per arm only a huge ORR gain would be called met, and the sponsor may not report this substudy publicly before mid-2027.
evidence: STAR-221 domvanalimab gastric phase 3 futility stop (2025)
KEYNOTE-048 pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in head and neck cancer (2019)

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab plus platinum/5-FU gave an objective response rate near 36% in first-line recurrent or metastatic HNSCC.
Adding anti-TIGIT to anti-PD-1 did not improve survival in the SKYSCRAPER-01 lung cancer phase 3.

reason: Most novel-mechanism IPF phase 2 trials with about 75 patients per arm fail to show a significant FVC benefit at 28 weeks; the monthly IV antibody effect size is unknown and FVC is a noisy endpoint.
rationale: Phase 2 IPF trials need roughly a 70-90 mL FVC difference to reach significance with 75 per arm and an SD near 190 mL. A new IV antibody with an unproven antifibrotic mechanism has a modest chance; mechanisms with real efficacy (nerandomilast, admilparant) have shown such effects, but many others (bexotegrast, pamrevlumab) did not. Placebo decline over 28 weeks is about 100 mL.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated IPF patients lose roughly 100 mL of FVC over about 24-28 weeks.
assumptions.source: FIBRONEER-IPF and admilparant phase 2 placebo arms, 2024-2025

assumptions.claim: Phase 2 IPF trials with about 75 patients per arm have had mixed results, with several novel mechanisms missing the FVC primary.

reason: All four primary immunogenicity criteria (three-lot consistency and non-inferiority to Varivax on seroresponse and GMC) must pass; the likeliest miss is a GMC ratio against Varivax or one lot pair falling outside the margin.
rationale: GSK's new varicella vaccine is an Oka-strain product, and prior phase 2 data supported progression. Healthy toddlers respond near-universally, so seroresponse non-inferiority is easy; lot consistency with about 400 per lot usually succeeds. The risk is a GMC ratio against Varivax or one of the lot pairs missing a 0.67-1.5 margin, as all primaries must succeed. GSK's phase 3 consistency record is generally strong.
evidence: GSK Priorix US phase 3 lot-to-lot consistency vs M-M-R II (2012-2013)

assumptions.claim: Seroresponse after one dose of licensed varicella vaccine in 12-15 month olds is typically above 90%.
Standard lot-to-lot consistency criteria require the two-sided 95% CI of the GMC ratio between any two lots to fall within 0.67-1.5.
assumptions.source: WHO/EMA guidance on vaccine lot consistency

reason: Single-arm ViiV PK study, already past registered primary completion and active not recruiting. Primary window runs to Month 25, so the date may be revised; ViiV usually posts results only near the 12-month deadline and a stop is unlikely.
Patients are already stable on optimised maintenance IVIg, so beating it on grip strength is hard; the likely outcome is comparable efficacy rather than clear superiority.
rationale: Head-to-head against active IVIg in IVIg-responsive MMN patients with a record that states no superiority or non-inferiority hypothesis. The phase 2 showed empasiprubart reduced IVIg need and maintained grip strength, and the 4-week averaging may capture IVIg wearing-off. Superiority over optimised IVIg is still a high bar, though argenx would not run 154 patients without confidence. Primary completion was 2026-09, so topline is likely within months.

assumptions.claim: Phase 2 empasiprubart in IVIg-treated MMN patients reduced IVIg need and maintained or improved grip strength versus placebo.
Registered primary completion is 2026-09, with week 24 grip strength as the primary endpoint.

reason: Single-site Chinese open-label phase 2 dose-exploration trial from Henlius, with descriptive ORR and PFS primaries. Henlius rarely posts phase 2 results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and the trial is still recruiting, so the dates will probably slip. A stop is unlikely, though HCC could be deprioritised behind other HLX43 indications.

TSLP blockade reliably lowers FeNO, so the biomarker primary should be met. The main risk is that disclosure is only called positive without a statement on the primary endpoint, or that the model-based dose analysis is reported differently.
rationale: Anti-TSLP antibodies cut FeNO by roughly half versus placebo (tezepelumab PATH and NAVIGATOR), and a long-acting TSLP antibody at the highest dose should do the same. FeNO is a sensitive pharmacodynamic endpoint with about 60 or more patients per arm, so power is high. Uncertainty is mostly about how and when GSK discloses, not about efficacy.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab produced a large placebo-adjusted reduction in FeNO in phase 2b and phase 3 asthma trials.
Part A primary completion is registered as 2026-07-14, with results due on ClinicalTrials.gov about 12 months later.

reason: Only 65 patients per arm against an active control (step-up to high-dose ICS-LABA) with an eosinophil floor of 150, so a plausible rate ratio of about 0.65 gives only modest power.
rationale: Benralizumab cut exacerbations by 28 to 51 percent versus placebo on high-dose ICS-LABA in SIROCCO and CALIMA, mostly at eosinophils of 300 or more. Here the comparator also gets a step-up to high-dose ICS-LABA, the eosinophil floor is 150, and the study has about 85 events, so power is roughly 40 to 60 percent. The completed study is small but the sponsor chose this head-to-head.

assumptions.claim: Benralizumab Q8W reduced annualised exacerbation rate by 28 to 51 percent versus placebo on high-dose ICS-LABA in patients with eosinophils of 300 or more.
The record shows 130 patients enrolled and status completed with primary completion 2026-09-21.

reason: Large 808-patient biosimilar equivalence trial with ORR around 50 percent is well powered for usual margins. The main risk is a chance miss of the ORR margin or a stricter protocol margin, and results are also unlikely to be public by mid-2027.
rationale: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed and platinum gives about 50 percent ORR in non-squamous NSCLC. With about 400 patients per arm the 90 percent interval on the ORR ratio is roughly plus or minus 0.16, which fits typical 0.8 to 1.25 or plus or minus 13 percent margins. Biosimilar equivalence trials usually succeed. Recruitment is still open and 24-week follow-up is needed, so timing is the real uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed and platinum gave an ORR of about 48 percent in first-line non-squamous NSCLC.
The registry lists primary completion 2026-12 and status still recruiting.

reason: Congenital hypothalamic obesity may respond less than acquired hypothalamic obesity, and with 39 patients including growing children an attenuated effect or high variance could miss significance.
rationale: Setmelanotide produced about a 20 percentage-point BMI difference versus placebo in acquired hypothalamic obesity (TRANSCEND). The same MC4R pathway rationale applies to congenital hypothalamic dysfunction. With 39 patients and an SD near 8 percent, even half the acquired-HO effect would be significant. Risk comes from population heterogeneity, growth in children, and small numbers. Timing depends on recruiting a rare population.

assumptions.claim: In acquired hypothalamic obesity, setmelanotide gave a large placebo-adjusted BMI reduction at 16 weeks (about 19.8 percentage points).
Registered primary completion is 2027-03-13 and status is recruiting, with 39 planned patients.

reason: Small biotech single-arm two-stage pivotal phase 2 enrolling 120 brain-metastases patients at 12 US sites, with a 12-month IC-ORR window. The registered completion of January 2027 looks unrealistic, so the date will probably slip. Some risk of sponsor stop or primary tweaks after the stage 1 review.
PFS is very likely positive, but OS is a co-primary and will be immature at the PFS analysis, so the sponsor may not be able to say all primary objectives were met by the deadline.
rationale: Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy has shown strong effects (HARMONi-A HR about 0.46, HARMONi-2 HR about 0.51) and strong phase 2 TNBC activity. The placebo plus nab-paclitaxel control in Chinese TNBC has had median PFS of about 5.5 to 6 months (TORCHLIGHT, IMpassion130). PFS success is likely (about 85 percent); discounting for the OS co-primary and for how Akeso words an interim statement gives about 0.65.

assumptions.claim: Placebo plus nab-paclitaxel had a median PFS of about 5.5 to 5.6 months in first-line TNBC trials.
Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy reduced the PFS hazard ratio to about 0.46 to 0.51 in NSCLC phase 3 trials.
The record lists PFS by IRRC and OS as dual primary outcomes with registered primary completion 2026-12.

reason: Geographic atrophy phase 2 programmes have a poor hit rate, particularly for novel mechanisms, and about 38 patients per dose group over 50 weeks gives limited power unless the effect is 20 to 25 percent or more.
