rationale: Dose-finding phase 2 with three doses against placebo in geographic atrophy, 50 weeks, FAF square-root growth. Complement inhibitors have shown effects of about 20 to 30 percent, but many phase 2 agents have failed. A 25 percent effect would give about 0.08 mm per year with an SD near 0.14, which is detectable. With several doses, one significant dose suffices, but the prior that a novel mechanism works is modest. Public disclosure is more likely after a positive result.

assumptions.claim: Sham or placebo arms in recent GA phase 2 trials show square-root GA area growth of about 0.3 mm per year.
The registry lists three dose groups plus placebo, with primary completion 2026-12-22.

reason: Only 14 subjects in a single-centre crossover with EEG-counted absence seizures, which vary a lot between 72-hour recordings; a real T-type-like effect could show, but chance noise is large and the higher-dose subset may be small.
rationale: Small proof-of-concept crossover (n=14, two doses) with a high-variance EEG endpoint. A mechanism-driven drug could cut absence seizures by 40-60% against a near-flat placebo, which would reach significance even in 14 subjects, but unknown mechanism and a split across two doses make a clear win about a coin flip. A private sponsor reports mainly when positive.
evidence: Ethosuximide vs valproate vs lamotrigine childhood absence epilepsy trial (Glauser 2010)
Ezogabine/XEN1101 photoparoxysmal EEG response studies (EEG-based proof-of-concept design)

assumptions.claim: Placebo effect on EEG-recorded absence seizure burden is small, near zero on average.
assumptions.source: Glauser et al., NEJM 2010 (CAE trial) and EEG-based placebo-controlled absence studies

assumptions.claim: The record lists a single-centre, 14-subject double-blind crossover with a 14-day washout and two NPT 2042 doses.

reason: Add-on dapagliflozin lowers HbA1c about 0.5-0.8 points over rosuvastatin alone and rosuvastatin cuts LDL-C about 40-50% over dapagliflozin; the factorial FDC design is very likely to win both co-primaries. Residual risk is a recruitment-driven delay or no public report.
rationale: Both components have well-known effects: dapagliflozin on metformin background gives about -0.5 to -0.8 HbA1c versus placebo, and rosuvastatin gives about -45% LDL-C versus a non-statin arm. With 80 per arm and HbA1c SD near 0.9 the HbA1c comparison has high power, and the LDL-C comparison is near-certain. Korean FDC registration trials almost always meet endpoints.
evidence: Bailey 2010 dapagliflozin add-on to metformin, Lancet
Korean dapagliflozin plus statin or metformin FDC phase 3 trials (2020-2024)

assumptions.claim: Dapagliflozin 10 mg added to metformin lowered HbA1c by about 0.5-0.8 points more than placebo at 24 weeks.
Rosuvastatin 10-20 mg lowers LDL-C by roughly 45-52%.
assumptions.source: STELLAR trial, Jones et al., Am J Cardiol 2003

reason: A 62-patient, 28-week study of an antibody in early Parkinson's on levodopa has little power for the MDS-UPDRS (SE about 2.3 points), and no disease-modifying PD drug has shown a clear symptomatic gain of that size in a trial this size.
rationale: TB006 is an anti-galectin-3 antibody with no proven clinical effect in Parkinson's. Early-stage patients on levodopa progress slowly, 28 weeks is short, and with 31 per arm only a gain near 5 MDS-UPDRS points would reach significance. Prior disease-modifying PD trials mostly failed. A private sponsor tends to report only if positive, so I raise the figure a little given public.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated early PD patients worsen by only about 1-4 MDS-UPDRS total points over 6-12 months.
The registry lists a placebo-controlled phase 2a of TB006 with 62 participants and 28-week primary timing.

reason: A potent long-acting GLP-1 agonist against placebo in drug-naive Chinese T2DM at 44 weeks should lower HbA1c by well over a point more than placebo; failure would need an unusual design or analysis problem.
rationale: GLP-1 receptor agonists versus placebo in diet-and-exercise T2DM routinely reduce HbA1c by 1.3-2.0 points more than placebo (semaglutide SUSTAIN 1, Chinese semaglutide monotherapy data). GZR18 (bofanglutide) showed large HbA1c and weight reductions in phase 2. With about 137 per arm and SD near 1.0, power is essentially complete. The only real uncertainty is whether and when the sponsor reports.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide monotherapy versus placebo in drug-naive T2DM lowered HbA1c by about 1.4-1.5 points more at 30 weeks.
assumptions.source: SUSTAIN 1, Sorli et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2017

assumptions.claim: The record lists a placebo-controlled phase 3 of GZR18 with HbA1c change at week 44 as primary.

reason: The head-to-head against semaglutide most likely meets non-inferiority, but if it is strictly a superiority test the margin over semaglutide is small (about 0.2-0.3 points) and could fall short.
rationale: With 550 per arm the study is powered for a small HbA1c difference. Semaglutide 1 mg gives about -1.8 in Chinese metformin-treated T2DM; GZR18 high dose showed larger reductions in phase 2, so a 0.2-0.3 point edge is plausible. Non-inferiority is very likely and strict superiority perhaps 50-55%. The design is likely non-inferiority with superiority testing after it, which lifts the odds of reporting a met objective.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide 1 mg lowers HbA1c by about 1.7-1.9 points from a baseline near 8.1-8.5 in Chinese T2DM.
The record lists semaglutide as the only comparator with 1100 planned patients and HbA1c change at week 44 as primary.

reason: The 2a stage has only about 26 per arm, response requires a clear GC taper, and an any-time responder endpoint admits placebo responders; a genuine JAK-driven effect could still separate, but the margin for significance is thin.
rationale: Open-label JAK inhibition (ruxolitinib) in VEXAS gave frequent responses, and pacritinib (JAK2/IRAK1) has a plausible rationale. But blinded placebo-controlled VEXAS data are absent, the 2a arms hold about 26 each, and the response needs a GC taper. With placebo about 15% a sponsor-reported significant result needs a 30 point gap. Reporting before mid-2027 would likely be a positive dose-selection announcement.

assumptions.claim: The registry describes about 26 patients per arm in phase 2a and a later 2:1 phase 2b, with primary completion registered as 2026-12-30 for the whole trial.
Ruxolitinib produced clinical responses in a majority of VEXAS patients in open-label series.

reason: Only about 110 exacerbations are expected in 24 weeks across 256 patients, so even a 25-30% true rate reduction is detected less than a third of the time; the population is not enriched by eosinophils or type 2 markers.
rationale: A 24-week exacerbation endpoint in phase 2 is underpowered: at about 1 event per patient-year, 128 per arm yields roughly 55 events each. Biologics in unselected COPD have had mixed results (itepekimab AERIFY, tozorakimab), and the sponsor rarely issues phase 2 press releases. Primary completion is March 2027, so a report before June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Unselected moderate-to-severe COPD placebo arms have about 0.8-1.3 moderate-to-severe exacerbations per patient-year.
assumptions.source: AERIFY-1/2 and BOREAS trial placebo arms

assumptions.claim: The registry lists a 256-patient placebo-controlled phase 2 with AECOPD rate over 24 weeks as primary and primary completion on 2027-03-17.

reason: Phase 2b showed a large responder gap (about 70% vs 25%), but it was a 36-patient study and phase 3 effects shrink; with 64 per arm a placebo rate near 35% would need a gap of 20 points to be significant.
rationale: Descartes-08 (mRNA CAR-T, no lymphodepletion) in phase 2b gave MG-ADL responder rates of about 70% vs 25% on placebo, with durable benefit to month 4+. Phase 3 MG trials of FcRn blockers and complement inhibitors were mostly positive on MG-ADL, but a cell therapy study with a placebo infusion and 128 patients has real shrinkage and placebo-response risk. Cartesian is public and the primary completion of 2026-12-30 makes topline likely in H1 2027.
evidence: Descartes-08 phase 2b MG (Granit 2023, Lancet Neurol; Cartesian 2024)

assumptions.claim: Phase 2b Descartes-08 in gMG reported MG-ADL responder rates of about 70% versus about 25% on placebo.
assumptions.source: Cartesian Therapeutics phase 2b results 2024; Granit et al., 2023

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in gMG phase 3 trials typically show 25-45% MG-ADL responders (varying by threshold).
assumptions.source: ADAPT, Howard et al., Lancet Neurol 2021

reason: The 3-6 mg QLM1016 arm is compared with active aripiprazole; if the design is superiority over a good active comparator it likely fails, but a Chinese active-controlled trial is usually a non-inferiority design that would pass.
rationale: Active-controlled 6-week PANSS trial in China with 201 per arm and a PANSS change SD near 19. The record gives no hypothesis or margin. Chinese head-to-head antipsychotic trials are mostly non-inferiority, where a likely cariprazine-like agent at 3-6 mg would meet the margin. If superiority was intended, aripiprazole 10-20 mg is a strong comparator and success is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Aripiprazole 10-20 mg lowers PANSS total by roughly 20-25 points over 6 weeks in acute schizophrenia.
assumptions.source: Aripiprazole registration trials in acute schizophrenia (Kane 2002, PMID 12069698)

assumptions.claim: Cariprazine 3-6 mg reduced PANSS total by about 20-23 points at week 6 in phase 3.

reason: With 135 patients and a TKV percent-change SD near 8, a vasopressin V2-type effect of about 3 points gives only around 55 percent power, and MRI measurement noise adds more.
rationale: The exclusions (tolvaptan, thirst, fluid intake) point to a V2 antagonist. Tolvaptan cut TKV growth by about 3 points in year 1 in TEMPO 3:4. In a rapidly progressive population the effect may be somewhat larger, but 68 per arm with an SD near 8 gives SE near 1.4. Chance of significance is about 50-55 percent. It is still recruiting, so results are unlikely before mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Tolvaptan reduced annual TKV growth from about 5.5 to 2.8 percent in TEMPO 3:4.
Placebo TKV growth in rapidly progressive ADPKD is about 5-8 percent per year.

reason: A 45-per-arm phase 2a in agitation with a novel mechanism and the usual large placebo response in hospitalised patients has little power to show a CMAI difference.
rationale: Phase 2a with 45 per arm, a CMAI change SD near 15 and a hospitalised setting with a strong placebo response. A significant difference needs about 5 CMAI points, which is large for an unproven mechanism. Agitation trials often fail on the primary, and Ono does not usually publicise phase 2a results quickly.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in Alzheimer's agitation trials improve by roughly 5-10 CMAI points over 6-12 weeks.
The study is a 90-patient phase 2a in Japan with CMAI as the efficacy primary.

reason: Icotrokinra showed a 28-point ACR20 gain at week 16 in the phase 2 ANTHEM-PsA trial, and 375 per arm gives overwhelming power; the only plausible miss is a dilution from biologic-experienced patients.
rationale: Phase 2 ANTHEM-PsA gave ACR20 of about 66 percent versus 38 percent at week 16 for the 100 mg BID dose. IL-23 pathway drugs reach about 60 percent versus 30 percent in phase 3. With 375 per arm the primary is nearly certain. Biologic-experienced patients dilute the effect slightly. Timing depends on a primary completion near Feb 2027 and J&J topline communication.

assumptions.claim: Icotrokinra 100 mg BID achieved ACR20 at week 16 in about 66 percent versus about 38 percent on placebo in phase 2.
Placebo ACR20 at week 16 in PsA phase 3 trials is about 20-35 percent.

reason: A safety-primary phase 2 dose-finding study in rare idiopathic hypersomnia that is still recruiting a month before the registered completion, so a slip beyond February 2027 is close to a coin flip; Takeda usually posts results within about a year.
Endothelin A antagonists reliably cut proteinuria by 35-45 percent in IgAN, so the 36-week primary should be met in 360 patients; the main uncertainty is whether the result is announced by June 2027.
rationale: SC0062 is a selective endothelin A antagonist. Atrasentan (ALIGN) cut UPCR 36 percent versus placebo at week 36 and sparsentan (PROTECT) about 40 percent. Phase 2 of SC0062 showed similar proteinuria reduction. A 360-patient phase 3 with a robust biomarker primary is very likely to be met. The 108-week eGFR secondary will not be known at the 36-week analysis.

assumptions.claim: Atrasentan reduced 24-hour UPCR by 36 percent relative to placebo at week 36 in IgAN.
Sparsentan reduced proteinuria by about 50 percent versus 15 percent at week 36 in IgAN.

reason: An oral GLP-1 agonist over 36 weeks in 225 patients should clearly beat placebo on weight; the risk is a low dose arm or limited weight loss in HFpEF, not significance.
rationale: HRS-7535 is an oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist that produced clear weight loss in Chinese phase 2 obesity trials. Even a 4-5 point difference in percent weight change is significant with about 110 per arm and an SD near 5. HFpEF patients lose slightly less weight. It is still recruiting, so results before mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonists give about 8-12 percent weight loss over 26-36 weeks in obesity phase 2.
Semaglutide gave about 13 percent weight loss versus 2.6 percent on placebo in HFpEF with obesity at 52 weeks.

reason: Ruxolitinib cream beat vehicle by about 30 points on EASI75 in earlier TRuE-AD trials, so 80 per arm is enough; the only real risk is a high vehicle response in a moderate-AD paediatric cohort.
rationale: TRuE-AD1/2/3 gave week 8 EASI75 around 55-62 percent on 1.5 percent ruxolitinib cream versus about 25 percent on vehicle. A paediatric moderate-AD phase 3b with about 80 per arm has high power for a 30-point difference. Vehicle response in children can run higher, which is the main risk.

assumptions.claim: Ruxolitinib 1.5 percent cream gave EASI75 at week 8 of about 62 percent versus about 24 percent on vehicle in adolescents and adults.
Ruxolitinib cream in children aged 2-11 gave IGA treatment success of about 45-51 percent versus about 15 percent on vehicle.

reason: The weight primary is near certain for an amylin-type agonist, but the co-primary WOMAC pain endpoint must also be met and knee OA pain trials carry large placebo responses.
rationale: KBP-336 is a long-acting dual amylin-calcitonin receptor agonist, with weight loss likely 6-12 percent at 26 weeks. Semaglutide STEP 9 showed that weight loss in obese knee OA also reduces WOMAC pain significantly. With 300 per arm the pain co-primary is likely to be met, but it adds risk, and both must pass. The trial is still recruiting, so timing is later.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide 2.4 mg lowered WOMAC pain by about 14 points more than placebo (0-100 scale) in obese knee OA at 68 weeks.
Amylin analogue cagrilintide gave about 10 percent weight loss at 26 weeks in obesity phase 2.

reason: A fully enrolled Sanofi vaccine safety and immunogenicity trial with a firm completion date, descriptive immunogenicity outcomes and a standard posting cadence of around a year after primary completion.
With about 60 patients per arm and Day-14 mortality near 12%, a superiority win over meropenem is very unlikely; any claim would rest on comparability.
rationale: Phase 2, single-site, 120 patients, active-controlled on Day-14 all-cause mortality. Meropenem arms in HABP/VABP run about 12% mortality, so the standard error of the difference is about 6 points and superiority cannot be shown unless the drug is far better. The record states no margin; a non-inferiority claim is possible but unlikely to be clearly labelled. Hengrui seldom announces phase 2 antibacterial results or posts on ClinicalTrials.gov.

assumptions.claim: Day-14 all-cause mortality with meropenem in HABP/VABP was about 12%.

reason: Plasma kallikrein-class prophylaxis effects in HAE are large against placebo; the main risk is an unexpectedly weak low dose arm or high placebo response, not the primary.
rationale: Navenibart (anti-factor XIIa) showed about 90% attack-rate reduction from baseline in the phase 1b/2 ALPHA-STAR with dosing every 3 or 6 months. HAE prophylaxis phase 3 trials (lanadelumab, garadacimab, donidalorsen) all beat placebo by 80-90% with p well under 0.001, and 157 patients is adequate. Sponsor guided topline for early 2027, after primary completion in December 2026.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arm mean attack rate in the lanadelumab HELP study was 1.97 per month.
Navenibart cut monthly attack rate by about 90% in ALPHA-STAR.

reason: Functional biliary and dyspeptic pain shows large placebo responses on VAS; a modest dose effect may not separate from placebo at 100 per arm.
rationale: Placebo-controlled phase 2 from a Russian sponsor, 300 patients over several doses, VAS pain at day 29 with baseline at least 40 mm. Placebo responses in biliary dyskinesia and functional dyspepsia are large (about 20 mm), and the effect of a symptomatic drug is typically 5-8 mm with SD near 20. Reported results from such sponsors skew positive, and one dose suffices.

assumptions.claim: Placebo response in functional GI pain trials on VAS is often 20 mm or more at 4 weeks.

reason: Orexin-2 agonist should lower ESS at the top dose; with only about 30 patients per arm and a noisy self-rated scale the margin is not huge.
rationale: ALKS 2680 (alixorexton) was clearly positive on wakefulness and ESS in the narcolepsy phase 2 studies Vibrance-1 and -2. IH has normal orexin levels but patients respond to wake-promoting drugs, and the top dose of a three-dose range only has to beat placebo. Arms are small (about 30), ESS is noisy and placebo response in IH is sizable, so some failure risk remains. Sponsor likely reports topline early 2027.

assumptions.claim: ALKS 2680 produced statistically significant ESS improvements at higher doses in narcolepsy type 2.

reason: Adjunctive psychiatric phase 2 trials often miss on HAM-A because of high placebo response and a modest drug-placebo gap.
rationale: Novel adjunctive agent in inadequate responders with GAD; HAM-A placebo change at week 6 is typically 9-11 points and true drug effects are 2-3 points at best, so a 210 vs 105 trial has marginal power. Phase 2 psychiatry success rates are low. The record still shows recruiting, so primary completion is likely to slip and AbbVie rarely issues press releases for phase 2.
evidence: Adjunctive GAD trials (e.g. quetiapine XR add-on, 2010)

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in GAD trials typically improve 9-11 HAM-A points over 6-8 weeks.
assumptions.source: GAD pharmacotherapy meta-analyses (Cochrane, Cipriani 2018 network meta-analysis of antidepressants/anxiolytics)

reason: A potent URAT1 inhibitor against placebo on serum urate below 6 mg/dL is near-certain to win; the only uncertainty is the size of the gap.
rationale: AR882 (pozdeutinurad) lowered serum urate to below 6 mg/dL in most patients at 75 mg in phase 2, and URAT1 inhibitors reliably separate from placebo on this surrogate endpoint with 289 patients per arm. Placebo response is single-digit unless background ULT is continued. The trial has completed, so the sponsor is likely to announce topline in the next few months.

assumptions.claim: In the AR882 phase 2b, most patients on 75 mg reached serum urate below 6 mg/dL.
assumptions.source: Arthrosi phase 2b results presented at EULAR/ACR 2023

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in URAT1 monotherapy gout trials reach sUA <6 mg/dL in under 10% of patients.

reason: Biosimilar PK equivalence in patients usually succeeds; risk is AUC variability and the need to hit margins versus both EU and US reference.
rationale: A three-arm biosimilar PK study (CYB704, EU and US Ocrevus) with AUC ratios against standard 80-125% margins. Well-characterized IgG1 biosimilars nearly always show PK similarity once manufacturing comparability is established. All comparisons (EU and US, two intervals) must pass, which lowers the chance slightly. Sandoz usually discloses biosimilar results only at filing or congress.
evidence: Biosimilar rituximab PK equivalence trials in RA (CT-P10, 2016)

assumptions.claim: Ocrelizumab is an IgG1 anti-CD20 antibody given every 24 weeks, so a six-month AUC window covers the first full cycle.

reason: Histologic response to acid suppression in EoE is about 40-50% against single-digit placebo, so only a weak P-CAB effect would sink it.
rationale: PPIs bring about half of EoE patients below 15 eos/hpf in meta-analyses, with placebo near 5-10%. Vonoprazan gives more potent and durable acid suppression and is expected to match or exceed this. With 48 vs 47 patients, even a 25-point gap is significant. Phathom is a small public company, so topline will be announced soon after primary completion.
evidence: Lucendo meta-analysis of PPIs in EoE, Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2016

assumptions.claim: About 50% of EoE patients on PPI achieve histologic response (<15 eos/hpf).
assumptions.source: Lucendo et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2016 meta-analysis

assumptions.claim: Placebo histologic response in EoE trials is typically under 10%.
assumptions.source: Dellon NEJM 2022 dupilumab phase 3 (placebo remission 2% for <=6 eos/hpf)

reason: A Topo1-payload ADC against single-agent chemo in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer is likely to win on PFS; the real uncertainty is whether any result is public by mid-2027.
rationale: HS-20089 (B7-H4 ADC, Topo1 payload, partnered with GSK) showed high response rates in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in China phase 1/2. Single-agent chemo gives median PFS near 3.5-4 months, so an HR around 0.5 is plausible, as with mirvetuximab (HR 0.65) and other ADCs. The trial is still recruiting, primary completion is likely to slip, and Hansoh rarely posts results.

assumptions.claim: Chemotherapy arm median PFS in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer was about 4 months in MIRASOL.
Single-agent chemotherapy gave median PFS of about 3.4 months in AURELIA.

reason: A single Ixo-vec injection must stay within the non-inferiority margin of aflibercept on BCVA; phase 2 LUNA supports this, but the margin is unstated and the gene therapy could fall slightly short.
rationale: Non-inferiority in BCVA (likely 4-5 letter margin) with about 155 per arm and SD near 11 letters gives high power if the true difference is near zero. Phase 2 LUNA showed BCVA maintained against aflibercept with about 80 percent fewer injections, and supplemental aflibercept rescue protects vision. Risks are a slight negative drift in a broad treated population and unknown margin. Lilly now owns Adverum, so disclosure timing is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Ixo-vec 6e10 vg/eye maintained BCVA versus aflibercept in the phase 2 LUNA study with a large reduction in injections.
Aflibercept 2 mg every 8 weeks controls gave a mean BCVA gain of roughly 5-6 letters in treatment-naive pivotal trials, less in treatment-experienced populations.

reason: Highest dose of a six-monthly RAAS-pathway agent versus saline should clearly lower 24-hour SBP; failure would need an unexpectedly weak molecule or high placebo response.
rationale: QCZ484 is a six-monthly subcutaneous antihypertensive; the closest precedent is zilebesiran (angiotensinogen siRNA), which lowered 24-hour ambulatory SBP by about 10-16 mmHg versus placebo at month 3 in KARDIA-1. With roughly 70-100 patients per arm and SD near 9 mmHg, the highest dose should clear significance easily. Placebo ABPM response is typically a few mmHg. Main uncertainty is disclosure timing by Novartis for a phase 2b.

assumptions.claim: Zilebesiran 300 mg every 6 months reduced 24-hour ambulatory SBP at month 3 by about 10 mmHg or more versus placebo.
Placebo arms in ABPM hypertension trials change by a few mmHg over 3 months.

reason: Efficacy failure is very unlikely given phase 2 weight loss of 16-20 percent at 52 weeks; the only real risk is tolerability-driven dropout shrinking the treatment-regimen effect.
rationale: Phase 2 maridebart cafraglutide gave about 16 percent weight loss (treatment-regimen) and about 20 percent (efficacy estimand) at 52 weeks versus roughly 2.5 percent on placebo. A 72-week phase 3 with dose escalation and 1900 per arm will be overwhelmingly significant. Effect size is the uncertainty: estimand choice, tolerability dropouts and the 72-week plateau. Timing: last visits January 2027, so topline likely April to June 2027.

assumptions.claim: Maridebart cafraglutide produced up to about 16.2 percent (treatment-regimen) weight loss at 52 weeks versus about 2.5 percent on placebo in phase 2.
Placebo arms in 72-week obesity trials without diabetes lose about 2-3 percent body weight.

reason: Weight loss in type 2 diabetes is smaller than without diabetes but still large; success is near certain and the uncertainty is the size of the placebo-adjusted effect.
rationale: MariTide phase 2 reported about 17 percent weight loss at 52 weeks in the type 2 diabetes cohort versus small placebo losses. Comparable incretin trials in diabetes (SURMOUNT-2: 12.8 percent vs 3.2 percent) show smaller but robust effects. With 550 per arm the superiority test is essentially certain. Effect-size uncertainty comes from estimand choice and tolerability. Topline most likely April to June 2027.

assumptions.claim: Maridebart cafraglutide gave up to about 17 percent weight loss at 52 weeks in the type 2 diabetes phase 2 cohort.
Tirzepatide 15 mg lost 14.7 percent (efficacy) versus 3.2 percent placebo at 72 weeks in obesity with type 2 diabetes.

reason: Placebo-controlled trial after VEGFR TKI failure, where placebo PFS is very short and TKI effects are large; failure would come only from a small sample or atypical control performance.
rationale: AL2846 is a multi-target VEGFR/MET/TAM TKI. In RAI-refractory thyroid cancer after VEGFR TKI, cabozantinib (COSMIC-311) cut progression risk by about 78 percent with placebo PFS near 2 months, and anlotinib showed HR near 0.2 in first line. A 144-patient randomized placebo trial should show a large PFS benefit. The record still shows recruiting, so reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely; if it does report it is likely a strongly positive interim.

assumptions.claim: Cabozantinib after VEGFR TKI failure in RAI-refractory DTC gave PFS HR about 0.22 with placebo median PFS about 1.9 months.
Anlotinib improved PFS in RAI-refractory DTC with HR about 0.26.

reason: Weight co-primary is near certain, but the KCCQ-CSS co-primary with about 47 per arm and SD near 18 points has only about even odds of significance despite a plausible 6-8 point benefit.
rationale: Both co-primaries must be met. Mazdutide will clearly reduce body weight at week 36. For KCCQ-CSS, STEP-HFpEF (semaglutide) and SUMMIT (tirzepatide) showed 7-8 point gains versus placebo at 52 weeks in about 500-700 patients. Here there are about 47 per arm, SE of the difference is about 4 points, and week 36 is earlier, so significance for 6 mg is about a coin flip; the second dose adds some chance. Single-site Chinese phase 2.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide improved KCCQ-CSS by 7.8 points more than placebo at 52 weeks in obese HFpEF.
Tirzepatide improved KCCQ-CSS by about 6.9 points more than placebo at 52 weeks in obese HFpEF.

reason: Etoricoxib alone is already very effective in acute gout, so adding betamethasone must show an incremental pain benefit on a coarse 4-point scale in only about 36 patients per arm.
rationale: A sponsor-run fixed-dose combination trial in Mexico aims to show that adding a corticosteroid to etoricoxib speeds pain relief. Steroids work quickly in gout flares, so superiority at day 2 or 5 is plausible, and such trials usually report positively when published. Against that: very small sample, coarse Likert pain scale, strong NSAID control, and a single site. Public reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely for a small Mexican sponsor, and still-recruiting status suggests slippage.

assumptions.claim: Etoricoxib 120 mg is as effective as indomethacin in acute gout.
Oral corticosteroids are comparable to NSAIDs in acute gout pain relief.

reason: Phase 2 safety-primary study with enrolment closed and primary completion in March 2027; a small sponsor adds some risk of delay, funding stops and slow results posting.
Remote symptom monitoring shifts global quality of life only modestly at 3 months across a heterogeneous cancer population, and effects of 2 points on QLQ-C30 are near the detection limit.
rationale: ePRO monitoring trials show inconsistent HRQoL benefit; PRO-TECT and Basch's trial showed benefits mainly in survival and symptom control, others null at 3 months. With 729 per arm and SD near 20, the trial detects about 2.1 points, so a plausible 1.5-3 point effect gives roughly a 40 percent chance. Recruitment still open in October 2026 means the primary analysis will likely come late 2027 or later.

assumptions.claim: Electronic symptom monitoring in routine oncology care improved quality of life modestly in some trials and not in others.

reason: Remibrutinib's rapid onset versus dupilumab's slower rise should favour remibrutinib at week 4, but the margin is moderate and dupilumab's loading dose narrows it.
rationale: The trial is designed around early onset. In REMIX-1/2, remibrutinib lowered UAS7 by about 15-17 points at week 4 with separation from placebo by week 1-2. Dupilumab in CUPID needed weeks to build effect, about 10-12 points at week 4 even with loading. A 4-6 point difference with about 205 per arm and SD near 10.5 gives high power. Novartis designed and funded this to demonstrate speed, which supports a positive readout.

assumptions.claim: Remibrutinib 25 mg twice daily produced UAS7 improvement of roughly 15-17 points at week 4 in CSU.
Dupilumab in antihistamine-refractory CSU improved UAS7 by about 20 points at week 12 versus about 12 for placebo.
assumptions.source: CUPID Study A, J Allergy Clin Immunol 2024

reason: Large sham-controlled phase 3 of a disease-modifying ASO with a big phase 2 signal; the main way to fail is a strong sham response or a smaller effect than the open-label data suggested.
rationale: Zorevunersen raised Nav1.1 and cut major motor seizures sharply in phase 1/2a and the extension study (median reductions of roughly 50% or more), though those were open-label. EMPEROR is sham-controlled, 170 patients, so even a 25-30 point real effect over a sham reduction of about 15% is well powered. Failure would come from a large sham response or dose/regimen issues. Topline is guided for the second half of 2027, so a public result by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Open-label zorevunersen in Dravet syndrome gave median major motor seizure reductions of roughly 40-85% depending on dose and timepoint.
Placebo arms in Dravet phase 3 trials had median convulsive seizure reductions of about 10-20%.
Stoke guided EMPEROR topline data to the second half of 2027.

reason: The record is a combined phase 2/3 with a 26-week primary but still 'enrolling by invitation', so the January 2027 completion date is likely to slip or be rewritten when the placebo-controlled phase 3 part is added.
rationale: Status enrolling by invitation in Oct 2026 with a 26-week primary endpoint makes a January 2027 primary completion hard to reach, and the phase 3 double-blind part is not yet reflected in arms or enrollment (24), so the record is likely to be restructured. BridgeBio is a reliable sponsor and the drug is well-tolerated, so stopping is unlikely. Results posting by August 2027 is unlikely given the sponsor's habit of posting near the deadline.

reason: Vehicle response in mild-to-moderate topical AD trials is high (EASI-75 of 15-30% at week 8), which is the main threat to an otherwise well-powered 120-per-arm phase 3 of a topical with a presumably positive phase 2.
rationale: Topical agents (ruxolitinib, roflumilast, ivarmacitinib ointment) usually beat vehicle on EASI-75 at week 8 with 20-35 point gaps; a phase 3 started after a phase 2 is likely to succeed with 120 per arm. Vehicle response in mild-moderate AD with small BSA can be 20-30%, narrowing the gap. Qilu rarely issues press releases or posts to ClinicalTrials.gov, so public timing is slow, and recruitment was still open in Oct 2026.

assumptions.claim: Vehicle arms of topical AD phase 3 trials had EASI-75 rates of roughly 8-25% at week 4-8.
Active topical arms achieved EASI-75 of about 40-62% at week 4-8 in mild-to-moderate AD.

reason: Novel epigenetic mechanism in a 26-week phase 2 of about 87 per arm; the odds of a significant ADAS-cog 12 benefit are low, as with most symptomatic AD phase 2 programs.
rationale: A first-in-class oral epigenetic regulator in mild-to-moderate AD has no human efficacy proof. With about 87 per arm, SD near 6 and 26 weeks, only a true effect of 2 or more ADAS-cog points would be detected reliably; most such phase 2 programs show no separation (and the primary is mainly safety). The study is complete, so topline is probably available by early 2027, though Ono may only disclose via earnings or pipeline updates.
evidence: Phase 2 symptomatic AD trials ADAS-cog 12 26 weeks (e.g., idalopirdine, intepirdine)
Placebo decline ADAS-cog 11 over 24-26 weeks in mild-moderate AD

assumptions.claim: Placebo patients with mild-to-moderate AD worsen by about 2-3 ADAS-cog points over 26 weeks.
assumptions.source: Intepirdine MINDSET 2017 and idalopirdine STARSHINE 2018 placebo arms

assumptions.claim: The study is registered as completed with primary completion 2026-07-31.

reason: Mazdutide 9 mg should beat semaglutide 2.4 mg on weight and probably on liver fat; the residual risk is that the liver-fat co-primary or an open-label tolerability effect fails to separate.
rationale: Mazdutide 9 mg gave about 15-18% weight loss at 48 weeks in Chinese adults (GLORY-1/2) versus roughly 10-12% for semaglutide 2.4 mg in East Asians (STEP 7), and beat semaglutide in the T2D head-to-head DREAMS-3. With 240 per arm and SD about 6.5, a 4-5 point gap is highly significant. Both primaries must be met; mazdutide's glucagon component should also give larger liver-fat reduction. Innovent reports quickly by press release.
evidence: DREAMS-3 mazdutide vs semaglutide T2D with obesity 2025

assumptions.claim: Mazdutide 9 mg produced mean weight loss of about 15-18% at 48 weeks in Chinese adults with obesity.
Semaglutide 2.4 mg produced about 10-13% weight loss at 44 weeks in East Asian adults.
Mazdutide beat semaglutide on weight in the DREAMS-3 head-to-head.

reason: Part B enrollment depends on process-2 drug supply and the status is still recruiting in Oct 2026, so a November 2026 primary completion on a 52-week safety endpoint will almost certainly be pushed far beyond February 2027.
rationale: A 52-week primary endpoint with a 135-patient, two-part design whose second part (90 patients) was still recruiting in Oct 2026 cannot complete in November 2026; the registry date will have to move into late 2027 or beyond, or the study will still show as recruiting after February 2027. Pacira has some financial pressure, so termination is a small risk. No results will be posted this early.

reason: A 50-patient rare-disease trial on ICARS with a placebo response and heterogeneous ages is underpowered for the modest improvement seen in open-label data of a first-in-class replacement therapy.
rationale: Open-label phase 1/2 data of GLM101 suggested ICARS improvements of a few points, but PMM2-CDG is heterogeneous and slowly progressive, ICARS is rater-dependent and placebo/practice effects are common. With 25 per arm and SD of change near 5, a true benefit of 3 points gives only about 70% power; a smaller true effect gives much less. Glycomine is private and would likely announce topline if positive, perhaps after Part B.

assumptions.claim: GLM101 produced ICARS improvements in open-label PMM2-CDG patients over 6 months.
Untreated PMM2-CDG ataxia is slowly progressive or stable over months, so placebo change on ICARS is small.

reason: Ulotaront missed in two earlier phase 3 acute schizophrenia trials because of large placebo responses and small drug-placebo gaps; this repeat at 75/100 mg with enriched entry criteria is still more likely to fail than succeed.
rationale: DIAMOND 1 and 2 (50/75 mg) both failed on PANSS total at week 6 with large placebo responses, although the phase 2 study had been positive. This trial uses higher fixed doses (75/100 mg) and enrichment (prior good antipsychotic response, informant, short exacerbation), which may help, but the mechanism (TAAR1 agonism) has shown only small effects vs placebo. Either dose succeeding counts, helping slightly. Otsuka usually announces results by press release or in earnings updates.
evidence: Brexpiprazole acute schizophrenia phase 3 PANSS placebo response

assumptions.claim: Ulotaront 50 and 75 mg did not separate from placebo on PANSS total at week 6 in DIAMOND 1 and 2.
Placebo PANSS total change at week 6 in acute schizophrenia phase 3 trials is typically about -10 to -20 points.
assumptions.source: DIAMOND 1 2023 and Koblan 2020 NEJM (-9.7 placebo in phase 2)

reason: A seven-patient phase 2 closed out early by Novartis; the status may be flipped to terminated, and Novartis posts results to ClinicalTrials.gov reliably within about a year.
rationale: Enrollment of seven and a description saying the study is being closed out early point to a business-driven stop, so the record may be updated to terminated (or completed). Novartis normally posts results within 12 months of primary completion (October 2026), and often earlier for small studies. The safety-only primary outcome is unlikely to change.

reason: A fully enrolled, not-recruiting vaccine phase 2 whose fixed vaccination schedule should reach its February 2027 primary completion; results posting normally follows many months later.
rationale: The trial is no longer recruiting and the primary endpoint is two weeks after the third vaccination, so the schedule is largely fixed and primary completion should land near February 2027. A US government-supported (JPM CBRN) program makes termination unlikely. Bavarian Nordic typically posts results late in the 12-month window, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. The dose-selection primary outcomes are unlikely to be rewritten.

reason: Syk inhibitor in refractory chronic ITP with platelets <30; placebo durable response is near zero, so only a clearly weaker-than-class effect would fail.
rationale: Syk inhibitors have shown large durable-response differences versus placebo in chronic ITP (sovleplenib ESLIM-01: placebo near 0%, active roughly 36-48%; fostamatinib 18% vs 2%). Placebo durable response in a population with platelets <30 is close to 0%, so with ~100 per arm even a 15-point effect is significant. Main uncertainty is whether TQB3473 is as potent as sovleplenib, and when CTTQ discloses results (registry still recruiting).

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in refractory chronic ITP phase 3 trials with a durable-response endpoint have 0-2% responders.
assumptions.source: Sovleplenib ESLIM-01 (Lancet Haematol 2024); fostamatinib FIT trials (Am J Hematol 2018)

assumptions.claim: A Syk inhibitor produced a durable platelet response in a large share of chronic ITP patients versus near zero on placebo.

reason: If the hypothesis is non-inferiority against Mircera (likely, margin around -0.75 g/dL) it should be met easily; if it is truly superiority, TIW vadadustat will not beat an ESA on hemoglobin.
rationale: Active-controlled open-label hemoglobin trial in hemodialysis, 353 patients, SD about 1 g/dL gives a difference SE near 0.11. Vadadustat was non-inferior to darbepoetin in INNO2VATE and TIW dosing held hemoglobin in MO2DIFY, so non-inferiority is very likely met. The risk is the unstated hypothesis: a superiority test would fail. Akebia usually announces topline results.

assumptions.claim: Vadadustat hemoglobin change was non-inferior to darbepoetin alfa in dialysis patients with a margin of -0.75 g/dL.
Three-times-weekly vadadustat maintained hemoglobin in dialysis patients similar to daily dosing.

reason: Delayed-treatment control at week 12 should show about 0% composite response, so failure would require an unexpectedly weak combination effect at week 48.
rationale: Untreated chronic HDV essentially never achieves HDV RNA TND plus ALT normalization in 12 weeks, so the control arm is about 0-3%. Phase 2 SOLSTICE of tobevibart plus elebsiran showed roughly half of patients with composite virologic and biochemical response by week 24-48. With 62 per arm, a 40+ point difference is highly significant. Vir has guided to ECLIPSE 1 topline around year-end 2026 / early 2027.
evidence: SOLSTICE phase 2 tobevibart + elebsiran HDV, Vir 2025

assumptions.claim: Untreated or delayed-treatment arms in HDV phase 3 trials have near-zero composite virologic plus ALT response at 12-24 weeks.
Tobevibart plus elebsiran produced HDV RNA below LLOQ in a majority of participants in phase 2.

reason: Six patients per arm cannot reliably show a significant change in parenteral support volume; the primary set also includes descriptive safety outcomes and a sponsor claim of success is unlikely.
rationale: Phase 2 with 18 patients in three arms; efficacy outcomes (parenteral volume, stool volume) have high between-patient variance, so a significant difference needs a very large effect. Crofelemer has a plausible antisecretory rationale but no proven effect in SBS-IF. Registry shows recruiting with planned completion 2027-03, so readout before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In SBS-IF trials placebo patients reduce weekly parenteral support volume by roughly 0.5-1 L/week.
assumptions.source: Teduglutide STEPS trial, Jeppesen et al., Gastroenterology 2012

reason: Three co-primaries must all succeed; the ISGA 0/1 responder endpoint is the least powered and placebo response in acne is large.
rationale: Cyproterone acetate with ethinyl estradiol is an established antiandrogenic COC; COC-versus-placebo acne trials (e.g., drospirenone/EE 0.02) show modest but significant lesion reductions with n of a few hundred. With 354 vs 177 and SD about 9, the lesion endpoints are well powered; the ISGA 0/1 co-primary is borderline, and all three must be met. Recruitment started Aug 2026 with 24-week treatment, so results by mid-2027 are very unlikely.
evidence: Drospirenone/EE 20 mcg acne placebo trials, Maloney 2008
Cochrane review of combined oral contraceptives for acne, 2012

assumptions.claim: Combined oral contraceptives reduce inflammatory lesion counts about 3-4 more than placebo over 6 cycles.
assumptions.source: Cochrane review: Combined oral contraceptive pills for treatment of acne, Arowojolu 2012

reason: A 50-patient arm versus faricimab is underpowered to show BCVA superiority at week 16; the realistic outcome is parity, which only counts if the sponsor frames it as met.
rationale: Phase 2 dose-ranging versus an active anti-VEGF/Ang-2 comparator, about 50 per arm. Faricimab gives roughly +9 letters at week 16 in DME; IBI302 (VEGF/complement bispecific) is unlikely to be significantly better in a short 16-week window. Significant superiority is improbable; a non-inferiority or descriptive framing is the more likely public message.

assumptions.claim: Faricimab produces about +8 to +11 ETDRS letters at week 16 in DME.
assumptions.source: YOSEMITE and RHINE, Wykoff et al., Lancet 2022

reason: Enrolment appears complete with a 6-month safety endpoint due around December 2026, so only modest slippage is expected; jCyte is a private company unlikely to post results by August 2027.
rationale: Active, not recruiting, 31 patients, 6-month primary; close-out near on schedule. Small private sponsor rarely posts results early.

reason: Tirzepatide lowers HbA1c and weight robustly; failure would need an unexpectedly strong placebo response from intensified diabetes care or heavy dropout from GI adverse events.
rationale: GLP-1 add-on in type 1 diabetes consistently lowers HbA1c versus placebo (liraglutide ADJUNCT ONE about -0.3, semaglutide about -0.4); tirzepatide is more potent and induces large weight loss, which improves insulin sensitivity. With 905 patients, significance is near certain. Lilly typically issues topline press releases for large phase 3 programmes.

assumptions.claim: Adjunct GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce HbA1c by about 0.3-0.5 points versus placebo in type 1 diabetes.
assumptions.source: ADJUNCT ONE, Mathieu et al., Diabetes Care 2016

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide discontinuation for adverse events is about 4-7% versus 2-3% placebo in obesity trials.

reason: A 49-patient, 4-site BEAM-transplant trial from a small sponsor is likely to recruit slowly, so primary completion should slip past mid-2027; early termination is a modest risk and results will not be posted by August 2027.
rationale: Recruiting four-site transplant study with a narrow population and 30-day follow-up; registry dates for small sponsors usually slip.

reason: Placebo combined remission in perianal Crohn's fistula trials is high (about 35%) and the ADMIRE-CD II repeat of darvadstrocel failed, so a cell therapy margin is fragile.
rationale: Darvadstrocel succeeded in ADMIRE-CD (51.5% vs 35.6% combined remission) but did not confirm in ADMIRE-CD II, showing a high placebo rate and fragile effect. TH-SC01 is a Chinese allogeneic cell product with 114 per arm and a stringent MRI-based endpoint. Registry shows still recruiting despite a 2026-12 primary completion, so readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Placebo combined remission at week 24 was 35.6% in ADMIRE-CD versus 51.5% with darvadstrocel.
ADMIRE-CD II did not meet its primary endpoint.

reason: The trial is already completed (primary completion 14 Aug 2026), so stopping is very unlikely and the primary outcome should stay as registered. Boehringer Ingelheim usually posts results near the 12-month deadline, which falls about two weeks before the read date, so posting is roughly a coin flip.

An anti-oxLDL antibody has an unproven effect on pericoronary fat inflammation within 24 weeks on top of statins. FAI measurement noise is large and regression to the mean affects both arms, so a clean placebo-adjusted difference is uncertain.
rationale: Novel mechanism (orticumab, anti-oxLDL) with only small earlier imaging signals. FAI percent change is noisy; 120 per arm gives decent power only for a 3-5% placebo-adjusted drop. Phase 2 imaging biomarker trials of anti-inflammatory agents often miss. A small private sponsor reports positive results readily, which lifts p_met conditional on a public result.
evidence: Antonopoulos 2017 Sci Transl Med (FAI as marker of coronary inflammation)
Abcentra orticumab phase 2 psoriasis vascular inflammation study

assumptions.claim: FAI is a CCTA-derived measure of pericoronary inflammation that has been shown to change with statin therapy.
Orticumab is a monoclonal antibody against oxidised LDL epitopes that was tested in earlier phase 2 imaging studies.

reason: With about 41 patients per arm and a large placebo response on ESSDAI, a 2-point true effect gives only about 50% power. APRIL blockade lowers IgG, which mechanically helps the ESSDAI biological domain, but systemic activity in an IgG-high population is still small.
rationale: APRIL/BAFF-pathway agents (telitacicept, ianalumab, dazodalibep) have shown ESSDAI separation of about 2-3 points versus placebo in phase 2. Here n is about 83, placebo drops about 3 points over 28 weeks, and SD is about 5, so the SE of the difference is about 1.1. Needs a 2.2-point difference for p<0.05, so success is roughly a coin flip at best.
evidence: Telitacicept pSS phase 2 (Xu et al 2024, Rheumatology)

assumptions.claim: Telitacicept, a TACI-Fc that blocks APRIL and BLyS, reduced ESSDAI more than placebo in a phase 2 Sjogren's trial.
assumptions.source: Xu et al 2024, Rheumatology (Oxford), telitacicept pSS phase 2

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in Sjogren's disease phase 2 trials with baseline ESSDAI of 5 or more typically improve by about 2-4 points over 24-28 weeks.

reason: CRR should clearly favour the anti-CD79b ADC, as pola-R-GemOx did, but overall survival is a co-primary with a 5-year frame and is unlikely to be mature or reported as met in any early statement. Under the co-primary rule that is the main way this fails.
rationale: SHR-A1912 is a CD79b-MMAE ADC like polatuzumab; POLARGO showed pola+R-GemOx roughly doubled CR (about 42% vs 23%) with OS HR 0.48. CRR superiority is likely (about 85%). But CRR and OS are co-primary and both must be met. A statement by June 2027 would likely report CRR only with OS immature, which counts as not met.
evidence: SHR-A1912 + R-GemOx phase 1b/2 in R/R DLBCL (Hengrui)

assumptions.claim: In POLARGO, polatuzumab vedotin added to R-GemOx improved complete response and overall survival versus R-GemOx in R/R DLBCL.
SHR-A1912 is a CD79b-directed antibody-drug conjugate developed by Hengrui/Suncadia.

reason: Safety-primary phase 2 with enrolment closed and primary completion set for end of 2026. Sanofi, which now owns the asset, will likely keep it running to completion; a date slip beyond March 2027 is possible, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

Incretin-glucagon agonists give large MASH resolution rates, but central pathology reads and a 60-week window can lift placebo response. With about 60 per arm the effect still very likely reaches significance, so the main risk is a higher placebo rate than expected.
rationale: Mazdutide (GLP-1/glucagon) is close to survodutide (MASH improvement 83% vs 18% in phase 2) and tirzepatide (resolution 44-62% vs 10%, SYNERGY-NASH). A high dose should reach about 45-55% resolution versus 10-25% placebo, a 30+ point gap that is significant at 60 per arm. Residual risk is a high placebo response and results timing.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide produced MASH resolution without worsening fibrosis in 44-62% of patients versus 10% on placebo at 52 weeks.
Survodutide produced MASH improvement without worsening fibrosis in up to 83% versus 18% on placebo.

reason: Botulinum-toxin-class agents nearly always beat placebo on TWSTRS at week 4 in cervical dystonia. The risk is that the new toxin's highest dose is under-dosed or less potent than expected, and blinded data are probably not read out before late 2027.
rationale: Phase 2/3 trials of Dysport, Xeomin, Botox and daxibotulinumtoxinA all separated from placebo on TWSTRS total by roughly 8-12 points at weeks 4-6, with SD about 12. At 44 per arm this is well powered. The primary completion date appears to be the last patient's week 4 visit, with study completion at week 36 in Nov 2027, so results probably arrive late.

assumptions.claim: DaxibotulinumtoxinA met its TWSTRS total score primary endpoint versus placebo in cervical dystonia.
Registry dates are consistent with primary completion being the last patient's week 4 visit and study completion the week 36 visit.

reason: Zibotentan added to dapagliflozin lowered UACR by about 30% beyond dapagliflozin alone in the phase 2b ZENITH trial, and 112 per arm gives high power. Failure would need a much smaller effect in this Russian-only population.
rationale: ZENITH High Proteinuria phase 2b (NCT05384535) showed zibotentan/dapagliflozin lowering UACR roughly 30% more than dapagliflozin alone at week 12. Log-UACR SD is about 0.6, so 112 per arm has very high power for a 0.36 log difference. This is a regional replication for EAEU registration. Residual risk is tiny.

assumptions.claim: In the ZENITH High Proteinuria phase 2b trial, zibotentan/dapagliflozin reduced UACR by roughly 30% relative to dapagliflozin alone at week 12.
The record states the study supplies data for the zibotentan/dapagliflozin approval process in the Eurasian Economic Union.

reason: A sham-surgery-controlled cell therapy trial with an 18-month patient-diary endpoint faces a large placebo response, as sham-controlled PD gene and cell therapy trials have shown. Phase 1 was open-label, and the cell dose is unproven for efficacy. Results before mid-2027 are very unlikely.
rationale: Open-label phase 1 (Tabar, Nature 2025) suggested ON-time gains, but sham-controlled PD trials of AAV-GAD and GDNF failed on diary and UPDRS endpoints due to sham response. With 68 vs 34 patients and diary SD about 3 h, a 1.2 h true effect gives about 50% power, so odds are modest. Any public result by June 2027 is improbable, probably only a stop.

assumptions.claim: Bemdaneprocel phase 1 was open-label, with improvement in ON-time without troublesome dyskinesia at 18 months in the high-dose cohort.
Registered enrolment is 102 participants randomised 2:1 with a Week 78 primary endpoint and study completion in 2032.

reason: Active, not recruiting phase 2 PK study with short Cmax/AUC windows and a Cycle 7 trough, so the Feb 2027 primary completion should hold; BMS usually posts results near the 12-month deadline and the study runs to late 2028.

Pembrolizumab alone gives roughly 40-55% ORR in checkpoint-naive MCC, leaving little room; with 59 per arm a difference of about 18 points is needed for significance and an add-on injection effect is likely smaller.
rationale: Design (59 per arm) matches 40% vs 65% assumed ORR. Pembrolizumab in checkpoint-naive MCC already reaches ~50% (KEYNOTE-017), and the strict confirmed 12/24-week ORR definition lowers it only somewhat. A local immunotherapy add-on would need a very large increment. Small company, rare disease, recruitment of 118 within about 15 months unlikely, so readout is probably late 2027 or later.
evidence: TuHURA IFx-Hu2.0 phase 2 in checkpoint-failed MCC

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab alone gave an objective response rate of about 56% in checkpoint-naive advanced MCC.
assumptions.source: KEYNOTE-017, Nghiem et al, J Clin Oncol 2019

assumptions.claim: The planned 59 patients per arm corresponds to a design assumption of roughly 40% vs 65% ORR.
assumptions.source: NCT06947928 record enrollment and standard sample-size arithmetic

reason: Bevacizumab already blocks VEGF and MSS colorectal cancer is largely PD-1 insensitive, so the PD-1 arm of ivonescimab may add only a modest PFS gain, near the HR of about 0.8 needed for significance with roughly 340 events.
rationale: Ivonescimab (PD-1/VEGF bispecific) has beaten PD-1 comparators in NSCLC (HARMONi-2, HARMONi-6). In colorectal cancer, bevacizumab plus chemo is a strong comparator, but AtezoTRIBE hinted that PD-1 added to bevacizumab-chemo may lift PFS (HR 0.69 in a phase 2). Akeso is aggressive and discloses positive readouts quickly. Expected HR about 0.78 sits near the significance threshold, so it is close to a coin flip.

assumptions.claim: Atezolizumab added to FOLFOXIRI-bevacizumab improved PFS in mCRC (HR 0.69) in a randomized phase 2.
assumptions.source: AtezoTRIBE, Antoniotti et al, Lancet Oncol 2022

assumptions.claim: Bevacizumab plus oxaliplatin or irinotecan chemotherapy gives median PFS of roughly 9-11 months in first-line mCRC.

reason: Muscarinic M1/M4 agonism has no proven antimanic effect and lacks direct D2 blockade, the mechanism behind all approved acute mania drugs, so the drug may separate from placebo less than in schizophrenia.
rationale: Acute mania trials of antipsychotics usually succeed (placebo-controlled YMRS differences of 4-6 points at week 3 with about 130 per arm give high power). KarXT showed large effects in schizophrenia, but antimanic activity of muscarinic agonists is untested and there is no phase 2 mania data. Eastern European and Argentine inpatient sites add some placebo-response noise. About 55% for a hit.

assumptions.claim: Approved antipsychotics beat placebo on YMRS at week 3 in inpatient mania trials by about 4-6 points.
KarXT reduced PANSS total by about 9 points vs placebo in schizophrenia.

reason: Muscarinic M1/M4 agonism has no proven antimanic effect and lacks direct D2 blockade, the mechanism behind all approved acute mania drugs, so the drug may separate from placebo less than in schizophrenia.
rationale: Twin of BALSAM-1 with different sites (China, India, Israel, Western and Eastern Europe). Acute mania antipsychotic trials usually succeed with about 130 per arm, and KarXT was strong in schizophrenia, but antimanic activity of muscarinic agonists is untested and there is no phase 2 mania data. Outcomes of the two trials are correlated. About 55% for a hit.

assumptions.claim: Approved antipsychotics beat placebo on YMRS at week 3 in inpatient mania trials by about 4-6 points.
KarXT reduced PANSS total by about 9 points vs placebo in schizophrenia.

reason: Both AUC ratios must fall within the equivalence margins; daratumumab SC exposure is variable (target-mediated disposition) so imbalance in tumour burden between arms is the main risk, though about 236 per arm gives ample precision.
rationale: Biosimilar PK equivalence trials from Celltrion almost always succeed. With roughly 236 patients per arm and AUC CV near 50-60%, the 90% CI half-width is about 0.09 on the log scale, well inside the usual 80-125% margin if the true ratio is near 1. Both AUCs must pass, and a different hyaluronidase or formulation could shift exposure a little.

assumptions.claim: Daratumumab SC vs IV in COLUMBA met non-inferiority on Ctrough and ORR, with high but manageable PK variability.
assumptions.source: COLUMBA, Mateos et al, Lancet Haematol 2020

assumptions.claim: Celltrion biosimilar PK-equivalence studies have consistently met their margins.

reason: Recruiting a 88-patient narcolepsy type 2 dose-finding trial right at its planned Nov 2026 primary completion suggests a possible slip of a few months; Takeda posts results relatively promptly but usually 9-12 months after completion.

Oral SERDs versus fulvestrant mostly win only in ESR1-mutant disease; in an unselected population the PFS gain is modest (HR about 0.8), which with about 400 events is close to the significance threshold.
rationale: Large phase 3 (640 patients, about 400 events) gives good power for HR near 0.75, but oral SERDs vs fulvestrant benefit is concentrated in ESR1 mutations (EMERALD overall HR 0.70, ESR1-wt 0.86; SERENA-2 camizestrant HR 0.58-0.67; EMBER-3 overall not significant vs standard ET). Unselected Chinese population mostly CDK4/6-naive helps somewhat. Slow accrual since 2022 and private sponsor delay disclosure.

assumptions.claim: Elacestrant improved PFS vs standard endocrine therapy with HR 0.70 overall but only 0.86 in ESR1-wild-type patients.
assumptions.source: EMERALD, Bidard et al, J Clin Oncol 2022

assumptions.claim: Fulvestrant plus placebo had median PFS of about 5.4 months in a Chinese pretreated HR+/HER2- population.
assumptions.source: DAWNA-1, Xu et al, Lancet Oncol 2021

reason: A novel Wnt-pathway antibody must match monthly ranibizumab on BCVA within the margin; failure would need EYE103 to be clearly less effective than a potent monthly anti-VEGF, which phase 2 did not suggest.
rationale: Non-inferiority to monthly ranibizumab 0.5 mg with about 350 per arm and SD about 10 letters gives SE of about 0.75 letters, so a margin of 3-4 letters is passed easily unless the drug is truly inferior. Phase 2 (BRUNELLO) showed BCVA gains at least comparable to ranibizumab. Main uncertainty is the true effect of a Wnt-agonist antibody, and a monthly comparator that is fairly strong.

assumptions.claim: Monthly ranibizumab 0.5 mg gains roughly 10-12 ETDRS letters at one year in DME.
In phase 2 DME, EYE103 gave BCVA gains at least similar to ranibizumab.

reason: A topical JAK inhibitor must reduce deep inflammatory nodules and abscesses by 75% over vehicle in 16 weeks; topical HS therapies have historically had little effect and vehicle response in mild disease with low lesion counts is substantial.
rationale: Incyte proceeded to two phase 3 trials after phase 2 and chose HiSCR75, suggesting a signal, and oral JAK inhibitors work in HS (upadacitinib). But topical delivery to deep nodules is questionable, vehicle HiSCR75 in Hurley I/II with low AN counts is around 20-30%, and topical HS treatments have mostly failed. Large n (about 286 per arm) gives power only for an effect of about 10 points or more.

assumptions.claim: Vehicle response on HiSCR in mild-to-moderate HS is substantial (HiSCR50 around 40%).
assumptions.source: Placebo arms of HS trials such as PIONEER I/II (Kimball 2016)

assumptions.claim: Oral JAK inhibition (upadacitinib) achieved significant HiSCR improvement over placebo in HS.

reason: About 33 per arm in a dose-ranging phase 2; a real TNF-driven effect is plausible but power for the high dose versus placebo is only moderate, and the sponsor may not state significance.
rationale: Dose-ranging phase 2, about 33 per arm. TNF blockade gives endoscopic response of roughly 30-45% versus 10-15% on placebo in Crohn's, and brivekimig adds OX40L blockade, so a significant high-dose result is plausible. The sample is small, so power is moderate. Still recruiting in Oct 2026 with a Dec 2026 completion date, so readout is likely mid-to-late 2027.
evidence: Sanofi brivekimig phase 2 in hidradenitis suppurativa

assumptions.claim: In Crohn's phase 2/3 induction trials, week 12 endoscopic response was roughly 10-15% on placebo versus 25-45% on active drug.
Brivekimig is a bispecific nanobody neutralizing TNF and OX40L.

reason: Mild-moderate HS with few nodules gives a high vehicle HiSCR75 response, and a topical JAK1/2 cream may not reach deep nodules, so the gap may be under the roughly 9-10 points needed.
rationale: Phase 3 with 290 per arm is well powered for a gap of about 10 points. Doubts: topical JAK1/2 penetration to deep inflammatory nodules, and a vehicle HiSCR75 rate of roughly 25-35% in a mild population (AN count at least 4, no tunnels). Incyte went to phase 3 after a phase 2 signal, so slightly below even odds. Primary completion Oct 2026 implies topline by early 2027.
evidence: Incyte ruxolitinib cream phase 2 in hidradenitis suppurativa, 2024
Topical clindamycin trials in mild HS

assumptions.claim: Vehicle response rates on HiSCR in mild-moderate HS are high (HiSCR50 around 40-50%), putting HiSCR75 near 25-35%.
assumptions.source: Incyte ruxolitinib cream HS phase 2; topical HS trial vehicle arms

assumptions.claim: Study enrolls Hurley I or II patients with at least 4 abscesses and nodules and no draining tunnels.

reason: Tirzepatide's glycemic and weight effects are large; a 0.5-0.7 point HbA1c gap against placebo with 230 per arm is far beyond the detection threshold, so the only real uncertainty is timing of disclosure.
rationale: Tirzepatide in type 1 diabetes with overweight produces large weight loss and better glycemia; GLP-1 adjuncts such as liraglutide lowered HbA1c by 0.2-0.3 points and tirzepatide is considerably stronger. With about 230 per arm and an SD near 0.8, a 0.5-0.7 point difference is highly significant. Primary completion Nov 2026, so a Lilly readout in H1 2027 is likely.
evidence: ADJUNCT ONE liraglutide in type 1 diabetes, 2016

assumptions.claim: Adjunct liraglutide in type 1 diabetes lowered HbA1c by only about 0.2-0.3 points versus placebo at 52 weeks.
assumptions.source: ADJUNCT ONE, Mathieu et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2016

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide produces about 15-21% weight loss in adults with obesity without diabetes.

reason: Both parts' primaries must be met; TDF suppresses HBeAg-negative patients near ceiling, so superiority there with about 50 per arm is hard, and no formal hypothesis or margin is stated.
rationale: Two primaries (HBeAg-positive and HBeAg-negative) must both be met. ALG-000184 showed potent HBV DNA suppression in phase 1, plausibly beating TDF at week 48 in HBeAg-positive patients (TDF around 50-65% below LLOQ). In HBeAg-negative patients TDF is near ceiling and the record states no hypothesis or margin, so a clear superiority claim for both parts is uncertain. Small company, topline timing mid to late 2027.
evidence: Aligos ALG-000184 phase 1 study in chronic hepatitis B, 2024-2025
TDF Studies 102/103, Marcellin et al., NEJM 2008

assumptions.claim: In HBeAg-negative patients, TDF achieved about 93% HBV DNA below 400 copies/mL at week 48.
In HBeAg-positive patients, TDF achieved about 67% HBV DNA below 29 IU/mL at week 48.
assumptions.source: Chan et al., Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2016 (Study 110)

reason: Latanoprost drops already lower diurnal IOP about 7-8 mmHg; a sustained-release implant is likely comparable rather than superior, and the design hypothesis is not stated.
rationale: Single-site phase 2 with about 25 per arm comparing a sustained-release prostaglandin implant with latanoprost drops. Drops give about 7-8 mmHg diurnal IOP reduction, so the implant is likely similar rather than better; success depends on a non-inferiority-type reading that the record does not state. Private sponsor with sparse disclosure, so public statement by mid-2027 is uncertain.
evidence: iDose TR travoprost implant phase 3, Berdahl et al., 2022

assumptions.claim: Latanoprost 0.005% lowers mean diurnal IOP by about 7-8 mmHg from a washout baseline of about 24-25 mmHg.
assumptions.source: Latanoprost pivotal trials; glaucoma implant phase 3 comparator arms

assumptions.claim: Intracameral travoprost implants (iDose TR) showed IOP reduction non-inferior to timolol drops, not superior to prostaglandin drops.

reason: Open-label with 25 per arm in stable, nusinersen-pretreated type 2 SMA; a gain of about 2 HFMSE points over continued nusinersen is plausible but near the detection limit given an SD near 4-5.
rationale: Patients have been on nusinersen over a year and are stable, so the control arm changes little (about +0.5 HFMSE). A single intrathecal AAV9 dose gave +2.4 points over sham in STEER (treatment-naive), and switching from nusinersen should give a similar or smaller gap. With 25 per arm and SD near 4.5, power is modest. Recruitment still open means week 52 data are unlikely before late 2027.
evidence: STRENGTH OAV101 intrathecal in previously treated SMA

assumptions.claim: In STEER, intrathecal onasemnogene abeparvovec improved HFMSE by 2.39 points versus sham at week 52 in treatment-naive patients who can sit.
The trial was still listed as recruiting in October 2026 with 50 planned patients and a 52-week primary endpoint.

reason: IL-1alpha/beta blockade has historically weak RA efficacy and 30 per arm needs roughly 30% versus 10% ACR50 for significance in a b/tsDMARD-experienced population.
rationale: Platform phase 2, about 30 per arm, in RA patients failing 1-2 biologics or JAK inhibitors on methotrexate. IL-1 blockade (anakinra) gave only modest RA benefit, and no strong lutikizumab RA signal is known. At n=30, ACR50 needs about 30% versus 10% placebo to be significant. AbbVie rarely press-releases phase 2 RA data, so disclosure by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Anakinra in RA, Cohen et al., 2002

assumptions.claim: Anakinra added to methotrexate gave only modest ACR20 gains over placebo (roughly 15-20 points) in RA.
Enrolment is about 180 across three substudies, each versus placebo, in patients with 1-2 prior b/tsDMARD failures on methotrexate.

reason: A dual GLP-1/GIP agonist with large weight loss should cut AHI strongly, as tirzepatide did in SURMOUNT-OSA; the main uncertainty is whether anything is disclosed before mid-2027.
rationale: HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist with weight loss comparable to tirzepatide. In SURMOUNT-OSA tirzepatide cut AHI roughly 50-60% versus about 5-14% on placebo. With 70 per arm and SD of percent change near 45, a gap of 30-40 points is highly significant. Still recruiting in Oct 2026 with a 52-week endpoint, and Hengrui rarely discloses, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: HRS9531 phase 3 obesity trial in China, 2025

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-OSA, tirzepatide reduced AHI by about 25-29 events/h (roughly 50-60%) versus about 5 events/h with placebo.
HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual receptor agonist from Hengrui, licensed ex-China to Kailera.

reason: Strict mMS clinical remission with about 35 per arm needs a gap near 20 points; the population includes advanced-therapy-experienced patients where TNF blockade works less well.
rationale: Same compound and sponsor as the Crohn's trial. Modified Mayo clinical remission is strict (endoscopic 0-1 without friability, stool and bleeding scores), placebo about 5-10%, and prior-biologic-failure patients are included, where TNF blockade works less well. At 35 per arm a gap near 20 points is needed. Enrolment is complete and primary completion is due Dec 2026, so a Sanofi disclosure in H1 2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: In phase 2b/3 UC induction trials using stringent modified Mayo clinical remission, placebo rates are roughly 3-10%.
assumptions.source: ELEVATE UC 52 (NCT03945188); True North ozanimod induction (NCT02435992)

assumptions.claim: Enrolment is 105 across three arms (two doses plus placebo), with a primary completion date of 17 December 2026.

reason: Dose-ranging phase 2 with 252 patients over several arms leaves about 50-60 per arm, so even a dupilumab-like 140-200 mL FEV1 gain on top of ICS-LABA has only modest power at the highest dose.
rationale: PF-07275315 is a trispecific antibody against TSLP, IL-4R and IL-13, so a T2 and non-T2 effect on FEV1 is plausible. Dupilumab and tezepelumab gave roughly 130-200 mL over placebo at week 12. With about 50-60 patients per arm and an SD near 430 mL, the highest dose has roughly even-to-good odds of reaching p<0.05. Primary completion is March 2027 and Pfizer rarely issues press releases for phase 2, so little is public before mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Dupilumab 200-300 mg q2w improved pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by about 0.13-0.14 L more than placebo at week 12 in QUEST.
Placebo arms in moderate-to-severe asthma trials typically gain about 0.1-0.18 L in FEV1 by week 12.

reason: With roughly 75-80 patients per arm and about 70-80 exacerbations overall in 24 weeks, a time-to-first-exacerbation primary has limited power unless the DPP1 inhibitor matches brensocatib's WILLOW effect.
rationale: DPP1 inhibition is validated in bronchiectasis: brensocatib cut exacerbations in WILLOW (time-to-first HR about 0.6) and ASPEN (rate ratio about 0.8). This Chinese phase 2 has 24 weeks and about 78 per arm, so only about 50 events enter the comparison of one dose against placebo. Potency of XH-S004 is unknown, and either dose can win. Chinese sponsors seldom publish early.

assumptions.claim: In WILLOW, brensocatib reduced the hazard of a first exacerbation over 24 weeks by about 40% (10 mg and 25 mg) versus placebo.
In ASPEN, brensocatib 10 mg and 25 mg reduced the annualised exacerbation rate by about 19-21% versus placebo.

reason: Open-label, single-arm-per-dose phase 2 of 30 patients that is still recruiting in late 2026 against a February 2027 primary completion; Sanofi usually posts results a year after completion, so a posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
About 45 patients in total, large spontaneous motor recovery in the first weeks after stroke, and three motor primary endpoints that all need to be met leave very little chance of a clean win.
rationale: Proof-of-concept trial with about 22 patients per arm and three co-primary motor outcomes (Fugl-Meyer, TUG, NIHSS motor). Natural recovery in the first 12 weeks after stroke is large and noisy (SD about 20 points), so detecting a few points on all three is unlikely. Neflamapimod missed its primary in the DLB phase 2b. The sponsor is a listed company and will almost certainly announce topline soon after the September 2026 completion.

assumptions.claim: Patients 2-7 days after a moderate-to-severe stroke typically gain 20-30 Fugl-Meyer motor points over 12 weeks with no active treatment.
assumptions.source: Prabhakaran et al, Neurorehabil Neural Repair 2008

assumptions.claim: Neflamapimod did not meet the primary endpoint in the phase 2b REVERSE-SD study in early Alzheimer's disease.

reason: Tibulizumab is a BAFF/IL-17A bispecific; IL-17A blockade works in HS, but placebo response in AN count is large and the bispecific's IL-17A potency at the tested doses is uncertain.
rationale: IL-17A inhibitors (secukinumab, bimekizumab, sonelokimab) show clear AN count and HiSCR gains over placebo in HS at 12-16 weeks. About 82 patients per arm with an SD near 55 points gives good power for a 20-25 point advantage on percent change in AN count. Either dose counts, which helps. Risks are placebo response and weaker IL-17A activity of the bispecific. Primary completion was September 2026, so topline should come soon.

assumptions.claim: In the bimekizumab phase 2 HS trial, HiSCR at week 12 was about 57% versus 26% on placebo.
Placebo-treated HS patients usually show a 30-45% fall in abscess and inflammatory nodule count by week 12-16.

reason: Weight loss from a GLP-1/GIP agonist cuts AHI strongly (tirzepatide -20 to -24 events/h versus placebo), so success is very likely if reported; the real uncertainty is whether the 52-week result appears before mid-2027.
rationale: HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist with roughly 15-20% weight loss in Chinese obesity trials. Tirzepatide in SURMOUNT-OSA lowered AHI by 25-29 events/h versus 5 on placebo. With 70 per arm and an SD near 20, even a smaller effect would be significant. The record still shows recruiting with a 52-week treatment and a December 2026 completion, so timing is uncertain and may be stale.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide reduced AHI by 25.3 (no PAP) and 29.3 (PAP) events/h versus 5.3 and 5.5 on placebo at week 52.
HRS9531 produced mean weight loss near 17-19% at 48 weeks in Chinese adults with obesity.

reason: Phase 1b showed double-digit letter gains in macular edema secondary to inflammation, but sham arms can gain several letters and the phase 3 effect usually shrinks versus early single-arm data.
rationale: KSI-101 blocks IL-6 and VEGF, both drivers of uveitic macular edema, and the APEX phase 1b gave large BCVA gains and CST drops. A sham-controlled phase 3 with about 150 per arm and an SD near 11 letters is well powered for a 4-6 letter difference. Risks are a high sham response and effect shrinkage. The record still lists recruiting with a February 2027 completion, so topline may slip toward mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In the APEX phase 1b, KSI-101 5 mg improved BCVA by roughly 10+ letters at week 24 in MESI.
Sham arms in uveitic macular edema trials typically gain 0-5 letters at about 6 months.

reason: An oral PCSK9 inhibitor gave about -50% LDL-C versus placebo at 12 weeks in phase 2b; with 3,100 patients, failure on the primary is close to impossible, and the open question is only when AstraZeneca reports.
rationale: AZD0780 is an oral PCSK9 inhibitor. The PURSUIT phase 2b showed a placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction of about 50% at 12 weeks (30 mg) on top of statins. With roughly 1,550 patients per arm, a 40-55% effect is certain to be significant. The registered primary completion is January 2027 (end of 52 weeks), so a topline release or congress disclosure by June 2027 is likely but not certain.

assumptions.claim: AZD0780 30 mg lowered LDL-C by about 50.7% versus placebo at week 12 on top of statin in PURSUIT.
Enlicitide, another oral PCSK9 inhibitor, lowered LDL-C by about 55-60% versus placebo at week 24 in phase 3.

reason: Oral PCSK9 inhibition works in HeFH with intact LDL receptors; a 473-patient 2:1 trial should show a large LDL-C reduction, so the open question is only when AstraZeneca reports.
rationale: AZD0780 lowered LDL-C by about 50% versus placebo in the phase 2b PURSUIT. HeFH patients keep functional LDL receptors, and PCSK9 inhibitors lower LDL-C by 50-60% in HeFH (evolocumab RUTHERFORD-2, alirocumab). With 315 versus 158 patients, success is near certain. A small placebo group makes the placebo mean noisier. Disclosure timing is the main uncertainty, likely alongside AZURE-LDL.

assumptions.claim: Evolocumab lowered LDL-C by about 60% versus placebo at week 12 in HeFH patients in RUTHERFORD-2.
AZD0780 30 mg lowered LDL-C by about 50.7% versus placebo at week 12 on top of statin in PURSUIT.

reason: Single-dose RE104 trial in adjustment disorder with 100 patients across 32 US sites is still recruiting about 15 months after start. Registered primary completion of Nov 2026 looks tight for cancer and neurological patients, so a slip past Feb 2027 is more likely than not. Private sponsor, so results posting by Aug 2027 is unlikely.

Enrolment is complete (active, not recruiting) and the primary period is only 6 months, so the Nov 2026 primary completion should hold. The record also contains a long open-label extension, and a public sponsor usually posts results later, so posting by Aug 2027 is unlikely.

Small 36-patient, 14-day safety study started June 2026 at 8 US sites with strict criteria (non-smokers, BMI under 30, stable levodopa). Still recruiting in Oct 2026 with primary completion Dec 2026, so a slip beyond Mar 2027 is about a coin flip. Small sponsor and academic collaborators rarely post results within months.
Anti-CD73 add-on to PD-1 plus chemotherapy has a weak track record in unselected NSCLC, and a 150-patient randomized phase 2 with about 95 PFS events needs HR below roughly 0.67 for significance.
rationale: Uliledlimab (CD73) showed ORR signals mainly in CD73-high patients in earlier phase 2 work, but this enrolment is all-comer and the control is already strong sintilimab plus chemotherapy (ORIENT-11 median PFS 8.9 months). CD73 and adenosine blockade added to PD-(L)1 has not clearly improved PFS elsewhere. With about 95 events the significance bar is HR about 0.67, which looks demanding for a modest add-on effect.

assumptions.claim: Sintilimab plus pemetrexed and platinum gave median PFS of about 8.9 months in non-squamous NSCLC.
Anti-CD73 oleclumab added to durvalumab gave only a modest PFS signal in stage III NSCLC (phase 2).
assumptions.source: COAST, Herbst et al., Cancer Discovery 2022

reason: A 12-week study of a novel MAO-B inhibitor with only 22 vs 11 patients at the top dose can detect only a difference of about 2.3 percentage points of body weight, while the plausible true effect is smaller.
rationale: KDS2010 is a reversible MAO-B inhibitor with no established weight-loss effect in humans beyond preliminary phase 1 hints. Over 12 weeks with lifestyle modification, placebo loss is about 1-2%. With a 22 vs 11 split and an SD near 3%, significance needs a difference of about 2.3 points. I expect a modest effect, so reaching significance is unlikely but possible given sponsor optimism.

assumptions.claim: Placebo plus lifestyle intervention produces only small short-term weight loss in obesity trials (about 2.4% at 68 weeks in STEP 1).

reason: Enrolment spans heterogeneous developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, so a mix of etiologies may dilute the effect of a sodium channel blocker, and placebo response and seizure variability are high.
rationale: Relutrigine is a potent persistent-sodium-current blocker, and the sponsor reported large motor seizure reductions in the SCN2A/SCN8A EMBOLD study. This broader DEE trial with about 53 per arm has high seizure-count variability and mixed etiologies, but a 30%+ placebo-adjusted reduction would be significant. Sponsor has a recent record of positive, fast readouts and the trial is fully enrolled with primary completion Dec 2026.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-controlled DEE trials usually show placebo changes in motor seizure frequency of roughly -5% to -20%.
