assumptions.source: Marigold ganaxolone CDKL5 trial, Lancet Neurol 2022

assumptions.claim: Relutrigine produced a large reduction in motor seizures in the SCN2A/SCN8A DEE EMBOLD study.

reason: Failure is very unlikely: CagriSema produced about 17-20 points more weight loss than placebo in REDEFINE 1, and this trial has 609 patients. Main uncertainty is only the size of the effect and the timing of disclosure.
rationale: REDEFINE 1 showed -20.4% with CagriSema vs -3.0% placebo at 68 weeks in a similar population without diabetes. A 609-patient trial at 80 weeks with a 2:1 split is hugely powered for this difference. Effect size is the only open question, and it hinges on dose and estimand. Primary completion is Mar 2027, so public disclosure by June 2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: CagriSema 2.4/2.4 mg gave -20.4% weight change vs -3.0% with placebo at 68 weeks in adults with obesity without diabetes.
Placebo arms in obesity trials without diabetes lose roughly 2-4% of body weight at 68-80 weeks.

reason: Anti-TSLP antibodies have shown weak efficacy in atopic dermatitis (tezepelumab phase 2a), so a mean EASI difference of at least about 15 points with 55 per arm may not be reached.
rationale: ATI-045 (bosakitug) is an anti-TSLP antibody. Tezepelumab did not clearly beat placebo in atopic dermatitis in phase 2a, suggesting TSLP blockade alone is a less potent mechanism than IL-4Ra or IL-13. With 55 per arm and an SD of EASI percent change near 40, a difference of about 15 points is needed for significance. A longer 24-week window and long half-life may help somewhat.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab with topical corticosteroids did not significantly improve EASI-50 response vs placebo in moderate-to-severe AD in phase 2a.
assumptions.source: Simpson et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2019 (NCT02525094)

reason: Topical JAK inhibition is unproven in palmoplantar pustulosis, a mainly IL-17/IL-23-driven disease with thick skin that limits penetration, and a 68 vs 67 proof-of-concept needs a difference of about 13 points on PPPASI-75.
rationale: Delgocitinib cream works in chronic hand eczema (DELTA 1: IGA-CHE success about 20% vs 10%), but PPP is a neutrophilic pustular disease on thick palmoplantar skin. Vehicle response on PPPASI-75 is probably around 10-15%. With 68 vs 67 patients, a difference of about 13 percentage points is needed. A true effect near 10 points gives roughly one-third odds of reaching significance.
evidence: DELTA 1 delgocitinib cream chronic hand eczema (Lancet 2024)

assumptions.claim: Delgocitinib cream 20 mg/g beat vehicle in chronic hand eczema with IGA-CHE treatment success about 20% vs 10%.

reason: A 120-subject radiolabeled red cell recovery study at 2 sites is still recruiting with primary completion registered for Dec 2026. Each subject needs a 35-day storage cycle plus radioisotope work, so recruitment typically drifts. The sponsor is a motivated public company that wants the data for a regulatory filing, so a slip is likely but not certain to exceed 90 days.

Factor XI mAb with strong phase 2 signal against enoxaparin in TKA; risk is a smaller-than-hoped effect, a hierarchical testing structure (apixaban non-inferiority/superiority) or an enoxaparin arm that performs better than historical venography rates.
rationale: Factor XI inhibitors reduced venography-detected VTE after TKA by 50-80% versus enoxaparin in phase 2 (abelacimab, milvexian 200 mg bid, osocimab) and Regeneron's own REGN7508 phase 2 favoured it. With about 667 per arm and 13% control incidence, a halving gives high power. Residual risk: lower dose, small effect, multiple-comparison hierarchy.

assumptions.claim: In ANT-007, VTE after TKA was about 13% with enoxaparin versus about 4-5% with abelacimab 75-150 mg.
In AXIOMATIC-TKR, VTE was about 21% with enoxaparin versus about 8% with milvexian 200 mg twice daily.

reason: Only 16 patients in a diary-based symptom crossover; placebo response, period effects and high between-patient variance can hide a real effect of ophthalmic B-VEC, though the within-patient design helps.
rationale: Mechanistically sound (restoring COL7 in corneal epithelium) and earlier open-label/compassionate eye-drop reports were encouraging, and Krystal's topical B-VEC won GEM-3. But n=16, subjective symptom diaries and a crossover with possible carry-over make significance uncertain. Still recruiting in late 2026, so reading is likely mid-2027 or later.

assumptions.claim: Topical B-VEC significantly improved wound closure versus placebo in GEM-3 in DEB.

reason: Small safety/PK platform study in China with primary completion already passed; AstraZeneca usually posts results around 12 months after completion, so posting by August 2027 is possible but not likely.

Botulinum toxin has historically failed or been marginal in episodic migraine; placebo response is large with 6-14 migraine days at baseline, so a roughly 0.8 day separation may not reach significance.
rationale: Earlier botulinum toxin trials in episodic migraine (e.g. Relja 2007) did not beat placebo, and gains in CM-sized effects (about 1.5-2 days) do not carry over to lower-frequency patients. With about 332 per arm and SD about 3.8, a 0.8-day effect gives roughly 70% power, and true effect may be smaller. Merz designed this pivotal with two doses, hoping the higher exposure works.
evidence: Relja 2007 botulinum toxin episodic migraine trial

assumptions.claim: Onabotulinumtoxin A did not significantly outperform placebo in multiple episodic migraine prophylaxis trials.
In chronic migraine, botulinum toxin A beat placebo by about 1.4-2 headache days at week 24 in PREEMPT.

reason: Botulinum toxin A is an established chronic migraine preventive; main failure routes are a large placebo response or Dose A being the lower dose with a smaller effect than PREEMPT-like 1.5-2 days.
rationale: Class effect established: Botox beat placebo by about 2 migraine days in PREEMPT, and Xeomin is a comparable toxin. With about 269 per arm and SD about 7.5, a 1.8-day difference gives roughly 80% power. Risks are placebo response and modern diary scoring shrinking the gap; dose A is presumably the main efficacy dose.

assumptions.claim: In PREEMPT, onabotulinumtoxin A reduced headache days by about 8.4 versus 6.6 for placebo at week 24.
Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxin A) has similar potency units to onabotulinumtoxin A in clinical use.

reason: Chinese multi-arm phase 2 with 192 patients still recruiting; registry dates often slip and arms or outcomes (ORR/PFS in specific arms) may be refined, but a China-only sponsor rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

Exploratory open-label dosing-regimen study with primary completion Sep 2026; Vera will likely post within the 12-month window ending around Sep 2027, so posting before end-August 2027 is possible but not the default.

Cardiac myosin inhibitors have repeatedly beaten placebo in obstructive HCM with large effects; residual risk comes from the undefined response criteria and a high placebo response rate in a Chinese population.
rationale: Mavacamten (EXPLORER-HCM: 37% vs 17% responders) and aficamten (SEQUOIA-HCM) set a strong class precedent with 114 per arm and entry LVOT gradients of 50 mmHg or more. A responder difference of about 20-30 points gives very high power. The response definition is unknown, but any gradient- or NYHA-based definition favours a myosin inhibitor.

assumptions.claim: In EXPLORER-HCM, the composite response was 36.7% with mavacamten versus 17.2% with placebo at week 30.
Mavacamten reduced Valsalva LVOT gradient significantly versus placebo in the Chinese EXPLORER-CN trial.

reason: A metabolic modulator in nHCM has shown only small, noisy KCCQ gains versus a sizeable placebo response, and mavacamten failed in nHCM; a 12-week KCCQ endpoint needs about 5 points to reach significance with 83 per arm.
rationale: IMPROVE-HCM (phase 2, n=67) showed a signal on VE/VCO2 and KCCQ in nHCM, but small samples overstate effects. At SD about 16 and 83 per arm, significance needs a roughly 5-point separation; the likely true effect is nearer 3 points with a placebo gain of about 4-5. Mavacamten's ODYSSEY-HCM failure in nHCM adds caution.

assumptions.claim: IMPROVE-HCM reported improved VE/VCO2 and KCCQ in nHCM with ninerafaxstat versus placebo.
assumptions.source: Abozguia et al, JACC Heart Fail 2024 (IMPROVE-HCM)

assumptions.claim: Mavacamten did not meet its primary endpoints in non-obstructive HCM in ODYSSEY-HCM.

reason: A DPP-4 inhibitor added to dapagliflozin plus metformin reliably lowers HbA1c by about 0.4-0.6 points; the main uncertainty is the multi-arm comparison structure and whether this exact contrast is the tested primary.
rationale: DPP-4 inhibitors add roughly 0.4-0.6 points HbA1c on top of SGLT2i plus metformin (saxagliptin add-on to dapagliflozin plus metformin, Mathieu 2015), and prusogliptin is an approved Chinese DPP-4 inhibitor. With 163 per arm and SD about 0.85, standard error is about 0.1, so significance is very likely.
evidence: Mathieu 2015 saxagliptin add-on to dapagliflozin plus metformin (Diabetes Care)

assumptions.claim: Adding saxagliptin to dapagliflozin plus metformin lowered HbA1c by about 0.35-0.5 points more than placebo at week 24.
Dapagliflozin 10 mg added to metformin lowered HbA1c by about 0.8-0.9 points at week 24 from a baseline near 8.

reason: Only 20 per arm with a photo-based blister area endpoint in a heterogeneous rare skin disease; a topical keratin-aggregate targeting gel needs a large effect to reach p<0.05 against a vehicle that also soothes skin.
rationale: Small private sponsor, 40 patients, 2 sites, still recruiting a year after start so readout likely slips past mid-2027. Blister area in EBS is highly variable and vehicle responses are large, so significance with n=20 per arm needs a big effect. Any early report is more likely if positive, which lifts p_met given publication. Prior open-label signals of the gel exist but no controlled proof.
evidence: Diacerein 1% topical EBS phase 2/3 program (mixed results)

assumptions.claim: Randomised topical trials in EBS with small n have mostly shown modest or non-significant differences against vehicle.
assumptions.source: Diacerein topical EBS phase 2/3 trials (Castle Creek), 2019-2021

assumptions.claim: The trial is still recruiting with a registered primary completion of 2027-01 and 40 patients planned.

reason: Single-centre Italian cosmetic nail patch study with a safety primary; likely to finish roughly on time, but the record may simply not be updated and no results posting is expected from this sponsor/CRO.
Children 6 to <12 with severe AA, many with AT/AU, may respond less than adolescents; a lower-than-expected SALT<=20 or <=10 rate on the higher dose is the main way this misses.
rationale: Ritlecitinib 50 mg gave SALT<=20 in about 23% vs 1.6% placebo in ALLEGRO-2b/3 (ages 12+). With about 69 per arm, even 12-15% vs 3% is significant, and either dose may win. Risks are weaker response in younger children with AT/AU and a SALT<=10 co-requirement; placebo response in children is slightly higher. Pfizer data should be positive.

assumptions.claim: Ritlecitinib 50 mg achieved SALT<=20 at week 24 in about 23% of patients aged 12+ vs about 1.6% on placebo.
Trial enrolls 208 participants in 1:1:1 allocation with primary endpoints at week 24.

reason: If it misses, it is most likely a non-inferiority shortfall of the HA/CaHA filler against Perlane at month 6 or a tight margin, but registration-style China filler trials usually succeed.
rationale: Registration trial of a hybrid HA/CaHA filler against an established HA comparator in China; month 6 MFVDS responder rates are typically 75-90% with both products, and HArmonyCa is expected to last at least as long. Non-inferiority with 168 vs 84 patients is very likely met; superiority on secondaries is unlikely to be formally shown.
evidence: Restylane Lyft/Perlane mid-face volume pivotal trials (MFVDS responder rates)

assumptions.claim: Comparator HA fillers show about 75-90% MFVDS 1-point responder rates at month 6 in mid-face volume trials.
assumptions.source: Restylane Lyft mid-face pivotal study (FDA PMA summary)

assumptions.claim: Trial is complete with 252 participants in 2:1 allocation at 9 sites in China.

reason: TYK2 inhibition has a weak track record in ulcerative colitis, and with about 60 per arm a placebo remission rate near 8% means the drug needs roughly 22-25% remission to reach significance.
rationale: D-2570 is a TYK2 inhibitor; deucravacitinib did not clearly separate from placebo in UC induction. Chinese phase 2 with 120 patients and possibly several dose arms gives low power for the highest dose. Placebo remission by this stringent modified Mayo definition is likely under 12%. Results most likely to be shown if positive, lifting p_met modestly.

assumptions.claim: Placebo clinical remission at week 12 in UC phase 2 induction trials is typically 5-12%.
assumptions.source: Pooled UC induction trials (e.g. etrasimod ELEVATE UC 52, 2023)

assumptions.claim: Trial is a 120-patient placebo-controlled phase 2 with primary completion registered as 2026-07-30.

reason: Only about 40 per arm and a 12-week FVC change with SD around 150 mL means a difference of roughly 65 mL is needed for significance, which a novel IL-11 pathway antibody may not deliver.
rationale: Phase IIa, 81 patients, 12-week FVC. Placebo declines about 50 mL in 12 weeks; the SE of the difference is about 33 mL, so a significant result needs a true effect of at least 65 mL, similar to nerandomilast's phase 2. A first-in-IPF mechanism has modest prior odds. Also, the study completes 2027-06-22, so a public primary result by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: IPF placebo patients lose roughly 50-80 mL FVC over 12 weeks in phase 2 trials.
Trial plans 81 patients with primary completion 2027-03-11 and study completion 2027-06-22.

reason: Non-inferiority could fail if shorter-duration BEM/RZR underperforms in genotype 3 or cirrhosis, or if losses to follow-up at ex-US sites depress the ITT cure rate in one arm.
rationale: Phase 2 BEM/RZR gave SVR12 near 98% including 8-week regimens. SOF/VEL cures about 95-97% so non-inferiority with 440 per arm is likely at a standard 4-5% margin. Risks: genotype 3, compensated cirrhosis, missing data in ex-US sites. Atea is a listed company and should announce topline soon after primary completion in 2026-12.
evidence: Atea BEM/RZR HCV phase 2 (2024, SVR12 about 98%)

assumptions.claim: SOF/VEL achieves SVR12 of roughly 95-99% in treatment-naive patients across genotypes.
assumptions.source: ASTRAL-1/2/3, Feld et al and Foster et al, NEJM 2015

assumptions.claim: The trial enrols 880 DAA-naive adults with compensated or no cirrhosis, primary completion registered 2026-12.

reason: The primary population is the LA C/D subset, probably only 60-100 patients per arm, so even a real 12-15 point healing advantage over lansoprazole at week 4 can miss significance.
rationale: P-CABs heal severe erosive esophagitis faster than PPIs: vonoprazan beat lansoprazole in LA C/D subgroups and linaprazan glurate showed strong phase 2 healing. Week 4 lansoprazole healing in C/D is about 70-75%, leaving 10-20 points of headroom. Main uncertainty is the size of the C/D subset and whether superiority was prespecified. A listed Swedish sponsor should disclose topline promptly.

assumptions.claim: Lansoprazole 30 mg heals roughly 70-75% of LA C/D esophagitis by week 4, below P-CAB rates.
assumptions.source: PHALCON-EE and Japanese vonoprazan EE trials (Laine 2023; Ashida 2016)

assumptions.claim: The trial randomises 523 participants about 1:1:1 and the primary analysis is in baseline LA C/D at week 4.

reason: SARA effects of a TRH analog in slowly progressive ataxia are small versus placebo noise, and earlier Japanese confirmatory studies of this compound were at best mixed.
rationale: KPS-0373 (rovatirelin, a TRH analog) has a modest expected SARA benefit, about 0.4-0.5 points at 24 weeks, with SD near 2.2, so 71 per arm gives roughly 40% power. Kissei has already run earlier confirmatory studies and is running a third, which suggests the earlier ones did not cleanly succeed. Taltirelin showed small SARA gains in Japanese trials. Placebo drift is small. I put the chance of a significant result slightly below one in three.
evidence: Taltirelin hydrate Japanese phase 3 in spinocerebellar degeneration (2009-2010)
Kissei KPS-0373 (rovatirelin) earlier SCD confirmatory studies, Japan

assumptions.claim: Placebo-controlled SARA differences for TRH analogs in Japanese SCD trials were below one point at 24 weeks.
Kissei is running a third confirmatory phase 3 of KPS-0373 after earlier confirmatory studies.

reason: 177Lu-DOTATATE against SSA in progressive SSTR-positive NETs gave HR near 0.2 in NETTER-1; failure would come from crossover or an unusual Chinese population, but timing is the bigger issue, as it is still recruiting.
rationale: NETTER-1 showed 177Lu-DOTATATE gave a 20-month PFS rate of 65% versus 11% with high-dose octreotide (HR 0.21) in midgut NETs progressing on SSA; NETTER-2 and COMPETE support a large effect. Same mechanism, SSTR-positive confirmed, and an 18-month PFS design with 184 patients are well powered for an HR near 0.3. Main uncertainty is timing: the trial is still recruiting, so an 18-month rate cannot read out soon.

assumptions.claim: In NETTER-1, 177Lu-DOTATATE gave a 20-month PFS rate of 65.2% versus 10.8% for high-dose octreotide LAR, HR 0.21.
The record lists the trial as recruiting with a registered primary completion of 2026-11-24 and an 18-month PFS-rate primary.

reason: A GLP-1/GIP agonist added to basal insulin lowers HbA1c far more than placebo; the only realistic failure is a large placebo response from insulin titration, which is unlikely to erase a 1+ point gap.
rationale: Tirzepatide in SURPASS-5 (basal insulin add-on, 40 weeks) reduced HbA1c by about 1.7 points versus placebo; HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist with similar phase 2 HbA1c efficacy in Chinese T2D. With 100 per arm and SD near 1.0, power is essentially complete. Risk is timing (recruiting at snapshot, 40-week treatment) rather than efficacy.

assumptions.claim: In SURPASS-5, tirzepatide 15 mg reduced HbA1c by 2.59% versus 0.93% for placebo at 40 weeks on top of titrated basal insulin.
HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist from Hengrui being developed for T2D and obesity in China.

reason: Denosumab biosimilar equivalence trials on lumbar spine BMD at month 12 almost always show equivalence; the likelier problem is timing, since the study is recruiting and 12-month data will come late.
rationale: Denosumab is a highly characterised biologic and biosimilar programs (GP2411, SB16, CT-P41, FKS518) have all met their LS-BMD equivalence margins, with 278 patients giving good power against typical margins of about 1.45-1.5 points. Qilu already has an approved denosumab biosimilar (QL1206, bone metastasis). The main uncertainty is publication timing, as Qilu rarely issues press releases and month-12 data may not exist before mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Denosumab biosimilar candidates have met their LS-BMD percent-change equivalence margins at month 12 in postmenopausal osteoporosis trials.
The trial has a month-12 LS-BMD primary and a registered primary completion of 2027-01.

reason: MDD monotherapy trials carry large placebo responses (about 10 HAM-D points at day 42), and an oral allopregnanolone prodrug needs about a 2.5-point effect; neurosteroid MDD results have been mixed.
rationale: Phase 2 MDD trials succeed roughly 40-45% of the time. Zuranolone had mixed results across MOUNTAIN, WATERFALL and CORAL, and the placebo response in 6-week MDD monotherapy trials is large, about 10 HAM-D points. With 180 per arm and SD near 8, a 2.5 point difference is detectable, but the dose is unknown and the effect of an oral prodrug is unproven. Sponsor is private, so topline timing is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Placebo HAM-D-17 improvement in MDD monotherapy trials is typically 9-12 points by week 6.
SPT-300 is an oral prodrug of allopregnanolone in a 360-patient phase 2 with a day-42 HAM-D-17 primary.

reason: With about 20 patients per arm and SPPB change SD near 1.7, only a large effect would reach significance; sarcopenia drug trials rarely show clear SPPB benefit in 12 weeks.
rationale: A 12-week phase 2 with 20 patients per arm has roughly 25-30% power for a 0.8-point SPPB difference, and sarcopenia drugs have mostly failed on functional endpoints. Several dose arms against one placebo help slightly (any dose counts), and small sponsors often report favourable subgroup or trend language, but the strict criterion is a significant primary. Control SPPB change is near zero to +0.5 with practice effects.

assumptions.claim: Placebo SPPB change over 12 weeks in sarcopenia trials is small, about 0 to +0.5 points.
The record lists 80 patients across three doses and placebo, with SPPB change at week 12 as primary.

reason: A small Australian psilocybin trial with specialised dosing sessions and an 87-patient target, started Oct 2025 and still recruiting; enrolment is likely slower than the 2027-03 completion date, and a small sponsor carries some funding risk.
Roche's formulation bridging studies usually show bioequivalence; failure would come from a true formulation PK difference or high between-patient variability in AUC or Cmax.
rationale: Roche designs bioequivalence bridging studies after confirming formulation PK; OCARINA II met its AUC non-inferiority between SC and IV ocrelizumab. Here 193 patients and standard 80-125% margins give good power for AUC0-12W if formulations are close. Both AUC and Cmax must pass, which lowers the chance slightly. Primary completion has passed, so data should exist; public release timing depends on Roche's posting practice and congress timing.

assumptions.claim: OCARINA II met its pharmacokinetic primary (AUC0-12W) for SC ocrelizumab versus IV.
The record lists AUC0-12W and Cmax as co-primary with a registered primary completion of 2026-09-17.

reason: A small Galderma PK/PD proof-of-concept study that is no longer recruiting with primary completion 2026-12; unlikely to slip beyond March 2027, and results posting by August 2027 is possible but not routine for a phase 2.

ONWARDS 6 showed icodec non-inferior to degludec in T1D (ETD 0.04); with 877 patients a 0.3-0.4 point margin is very likely met, and the only realistic risk is a surprise efficacy gap versus glargine.
rationale: ONWARDS 6 (T1D, icodec vs degludec) met HbA1c non-inferiority with an estimated difference of 0.04 points. Glargine U100 is a comparable basal comparator, and 877 patients give a very narrow confidence interval against the usual 0.3-0.4 margin. Novo typically reports completed phase 3 trials in its quarterly report, so a public statement by June 2027 is likely. Time-in-range is unlikely to be significantly better than glargine.

assumptions.claim: In ONWARDS 6 (T1D), icodec was non-inferior to degludec for HbA1c change, with an estimated treatment difference of 0.04 points.
assumptions.source: Philis-Tsimikas et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2023 (NCT04848480)

assumptions.claim: The record lists a 26-week HbA1c change primary and a registered primary completion of 2027-01-25.

reason: Class effect of anti-TL1A is large, but about 40 per arm in a refractory Russian population leaves a real chance that no dose clears p<0.05 on week-14 remission.
rationale: TL1A blockade has shown large phase 2 effects in UC (tulisokibart 26% vs 1% remission; duvakitug roughly 16-27 points over placebo). Placebo remission on the strict modified Mayo definition with central reading is usually under 12%. With about 40 per arm and any dose counting, a 20-point difference is significant about 65-75% of the time. Biocad molecule potency is unknown and the population is refractory.

assumptions.claim: Tulisokibart induction gave clinical remission of 26% vs 1% on placebo at week 12 in moderate-to-severe UC.
Duvakitug phase 2 in UC showed placebo-adjusted clinical remission of roughly 16 to 27 points.

reason: An oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist at the top dose should beat dapagliflozin on HbA1c, but the margin may be modest if the dose is limited by GI tolerability.
rationale: HDM1002 is an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist. Orforglipron beat dapagliflozin 10 mg on HbA1c by about 0.5-0.9 points in ACHIEVE-2. Dapagliflozin add-on to metformin lowers HbA1c about 0.8-1.0, and baseline here is 7.5-11%. About 200 per arm with SD near 1.0 gives ample power for a 0.5-point gap. Risks are a weaker molecule than the orforglipron class benchmark and the possibility that the comparison is non-inferiority.
evidence: Dapagliflozin add-on to metformin, Bailey Lancet 2010

assumptions.claim: Dapagliflozin 10 mg added to metformin lowered HbA1c by about 0.8 points at 24 weeks.
Orforglipron lowered HbA1c more than dapagliflozin 10 mg in T2DM on metformin.

reason: Only 30 patients (20 vs 10) and perhaps 15-20 PFS events: even a real benefit would rarely reach p<0.05, and OS will be immature.
rationale: Single-centre 2:1 phase 2 of an unfamiliar agent added to pazopanib in first-line clear cell RCC. First-line pazopanib gives median PFS near 8-10 months (COMPARZ). With about 18 events a significant hazard ratio needs roughly 0.4 or lower. Small phase 2s are often reported descriptively, and a combination with a TKI could still fail. Reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely, since follow-up started in late 2025.

assumptions.claim: First-line pazopanib in advanced RCC gives median PFS of about 8.4 months.

reason: 80 patients split over five infection types leave very few cUTI patients per arm, and all co-primaries must be met, so formal superiority on every one is unlikely.
rationale: The new beta-lactamase inhibitor combination likely beats colistin or tigecycline regimens numerically in CRE infections (TANGO II showed 59% vs 27% cUTI/overall cure with meropenem-vaborbactam). But with perhaps 10-20 cUTI patients per arm and three co-primary endpoints across other sites, statistical significance on all is improbable. Recruitment in CRE is slow and an open-label BAT comparator is heterogeneous.
evidence: TANGO II meropenem-vaborbactam vs BAT in CRE, 2018

assumptions.claim: In CRE infections, meropenem-vaborbactam gave clinical cure at test of cure of 59% vs 27% for best available therapy.
assumptions.source: Wunderink et al., Infect Dis Ther 2018 (TANGO II, NCT02168946)

reason: A capsid assembly modulator on top of NA should clearly lower HBV DNA, but the main risk is spontaneous HBV DNA decline to below the limit on placebo plus NA over 48 weeks.
rationale: Capsid assembly modulators have direct antiviral action and added to NA in viremic HBeAg-positive patients produce much larger HBV DNA suppression than NA alone. GST-HG141 phase 2 data on NA add-on showed marked DNA declines. The population is NA-treated with DNA above 50 IU/mL, so placebo patients also improve slowly, but with 263 per arm a difference around 40 points is hugely significant.

assumptions.claim: Capsid assembly modulators added to NA give greater HBV DNA suppression than NA plus placebo in viremic CHB.
assumptions.source: GST-HG141 phase 2 results presented at EASL/APASL, 2023-2024

reason: Placebo-controlled add-on of a well-established SGLT2 inhibitor to metformin plus DPP-4 inhibitor; a 0.5-0.7 point placebo-adjusted HbA1c drop is near certain to be significant at 85 per arm.
rationale: Empagliflozin add-on to metformin gave placebo-adjusted HbA1c reductions of 0.57-0.64 at 24 weeks (EMPA-REG MET), and similar effects occur on a DPP-4 background. With about 85 per arm and SD near 0.8, the standard error is about 0.12, so significance is almost assured. This is a fixed-dose-combination development trial where such outcomes are the norm.
evidence: Empagliflozin add-on to linagliptin plus metformin, Rosenstock 2015

assumptions.claim: Empagliflozin 10 or 25 mg added to metformin lowered HbA1c by 0.57 to 0.64 points vs placebo at week 24.
assumptions.source: Haring et al., Diabetes Care 2014 (EMPA-REG MET)

reason: Small 24-patient crossover in a rare disease at a single Belgian site; recruitment likely slips, results are unlikely to be posted on the registry by August 2027, and the long list of safety primaries invites edits.
A triglyceride-lowering injectable dosed at the top level against saline should give a large, significant drop; failure would mainly come from reporting on a different form of the measure.
rationale: TG is the sole primary of a dose-finding phase 2 and the drug is presumably a lipid-targeting siRNA or antibody (APOC3 or ANGPTL3 class), where placebo-adjusted TG reductions of 40-60% are typical (plozasiran SHASTA-2). With 224 patients over several arms, the top dose has about 40 patients and SD of percent change near 35, so significance is very likely. Variability in how the TG endpoint is reported is the main uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: APOC3 siRNA plozasiran lowered triglycerides by roughly 50-57% vs placebo at week 24 in hypertriglyceridemia.

reason: A beta-blocker-derived lean-mass preserving drug needs about 150 g per 4 weeks over placebo to be significant at 40 per arm, and both primaries (on and after semaglutide) must be met.
rationale: Semaglutide causes lean mass loss of roughly 2 kg over 20 weeks. The (S)-pindolol mechanism showed lean mass gain in cachexia, but the effect in obesity on semaglutide is unproven. With about 40 per arm and an SD near 300 g per 4 weeks, power for a 100 g effect is only about 40%. Both primaries (PROACT 1 and 2) must succeed, which lowers the chance further.

assumptions.claim: In obese adults on semaglutide, lean body mass falls by roughly 25-40% of total weight lost.
assumptions.source: STEP-1 DXA substudy, Wilding et al., NEJM 2021

reason: Inclisiran's LDL-C effect is robust and 150 per arm is ample, so only an unusually strong placebo-arm LDL fall after ACS (statin intensification) could shrink the gap.
rationale: Inclisiran lowered LDL-C by about 50% vs placebo in ORION-10/11, and in-hospital ACS initiation in V-INCEPTION gave about 60% reduction. In ACS, placebo patients also fall 25-40% from the acute baseline as statin is intensified, but the placebo-adjusted gap should still be 25-35 points. With 150 per arm and SD near 28, power is above 99%. Reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely because Novartis tends to present at ESC or AHA.

assumptions.claim: Inclisiran lowered LDL-C about 50% vs placebo at day 510 in ASCVD patients on statins.
In-hospital start of inclisiran after ACS gave much greater LDL-C reduction than usual care at day 90.

reason: Dose-ranging phase 2 in moderate-to-severe AD with 225 patients over several arms; the top dose only needs to beat placebo on percent change in EASI at week 16, but the mechanism is undisclosed and a private sponsor may be slow or selective in disclosure.
rationale: Phase 2 dose-ranging AD trials of active biologics or oral agents usually separate from placebo on EASI percent change at week 16 at the top dose, with placebo around -30%. The mechanism is not disclosed, the arms are small (225 over several doses), and the primary outcome wording is vague, so I discount the success chance. Disclosure by a private sponsor tends to follow positive data.
evidence: NCT04837573 lebrikizumab phase 2b ADhere-style placebo EASI change

assumptions.claim: In SOLO1 the placebo arm had a mean EASI percent improvement of about 38% at week 16 against about 72% with dupilumab.

reason: Small two-site randomized dose-exploration phase 2 in Chinese CRC with an enrollment pause and dose selection step, so the registered end date of 2026-12-30 is likely to slip or the status to stay recruiting; early stopping and posted results are unlikely.

Anti-TSLP in CRSwNP has strong precedent, so NPS and NCS in all patients should be met; the extra risk is that all four co-primaries, including the two in the smaller eosinophilic subgroup, must pass.
rationale: Tezepelumab cut NPS by about 2 points versus placebo in WAYPOINT and other type 2 biologics do similarly in China, so 123 per arm is ample for NPS and NCS in all patients. The four co-primaries must all pass, and the eosinophilic subgroup is smaller, which trims the probability. A TSLP antibody should work in both subtypes.

assumptions.claim: In WAYPOINT tezepelumab reduced endoscopic NPS by about 2 points versus placebo at week 52 and nasal congestion score by about 1 point.
In SINUS-24 the placebo arm's NPS changed by roughly 0 from baseline at week 24 while dupilumab changed by about -2.
assumptions.source: SINUS-24, NCT02912468, Bachert et al. Lancet 2019

reason: Strict clinical cure (all signs and symptoms zero) at day 28 carries a placebo response around one third; with about 111 per arm, a 15-point benefit gives only moderate power, though two active arms give two chances.
rationale: Boric acid has real antifungal activity and either of two regimens can win, but the endpoint is strict (composite score zero at day 28) and the placebo arm usually reaches 28-35% in VVC trials, as in the ibrexafungerp trials. With 111 per arm a 15-point gain gives about 60-70% power, and sponsors disclose mainly positive results.

assumptions.claim: In VANISH-303 the placebo arm had a clinical cure rate of about 28% against about 50% with ibrexafungerp at the test-of-cure visit.

reason: About 40 per arm and a demanding endpoint (staining fully resolved in a Sjogren's population with mild baseline staining) leave little power; vehicle effects on staining and symptoms are sizeable in dry eye trials.
rationale: Lubricin may help the ocular surface, but complete resolution of corneal staining after 28 days is a high bar, and baseline grades of only 1-2 limit the room for a difference. With about 40 per arm, a 15-point gain from a vehicle rate near 12% is borderline significant. Small private sponsor, still recruiting, so late and uncertain disclosure.

reason: Crossover with only about 15 patients and two co-primary outcomes (corneal staining and total symptom VAS) that must both be met; enrolment of a rare population is slow.
rationale: A 15-patient within-patient crossover can detect a one-grade staining difference but is fragile, and the VAS co-primary is noisy with a large vehicle response. Both must reach significance, and recruiting in a rare disease at three sites is likely to push completion beyond June 2027.

reason: Phase 2a multiple ascending dose study with about one year of follow-up per patient and 48 planned; it was still recruiting in October 2026, so the registered end of 2026-12-31 cannot hold and the date is very likely to move.

Phase 3 versus cinacalcet needs only non-inferiority (margin unknown) on the share with more than 50% iPTH reduction; a new dual-target agonist is likely to match or beat an oral calcimimetic, but dose and margin are undisclosed.
rationale: Phase 3 designs in China against cinacalcet are usually built on strong phase 2 data and a non-inferiority margin the drug clears. Cinacalcet achieves more than 50% iPTH reduction in roughly 40-50% of dialysis patients, and etelcalcetide beat it by about 12 points. A new-mechanism agent should at least match it. Trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026, so reporting before mid 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the head-to-head etelcalcetide versus cinacalcet trial, more than 50% iPTH reduction was reached by 52.4% versus 40.2%.

reason: Randomized phase 2 with about 85 per arm and no stated hypothesis; pCR may look higher with IBI363 but a significant gap needs about 18 points, and event-free survival will be immature at any reading.
rationale: IBI363 is a PD-1/IL-2 bispecific with strong early signals, so a numerically higher pCR rate than pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy is likely, but with 85 per arm a formal significant difference needs roughly 18 points over a control near 30%. Randomized phase 2 results are often reported descriptively, which counts against a clear met statement.

assumptions.claim: In KEYNOTE-671 the pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy arm reached pCR in 18.1% versus 4.0% with placebo plus chemotherapy.
assumptions.source: KEYNOTE-671, NCT03425643, Wakelee et al. NEJM 2023

reason: Cabergoline is established as more effective than bromocriptine for normalizing prolactin; the trial only needs non-inferiority (margin unknown), so failure would come from conduct or a tight margin.
rationale: Earlier head-to-head work (Webster 1994) found prolactin normalized in 83% on cabergoline versus 59% on bromocriptine, so non-inferiority and probably superiority is very likely with 191 per arm. Reporting is the uncertainty: a domestic Chinese sponsor rarely announces or posts results, and the trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026.

assumptions.claim: In the Cabergoline Comparative Study Group trial, prolactin normalized in 83% of cabergoline and 59% of bromocriptine patients.

reason: Phase 2 head-to-head against IV tranexamic acid, an effective standard; beating it on Day-3 Gross-formula blood loss with 90 per arm needs a clear advantage, and the record states no non-inferiority design.
rationale: Tranexamic acid already cuts TKA blood loss by about a third, so a new agent at 90 per arm and SD near 300 mL has only about 45 mL of standard error; a superiority win needs a 100 mL advantage or more. A non-inferiority design is possible but the record does not state it. Small Chinese sponsor, so public results are likely selected toward positive ones.
evidence: Meta-analyses of IV tranexamic acid in TKA (Gross-formula total blood loss about 700-1000 mL)
Typical Chinese phase 2 antifibrinolytic TKA trials

assumptions.claim: Total blood loss by Day 3 with IV tranexamic acid in TKA is typically about 700-1000 mL by the Gross formula.

reason: Control patients are by definition not suppressed on bulevirtide, so TND is near zero; the combination only needs a modest TND rate for significance. The durability co-primary after end of treatment is the main uncertainty.
rationale: Patients enrolled have persistent viremia on bulevirtide, so continued bulevirtide gives almost no target-not-detected responses at week 24. Tobevibart plus elebsiran produced high HDV RNA suppression in the phase 2 SOLSTICE study, including TND in a large share. Open-label, so a large effect is very likely; the sustained-response co-primary adds some risk.

assumptions.claim: Bulevirtide 2 mg monotherapy rarely achieves HDV RNA target not detected, roughly 10 percent at week 48 even in unselected patients.
Tobevibart plus elebsiran gave a majority of patients HDV RNA below LLOQ by week 24-48 in SOLSTICE.

reason: Likely a non-inferiority design versus prednisolone acetate, which is a strong comparator; a JAK-class topical may be slightly less potent at Day 14. If the hypothesis is superiority, success is unlikely.
rationale: VVN461 (selective JAK-class topical) showed anterior chamber cell reductions comparable to prednisolone acetate in phase 2. A phase 3 against 1 percent prednisolone acetate is typically designed for non-inferiority, which is plausible but the record does not state it. Superiority over a potent steroid at Day 14 is unlikely.
evidence: Loteprednol/difluprednate vs prednisolone acetate uveitis trials

assumptions.claim: 1 percent prednisolone acetate typically clears most anterior chamber cells by Day 14, a drop of about 1.5-2 grades.
assumptions.source: Prednisolone acetate anterior uveitis trials, e.g. difluprednate vs prednisolone (Foster 2010)

reason: Phase 2b dose-ranging in resistant hypertension with 70 per arm; the highest dose needs about 5 mmHg placebo-corrected effect, and placebo response in office SBP is sizeable.
rationale: With SD near 13 mmHg and 70 per arm the standard error is about 2.2 mmHg, so a true placebo-corrected effect of 5 mmHg is needed for solid success. Phase 2b hypertension dose-finding often shows a significant top dose, but placebo response of 6-8 mmHg in resistant, uncontrolled patients reduces separation. Primary completion likely slips.
evidence: Aprocitentan PRECISION 2022 (placebo-corrected office SBP about -4 to -5 mmHg)

assumptions.claim: Placebo-corrected office SBP effect in resistant hypertension phase 2/3 trials is typically 4-10 mmHg.

reason: Bulevirtide monotherapy rarely produces target-not-detected HDV RNA at week 48, while the antibody plus siRNA combination reached high rates in phase 2; the co-primary sustained response after end of treatment is the main risk.
rationale: Control TND at week 48 is about 10 percent in bulevirtide-treated patients, whereas tobevibart plus elebsiran reached a majority with HDV RNA below LLOQ in SOLSTICE. With 50 per arm a 40-point difference is clearly significant. Risks are the post-treatment durability co-primary and the safety co-primary being counted.

assumptions.claim: Only about 10 percent of bulevirtide 2 mg patients have HDV RNA target not detected at week 48.

reason: ALA PDT versus vehicle PDT for face and scalp AK has consistently shown large complete clearance differences; only the small sample size (40 per arm) and a possible weaker new formulation or short incubation are risks.
rationale: Earlier Levulan face/scalp phase 3 trials showed week 12 complete clearance of about 77-89 percent versus 11-19 percent with vehicle plus blue light. The reformulated product is expected to match; with 40 per arm a 40-point gap is highly significant. Sun Pharma seldom press-releases such data, so publication timing is the main uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: Vehicle plus blue light gives complete clearance of face/scalp AK in roughly 10-20 percent at week 12.
Levulan PDT gave complete clearance in roughly 77-89 percent in face/scalp trials.

reason: Upper-extremity AK clears less well than face/scalp with ALA PDT, so the gap is smaller, but with 130 per arm a 25-35 point difference is very likely significant.
rationale: Prior Levulan and Ameluz upper-extremity trials showed complete clearance around 40-55 percent versus 10-20 percent with vehicle PDT. Treatment of arm lesions has lower response than face/scalp but 130 per arm gives strong power; the main risk is a weaker effect from the new formulation or short incubation.

assumptions.claim: ALA PDT on upper extremity AK yields complete clearance of roughly 40-55 percent versus 10-20 percent with vehicle PDT.
assumptions.source: Published Levulan and Ameluz extremity AK trials

reason: Pembrolizumab biosimilar PK equivalence on two AUC endpoints with about 73 per arm; both must fall within the margins, and interpatient PK variability in patients can make the 90% interval tight.
rationale: Biosimilar candidates with matched analytics usually show PK equivalence; other pembrolizumab biosimilar PK trials were reported successful. The risk is that two co-primary AUC endpoints must both fall within 80-125 percent at about 73 per arm with CV near 30 percent. Qilu rarely issues public results quickly.
evidence: Samsung Bioepis SB27 pembrolizumab PK trial 2025

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab AUC ratios in biosimilar PK trials typically fall within 80-125 percent when analytical similarity is shown.

reason: Only 24 patients per arm with a UAS7 SD near 11 needs a difference of about 6.5 points; a TSLP/IL-13 bispecific has an uncertain CSU effect and placebo response on background antihistamine is sizeable.
rationale: Small single-site phase 2 (24 v 24) of a TSLP/IL-13 bispecific in CSU. Anti-TSLP and anti-IL-4R agents give moderate UAS7 benefit in CSU (dupilumab about -8 vs placebo), and placebo response is large. With SD near 11, significance needs roughly -6.5 points. Plausible but far from certain; company is likely to publish mainly if positive.

assumptions.claim: Dupilumab beat placebo on UAS7 by roughly 8 points at week 24 in omalizumab-naive CSU patients, with placebo improving by about 12 points.
assumptions.source: CUPID Study A, J Allergy Clin Immunol 2022

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated CSU patients on background antihistamines typically improve UAS7 by 5 to 12 points within 12 to 24 weeks.

reason: First-in-class KLK5/7 barrier mechanism in AD is unproven; upstream or novel mechanisms often show only a modest margin over placebo in a phase 2a of about 48 per arm, and the response threshold is undefined.
rationale: Phase 2a proof of concept of a KLK5/7 inhibitor in moderate-severe AD, about 48 per arm. Mechanism is plausible (barrier, TSLP/IL-1 upstream) but novel; tezepelumab in AD missed significance. The responder threshold is unknown (EASI-50/75 or IGA), placebo about 15-25%. A private sponsor will probably announce mainly when the result is positive.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab in AD phase 2a gave EASI-50 of 64.7% vs 48.2% placebo at week 12, not statistically significant.
assumptions.source: Simpson et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2019

reason: Active comparator ciclosporin already lowers corneal staining well in VKC; the unknown T1695 must match or beat it at 4 weeks in 60 children per arm, and superiority is much harder than non-inferiority.
rationale: Head-to-head phase 2 against ciclosporin emulsion in paediatric VKC; the record states no hypothesis, so non-inferiority is likely though superiority is assumed by the card. Ciclosporin gives a robust 4-week staining improvement, leaving little room for superiority. T1695 mechanism is unknown to me. Reporting by a private sponsor is slow and sparse.
evidence: VEKTIS ciclosporin 0.1% cationic emulsion VKC trial 2018

assumptions.claim: Ciclosporin 0.1% cationic emulsion improved keratitis (corneal staining) in children with severe VKC versus vehicle over 4 months.

reason: Placebo plus standard antiemetics (NK1, 5-HT3, dexamethasone) already gives roughly 60-75% delayed-phase complete response, leaving a ceiling; about 100 per arm needs roughly +13 points to reach significance.
rationale: Add-on to standard antiemetics in highly emetogenic chemo. Delayed-phase no-vomiting/no-rescue rates on placebo are high (about 65-70%), so the achievable gain is limited and a 102-per-arm phase 2 needs about 13 points. Novel nausea mechanism may help, but the primary endpoint ignores nausea, where benefit is likelier. Lilly reports mostly via ClinicalTrials.gov and congresses.

assumptions.claim: With aprepitant-containing triple therapy in cisplatin chemotherapy, delayed-phase (days 2-5) freedom from vomiting is about 70-80%.
assumptions.source: Hesketh et al., J Clin Oncol 2003

reason: Effect is very likely large (aleniglipron gave 11-15% placebo-adjusted weight loss), so the main risk is only that the sponsor reports no explicit significance test or that only 12 placebo patients widen the variance.
rationale: Oral GLP-1 agonist; ACCESS gave about 11% placebo-adjusted weight loss at 36 weeks (120 mg) and about 15% at higher doses. Fat mass falls roughly 70-75% of weight lost, so about -20 to -28% of baseline fat versus about -1% on placebo. 59 versus 12 easily detects that. Trial is complete, so a readout is likely within months.

assumptions.claim: Aleniglipron 120 mg produced 11.3% placebo-adjusted weight loss at 36 weeks in ACCESS.
assumptions.source: Structure Therapeutics press release, Dec 2025 / ACCESS phase 2b

assumptions.claim: In ACCESS II the 240 mg dose gave about 15% placebo-adjusted weight loss at 36 weeks.

reason: HiSCR75 is a demanding endpoint and a dose-ranging design leaves only about 50 patients per arm, so even a real TNF/OX40L effect of 15 points sits near the significance threshold.
rationale: Phase 2b of a TNF/OX40L bispecific nanobody in HS with earlier phase 2 signal. HiSCR75 placebo about 20%; effective biologics reach 40-47%. With roughly 50 per arm at the top dose, a 15-20 point gain is needed for p<0.05. Dose-ranging analysis may use dose-response modelling. Primary completion Feb 2027 pushes disclosure to mid or late 2027.

assumptions.claim: In BE HEARD I, bimekizumab q2w achieved HiSCR50 of about 48% versus about 29% on placebo at week 16.

reason: Large (1200) open-label safety trial in AF with a primary completion of Feb 2027 while still recruiting; slippage of a quarter is plausible but Regeneron usually posts results about a year after completion.
TL1A blockade has no proven efficacy in RA; with about 62 per arm, ACR20 needs roughly +17 points over a 35-40% placebo+MTX response, and a multiple-dose design adds multiplicity.
rationale: Phase 2b of an anti-TL1A antibody on MTX background in RA. Rationale is plausible (TL1A/DR3 in synovium) but untested clinically in RA; tulisokibart's proven efficacy is in UC. Placebo+MTX ACR20 at week 12 about 35-40%. About 62 per arm requires about +17 points, and Merck often discloses only positive or pipeline-changing news.

assumptions.claim: In RA-BUILD, placebo ACR20 at week 12 was about 39-40% in csDMARD-inadequate responders.
assumptions.source: Dougados et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2017

assumptions.claim: Tulisokibart achieved clinical remission in 26% versus 1% placebo at week 12 in UC.

reason: A potent weekly incretin/amylin-class candidate versus placebo over 36 weeks should win clearly; residual risk is only that smaller Part B arms or tolerability dropouts blunt the effect, or the headline gives no formal test.
rationale: Novo Nordisk once-weekly obesity candidate with prior human data; eligibility asks for willingness to lose more than 25%, implying high potency. Against placebo (about -2%), a 36-week phase 2 high dose should deliver 12-20 points difference, easily significant even with small arms. Main uncertainty is reporting timing (company announcement, ADA/EASD, CT.gov).

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in 24-48 week phase 2 obesity trials lose about 1.5-2% of body weight.
assumptions.source: Retatrutide phase 2, Jastreboff et al., N Engl J Med 2023

assumptions.claim: Subcutaneous amycretin 20 mg weekly gave about 22% weight loss at 36 weeks.

reason: Trifarotene already won two global phase 3 trials with 10-17 point IGA gains; with 280 per arm a China bridging study should replicate, but all three co-primaries (IGA plus two lesion counts) must be met.
rationale: Approved retinoid with two positive global phase 3 trials (IGA success 29% vs 20%, 42% vs 26%). 561 patients give over 95% power for a 10-13 point difference; Chinese population should respond similarly. Risk is the triple co-primary requirement and a possibly higher vehicle response. Galderma seldom press-releases regional bridging studies, so disclosure may be slow.

assumptions.claim: In the global phase 3 trials, facial IGA success at week 12 was 29.4% vs 19.5% (study 1) and 42.3% vs 25.7% (study 2) for trifarotene vs vehicle.
assumptions.source: Tan et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2019 (PERFECT 1/2)

reason: Drusen area percent change over 24 weeks is a noisy imaging surrogate with drift in placebo; a Chinese herbal granule may show a modest drusen reduction but a short window and measurement variability could blur it.
rationale: Phase 3 of a TCM granule built on presumably positive phase 2 drusen data, 400 patients, placebo-controlled. Chinese pivotal trials of this kind are usually reported positive, but drusen area percent change has large between-patient variance (SD about 40 percent) and 24 weeks is short. Public disclosure by a Chinese private sponsor is slow; recruiting was still open in Oct 2026, so completion likely slips.

assumptions.claim: Drusen area changes slowly and variably over months in intermediate AMD, so a 24-week percent change has large between-patient variance.

reason: A 28-day DAAO-type cognition trial with about 37 per arm has low power against a modest true effect, and prior DAAO inhibitors (luvadaxistat, iclepertin) failed on cognition.
rationale: Phase 2 in cognitive impairment associated with schizophrenia, four arms of about 37, 28 days. Prior DAAO inhibitor programs (luvadaxistat INTERACT, iclepertin CONNEX) missed cognition endpoints, and digital BACS composite change has a large practice effect in placebo. Multiple doses give some chance that one dose is significant. Private sponsor likely to announce topline in H1 2027, more readily if positive.

assumptions.claim: Luvadaxistat, a D-amino acid oxidase inhibitor, did not meet its primary cognition endpoint in the phase 2 INTERACT trial.

reason: With 5-fraction radiotherapy most patients develop at least grade 1 erythema, so the grade 0 responder rate is low in both arms and a topical radioprotector needs about a 14 point gain to reach significance with 91 per arm.
rationale: Dose-finding phase 2 of topical amifostine thiol versus vehicle, about 91 per arm. Primary is the share staying at CTCAE grade 0 through 4 weeks after ultra-hypofractionated RT, where vehicle grade 0 is perhaps 30 percent. A true gain of 8 to 10 points gives roughly one-in-three odds of significance for the top dose. Grade 2 or higher events are rare after 26 Gy in 5 fractions, so the key secondary is underpowered.

assumptions.claim: After 26 Gy in 5 fractions, acute skin toxicity is mostly grade 1 with grade 2 or higher in a minority of patients.

reason: Thirty per arm and a CAP change with SD around 40 dB/m leave only about 20 dB/m detectable; probiotics usually shift CAP by 10 to 15 dB/m at best, and the primary also names FAST score.
rationale: Single-site 60-patient mechanistic probiotic trial in MASLD, 6 months. CAP change between-patient SD is about 40 dB/m, so a 10 to 15 dB/m true effect is detected only about a third of the time; placebo arms often improve through regression to the mean and lifestyle. The primary combines CAP and FAST, which lowers the chance of a clean positive. Still recruiting in Oct 2026, so completion slips.

assumptions.claim: Probiotic RCTs in NAFLD show small average reductions in CAP that are often not significant in samples under 100.

reason: Twelve-week FVC change with about 53 per arm and SD near 150 mL can only detect an effect of roughly 60 mL, while oral nintedanib shows about 30 to 40 mL benefit over 12 weeks.
rationale: Phase 2 POC of inhaled nintedanib, two doses versus placebo, 12 weeks, treatment-naive IPF. Oral nintedanib slows FVC decline by about 110 to 125 mL per year, so about 30 to 40 mL at 12 weeks; inhalation could add lung exposure. Standard error of the difference is about 30 mL, so significance needs roughly 60 mL; two doses help a little. Recruitment of drug-naive IPF patients is slow, so readout likely slips.

assumptions.claim: Nintedanib 150 mg twice daily reduced the annual rate of FVC decline by about 110 to 125 mL versus placebo in INPULSIS.

reason: A quail-cell versus chicken-cell comparability design with about 485 per arm is well powered for a standard GMT-ratio margin; the main risk is a real shift in immunogenicity from the new production cells or a co-primary safety endpoint.
rationale: Bavarian Nordic comparability trial of MVA-BN made in CCX.E10 quail cells versus Jynneos, 970 adults, PRNT GMT ratio 2 weeks after dose 2. A listed company usually announces topline results within a few months; the trial ends Nov 2026. Lot consistency and process-change studies for this vaccine typically succeed, but a cell-substrate change carries more risk than a lot-to-lot comparison.

assumptions.claim: MVA-BN showed lot-to-lot consistency in the phase 3 POX-MVA-013 study.

reason: A weekly triple-agonist class drug at its top dose over 36 weeks is very likely to beat placebo on percent weight change; the risk is a lower-than-expected effect from tolerability-limited titration.
rationale: Phase 2 of Hanmi's weekly GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist in non-diabetic obesity, four doses versus placebo, 36 weeks. Incretin-class agents give 8 to 15 percent weight loss at this duration versus about 2 percent on placebo; with about 53 per arm and SD near 6 percent, even a 5 point effect is significant. Timing is the main uncertainty; Hanmi usually releases topline to the press, possibly around ADA June 2027.

assumptions.claim: The triple agonist retatrutide at its top dose produced about 17 percent weight loss at 24 weeks and 24 percent at 48 weeks versus about 2 percent on placebo.

reason: Dose-finding plague vaccine trial with descriptive immunogenicity, DoD collaboration; Part 2 selection from Part 1 could stretch the registered timeline but a stop is unlikely, and posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
rationale: Phase 2 dose-finding of six regimens in Part 1 with up to two carried into Part 2, 148 adults. Primary completion is registered for Jan 2027 and study completion Aug 2027, so results posting by 31 Aug 2027 is unlikely. Part 2 sequencing may delay the registered primary completion date. Funding by the Department of Defense keeps termination risk low but not zero.

reason: Botulinum toxin has a clear, fast effect on platysma bands, so a 2-grade composite at week 2 versus a near-zero placebo rate is very likely met; the composite of two raters is the only real risk.
rationale: Phase 3 of incobotulinumtoxinA versus placebo, 150 per arm. OnabotulinumtoxinA won FDA approval for platysma prominence in 2024 on placebo-controlled phase 3 trials, showing large responder differences. Even a 15 point gain over a placebo rate near 3 percent would be significant at this size. The strict 2-grade composite by both investigator and participant lowers the rate but not the contrast. Merz is private and reports mainly at congresses.
evidence: OnabotulinumtoxinA platysma prominence phase 3 program, FDA approval 2024

assumptions.claim: OnabotulinumtoxinA was approved by the FDA in 2024 for platysma prominence on the basis of placebo-controlled phase 3 trials.

reason: Open-label PK bridging trial of SC versus IV ublituximab; the registered primary (Week 24 AUC) is already past, long extension to 2028 delays posting, and a stop or primary change is unlikely.
rationale: Phase 3 open-label pharmacokinetic non-inferiority study with AUC over 24 weeks as the single primary, 360 patients, primary completion Oct 2026 and study completion Dec 2028. Results are due about a year after primary completion and a public company often posts near the deadline, so posting by 31 Aug 2027 is unlikely. A well-defined PK primary rarely changes.

reason: IGF-1R blockade gives large proptosis responder gains over placebo in active TED; a Chinese phase 3 of 108 patients is well powered, so failure would need an unexpectedly weak effect or a high placebo response.
rationale: VRDN-003 is a subcutaneous IGF-1R antibody; the class (teprotumumab OPTIC 83% vs 10%, veligrotug THRIVE ~70% vs 5%) shows 50-70 point proptosis responder gains in active TED. Chinese phase 3 with ~54 per arm would be near-certain to hit if even half that effect holds. Main uncertainty is timing of Zai Lab disclosure, not the result.

assumptions.claim: Teprotumumab produced a 2 mm proptosis response in 83% vs 10% on placebo at week 24 in active TED.
Veligrotug had a markedly higher proptosis responder rate than placebo (about 70% vs 5%) in THRIVE.

reason: Three co-primary viral-load time points must all hit; Day 2 is early and placebo viral load also falls on its own, and enrolment of high-risk RSV outpatients is seasonal and may run past the registered date.
rationale: Direct-acting RSV antivirals usually lower nasopharyngeal viral load vs placebo within days, and 96 per arm gives good power on a log10 endpoint with SD around 1.2. Risk comes from requiring Day 2, 4 and 6 all to be significant and from variable viral kinetics in older high-risk patients enrolled up to 72 h after onset.

assumptions.claim: Registered primary completion is 2026-12-30 while the trial is still recruiting, which makes slippage into the 2026-27 RSV season likely.

reason: A 60-patient phase 2 focused on safety cannot show a significant day-21 mortality difference when comparator mortality is only around 10%; at most a numerical trend will be reported.
rationale: With 30 per arm and early-therapy day-21 mortality of roughly 5-15%, only a handful of deaths will occur, so superiority is nearly unreachable and the study reads as a safety and signal-finding trial. Private sponsor, recruiting at launch with a December 2026 completion that is likely to slip, so a public readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Invasive aspergillosis trials, e.g. SECURE voriconazole vs isavuconazole (2016)

assumptions.claim: Enrollment is 60 participants across 30 sites, about 30 per arm.

reason: Non-inferiority on CGM time in range with only 50 per arm gives a confidence interval about 6 points wide, and the margin is not stated, so a miss is plausible even if the new insulin is truly equivalent.
rationale: A basal insulin with degludec-like glycaemic efficacy should land near zero difference in time in range. With SD about 15 points and n=50 per arm the SE is about 3 points, so non-inferiority depends on the unstated margin. Lilly usually discloses phase 2 via ClinicalTrials.gov results several months after completion.

assumptions.claim: Weekly basal insulin efsitora showed time in range similar to daily degludec in QWINT phase 3 trials.

reason: Safety-only phase 2a that has finished its 180-day follow-up; small private sponsor makes a results posting within a year of completion uncommon.
rationale: Primary completion 2026-09-06 has passed and the study is active, not recruiting, so termination is unlikely. Primary outcome is a stable safety description; CastleVax is a small private company, so ClinicalTrials.gov results by August 2027 are possible but not likely.

reason: An amylin plus incretin combination should clearly outperform placebo on weight at week 32; the realistic downside is GI-driven dropouts diluting the effect.
rationale: Eloralintide alone produced up to about 20% weight loss at 48 weeks in obesity, and incretin therapy adds weight loss in type 2 diabetes. With placebo around -2% and the combination roughly -13 to -15% at week 32, p<0.001 is near certain. Timing is the issue: completion in March 2027 makes a June readout unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Eloralintide gave up to about 20% mean weight loss at 48 weeks in adults with obesity in phase 2.
Placebo weight change in T2D obesity trials is around -2 to -3%.

reason: Superiority over vehicle is almost certain, but the stated hypothesis also compares the combination with SnF2-only and KNO3-only dentifrices on two primary endpoints, where the margin of benefit is small.
rationale: Both SnF2 and KNO3 are established desensitizing agents, so the combination should beat vehicle by 0.5-0.8 Schiff points at week 8. Beating each active reference on both Schiff and tactile threshold is harder, with likely differences of 0.1-0.2 points; n=180 per arm gives moderate power. If the sponsor requires superiority over all references, the chance of success falls to about half.
evidence: Stannous fluoride dentifrice dentin hypersensitivity trials, J Clin Dent

assumptions.claim: Randomization was planned about 180 per active arm and 90 for vehicle.

reason: Enlicitide alone cuts LDL-C by over 50% and rosuvastatin adds more, against a flat placebo, so the primary is essentially certain; the open question is disclosure timing.
rationale: Oral PCSK9 inhibitor enlicitide gave about 56% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction in CORALreef Lipids; adding rosuvastatin in LLT-naive adults should reach 70-75% at week 8. With about 250 per arm and SD about 14, significance is certain. Merck typically posts results within a year of primary completion (August 2026).

assumptions.claim: Enlicitide reduced LDL-C by roughly 55-60% vs placebo in adults on background statin in CORALreef Lipids.
Rosuvastatin 10-20 mg lowers LDL-C by about 45-50% alone.
assumptions.source: STELLAR trial, Jones et al., Am J Cardiol 2003

reason: Paediatric colonoscopy-prep trials recruit slowly and this one was still recruiting 10 months in; completion likely slips past April 2027, and a European sponsor is unlikely to post results by August.
rationale: 212 children at 46 European sites started late December 2025 and were still recruiting at launch, with primary completion January 2027. Paediatric enrolment commonly runs behind, so the registered date probably moves. Results postings on ClinicalTrials.gov for this Norgine study by August 2027 are unlikely.

reason: AZD0780 gave about 50% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction at 30 mg on background statin in PURSUIT, so a 76-patient trial should be strongly significant; the main risk is a lower dose or odd baseline definition.
rationale: AZD0780 phase 2b PURSUIT showed up to about 50.7% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction at week 12. With 38 per arm and SD about 20 points, an effect of 40-50 points gives z above 8. The placebo mean depends on whether baseline is taken before or after the 28-day rosuvastatin run-in, which widens the control range. Disclosure may be limited to a registry posting.

assumptions.claim: AZD0780 30 mg lowered LDL-C by up to about 50.7% vs placebo at 12 weeks in PURSUIT.
All participants complete a 28-day rosuvastatin run-in before randomization.

reason: Ritlecitinib (JAK3/TEC inhibitor) is unproven in CSU and CSU placebo response is large (about -10 UAS7 at Week 12), so roughly 4-5 points of separation is needed with about 67 per arm.
rationale: Ritlecitinib covalently inhibits JAK3 and TEC-family kinases (including weak BTK activity); BTK inhibitors work in CSU but ritlecitinib's BTK inhibition is much weaker and no CSU efficacy data exist. CSU placebo UAS7 improvement is about 10 points by Week 12, so with 67 per arm and SD about 12 a difference near 4-5 points is needed. Two doses, one suffices. Pfizer rarely press-releases phase 2 results, so early public data skew positive.
evidence: REMIX-1 and REMIX-2 remibrutinib phase 3 CSU trials, 2024-2025
Xu et al. 2015 PF-06651600 kinase selectivity (JPET)

assumptions.claim: Placebo UAS7 improvement at Week 12 in remibrutinib phase 3 CSU trials was about 10-11 points.
Ritlecitinib is a covalent JAK3 and TEC-family kinase inhibitor, with much weaker BTK inhibition than dedicated BTK inhibitors.
assumptions.source: Xu et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther 2015 (PF-06651600)

reason: Immunobridging study with primary completion already passed (July 2026); GSK generally posts CT.gov results within about 12 months of primary completion, so posting by Aug 2027 is more likely than not; stop or primary-outcome change is unlikely.
rationale: Completed-enrollment GSK vaccine bridging study; GSK is usually compliant with the 12-month results-posting rule, primary outcomes are detailed and stable, and termination risk is minimal.

reason: Dapagliflozin's UACR lowering is well established and roughly additive with MRA-type drugs, so the combination should beat baxdrostat alone; the residual risk is the high variance of UACR with about 105 per arm.
rationale: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce UACR about 30% in CKD, and combined with an MRA the effect is largely additive (CONFIDENCE: finerenone+empagliflozin about 52% vs about 30% for each alone). Expected combination/baxdrostat ratio is roughly 0.70-0.75; with about 105 evaluable per arm and log-UACR SD near 0.9 power is about 85%. Dropouts, washout effects and baxdrostat's own UACR effect add uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: Finerenone plus empagliflozin lowered UACR by about 52% versus about 30% for either alone over 6 months.
Dapagliflozin lowers UACR by roughly 30% versus placebo in albuminuric CKD.

reason: Unproven first-in-patient antibody with only healthy-volunteer data, 23 vs 22 patients, and a noisy facial VASI endpoint; only a large effect (about 25+ points) reaches significance.
rationale: Proof-of-concept with 45 patients, dose unknown, first efficacy exposure after a healthy-volunteer phase 1. Vitiligo F-VASI percent change is variable (SD about 35-40), so significance needs about 25 points of separation, seen with effective JAK inhibitors but rarely with unproven biologics. The trial is still recruiting, so week-24 data likely slip past mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated patients in vitiligo trials show small facial VASI improvement (about 5-10% at 24 weeks).
assumptions.source: Ritlecitinib vitiligo phase 2b, Ezzedine et al. 2023

reason: GIP/GLP-1 agonists have shown inconsistent, modest effects on smoking abstinence, and with about 111 per arm a 10-15 point gain is borderline for significance against a sizeable placebo abstinence rate.
rationale: Prior GLP-1 smoking trials (exenatide with NRT, dulaglutide) were null or marginal; semaglutide/tirzepatide data are mixed. A 15-point gain over a 25-35% placebo rate is needed with only 111 per arm (power about 60% if real). Still recruiting in Oct 2026 against a Feb 2027 registered primary completion, so results likely come after mid-2027.
evidence: Exenatide plus NRT smoking cessation, Yammine 2021

assumptions.claim: In the varenicline relapse-prevention trial, placebo continuous abstinence for weeks 13-24 was about 50% among 12-week abstainers.

reason: Intra-articular saline in knee OA gives a large placebo response on pain at Week 4, and with 65 per arm a 0.8-point separation on a 0-10 scale is needed.
rationale: Phase 2a proof-of-concept of a single intra-articular injection enriched for synovitis; saline placebo typically improves WOMAC pain by about 2 points (0-10 equivalent) by Week 4, and the SD of change is about 2.3, so about 0.8 points is needed for significance at 65 per arm. Mechanism and effect size are unknown; most intra-articular OA phase 2 studies miss at least some primaries.
evidence: Zhang et al., Osteoarthritis Cartilage 2008 placebo meta-analysis
Bannuru et al. 2015 intra-articular therapies network meta-analysis

assumptions.claim: Intra-articular saline placebo produces a large pain improvement in knee OA trials (effect size about 0.3-0.7).

reason: Saline placebo in knee OA pain trials produces a large response and a block-response-enriched population may inflate it further; the drug needs about 0.8-1 NRS points of separation at Week 12 with 75 per arm.
rationale: Phase 3 single-injection trial enriched by a diagnostic nerve-block response, which suggests a nerve-targeted mechanism with durable effect; such designs can yield separation of 1-1.5 NRS points, but OA knee-pain trials suffer high placebo responses and unblinding can help or distort. With SD about 2.5 and 75 per arm, 0.8 points reaches significance; power is about 50-60% if the true effect is around 1 point.
evidence: Davis et al. 2018 genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation RCT
Zhang et al. 2008 placebo effect in OA trials

assumptions.claim: Pain-while-walking NRS typically falls about 2 points over 12 weeks with saline injection in knee OA.

reason: Adjunctive MDD trials have placebo MADRS improvement of about 9-11 over 4 weeks and a typical SD near 9.5, so a novel agent needs about 2.3 points of separation with 115 per arm; the sponsor's prior adjunctive MDD candidate missed.
rationale: Adjunctive MDD phase 2 trials of novel mechanisms mostly fail: placebo MADRS change over 4 weeks is about -9 to -11 and effect sizes of 1-2 points are typical, below the 2.3 needed at 115 per arm. Supernus's earlier adjunctive MDD agent SPN-820 missed its phase 2b primary. As a public company Supernus would announce topline, likely in H1 2027 if enrollment completes around Q1.

assumptions.claim: Supernus's SPN-820 failed to separate from placebo on MADRS in its adjunctive MDD phase 2b trial.
assumptions.source: Supernus press release, SPN-820 WAVE study

reason: Ritlecitinib's JAK3/TEC profile and AA-type dosing are unproven in HS; with 64 per arm and placebo HiSCR50 near 30%, roughly a 16-point gain is needed for significance.
rationale: JAK1 inhibitors (povorcitinib, upadacitinib) showed HiSCR50 gains of about 15-25 points over a placebo near 26-30% in phase 2, but ritlecitinib is a JAK3/TEC inhibitor at lower systemic exposure and its HS rationale is weaker. With 64 per arm a 16-point difference is needed for p<0.05, giving roughly a one-in-four chance. Pfizer seldom publicizes phase 2 results early.

assumptions.claim: In the povorcitinib phase 2 HS trial, placebo HiSCR50 at Week 16 was roughly 26-27%.

reason: An oral incretin-type tablet at the top dose for 28 weeks should clearly beat placebo even with about 46 per arm; the main risk is a weak molecule or poor tolerability at the high dose.
rationale: Oral GLP-1-type obesity agents give a clear placebo-adjusted weight loss at 26-28 weeks (orforglipron phase 2: roughly 9-13% vs 2% placebo). Up-titration to three target doses, a placebo arm of about 46 and an SD near 5.5% give very high power for the top dose. Placebo with lifestyle advice loses about 1-2%. Residual risk is a low-potency molecule or high dropout from GI effects.

assumptions.claim: In the orforglipron phase 2 obesity trial, 26-week weight loss was 8.6-12.6% vs about 2% with placebo.
Placebo arms in 26-36 week obesity trials with lifestyle advice lose about 1-3% of body weight.

reason: Janssen phase 2b dose-ranging in AD with about 63 per arm; a mechanism with real activity should beat a 15-20% placebo EASI-75 at the top dose, but a novel target could underdeliver and placebo response varies.
rationale: Janssen advancing a phase 2b in AD with 62 sites suggests encouraging earlier data. Placebo EASI-75 at week 12 in AD phase 2b trials is about 10-25%. With roughly 63 per arm, a 20+ point gap at the top dose is significant. Any dose meeting the objective counts. Risk is a novel mechanism with modest AD activity.

assumptions.claim: Placebo EASI-75 rates in AD phase 2b trials are typically 10-25% at weeks 12-16.
Highest doses of active AD biologics and JAKs reach EASI-75 of 40-60% in phase 2b.

reason: Phase 2 with about 52 per arm and four arms; mRS 0-1 at 90 days in a late-window population needs roughly a 15-20 point gain to reach significance, while plausible effects are about 8-10 points.
rationale: Late-window (4.5-24 h) reperfusion-type therapy without planned thrombectomy: TRACE-III showed mRS 0-1 of 33% vs 24%, a gain of about 9 points in 500 patients. Here about 52 per arm gives low power for such a difference on mRS 0-1. Dose arms add a little chance of one dose passing. Phase 2 stroke trials with an mRS primary often miss.

assumptions.claim: In TRACE-III, mRS 0-1 at 90 days was 33.0% with tenecteplase vs 24.2% with standard medical treatment.
A 52-per-arm trial has under 30% power to detect a 9-point difference in a roughly 30% event rate.

reason: Large phase 3 (about 310 per arm) of a sustained-release VEGFR inhibitor against sham; anti-VEGF in NPDR gives 65-80% 2-step improvement vs about 15% with sham, so failure would mostly come from low implant exposure or trial conduct.
rationale: Anti-VEGF therapy in NPDR produces large DRSS gains (PANORAMA: 65-80% vs 15% sham at week 52), and OTX-TKI's phase 1 HELIOS-1 showed strong DRSS effects with sustained release. With about 310 per arm, power is near complete. Redosing at week 24 supports exposure. Residual risk is a lower-than-expected effect at the lower exposure or conduct problems.

assumptions.claim: In PANORAMA, 65-80% of eyes with aflibercept gained at least 2 DRSS steps at week 52 vs about 15% with sham.
Sham arms in NPDR DRSS trials show 2-step improvement in roughly 10-15% of eyes at week 52.

reason: Phase 2 with about 45 per arm; itch scores in PN carry large placebo responses of 20-30% and SD near 35%, so a TYK2 inhibitor must show a 15+ point gap at the top dose to reach significance.
rationale: ICP-332 is a TYK2 inhibitor with earlier positive phase 2 results in atopic dermatitis, and JAK-type agents relieve itch in PN. With about 45 per arm and SD near 35 points of percent change, a 16-point difference gives roughly 50-60% power. Placebo itch response in PN is sizable (20-30%). Multiple doses give a small extra chance.

assumptions.claim: In OLYMPIA 2, a 4-point PP-NRS improvement at week 16 occurred in 56.3% with nemolizumab vs 20.9% with placebo.
Placebo-treated PN patients typically show 20-30% mean itch reduction at week 16.

reason: JAK1 inhibitors reliably beat placebo on ASAS40 at week 16 in AS (about 50% vs 25%); with 176 per arm failure would need an unusually weak dose or high placebo response.
rationale: JAK inhibitors in AS (upadacitinib SELECT-AXIS 1: ASAS40 52% vs 26%; tofacitinib 41% vs 13%) show large placebo-adjusted gains. LNK01001 is a JAK1 inhibitor with positive phase 2 data in AS and RA. At 176 per arm a 20+ point difference is almost certainly significant.
evidence: Tofacitinib phase 3 in AS, Ann Rheum Dis 2021

assumptions.claim: In SELECT-AXIS 1, ASAS40 at week 14 was 52% with upadacitinib vs 26% with placebo.
assumptions.source: van der Heijde et al., Lancet 2019

assumptions.claim: In the tofacitinib AS phase 3, ASAS40 at week 16 was about 41% vs 13% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Deodhar et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2021

reason: Completed single-site Australian bioavailability study of omega-3 products in healthy adults; low chance of stopping, an amended primary outcome or posted results, as the sponsor is a CRO/nutrition partner without a regulatory posting duty.
Head-to-head against enzalutamide, which already clears PSA below 0.2 in most low-volume patients; with about 103 per arm a difference under about 13 points will not reach significance.
rationale: Two second-generation AR antagonists give similar PSA depth; enzalutamide in ARCHES reached undetectable PSA in about two thirds of patients, and low-volume disease has even higher rates. A rezvilutamide advantage on PSA <0.2 at 6 months is plausible but probably under 10 points, and 103 per arm needs about 13 points for significance. The open-label design adds no help.
evidence: CHART rezvilutamide high-volume mHSPC, Lancet Oncol 2022

assumptions.claim: In ARCHES, undetectable PSA (<0.2 ng/mL) occurred in about 68% of enzalutamide-treated vs 18% of placebo-treated mHSPC patients.
In the CHART trial, rezvilutamide plus ADT gave high PSA response and deep PSA decline in high-volume mHSPC.

reason: Only about 20 per arm: a HiSCR75 gap of 30+ points is needed for significance at week 16, while a plausible effect for an IL-17-class agent is about 25 points.
rationale: SCT650C is an IL-17-axis antibody; IL-17 blockade works in HS (bimekizumab BE HEARD; sonelokimab MIRA HiSCR75 about 40% vs about 15% placebo at week 12). With 20 per arm, a 25-point difference (about 40% vs 15%) is borderline for Fisher's test, so the chance of a significant top dose is modest.

assumptions.claim: In MIRA, HiSCR75 at week 12 was about 40% with sonelokimab vs about 15% with placebo.
BE HEARD placebo HiSCR50 at week 16 was about 29% vs about 48% for bimekizumab.

reason: Cantharidin clears warts well in small series, but complete clearance of all baseline and new warts at Day 84 is a demanding bar, especially in adults with many warts; the vehicle arm should stay low.
rationale: VP-102 beat vehicle clearly in two molluscum phase 3 trials (about 46-54% vs 13-18%), and cantharidin is an established wart treatment. With 151 per arm, a 12-point gap is enough for significance. Vehicle clearance of every wart, including new ones, should be about 5-20%. The risk is a lower drug effect in adults with many or thick warts.
evidence: CAMP-1 and CAMP-2 phase 3 molluscum trials of VP-102 (Eichenfield, JAMA Dermatol 2020)

assumptions.claim: VP-102 achieved complete clearance in about 46% and 54% of molluscum patients vs 18% and 13% on vehicle in two phase 3 trials.
assumptions.source: CAMP-1/CAMP-2, Eichenfield et al., JAMA Dermatol 2020

reason: The endpoint needs HBsAg loss and DNA suppression held 24 weeks after stopping all treatment, so relapse after NA withdrawal could erode the effect; placebo cure should be near zero.
