rationale: AHB-137 is an antisense oligonucleotide that gave high HBsAg loss in NA-suppressed patients with HBsAg of 3000 IU/mL or less in phase 2, and this phase 3 enrols that population. Placebo plus NA gives almost no functional cure, and 289 per arm is large. Residual risk is durability after NA withdrawal and trial-specific design details such as dose and treatment length.
evidence: AHB-137 phase 2 in NA-treated CHB, Ausper (AASLD/EASL 2024-2025 presentations)

assumptions.claim: In phase 2, AHB-137 weekly dosing gave HBsAg loss in a large share of NA-suppressed HBeAg-negative patients with baseline HBsAg of 3000 IU/mL or less, far above placebo.
assumptions.source: Ausper AHB-137 phase 2 data, AASLD 2024 / EASL 2025

reason: Sanofi vaccine safety and immunogenicity study in 100 children with sickle cell disease; it was still recruiting in Oct 2026 and the primary set includes safety through day 181, so the registered Jan 2027 completion probably slips. Results likely come after the Aug 2027 read.
Illness in the challenge model resolves on its own within days, so the Day 3-5 stool grade window may leave little room to show a drug effect with only 40 per arm.
rationale: EDI048 is a potent gut-restricted PI(4)K inhibitor active against Cryptosporidium in preclinical models, so a clinical effect is plausible. But the human challenge model has self-resolving diarrhoea, a short Day 3-5 window, a stool grade scale of unknown variance, and a small sample of 40 per arm. Novartis rarely issues phase 2 press releases, so timing also matters.
evidence: Cryptosporidium controlled human infection model studies (Chappell 2006)

assumptions.claim: Cryptosporidium challenge in healthy adults produces self-limited diarrhoea lasting several days.
assumptions.source: Chappell et al., Am J Trop Med Hyg 2006

reason: Patient-reported ocular scores in mild ocular-only myasthenia on stable background therapy carry a large placebo response, and 60 per arm leaves little margin if the effect is only modest.
rationale: Telitacicept (BLyS/APRIL inhibitor) was positive in a China phase 3 in generalized myasthenia and is approved there. Ocular-only disease has fewer outcome items and a notable placebo response in a patient-reported score, with 60 per arm. A Chinese sponsor phase 3 is probably designed with a generous effect assumption. Last-patient timing likely pushes the readout past mid-2027.
evidence: Telitacicept generalized myasthenia gravis phase 3, China (RemeGen, 2024-2025)

assumptions.claim: Telitacicept beat placebo on MG-ADL in a phase 3 in generalized myasthenia gravis in China.

reason: Vitiligo repigments slowly, so a 24-week facial percent change vs placebo may be modest relative to between-patient variation with only about 59 per arm.
rationale: Oral JAK inhibitors such as ritlecitinib and upadacitinib showed dose-related facial repigmentation vs placebo in phase 2, but 24-week effects are modest and variable. Ivarmacitinib is a JAK1 inhibitor and the combination with gel adds a topical component. With about 59 per arm the trial has moderate power. Hengrui seldom issues phase 2 press releases, so publication would come later.

assumptions.claim: Oral ritlecitinib showed greater facial repigmentation than placebo at week 24 in a phase 2b vitiligo trial.

reason: A probiotic lozenge is likely to have a modest effect on bleeding on probing against the large inflammatory rise in the no-brushing model, and 30 per arm gives limited power.
rationale: In the 3-week no-brushing model, bleeding sites rise by roughly 30-40 points in placebo. Probiotic and salivaricin-producing strains have small to moderate effects on gingival indices in other trials, often non-significant at this sample size. With SD about 15 points and 30 per arm, an effect under about 8 points would miss significance.
evidence: Streptococcus salivarius K12 oral probiotic studies

assumptions.claim: In the experimental gingivitis model, abstaining from oral hygiene for 21 days produces clinically evident gingivitis in healthy adults.

reason: A weekly long-acting growth hormone against daily growth hormone is designed to match it rather than beat it, so a significant superiority result on height velocity is unlikely in 24 per arm.
rationale: This is an open-label dose-finding phase 2 of weekly PEG-rhGH against daily hGH in SGA children, with about 24 per arm. Long-acting growth hormones usually show similar or slightly lower early height velocity than daily hGH, and a superiority claim is unlikely. No formal hypothesis is stated, and the sponsor rarely announces phase 2 data promptly.
evidence: Weekly PEG-rhGH vs daily rhGH trials in growth hormone deficiency, China

assumptions.claim: Long-acting growth hormone has usually shown height velocity similar to daily growth hormone in head-to-head pediatric trials.
assumptions.source: Published head-to-head long-acting vs daily GH pediatric trials

reason: With 12 per arm and a variable skin biopsy gene-signature readout at day 28, even a real pharmacodynamic effect may miss significance; enrolment across 34 sites for 24 patients is slow.
rationale: VENT-03 is a cGAS inhibitor that should reduce interferon signalling, and the primary is a pharmacodynamic biomarker that moves faster than clinical scores. However, skin biopsy gene signatures vary a lot between patients, the sample is 12 per arm, and the treatment period is only 4 weeks. Public disclosure may come only as a company update or congress abstract.

assumptions.claim: cGAS-STING pathway activation drives type I interferon signature in lupus skin disease.

reason: An IL-17A antibody in AS with 250 per arm is very likely to beat placebo on ASAS40; the main risk is a higher than expected placebo response.
rationale: 608 is an anti-IL-17A antibody, a class with consistent ASAS40 benefit in AS (secukinumab MEASURE 1/2, Chinese IL-17A phase 3 trials with about 45-50% vs 15-20% at week 16). With 250 per arm, a 30-point gap gives power near 100%. Residual risk is a large Chinese placebo response, a dosing issue, or a result not announced by the deadline.

assumptions.claim: In MEASURE 1 and 2, secukinumab gave ASAS40 response at week 16 of about 41-46% versus about 11-13% with placebo.
608 is an anti-IL-17A monoclonal antibody from Sunshine Guojian (3SBio).

reason: ANGPTL3 siRNA should cut triglycerides strongly, but 30 per arm with very variable TG values leaves some sampling risk; the larger issue is the timing of any public report.
rationale: Solbinsiran is an ANGPTL3 siRNA; earlier Lilly phase 1/2 work showed large, durable TG reductions and ANGPTL3 inhibition lowers TG about 50% in other settings. In sHTG with TG of 500 mg/dL or more, percent change has a large SD, but a 40-60 point gap with 30 per arm is still well powered. Placebo changes are modest but noisy.

assumptions.claim: Solbinsiran lowered triglycerides substantially versus placebo in earlier phase 1 and 2 studies in dyslipidemia.
Placebo arms in sHTG trials typically show a TG change of roughly -10 to -25%.

reason: Single-site Chinese phase 2 safety study of 48 patients with 24-week treatment; plausible modest slippage of the primary completion date, low odds of stopping, and Chinese sponsors rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov.
Myostatin-pathway inhibition alone is expected to give modest weight loss; the trial needs about a 2-point gap versus placebo at 24 weeks, which is plausible but not certain.
rationale: Taldefgrobep alfa blocks myostatin signalling; this is a monotherapy phase 2b in obesity for 24 weeks. Muscle-pathway agents such as bimagrumab cut weight and fat mass but with modest monotherapy weight loss, and taldefgrobep failed to show clear benefit in SMA. With about 75 per arm and SD near 4.5%, a 2-point gap would be significant, so the outcome hinges on drug potency.

assumptions.claim: Bimagrumab monotherapy produced about 6.5% weight loss versus 0.8% with placebo at 48 weeks in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
assumptions.source: Heymsfield et al, JAMA Netw Open 2021

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in 24-week obesity trials typically lose about 1-2% of body weight.

reason: Oral GLP-1 peptide at the top regimen over 20 weeks should separate clearly from placebo; the main risk is poor oral exposure at the highest Schedule A regimen.
rationale: Ecnoglutide is a biased GLP-1 agonist with strong weight loss in injectable form. Oral GLP-1 agents (oral semaglutide, orforglipron) lose about 7-12% by 20-36 weeks. With about 34 per arm, a 5-7 point gap is well beyond sampling noise, so the main uncertainty is oral bioavailability and the dose regimen.

assumptions.claim: Oral GLP-1 agonists in obesity phase 2 trials gave placebo-adjusted weight loss of roughly 6-12% within 26 weeks.
assumptions.source: Orforglipron phase 2, Wharton et al, NEJM 2023

assumptions.claim: Verdiva Bio is developing oral ecnoglutide (VRB-101) for obesity.

reason: Two artificial tears usually differ by only a few OSDI points, and the comparator also improves symptoms; superiority needs about 4-5 points at 130 per arm.
rationale: Active-controlled artificial tear trial; both arms improve after the Refresh Plus run-in and in the vehicle-like response range of 10-15 points. AbbVie likely seeks a symptom claim, so superiority on OSDI is possible but differences between lubricant formulations are typically 2-4 points against SD near 17. The record does not say whether the hypothesis is superiority or non-inferiority, which adds uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: OSDI changes of roughly 10-16 points occur in artificial-tear arms at 12 weeks in dry eye trials.

reason: A phosphate absorption inhibitor added to stable binders should raise the share reaching the target range clearly above placebo; 50 per arm is small but the expected gap is large.
rationale: TS-172 is an intestinal phosphate transport inhibitor. Earlier Japanese phase 2 data showed dose-dependent serum phosphorus lowering, and the NaPi/NHE3-type class (tenapanor) added to binders lowers phosphorus by about 1-2 mg/dL. Placebo plus binders typically gets 15-25% to target, so a 35-45 point gap is expected; 50 per arm is adequate for that.
evidence: Tenapanor with binders PHREEDOM and NORMALIZE 2019

assumptions.claim: Tenapanor added to binders lowered serum phosphorus by roughly 1-2 mg/dL more than placebo in hemodialysis patients.
assumptions.source: Tenapanor Japanese phase 3 and NORMALIZE trials 2019-2021

assumptions.claim: In Japan, the target serum phosphorus range for dialysis patients is 3.5-6.0 mg/dL.

reason: A GLP-1/GIP dual agonist should beat semaglutide on 52-week weight loss, but the semaglutide dose is unknown and a head-to-head gap may be only a few points.
rationale: HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP agonist whose Chinese placebo-controlled phase 3 produced tirzepatide-like weight loss of around 15-18% at 48 weeks, while semaglutide 2.4 mg in Chinese adults loses about 9-11%. A gap of 4-8 points with 286 per arm is very likely significant, so risk lies in the semaglutide dose, open-label bias, and a lower HRS9531 dose being used.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide 2.4 mg gives about 9-11% weight loss at 44-52 weeks in East Asian adults with obesity.
assumptions.source: STEP 7, Kadowaki et al, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2022

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide beat semaglutide by about 6.5 points on weight loss at 72 weeks in a head-to-head trial.

reason: Exploratory phase 2a with about 17 boys per arm, a noisy dynamometry endpoint over 12 weeks, and a first-in-class mechanism makes a significant strength gain unlikely.
rationale: SAT-3247 is a first-in-class AAK1 inhibitor aiming to restore muscle stem-cell polarity; human efficacy data are limited. The study is labelled exploratory, has about 17 per arm, and measures dynamometry-based force over 12 weeks, which is noisy in boys aged 7-9. A nominally significant gain is possible if the company reports it, but safety co-primaries are descriptive and the bar is high.

assumptions.claim: SAT-3247 is an oral small-molecule AAK1 inhibitor developed by Satellos for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
Part 1 is a 12-week placebo-controlled phase with up to 51 participants in total.

reason: If HRS-9563 is an RAAS-pathway siRNA like zilebesiran, a 10-15 mmHg ambulatory SBP drop versus placebo is expected, and 119 per arm is ample; main risk is a weak lowest or only tested dose.
rationale: HRS-9563 appears to be a long-acting injectable acting on the RAAS (likely an angiotensinogen siRNA, exclusion of RAAS-inhibitor-requiring patients fits). Zilebesiran produced 24-hour SBP falls of about 10-17 mmHg versus placebo at months 3-6 in KARDIA-1. With 238 patients and SD near 9, an effect of that size is significant; dose-ranging and a possible smaller top-dose arm add variance.

assumptions.claim: Zilebesiran gave placebo-adjusted 24-hour SBP reductions of about 10-17 mmHg at 3 months in KARDIA-1.
The enrolment target is 238 patients, split across HRS-9563 and saline placebo.

reason: Untreated chronic HDV rarely achieves a 2-log RNA drop plus ALT normalization in 12 weeks, so the comparison against brelovitug 300 mg weekly is very likely to be met; the trial mainly supports a larger pivotal programme.
rationale: Open-label, delayed-treatment control with an untreated week-12 composite expected near 0-5% (bulevirtide MYR301 delayed arm 2% at week 48). Brelovitug (BJT-778) phase 2 showed deep HDV RNA falls and high ALT normalization by week 24, so a response of roughly 55-70% is likely. With 40 vs 20 patients the difference is far beyond chance. Main uncertainty is timing of disclosure, not the result.

assumptions.claim: In MYR301 the delayed-treatment arm had about 2% combined response (HDV RNA and ALT) at week 48 versus about 45-48% on bulevirtide.
assumptions.source: MYR301, Wedemeyer et al., Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol/J Hepatol 2023 (NCT03852719)

reason: Novel oral mechanism with unproven AD efficacy; about 52 per arm needs a roughly 15-point EASI percent difference to reach significance against a placebo arm that typically improves 25-40%.
rationale: First-in-class oral drug from a private company, phase 2 with ~52 per arm and EASI percent change SD around 40 points; detectable difference is about 15 points. Phase 2 AD trials of novel oral agents often show 10-25 point separations when the mechanism is valid, but placebo response is large and mechanism is unvalidated. Early companies tend to announce when positive, nudging conditional probability up slightly.

reason: Event-driven prevention trial: a potent mAb should show large relative efficacy, but low placebo attack rate over 90 days or variant escape could leave too few events for significance.
rationale: Potent half-life-extended mAb designed against current variants; prior COVID prophylactic mAbs (PROVENT 77%, EVADE 66% relative risk reduction) met clinical-endpoint primaries. Risks are a low 90-day attack rate in healthy volunteers (about 3%, giving only ~20 placebo events) and variant mismatch. Either VYD2311 dose meeting the objective is enough, and Invivyd tends to announce promptly.

assumptions.claim: In PROVENT, tixagevimab/cilgavimab reduced symptomatic COVID-19 by 77% versus placebo in a prophylaxis setting.

reason: Small safety-primary phase 2 in moderate-to-severe asthma with strict spirometry and ACQ criteria and 20 US sites; the registered December 2026 completion looks optimistic while still recruiting in late October 2026, so a slip beyond March 2027 is about a coin flip. Private sponsor, so results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
Novel oral CNS mechanism in heterogeneous isolated dystonia on the BFM scale, where placebo response is noisy and true effects are small relative to a 50-per-arm sample.
rationale: No oral drug is approved for dystonia and earlier oral candidates have mostly failed to separate from placebo on BFM. Heterogeneous multi-region dystonia, BFM change SD around 5-6 points, 50 per arm gives power only for a 3-point difference. Phase 2 novel mechanism success base rate for CNS drugs is about 25-35%. Primary completion March 2027 likely slips, so readout by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Phase 2 trials in dystonia using BFM, e.g. zolpidem and trihexyphenidyl studies (various)

reason: Three co-primary self-reported outcomes (stress, anxiety, sleep) must all be met by the same arm in a 60-per-arm supplement trial with a large placebo response.
rationale: Four-arm single-site supplement trial, 60 per arm, with PSS-10 change SD near 6 and a sizeable placebo effect (about 3 points). Lavender oil has some positive literature for anxiety and sleep, but requiring all three co-primary outcomes lowers the chance. Publication by June 2027 is unlikely (primary completion February 2027), and results that appear early are more often positive.
evidence: Silexan (lavender oil) anxiety RCTs, Kasper et al. 2014
PEA sleep and stress supplement trials (various)

reason: Pilot-sized digital therapeutic trial (20 per arm) against an active comparator app; PCL-5 change SD about 14 means only a difference of roughly 9 points would be significant.
rationale: Small NIMH-supported efficacy pilot comparing an interoceptive-exposure app with a comparator app, so the control arm also improves. With 20 per arm and PCL-5 change SD about 14, power to detect a 6-point difference is low. Digital therapeutic pilots are often positive when published, and company-driven disclosure favours positive results.
evidence: Digital interoceptive exposure for anxiety sensitivity pilot studies (various)

reason: Phase 2 safety-primary trial in generalized social anxiety disorder, 100 patients at 11 US sites; registered January 2027 completion is tight for a psychiatric population, so a slip past the May 2027 threshold is about as likely as not. Private sponsor, results posting by August 2027 unlikely.
Subcutaneous Lp(a)-lowering agent should reduce Lp(a) massively versus placebo; the realistic risk is unexpectedly low potency of a new molecule or disclosure that never states the primary result.
rationale: Subcutaneous dose-finding study of Lp(a) lowering; siRNA and antisense agents in this class cut Lp(a) 70-100% versus placebo (olpasiran phase 2, pelacarsen phase 2). The highest dose against placebo with about 100 patients easily reaches significance if the molecule works at all. Placebo change is near zero. Uncertainty lies in the potency of a first-generation candidate.

assumptions.claim: Olpasiran 75 mg or more every 12 weeks lowered Lp(a) by roughly 97-101% versus placebo at week 36 in the phase 2 dose-finding trial.

reason: ANGPTL3 antibody should cut triglycerides by about half; a 367-patient trial with a 24-week mean endpoint is well powered, so failure would need an unexpectedly weak drug effect or a large placebo response.
rationale: SHR-1918 is an ANGPTL3 monoclonal antibody. ANGPTL3 inhibition (evinacumab, zodasiran, vupanorsen) lowers triglycerides roughly 40-60% in dyslipidemia, versus little change on placebo. With about 180 per arm and an SD near 35 points, a 40-point difference is far beyond the significance threshold. Hengrui rarely issues timely result releases, so public timing is the main uncertainty, not the result.

assumptions.claim: ANGPTL3 inhibitors lower triglycerides by roughly half in dyslipidemia patients.
assumptions.source: Gaudet et al., NEJM 2024 (zodasiran phase 2); Raal et al., NEJM 2020 (ELIPSE)

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in hypertriglyceridemia trials show small mean TG changes (within about 15 percent).

reason: Baseline is IOP after a latanoprost run-in, so the fixed combination must add lowering on top of latanoprost within 14 days in only 32 patients per arm; the add-on effect may be small.
rationale: Patients are run in on preservative-free latanoprost, so the control arm should move little (about -1 mmHg). QLS-111 (episcleral venous pressure lowering, different mechanism) should add roughly 1.5-2.5 mmHg. With 32 per arm and SD near 2.8, power is moderate. A small private sponsor is more likely to announce when the result is favourable, which lifts p_met given a public statement.

assumptions.claim: QLS-111 lowers IOP by a clinically relevant amount, including as add-on to a prostaglandin analogue, in earlier Qlaris phase 2 work.
assumptions.source: Qlaris Bio press releases on QLS-111 phase 2 (2024-2025)

reason: Oral incretin-type weight-loss drug in overweight hypertensive patients should lower SBP clearly, but a large placebo response (regression to the mean, lifestyle management) could shrink the difference in a 160-patient phase 2.
rationale: VCT220 is an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist; weight loss of around 8-10 percent over 20 weeks should bring SBP falls of about 8 mmHg beyond placebo, in line with tirzepatide and other incretin trials in obesity. With 80 per arm and SD near 12 mmHg, a difference of 8 mmHg gives z near 4. Placebo response and dose uncertainty are the main risks.

assumptions.claim: Incretin-based weight loss therapy lowers systolic BP by about 5-8 mmHg more than placebo in people with obesity.

reason: Randomized withdrawal from an orexin agonist should bring rapid relapse on placebo versus maintained response on drug; failure would need unusually few events or a loose loss-of-response definition.
rationale: TAK-861 (oveporexton) produced large, fast gains in sleepiness and wakefulness in NT1 in phase 2b and phase 3. Withdrawal designs for symptomatic drugs with short effect duration give large placebo-versus-drug separation within days, so about 60-90 randomized patients are enough. Main uncertainty is the loss-of-response threshold and how many are randomized; timing of any Takeda disclosure is also uncertain.

assumptions.claim: TAK-861 improved MWT sleep latency and ESS markedly versus placebo in NT1 patients in the phase 2b trial.

reason: Vaxcyte phase 3 coadministration study already fully enrolled with primary completion registered for March 2027; slippage past June is unlikely, results posting by August 2027 is unlikely, and one primary time frame looks like a typo that could be edited.

Single-centre German ovulation-inhibition study was still recruiting in October 2026, 11 months after start, with 84 days of treatment per participant; the November 2026 completion date will likely slip, though an unedited record counts as late.

Small Australian phase 2a already past recruitment with primary completion at day 28, registered for December 2026; a delay past March 2027 is unlikely, and a small sponsor is unlikely to post results by August 2027.

Dose-exploration study against remifentanil with no stated hypothesis; remifentanil is highly titratable and likely to keep patients in target range most of the time, so superiority is unlikely and a formal win may not be declared.
rationale: Phase 2 dose-exploration with a positive comparator and no stated superiority or non-inferiority hypothesis. Remifentanil is a short-acting, easily titrated opioid and should achieve target analgesia-sedation for most of the time, leaving little room for superiority. Hengrui seldom releases phase 2 results promptly, so a statement by mid-2027 is unlikely; if one appears, it more likely reports comparable efficacy than a formal win.

assumptions.claim: Remifentanil-based analgesia-sedation keeps most ventilated ICU patients within target sedation range most of the time.
assumptions.source: Muellejans et al., Crit Care 2004 (remifentanil vs fentanyl-based sedation in ICU)

reason: Tenapanor 50 mg BID is an active secretagogue-type laxative with proven benefit in IBS-C, but the durable CSBM criterion is strict and placebo response in CIC may erode the gap.
rationale: Tenapanor 50 mg BID beat placebo in IBS-C phase 3 (27.0% vs 18.7% responders) and works by increasing luminal sodium and water. In CIC, durable CSBM response (9 of 12 weeks, 3 of last 4) is strict: placebo should be about 7%, active about 18-20%, as with linaclotide and plecanatide. About 173 per arm gives good power, and three doses give extra chances. Topline probably arrives after the 26-week study ends, around Q3 2027.

assumptions.claim: In T3MPO-1, tenapanor 50 mg BID gave a 6/12-week responder rate of 27.0% versus 18.7% on placebo in IBS-C.
assumptions.source: Chey et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2020 (T3MPO-1)

assumptions.claim: In linaclotide CIC phase 3 trials, the 12-week overall responder rate was roughly 20% versus 6% on placebo.

reason: DLCO% is a noisy endpoint with spontaneous recovery in the placebo arm, and 600 mg pirfenidone is a lowish dose; a modest benefit may not reach significance with about 99 per arm.
rationale: Pirfenidone has antifibrotic activity and small Chinese studies suggest benefit in radiation pneumonitis/fibrosis, so some true effect on DLCO is plausible. But DLCO% change has large between-patient variance (SD about 9-10 points), placebo patients recover spontaneously as steroids taper, and a 600 mg arm vs placebo with about 99 per arm needs roughly 3.5 points for significance. Recruitment started March 2026, so reporting before mid-2027 is very unlikely.
evidence: Pirfenidone for radiation pneumonitis, small Chinese RCTs

assumptions.claim: Pirfenidone slows FVC decline in IPF versus placebo.
DLCO measurement in lung-injury populations has an SD of change of roughly 8 to 12 points of predicted.
assumptions.source: Pulmonary function trials in ILD, e.g. INBUILD 2019

reason: A GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonist at its top dose over 28 weeks should clearly beat placebo on weight; the main risk is tolerability-driven dropouts or an under-dosed top dose, not lack of effect.
rationale: UBT251 is a triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon receptor agonist licensed to Novo Nordisk. Comparable agents (retatrutide, survodutide) gave 10-17% weight loss versus about 1-2% on placebo within 24-46 weeks, so a significant difference at the top dose of a 28-week Part B is near certain if it is reported. Uncertainty is mainly how and when the sponsor discloses a phase 2 readout.
evidence: Survodutide phase 2 obesity, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2024

assumptions.claim: Triple agonist retatrutide gave about 17.5% weight loss at 24 weeks at the 12 mg dose versus about 1.6% on placebo.
UBT251 is a GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist developed by United Laboratories and licensed to Novo Nordisk.
assumptions.source: Novo Nordisk/United Laboratories licence announcement, March 2023

reason: Tiny pilot (8 enrolled against 40 planned, enrollment closed) by a Chinese sponsor; completion is likely on time, but a stop or primary-outcome trimming is plausible and results posting within the window is unlikely.
About 80 per arm and a dichotomous mRS 0-1 endpoint at day 90 give wide noise; a plausible 7-10 point gain would often miss significance, and three doses add multiplicity.
rationale: Phase IIb dose-finding in non-thrombolysed AIS (NIHSS 6-20) with 3 doses vs placebo, 80 per arm. Placebo mRS 0-1 likely around 30-35%; an effective neuroprotective agent might add 8-12 points, but the SE of the difference is about 7 points, so significance at one dose is roughly a one-in-three event. Chinese stroke phase 2 trials report positive outcomes somewhat more often than Western ones, offset by small size. Public disclosure before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Human urinary kallidinogenase stroke trials, China

assumptions.claim: In non-thrombolysed Chinese AIS trials with moderate NIHSS, placebo mRS 0-1 at 90 days is roughly 30-40%.
The record states 320 patients over 4 arms at a single listed site with three doses (5600, 8400, 12600 IU) and placebo.

reason: Sponsor-run zinc citrate versus fluoride-only toothpaste comparisons on organoleptic malodor usually favour the zinc product and are mostly disclosed when positive; the risk is a null result.
rationale: Colgate trials of zinc-containing toothpaste against a regular fluoride dentifrice for oral malodor typically report significant organoleptic reductions at 3 weeks, since the control has no malodor-active ingredient and the organoleptic score has small variance. Forty per arm is adequate for such effects. The comparison is superiority on change from baseline; publication/disclosure is selective toward positive results.
evidence: Colgate zinc citrate oral malodor studies, J Clin Dent

assumptions.claim: Zinc-containing dentifrices reduce organoleptic malodor more than non-zinc fluoride dentifrices over 3 weeks.
assumptions.source: Colgate-sponsored clinical studies, J Clin Dent 2010-2020

assumptions.claim: The study is registered as completed on 2026-07-05 with 80 participants at one site in China.

reason: An IL-4R-pathway biologic at its top dose should clearly beat placebo on EASI percent change; with only about 24 per arm the chance risk is small but non-zero.
rationale: IBI3002 targets the IL-4R-alpha/TSLP axis, and dupilumab-like blockade gives about 70% EASI improvement versus 30-37% on placebo at week 16. A proof-of-concept study with a dupilumab reference arm and a top-dose arm of about 24 versus 24 should easily reach significance on a large difference of 35-45 points. Public disclosure before mid-2027 is unlikely given primary completion in March 2027.

assumptions.claim: In SOLO 1/2, mean EASI percent change at week 16 was about -72% on dupilumab and about -38% on placebo.
IBI3002 is an IL-4R-alpha/TSLP bispecific antibody from Innovent.

reason: Already completed in September 2026; a US biotech subsidiary typically posts results near the 12-month deadline (September 2027), so posting by August 2027 is less likely than not, and primary outcomes rarely change after completion.
Only about 30 per arm, so a lower-than-expected response at 50 mg or a high placebo response could miss significance, though hormone-suppressing agents usually show large bleeding effects.
rationale: Fibroid menorrhagia trials of oral GnRH antagonists show responders (MBL under 80 mL and at least 50% reduction) of about 65-80% on drug versus 10-19% on placebo (elagolix, relugolix, linzagolix). If CMS-D002 has a similar mechanism, the top dose of 50 mg should separate easily even at n=30 per arm. A novel mechanism and one-site recruitment add uncertainty. Early public disclosure is unlikely from a small Chinese sponsor.

assumptions.claim: In LIBERTY 1 and 2, the responder rate on placebo was about 15-19% versus 73-77% on relugolix combination therapy.
The record lists 120 patients over four arms at one site in China with 12-week dosing.

reason: Rare disease (primary vitreoretinal lymphoma) with a single site and 20 planned patients: recruitment is slow and completion past March 2027 is about as likely as not; results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
Single-site Chinese phase IIa with 24 patients, started September 2025 and still recruiting in October 2026, so completion slipping past March 2027 is common; results posting is unlikely.

Phase 2 topical analgesic with two doses against vehicle in a PRK pain model; n of about 43 per arm gives only modest power for a 0.5 to 1 point NRS difference, and the vehicle arm gets bandage lens and rescue medication.
rationale: Novel topical agent, mechanism unknown to me. PRK pain is a sensitive model that has separated active drugs from vehicle, and either dose meeting the objective is enough, which helps. Against that, about 43 per arm, an NRS SD near 2.4 and a vehicle arm that also gets rescue analgesia make a clear win uncertain. Phase 2 pain trials succeed in roughly 40 percent of cases.
evidence: Nepafenac and ketorolac PRK pain trials (2000s)
FACTT-style typical NRS variability in post-PRK pain studies

assumptions.claim: Post-PRK ocular pain peaks within the first 24 to 72 hours and is usually reported at about 4 to 6 on a 0 to 10 scale in control groups.
assumptions.source: Published PRK postoperative pain studies (e.g., ketorolac/NSAID vs vehicle trials)

reason: ARDS drug trials on ventilator-free days have a very poor record, VFD has a large SD driven by deaths, and the drug is a new injectable of unknown mechanism; a one-site record with 309 patients will also likely slip.
rationale: Sepsis-associated ARDS trials of novel agents have rarely shown a VFD gain; SD of VFD near 10 days with 155 per arm gives a standard error of about 1.1 days, so a true gain of 1 to 2 days is borderline. Chinese phase 2 programmes publish mainly positive results, which lifts the conditional chance somewhat. Oxygenation index is a more sensitive secondary.

assumptions.claim: Mean ventilator-free days to day 28 in ARDS control arms are typically 10 to 15.

reason: Glabellar line toxin trials against placebo almost always succeed; the only realistic failure is an unexpectedly weak product or an unusual dose, and the composite ILA plus SSA endpoint is stricter but still easily met.
rationale: Botulinum toxin products have met placebo-controlled glabellar line endpoints in essentially every pivotal trial, with placebo responders near zero and active composite responders of 60 to 75 percent. Corabotase is a modified toxin with positive phase 2 data, 309 patients gives huge power for a roughly 60 point difference, and the sponsor has two pivotal studies. Residual risk is dose or formulation surprises.

assumptions.claim: Placebo composite responder rates in glabellar line phase 3 trials are below 3 percent at week 4.
Active-arm composite responder rates in recent toxin pivotal trials are about 60 to 75 percent.

reason: Active, not recruiting phase 2 with a registered primary completion in November 2026; Regeneron tends to post results close to the 12-month deadline, so posting before September 2027 is unlikely.

On-demand SERT inhibitors reliably prolong IELT in lifelong premature ejaculation and a within-patient crossover with 40 men is well powered; the risk is a novel agent with weak sublingual exposure or a large placebo response.
rationale: Dapoxetine and other on-demand SSRIs raise geometric mean IELT about two to three fold over baseline of under 1 minute, versus smaller placebo gains. A two-period crossover removes between-patient variance, so 40 men detect a 0.5 minute difference easily. Residual risk comes from an unproven sublingual formulation, carry-over and a small single-site Australian study.
evidence: McMahon et al. dapoxetine phase 3 trials

assumptions.claim: In dapoxetine pivotal trials baseline IELT was about 0.9 min, placebo reached about 1.75 min and dapoxetine 30 mg about 2.8 min.

reason: Large placebo-controlled toxin pivotal; the North America and EU/ROW primaries each need to be met and the Japan and European subsets are smaller, but a high-potency toxin should clear both comfortably.
rationale: Same product and endpoints as the sister trial LAURITE 1 with a larger double-blind phase. Glabellar line toxins virtually always beat placebo by 60 points or more on composite ILA and SSA response. The only extra risk is the dual regional primaries, which need both to be reported met, and that the long open-label design delays or dilutes reporting.

assumptions.claim: Placebo responders on composite glabellar line endpoints are near zero in toxin phase 3 trials.

reason: TYK2 inhibition acts on the type I interferon axis that drives CLE, but percent change in CLASI-A has a wide SD and a large placebo response, and 35 per arm leaves little margin.
rationale: ICP-488 is an oral TYK2 JH2 inhibitor with positive psoriasis data, and TYK2 or interferon blockade has shown benefit in SLE and CLE (deucravacitinib PAISLEY, anifrolumab, litifilimab). The test is a percent change in CLASI-A at week 16 with a placebo response of roughly 30 percent and SD near 40, so 35 per arm detects only a 20 to 25 point gap. Either dose may meet it.

assumptions.claim: Deucravacitinib, a TYK2 inhibitor, improved SLE response rates over placebo in a phase 2 trial (SRI-4 58 percent vs 34 percent).

reason: Enrolling by invitation with a registered primary completion of December 2026 and a week-16 primary, so last-patient timing could push the date past March 2027; Tarsus is a US-listed company that tends to post results near the deadline.

The stated hypothesis is only effective relaxation with acceptable safety, so a formal superiority test may not be reported; a differentiating shorter recovery than cisatracurium would give a clear significant result, but publication is uncertain.
rationale: HRS-9190 is a novel neuromuscular blocker; a new agent would be pursued mainly if recovery is faster than cisatracurium, which takes about 45 to 70 minutes to TOFr 0.9 after infusion. But the summary frames the hypothesis as effective relaxation with acceptable safety, not superiority, and a Chinese sponsor may publish only at a congress or in a journal later. If a result is public it is likely favourable.
evidence: Gantacurium and CW002 fumarate NMB phase 2 reports

assumptions.claim: After continuous cisatracurium infusion, spontaneous recovery to TOFr 0.9 takes roughly 45 to 70 minutes.

reason: With about 10 women per arm a significant difference needs roughly 5 of 10 against 0 of 10; the biology (chlorhexidine clearing plus Lactobacillus supplementation) points to a large effect but the sponsor may report descriptively without a formal test.
rationale: FB301 is a live Lactobacillus-dominant vaginal product, given after chlorhexidine to reduce the dysbiotic flora; a large conversion to Lactobacillus dominance is plausible, perhaps 50 percent against 10 percent on placebo. But a Fisher test with 10 per arm needs a big gap, spontaneous conversion varies with the cycle, and a small private sponsor may report only descriptive molecular results.

assumptions.claim: Live biotherapeutic L. crispatus CTV-05 after antibiotic reduced recurrent bacterial vaginosis (30 vs 45 percent recurrence) in a phase 2b trial.

reason: A single-site 8-week supplement study in healthy adults with a research metabolite (ImP) that varies a lot between people; a real shift in ImP is biologically uncertain and 45 per arm gives modest power.
rationale: Oleoylethanolamide acting on gut-microbiome histidine metabolism to lower plasma imidazole propionate in healthy, non-diabetic adults within 8 weeks is a speculative mechanism. ImP has large between-person variability and healthy baselines are low. Industry-sponsored supplement trials publish selectively and favour positive findings, which lifts p_met slightly given a public result.
evidence: Koh 2018 Cell (imidazole propionate impairs insulin signalling)

assumptions.claim: Plasma imidazole propionate is elevated in type 2 diabetes and linked to insulin resistance.

reason: About 30 patients per arm with an 8-week office SBP endpoint; a presumed aldosterone synthase inhibitor should lower SBP by roughly 8 to 12 mmHg versus placebo, but the small sample leaves a real chance of a miss.
rationale: HRS-1780 is presumably an aldosterone synthase inhibitor, a class that lowers blood pressure in primary aldosteronism (baxdrostat and lorundrostat phase 2 data, roughly 10 to 20 mmHg placebo-adjusted). Primary aldosteronism is a high-renin-independent, aldosterone-driven disease, so response should be strong. With SD about 14 and 30 per arm, a 9 mmHg effect gives roughly 70% power.

assumptions.claim: Aldosterone synthase inhibitors lowered office SBP by roughly 8 to 20 mmHg versus placebo in hypertension trials.

reason: Open-label phase 2 titration comparison with a hypoglycemia-incidence primary; last participant already enrolled and a 20-week treatment fits the registered completion, so on-time completion is likely. Hengrui rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov.
rationale: Operations only. Status active, not recruiting with 20-week treatment; Chinese sponsor seldom posts results by the read date.

reason: Tafolecimab (anti-PCSK9) is already approved in China with a roughly 60 to 70 percent LDL-C lowering; a placebo-controlled monotherapy trial of about 99 per arm will almost certainly be positive, so the risk is only reporting or analysis quirks.
rationale: IBI306 is tafolecimab, a PCSK9 monoclonal antibody already approved in China. CREDIT-1, CREDIT-2 and CREDIT-4 showed placebo-adjusted LDL-C reductions of about 55 to 70 percent at week 12. Without background statin the effect is large and the trial is a near-certain success on the primary; baseline LDL-C 2.6 to 4.9 mmol/L makes the <2.6 responder endpoint easy to meet.

assumptions.claim: Tafolecimab lowered LDL-C by about 55 to 70 percent versus placebo at week 12 in the CREDIT program.

reason: Descriptive dose-ranging study of weekly alirocumab by Regeneron; enrollment already closed with 438 participants and a 12-week primary, so on-time primary completion is likely, and Regeneron typically posts results around the 12-month deadline.
rationale: Operations only. Active, not recruiting; primary completion Dec 2026 means a results-posting deadline of about Dec 2027, so posting by Aug 2027 is unlikely.

reason: Nine co-primary measures must all be met in a 24-person crossover, which is very unlikely even if the drug has real effects; sponsors of such phase 2a studies typically report mixed or exploratory pharmacodynamic signals.
rationale: The round requires all co-primary outcomes to be met. With nine fMRI, behavioural and questionnaire outcomes in 24 participants, at least one will almost surely miss. Even a sponsor stating a positive pharmacodynamic signal would probably cite a subset. Small private company, one UK site, still recruiting.
evidence: Phase 2a experimental-medicine crossover designs in anxiety (e.g. amygdala fMRI studies)

assumptions.claim: The record lists nine primary outcomes for a 24-participant crossover study.

reason: Open-label microbiome study at two German sites that is still recruiting; the one-month recruitment tail and week-3 primary make a slip beyond June 2027 plausible but not the base case. Small private sponsor, so results unlikely to be posted by August 2027.
rationale: Operations only. Recruiting with 120 women across four groups; a delay past 1 June 2027 depends on enrolment pace.

reason: Oral RSV antivirals have struggled to show clinical benefit on symptom-resolution endpoints in treated patients, and 75 children per arm with a noisy clinician-rated endpoint leaves little power; zelicapavir's adult phase 2b missed or gave only subgroup signals.
rationale: Zelicapavir showed strong viral-load effects in the adult challenge study but clinical-symptom benefit in naturally infected patients was weak (adult phase 2b did not clearly meet its primary). Infants are mostly symptomatic at presentation and recover on their own within a week, so the window to show an effect is short; 150 children is small. Ziresovir succeeding in hospitalized infants is the main counterpoint.
evidence: Enanta EDP-938 adult RSV challenge study 2020

assumptions.claim: Zelicapavir reduced RSV viral load in the human challenge study.
assumptions.source: DeVincenzo et al., NEJM 2020 (EDP-938 challenge study)

reason: TL1A blockade has no proven efficacy in psoriatic arthritis, and with about 47 per arm a true 15 to 20 point ACR20 gain gives only borderline power; placebo ACR20 of 25 to 35 percent compresses the gap.
rationale: Tulisokibart works in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, but TL1A's role in psoriatic arthritis is less established. Phase 2 PsA trials of effective mechanisms typically show ACR20 of 50 to 65 percent versus 20 to 30 percent on placebo; if TL1A is only modestly active the 47-per-arm design will not reach significance. Multiple doses give some multiplicity benefit.

assumptions.claim: Placebo ACR20 at week 16 in biologic-naive PsA phase 2/3 trials is typically 15 to 33 percent.

reason: Oral HIF-PH inhibitors have matched ESA on Hb maintenance in non-inferiority designs; the main risks are an unstated margin, an open-label design with titration noise and slower-than-registered enrolment.
rationale: AND017 is an oral HIF prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor; class precedents (roxadustat, daprodustat, enarodustat) met non-inferiority against ESA for Hb maintenance in NDD-CKD in China and globally, with margins of 0.5 to 1.0 g/dL. 120 per arm and SD about 1 g/dL give a standard error near 0.13 g/dL. Still recruiting in Oct 2026, so timelines will slip well past the registered completion.

assumptions.claim: HIF-PH inhibitors were non-inferior to ESA for mean Hb in NDD-CKD in phase 3 trials.

reason: Highest of three doses against placebo on 2+ background drugs with 65 per arm; a placebo-adjusted drop near 8 mmHg is detectable, but a large placebo response or a weak dose could erase it.
rationale: Likely a novel oral antihypertensive (probably aldosterone-synthase-class) tested in uncontrolled or resistant hypertension; such agents lowered SBP by roughly 8-11 mmHg over placebo at top doses in phase 2. With SD about 14 and 65 per arm, SE is about 2.5 mmHg, so an effect near -8 gives good power. Placebo response in Chinese trials can be large. Highest dose of three counts.

assumptions.claim: Aldosterone-synthase inhibitors lowered seated SBP by about 9-11 mmHg versus placebo in resistant hypertension phase 2 trials.
Placebo arms in uncontrolled hypertension trials on background therapy fall by roughly 5-9 mmHg SBP at 12 weeks.

reason: Phase 2a with about 45 per arm and several co-primaries; HU6 likely cuts liver fat substantially, but the placebo response and a lower than expected dose effect could blur significance.
rationale: HU6 (controlled metabolic accelerator) reduced liver fat and weight in earlier phase 2a obesity work, and MRI-PDFF is sensitive to metabolic drugs: effects of 25-40 points relative to placebo are typical for active agents. With about 45 per arm and SD near 30 points, the highest dose should reach significance, and the 30 percent responder primary is highly correlated. Registered completion is optimistic since recruiting continues.

assumptions.claim: Active MASH agents reduce MRI-PDFF liver fat by roughly 30-50 percent relative at 12-26 weeks versus about 5-10 percent on placebo.

reason: Oral HIF-PH inhibitor against ESA in dialysis, a class that reliably shows non-inferior Hb maintenance; risk is a tight margin or unusual control-arm stability, not the drug.
rationale: HIF-PHIs (roxadustat, daprodustat, desidustat, enarodustat) met non-inferiority to ESA for Hb maintenance in dialysis in every phase 3 program, with mean Hb differences within about 0.2 g/dL. With 150 per arm and SD about 1.0, SE is about 0.12, which supports a usual margin of 0.5-1.0 g/dL. Remaining risk is an unusually strict margin or poor adherence.

assumptions.claim: HIF-PHIs showed non-inferior mean Hb versus ESA in dialysis patients in phase 3 trials.

reason: mRNA H5 vaccine in naive adults should produce HAI 1:40 in most recipients versus a few percent on placebo; the risk is how the sponsor frames the result, as thresholds or descriptive rather than a stated test.
rationale: Phase 1/2 data for mRNA-1018 showed high HAI seroresponse after two doses in naive adults, and H5 HAI titres are negligible in placebo recipients. With 2025 per arm a superiority comparison is trivially met. Main uncertainty is whether the sponsor states primary endpoints as met, and whether lower response in older adults pulls the overall rate down.

assumptions.claim: Two doses of mRNA-1018 in H5-naive adults produced HAI titres of at least 1:40 in the large majority of participants in phase 1/2.
Baseline H5 HAI titres of at least 1:40 are rare in adults without pandemic influenza exposure.
assumptions.source: published H5N1 seroprevalence surveys; mRNA-1018-P101 placebo arm

reason: Fluorescence imaging in lung surgery routinely finds additional lesions in a substantial share of patients, so a significant event rate is likely; the odd control group of 12 with no imaging adds a statistical formality risk.
rationale: Abenacianine showed clinically significant events (lesions missed by standard methods) in a large share of patients in earlier lung studies. The primary is a within-patient event rate; with 115 or more evaluable patients a rate near 25-45 percent would clear any plausible threshold, and even a Fisher test against 12 no-imaging controls is likely significant at high rates. A single IV dose makes dropouts for adverse events near zero.

assumptions.claim: In earlier abenacianine lung studies a sizeable fraction of patients (about a third or more) had at least one clinically significant event with NIR imaging.
assumptions.source: Vergent Bioscience VISUALIZE phase 3 / phase 2 reports

reason: Only 32 per arm with a modest expected placebo-adjusted HbA1c effect off treatment at week 26; a true effect near 0.6 points only gives moderate power.
rationale: Icovamenib (menin inhibitor) showed placebo-adjusted HbA1c reductions at week 26 after 12 weeks of dosing in COVALENT-111/112, larger in selected insulin-deficient patients. This trial restricts BMI to 32 or less and excludes GAD-positive patients, enriching for responders. With SD about 0.9 and 32 per arm, SE is about 0.23, so an effect of 0.6 is only borderline-to-good power. Biomea tends to report quickly.

assumptions.claim: Icovamenib 100 mg for 12 weeks produced placebo-adjusted HbA1c reductions at week 26 in T2D patients in COVALENT-111.

reason: Dry eye corneal staining shows a large vehicle response and phase 2 trials often miss the sign primary; a modest true effect with 209 per arm gives roughly one in three odds of significance.
rationale: Dry eye programs frequently miss signs endpoints against vehicle because vehicle drops corneal staining by about 1.5-2.5 NEI points. For an exploratory phase 2 of a novel agent with 209 per arm and SD near 2.8, a true effect of 0.5-0.7 points yields about 40 percent power. Staining is also less sensitive than symptoms to some mechanisms. Recruitment still open suggests delay.

assumptions.claim: Vehicle arms in dry eye trials show corneal fluorescein staining improvements of roughly 1.5-2.5 NEI points over 12 weeks.

reason: Oral arsenic should match IV arsenic on molecular remission, with rates near 95 percent in both arms; the main risk is an unstated margin or small-number noise, and the result will not come out before 2028.
rationale: ATO plus ATRA yields molecular CR near 95-100 percent after consolidation in low-risk APL (APL0406), and oral ATO formulations have produced similar results. A non-inferiority margin of 10 percent or so should be cleared with 75 per arm if the true rates are equal. Recruiting 150 low-risk APL patients and completing induction plus three consolidation cycles by 2027-03 is implausible, so reporting by mid-2027 is very unlikely.
evidence: Oral arsenic RIF/Ora-ATO trials in APL 2016-2021

assumptions.claim: ATO plus ATRA gives molecular remission in nearly all (about 95-100 percent) low-risk APL patients after consolidation.

reason: A THR-beta agonist adds little weight loss on top of semaglutide over 11 weeks, and five co-primaries including proportion with 5 percent loss must all be met.
rationale: THR-beta agonists such as resmetirom produce robust liver fat reductions but little weight loss, so a significant extra weight effect over semaglutide in an 11-week window is uncertain; semaglutide itself keeps lowering weight in both arms. Liver fat endpoints in the sub-study likely favour ECC4703, but co-primaries must all be met, including weight and the 5 percent proportion.

assumptions.claim: Resmetirom and other THR-beta agonists reduce liver fat markedly but cause little body weight change.

reason: The Part B primary is a pharmacodynamic knockdown of angiotensinogen, which an antisense agent achieves in nearly all treated patients; the only risk is reporting or design change.
rationale: Tonlamarsen is an antisense oligonucleotide against hepatic angiotensinogen; earlier studies of this class showed 60-90 percent plasma AGT lowering. Placebo AGT changes are near zero. With 70 per arm a difference of this size is overwhelming, so the PD primary will be met if reported. Part B follows Part A, so completion by 2026-12 is unrealistic and public results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Angiotensinogen-targeting antisense or siRNA agents lower plasma AGT by roughly 60-90 percent from baseline.

reason: Third molar model is highly sensitive to real analgesics, so the main risk is a novel-mechanism compound that is simply not efficacious at the tested single doses, or a small highest-dose arm.
rationale: Dental pain after impacted third molar removal is the classic assay-sensitive model: active analgesics separate from placebo with 40-50 per arm after a single dose, and highest dose alone suffices. Risk is an unproven novel mechanism with modest efficacy. Lilly seldom issues press releases for phase 2 pain; results mostly appear on ClinicalTrials.gov about a year after primary completion.
evidence: Suzetrigine (VX-548) phase 3 abdominoplasty and bunionectomy trials, 2024
Dental impaction pain model (ibuprofen vs placebo SPID) literature

assumptions.claim: Active analgesics reliably beat placebo on pain intensity difference after third molar extraction in single-dose studies of 40-50 patients per arm.
assumptions.source: Cooper and Beaver dental pain model reviews; Pain 2000s literature

assumptions.claim: Lilly posts phase 2 results on ClinicalTrials.gov roughly 12 months after primary completion rather than announcing them.
assumptions.source: ClinicalTrials.gov results-posting practice for Eli Lilly phase 2 studies

reason: P2X3 antagonism has no established proof of concept in IBS-D/M, and IBS pain trials carry a large placebo response, so a dose-ranging phase 2b may well show no separation on the primary.
rationale: Camlipixant is a selective P2X3 antagonist moved into IBS on a visceral hypersensitivity rationale without published efficacy in the disease. IBS abdominal pain trials typically show 1.7-2.3 point placebo improvements on a 0-10 scale and drug effects of 0.3-0.6 points at best. Several doses help (any dose counts) but 420 patients across arms is modest. GSK likely discloses at quarterly pipeline updates after June 2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in IBS-D phase 3 trials improve worst abdominal pain by roughly 1.7-2.3 points on a 0-10 scale over 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: Eluxadoline IBS-3001/3002, Lembo et al., NEJM 2016

assumptions.claim: No phase 2 efficacy data for camlipixant in IBS have been published before this study.

reason: With 18 per arm, only a very large cure-rate gap reaches p<0.05 at Day 8, and the strict VSS=0 definition keeps placebo cure low but also caps drug cure.
rationale: Occidiofungin is a potent antifungal, and VVC vehicle-controlled trials usually show 20-30% placebo cure versus 50-65% on active. With 18 per arm a Fisher test needs roughly 25% versus 65% or more to reach significance, so power is around 40-50%. A small private sponsor will likely publicise only if positive, which raises the conditional chance. Single site and acute VVC recruitment may slip.

assumptions.claim: Placebo clinical cure at test-of-cure in acute VVC phase 3 trials is about 20-30% versus 50-65% on active drug.
Fisher exact significance with 18 per arm requires a cure-rate gap of roughly 40 points at ~25% placebo cure.

reason: Beating tirzepatide on weight loss at week 40 in a 93-per-arm open-label phase 2 needs a 2+ point advantage, which few incretin candidates deliver; tirzepatide itself loses about 12-14% by then.
rationale: HDM1005 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist compared head-to-head with tirzepatide, a strong comparator giving about 12-14% loss at week 40 in Chinese adults. With SD near 6% and 93 per arm, a difference of about 2.3 points is needed for significance. A sponsor running such a design may expect parity or better, but superiority is a high bar. Key secondary (5% responders) hits a ceiling for both arms.
evidence: SURMOUNT-CN tirzepatide in Chinese adults with obesity, 2024

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide 10-15 mg in Chinese adults with obesity gives roughly 14-16% weight loss at week 52.
Over 95% of tirzepatide-treated participants reach at least 5% weight loss.

reason: Acute schizophrenia phase 2 with about 50 per arm detects only a 7-8 point PANSS difference; novel mechanisms have a high miss rate and placebo response in Chinese sites is sizeable.
rationale: Five-week inpatient design with PANSS at least 80 and two dose arms; the highest dose counts. A 7-point placebo-subtracted effect with SD 17 gives roughly 50% power at n=50. Novel antipsychotic mechanisms (ulotaront, emraclidine) have recently failed, while M1/M4 agonism and D2-active drugs succeed. Chinese biotech announcements are sporadic, favouring positive news.

assumptions.claim: Placebo mean PANSS change at week 5 was about -11.6 points in EMERGENT-2 versus -21.2 on xanomeline-trospium.
PANSS total change between-patient SD in acute schizophrenia trials is about 17-20 points.
assumptions.source: EMERGENT-2 and other acute schizophrenia trials

reason: The 15-minute effect of an alpha-agonist vasoconstrictor is near certain; the co-primary at 14 hours after Day 2 dosing is the risk because vasoconstrictor effect wanes and vehicle returns to baseline.
rationale: Apraclonidine is a potent alpha-2 (some alpha-1) vasoconstrictor; brimonidine 0.025% gave clear redness reduction versus vehicle within minutes in its phase 3 trials, so the 15-minute primary should be met. Both primaries must be met, and 840 minutes tests duration beyond the usual 8 hours. With 115 per arm and SD about 0.5, even a 0.2-point residual effect would be significant. Alcon rarely press-releases such trials.

assumptions.claim: Brimonidine 0.025% reduced investigator-assessed redness significantly versus vehicle at all measured timepoints up to 8 hours in phase 3.
Vehicle arms in ocular redness trials show a small reduction of about 0.2-0.4 scale points shortly after instillation.

reason: Postoperative pain models are assay-sensitive and any of three doses may win, so failure would need an unexpectedly weak compound or a high placebo plus rescue-medication effect.
rationale: Double-dummy post-abdominal-surgery trial with a morphine reference confirming assay sensitivity; analgesic candidates separate from placebo on 24-hour SPID in most phase 2 studies. Three doses give multiple chances. Residual risk is small arms (40 each), heavy rescue use in placebo, and sedation or tolerability limiting the dose. Haisco discloses Chinese phase 2 data selectively.

assumptions.claim: Opioid-type and other effective IV analgesics separate from placebo on SPID over 24 hours after abdominal or soft-tissue surgery in phase 2-3 trials.
Haisco has moved earlier postoperative-pain injectables from phase 2 to phase 3 within about a year.

reason: A 25-per-arm proof-of-concept needs a 30+ point IHS4-55 gap for p<0.05; even a truly effective biologic has only about 40% power.
rationale: IHS4-55 placebo response in HS trials is about 25%, while effective biologics reach about 45-55%. At 25 per arm, a 25-point difference has roughly 35-40% power, and efficacy of an unnamed mechanism is uncertain. Almirall tends to disclose at results updates, so public data by June 2027 is less likely and skewed toward positives.

assumptions.claim: Placebo HiSCR50 in HS phase 3 was about 29-32% in BE HEARD I/II versus about 48-52% on bimekizumab.
assumptions.source: BE HEARD I/II, Kimball et al., Lancet 2024

assumptions.claim: With 25 per arm, power to detect a 25-point responder difference is about 35-40%.

reason: Dry eye symptom trials have a very high failure rate from vehicle response; genotype enrichment and an earlier signal improve odds, but a 28-day symptom endpoint with about 80 per arm stays fragile.
rationale: Licaminlimab (OCS-02) is a topical anti-TNF antibody fragment; the sponsor reported a genotype-linked benefit on ocular discomfort in phase 2b, and this study prospectively tests the enriched population. Replication of a subgroup signal with about 80 per arm is uncertain, and vehicle effects in DED run high. Oculis is listed and announces topline results promptly, probably in Q1-Q2 2027.
evidence: Oculis OCS-02 phase 2b RELIEF genotype-guided dry eye, 2024
Dry eye phase 3 programmes (reproxalap, lifitegrast OPUS) with frequent failures

assumptions.claim: Oculis reported greater ocular discomfort improvement with licaminlimab versus vehicle in patients with the TNFR1 risk genotype in phase 2b.
assumptions.source: Oculis press release on RELIEF phase 2b, 2024

assumptions.claim: Enrolment is complete (status active, not recruiting) with primary completion registered for December 2026.

reason: With 20, 10 and 10 patients, a treatment-failure difference must be around 40+ points to reach p<0.05, so even a working oral agent will often miss.
rationale: Corticosteroid-taper design like VISUAL I, where most placebo patients fail by week 24 (about 70-78%). Effective oral agents bring failure to about 40-55%, which does not reach significance with 10 placebo patients unless the effect is dramatic. A slow-recruiting single-site Chinese study will finish late and Fosun rarely publicises phase 2 data quickly.
evidence: VISUAL I adalimumab in non-infectious uveitis, NEJM 2016
Brepocitinib phase 3 CLARITY in non-infectious uveitis, 2025

assumptions.claim: In VISUAL I about 78% of placebo patients had treatment failure by week 24 versus about 61% on adalimumab.
The record randomises 40 patients 2:1:1 to two FXS5626 doses and placebo, so the placebo arm has about 10 patients.

reason: Tiny 24-patient dose-comparison study by a small sponsor, 6 US sites, started Aug 2026 with a short Jan 2027 primary completion; enrolling mildly infected DFU patients with expert image confirmation will likely run slower than registered, and no results are likely on CT.gov by Aug 2027.

Only about 27 per arm on a coarse 0-3 staining grade after a vehicle run-in; vehicle response and regression to the mean will absorb much of any effect, so a significant difference is a coin-flip at best.
rationale: Stage 1 NK with grade 3 central staining, 27 per arm, 8-week TID dosing. Lacripep (lacritin fragment) improved corneal staining and sensation in earlier Sjogren's/dry-eye work, but the 0-3 scale is coarse, the vehicle run-in plus vehicle arm will improve, and n is small. A modest true effect gives about 30% chance of significance.
evidence: Lacripep phase 2 in primary Sjogren's dry eye (TearSolutions, NCT03226444)
Cenegermin NGF0214 trial 2016 (stage 2/3 NK, vehicle healing ~28%)

assumptions.claim: Lacripep reduced corneal staining and improved sensitivity in a phase 2 Sjogren's dry-eye study.
Vehicle arms in NK trials show substantial spontaneous improvement over 8 weeks.

reason: With 22-23 per arm and spontaneous regression of ASC-US/LSIL and HPV clearance in the placebo arm, both co-primary efficacy endpoints would need an implausibly large difference to reach significance.
rationale: Co-primary cytology regression and hr-HPV clearance must both be met with 22-23 per arm. Low-grade lesions and transient hr-HPV regress spontaneously (placebo roughly 25-40% cytology, 15-25% HPV clearance over ~80 days). EGCG/Polyphenon E has weak randomized evidence. Needs about 35-40 point difference on both, so success is unlikely.
evidence: Garcia 2014 Cancer Prev Res, Polyphenon E in HPV-related lesions
Ahn 2003 Eur J Cancer Prev, green tea extracts on cervical lesions

assumptions.claim: Low-grade cervical cytology abnormalities with hr-HPV regress spontaneously in a large share of untreated women within 3 months.
Randomized Polyphenon E trial in HPV-related lesions showed no clear benefit over placebo.
assumptions.source: Garcia FA et al, Cancer Prev Res 2014

reason: A systemic anti-IL-11 antibody must visibly change established scars (pliability, thickness) within 12 weeks in 15 patients per arm; placebo response on patient-reported items is sizable and the proof-of-concept is unproven.
rationale: Anti-IL-11 (profibrotic target) in pathological scar is early proof-of-concept; mVSS has pliability/thickness components that move slowly, with 12-week follow-up and n=15 per arm. SD of change around 2.3 requires a difference near 1.7 points. Placebo gets a modest change. Chinese phase 2 results often appear only at conferences, so disclosure is slow.

assumptions.claim: IL-11 is a driver of fibroblast activation and fibrosis in preclinical models.

reason: The 15-minute effect is near certain; the risk lies in the co-primary at 600 minutes, where vasoconstrictor effect wanes and a smaller difference must still be significant.
rationale: Apraclonidine 0.125% is a potent alpha-agonist vasoconstrictor; a large effect at 15 minutes is expected as for brimonidine 0.025% (Lumify) in Ora Calibra trials. Both 15-minute and 600-minute changes must be significant; effect at 10 hours is smaller but Lumify showed significance to 8 hours and apraclonidine lasts longer. Sample of 178 gives good power.

assumptions.claim: Brimonidine 0.025% significantly reduced redness versus vehicle through 8 hours after dosing in phase 3.

reason: Knee OA injection trials have a large placebo response on WOMAC pain, and both pain and function co-primaries must be significant for a cell-based product with limited controlled evidence.
rationale: Intra-articular placebo arms in knee OA typically improve WOMAC pain by 25-35%, shrinking drug-placebo gaps; cell therapies have a poor record in blinded OA trials. Enlivex's earlier phase 1/2 was promising but small. Both pain and function must be significant at n=91 per arm, so I give roughly one in four.
evidence: Meta-analyses of IA placebo response in knee OA (Bannuru 2015)

assumptions.claim: Intra-articular placebo produces large WOMAC pain improvements in knee OA trials.
assumptions.source: Bannuru RR et al., Ann Intern Med 2015

reason: An apoC-III-lowering agent should cut triglycerides by about half or more; the main uncertainty is that the dose is unknown and n=20 per arm leaves the variance in percent change large.
rationale: RBD5044 appears to be an apoC-III siRNA (secondary endpoint apoC-III, two doses 12 weeks apart). Plozasiran and olezarsen cut TG by 50-70% vs placebo even in small phase 2 studies, with SD of percent change about 35, so n=20 per arm is ample for a real drug. Residual risk is a weak molecule or low dose.

assumptions.claim: APOC3 silencing lowers TG roughly 50-70% vs placebo in hypertriglyceridemia.

reason: Topical JAK-type agents usually beat vehicle clearly on EASI at week 4; risks are a strong vehicle response in mild disease, a low concentration or a lower baseline EASI shrinking absolute change.
rationale: VC005 is presumably a topical JAK pathway inhibitor; ruxolitinib cream and delgocitinib beat vehicle on EASI within 4 weeks in mild-to-moderate AD, and 60 per arm is adequate for a moderate effect (SD about 3.5). Dose and concentration unknown and mild-to-moderate patients with low baseline EASI limit the absolute change; Chinese phase 2 success rates are decent.
evidence: Topical JAK inhibitor phase 2 AD trials

assumptions.claim: Topical ruxolitinib cream significantly reduced EASI versus vehicle by week 4 in mild-to-moderate AD.

reason: About 20 per arm in a rare, highly variable epilepsy, where seizure counts are noisy and placebo responses large; a potent KCNT1 inhibitor could still give a clear effect.
rationale: KCNT1-related epilepsy is gain-of-function, so a selective inhibitor has a clear rationale and seizure burden is high (at least 4 per week), which helps detection, but earlier quinidine attempts failed and n=20 per arm with percent-change variance (SD about 50) is thin. Enrolling 61 patients with this ultra-rare disease at two sites will be slow, so results probably come after mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Quinidine produced inconsistent seizure reduction in KCNT1-related epilepsy.

reason: Colgate stannous fluoride vs regular fluoride 24-week gingivitis/plaque studies almost always report significant benefit; the only real risk is one of the two co-primaries missing with n=85.
rationale: Stannous fluoride dentifrices consistently reduce gingivitis and plaque versus sodium fluoride in 6-month Colgate trials, typically by 0.15-0.3 GI points (15-25% relative). With SD of change around 0.25 and 43/42 per arm, power is good. Both GI and plaque must be significant, and Colgate sponsor studies are rarely published when negative. Public timing depends on IADR/AADOCR abstracts or J Clin Dent, probably after June 2027.
evidence: Paraskevas & van der Weijden, J Clin Periodontol 2006 (stannous fluoride and gingivitis review)
Colgate 6-month SnF2 vs NaF dentifrice trials (J Clin Dent)

assumptions.claim: Stannous fluoride dentifrices reduce gingival index more than sodium fluoride dentifrices in 6-month trials
assumptions.source: Paraskevas & van der Weijden, J Clin Periodontol 2006;33:1-13

assumptions.claim: Loe-Silness GI is scored 0-3 per surface and Colgate studies require baseline GI of at least 1.0

reason: Obicetrapib lowers LDL-C about 30% on statins versus about 15-18% for bempedoic acid, so superiority with 213 per arm is near certain; residual risk is a sponsor non-announcement or odd analysis.
rationale: Obicetrapib 10 mg gave about 30-33% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction at day 84 (BROADWAY, BROOKLYN, TANDEM). Bempedoic acid 180 mg gives roughly 15-18% on statins (CLEAR trials). A gap near 14 points with SD about 22 and 213 per arm gives z above 6. Non-HDL-C follows LDL-C. Main uncertainty is whether and when Menarini publicises results.

assumptions.claim: Obicetrapib 10 mg reduced LDL-C by about 33% placebo-adjusted at day 84 on top of maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy
Bempedoic acid 180 mg reduced LDL-C by about 17% placebo-adjusted at week 12 on maximally tolerated statins

reason: GSK propellant safety crossover in 110 asthma patients at 18 sites; no efficacy goal. Start was September 2026, so enrolment drift of a few weeks is likely but a delay beyond late May 2027 is less common. Results posting normally follows within about a year of completion.
Two co-primaries (2-hour pain freedom and MBS freedom) must both win; with 900 per arm power is high if the drug has gepant-like activity, but a novel mechanism carries real failure risk.
rationale: Acute migraine phase 3 trials with 900 per arm detect a 6-8 point pain-freedom gap easily (ubrogepant, rimegepant, zavegepant ~8-10 points; triptans ~15). Both co-primaries must be met, which trims probability. Unknown mechanism and a small private sponsor add uncertainty about true effect size. Placebo pain freedom is typically 11-15%. Timing of topline depends on enrolment of 1800 patients by early 2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo 2-hour pain freedom in recent acute migraine phase 3 trials is about 11-15%
Gepants gave about 7-10 percentage points over placebo on 2-hour pain freedom

reason: Inhaled DHE has shown about 38% vs 13% pain freedom at 2 hours in earlier work, so a 108-patient paired crossover should win; the risks are small size, patients missing a second attack, and a weaker dry powder delivery.
rationale: Orally inhaled DHE (Levadex/MAP0004) reached roughly 38% vs 13% pain-free at 2 hours in phase 3. A dry powder DHE at 2 mg should behave similarly if delivery is comparable. Paired crossover with 108 patients gives good power for a 15-20 point difference. Dropout from untreated second attack and phase 2 uncertainty lower confidence. Small private sponsor makes early disclosure unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Orally inhaled DHE achieved about 38% 2-hour pain freedom vs about 13% for placebo in phase 3
Acute migraine placebo 2-hour pain freedom is about 10-15%

reason: Pfizer descriptive safety and immunogenicity study of RSVpreF in India (540 adults, 13 sites) with no efficacy hypothesis; short follow-up and a registered completion of January 2027 make a large delay unlikely, and Pfizer usually posts results about a year after completion.
Aldosterone synthase inhibitors lowered seated SBP by 8-11 mmHg over placebo in phase 2; the high dose should win, though placebo response and dose choice in a 63-per-arm study add noise.
rationale: Aldosterone synthase inhibitors (baxdrostat BrigHtN, lorundrostat) cut seated SBP by about 8-11 mmHg versus placebo at higher doses in resistant or uncontrolled hypertension. With SD about 14 and 63 per arm, SE is about 2.5, so a 9 mmHg effect gives z near 3.5. Uncertainty is the true dose potency of SAL0140 and placebo response. Results likely emerge only at a conference or company report after mid 2027.

assumptions.claim: Baxdrostat 2 mg lowered seated SBP by about 11 mmHg versus placebo at week 12 in resistant hypertension
Placebo arm fell by about 9 mmHg in that phase 2 trial

reason: BGE-102 (brain-penetrant NLRP3 inhibitor) cut hsCRP by up to about 86% in obese phase 1 volunteers; at the top dose the win is near certain, with hsCRP variability the only noise.
rationale: BioAge reported phase 1 hsCRP reductions up to about 86% in obese participants with elevated hsCRP after short dosing. NLRP3 inhibition acts directly upstream of IL-1/IL-6/CRP, so a 12-week high dose should produce a very large placebo-adjusted fall. hsCRP is skewed and variable, but 40 per arm is ample for effects of 50-80 points. Listed company with fully enrolled study and primary completion November 2026 should disclose in Q1 2027.
evidence: NLRP3 inhibitor/IL-1 pathway hsCRP effects: CANTOS NCT01327846 (2017)

assumptions.claim: BGE-102 reduced hsCRP by up to about 86% in obese participants with elevated hsCRP in phase 1
Study is fully enrolled (active, not recruiting) with primary completion 2026-11-30

reason: An oral incretin agonist at its top dose over 20 weeks should separate clearly from placebo on percent weight change; the main risk is weak oral exposure or a published absolute-kg form.
rationale: BGM0504 is a GLP-1/GIP agonist with large weight loss in its injectable phase 2/3 work. Oral incretin agents (orforglipron) gave 8-12% weight loss over 26 weeks versus about 2% placebo. With 40 per arm and SD about 4%, even a 4% gap is significant at the top dose. Uncertainty is oral bioavailability of this formulation and unknown dose range. Recruiting still open implies delayed completion; Chinese sponsor disclosure may be slow.

assumptions.claim: Oral orforglipron produced 8.6-12.6% weight loss at 26 weeks versus about 2% with placebo
The record names the outcome only as fasting body weight at 20 weeks, with four dose arms and placebo

reason: Nutraceutical against placebo on a subjective fatigue score with two co-primaries that must both be met; placebo response and chemo-related fatigue swings can hide a small effect, though sponsor-run trials that report tend to be positive.
rationale: Small sponsor (Malaysian nutraceutical firm), Indian sites, subjective BFI/VAFS co-primaries both required. Placebo arm in chemo patients selected for fatigue will improve through regression to the mean. Trials from such sponsors that do report are usually positive, but a real effect of one BFI point is modest against an SD near 1.9 with 90 per arm.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-controlled ginseng trial in cancer-related fatigue showed modest benefit on fatigue scales with a large placebo response.
assumptions.source: Barton et al, N07C2, JNCI 2013, PMID 23690461

reason: Open-label lozenge versus short-acting viscous lidocaine on the last day of radiotherapy; the longer duration of bupivacaine should favour the lozenge over 3 hours, but pain scores are subjective and the sample is modest.
rationale: Lidocaine viscous gives relief for well under an hour, while a slow-dissolving bupivacaine lozenge should cover much of the 3-hour window, and the earlier phase 2 work supported the lozenge. Open-label design adds some bias in favour of the new product. 75 per arm is adequate for a clear difference. Risks are enrolment pace and a noisy composite pain measure.
evidence: BupiZenge phase 2 vs lidocaine in oral mucositis (OncoZenge)

assumptions.claim: Viscous lidocaine relieves mucositis pain only briefly after a dose.
assumptions.source: Standard product information and MASCC mucositis guidance

reason: Oral psoriasis agents in placebo-controlled week-16 trials almost always beat placebo on PGA 0/1 and PASI 75 by a wide margin; the main uncertainty is an unknown compound with a possibly weak dose.
rationale: Placebo PGA 0/1 at week 16 is typically 5 to 12 percent, and effective oral agents (TYK2, PDE4 class) reach 35 to 65 percent. With 188 per arm even a modest drug clears significance on both co-primaries. Risk is a poorly chosen dose of an unproven molecule, and delayed or non-public reporting from a private Chinese sponsor.

assumptions.claim: Placebo sPGA 0/1 response at week 16 in oral psoriasis phase 3 trials is about 7 percent.
assumptions.source: POETYK PSO-1, Armstrong et al, JAMA Dermatol 2023

reason: Next-generation HER2 ADC against T-DM1 in a pretreated population has a large expected effect; the main risks are a payload or dose that is not clearly better than T-DM1 and OS being immature at the PFS analysis.
rationale: Head-to-head HER2 ADC trials against T-DM1 in trastuzumab and taxane pretreated disease have been strongly positive (DESTINY-Breast03 HR 0.28; Chinese ADC trials similar). T-DM1 median PFS about 7 months. 228 patients give good power for HR near 0.5. Reporting timing is the uncertainty: the event-driven analysis may fall after mid-2027.
evidence: SHR-A1811 vs pyrotinib plus capecitabine phase 3 2024

assumptions.claim: T-DM1 median PFS was 6.8 months in DESTINY-Breast03 and 9.6 months in EMILIA.
assumptions.source: Hurvitz et al, Lancet 2023; Verma et al, NEJM 2012

reason: Anti-IL-4R alpha biologic as add-on in adolescents with SAR should beat placebo; the main risk is a short autumn pollen season with low symptom scores and a high placebo response in a 68-per-arm trial.
rationale: Stapokibart was clearly positive on rTNSS in adult SAR phase 3, and adolescent trials extend a validated mechanism. With 68 per arm and SD about 2.4, an effect of 1.3 points gives roughly 85 percent power. Risks are a weak pollen season, an add-on design on background therapy compressing the difference, and small size.
evidence: Stapokibart (CM310) SAR phase 3 in adults, China 2024

assumptions.claim: Stapokibart significantly improved rTNSS versus placebo in adult seasonal allergic rhinitis.
assumptions.source: Keymed Biosciences announcements 2024 for CM310 SAR phase 3

reason: IL-4R alpha blockade works in SAR and 110 per arm is well powered; residual risk is a weak autumn pollen season lowering symptom scores and compressing the treatment difference.
rationale: Same mechanism as stapokibart, which was positive in adult SAR. Enrolment already closed (active, not recruiting) so the trial should read out early 2027. With SD 2.5 and 110 per arm, a 1.5 point difference gives over 95 percent power. Hengrui often does not issue press releases for single phase 3 readouts, hence modest public probability.

assumptions.claim: Anti-IL-4R alpha antibodies reduce nasal symptom scores versus placebo in seasonal allergic rhinitis.

reason: Topical magnesium oral spray is an unproven mechanism in refractory chronic cough; a 30-per-arm pilot on a noisy cough count has little power unless the effect is large.
rationale: Refractory chronic cough trials show placebo reductions of 10 to 30 percent on objective monitors, and even gefapixant gave only about 15 to 20 percent placebo-adjusted. A magnesium spray has weak preclinical rationale, and n=30 per arm with a skewed outcome is underpowered. A positive signal needs a very large effect.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-adjusted reduction in 24-hour cough frequency for gefapixant 45 mg was about 15 to 18 percent.
