reason: Endothelial cell density change after phaco is noisy (SD near 280 cells/mm2) and a topical antioxidant is likely to preserve only a modest number of cells; 100 per arm detects roughly 80 cells.
rationale: Hard nuclear cataract surgery typically loses 5 to 10 percent of endothelial cells. Ascorbic acid 5% drops plausibly reduce oxidative injury but the protective effect is uncertain and likely modest. With SD about 280 and 100 per arm, SE is around 40, so a 50 cell benefit has about 25 to 35 percent chance of significance.
evidence: Endothelial cell loss after phacoemulsification (Zetterstrom, Richard et al reviews)

assumptions.claim: Phacoemulsification of dense nuclear cataracts causes mean endothelial cell loss of roughly 5 to 10 percent at 3 months.
assumptions.source: Richard et al, Acta Ophthalmol 2008; Hwang et al, 2015

reason: Adding a likely NK1-class agent to palonosetron in high-risk PONV patients should raise vomiting-free rate; with a dose-finding design any dose meeting the objective suffices, but 87 per arm is limited if palonosetron control is already strong.
rationale: In patients with at least 3 PONV risk factors, palonosetron alone leaves substantial vomiting over 72 hours, and NK1 antagonist combinations (aprepitant, fosaprepitant) cut vomiting markedly. Complete response here ignores nausea, so control is fairly high. A 15 to 20 point gain is plausible and detectable at 87 per arm. Sponsor rarely announces phase 2 results.
evidence: Aprepitant vs ondansetron PONV, Gan et al 2007

assumptions.claim: NK1 antagonists reduce vomiting after surgery substantially more than 5-HT3 antagonists alone.
assumptions.source: Diemunsch et al, Br J Anaesth 2007; Gan et al, Anesth Analg 2007

reason: Phase 2 dose-ranging in vitiligo with three doses and a placebo; any dose beating placebo on F-VASI percent change at week 24 suffices, but facial repigmentation is slow and noisy with 50 per arm.
rationale: Oral JAK-class agents (ritlecitinib, povorcitinib) showed dose-dependent F-VASI improvement at week 24 with placebo changes under 10 percent. With three active doses and SD about 35 percent, the top dose likely separates if the compound is a real JAK inhibitor. Uncertainty is the unknown molecule and enrolment still ongoing, so reading out by mid-2027 is doubtful.

assumptions.claim: Oral JAK inhibitors improved F-VASI at week 24 versus a small placebo change in phase 2b vitiligo trials.
assumptions.source: Ezzedine et al, JAMA Dermatol 2023 (ritlecitinib); Rosmarin et al, 2024 (povorcitinib)

reason: Placebo PASI 100 at week 12 is near zero, so even an IL-23-class response of 15-20% with 30 per arm is borderline significant; an IL-17-class response would clear it easily. Main risk is a weaker-than-expected antibody.
rationale: Placebo PASI 100 at week 12 is about 0-2%. A Hengrui biologic chosen with PASI 100 as primary suggests deep responses are expected (IL-17 class about 40-60%, IL-23 class about 15-30% at week 12). With 30 per arm, 6 or more responders vs 0-1 on placebo is significant. Top dose counts. Public timing is the main uncertainty, as Hengrui rarely announces phase 2 results early.
evidence: BE READY NCT03410992 (bimekizumab, PASI 100 vs placebo)

assumptions.claim: Placebo PASI 100 response at the primary timepoint in psoriasis biologic trials is about 0-2%.
IL-17A inhibitor ixekizumab gave PASI 100 of about 35-40% at week 12 versus about 0-1% on placebo.

reason: Only 13 weeks of exposure on top of semaglutide titration, so incremental weight loss from AT673 may be small relative to a noisy 50-per-arm comparison; HbA1c add-on benefit is even less certain.
rationale: Add-on to semaglutide in T2D with obesity over only 13 weeks; semaglutide itself gives about 3% loss by then, with SD about 3%. A GIPR-antagonist-type add-on needs roughly 2 points additional loss to reach significance at n=50 per arm. Preclinical and early clinical rationale supports additivity but the short window limits it. Small private sponsor likely announces topline mainly if positive.
evidence: STEP 2 semaglutide in T2D with obesity (NCT03552757)

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide 1.0 mg in T2D gives roughly 4-5% weight loss at 30 weeks, so less at 13 weeks with titration.
Antag's lead asset is a GIPR antagonist intended for combination with GLP-1 agonists.

reason: Small safety/immunogenicity phase 2 with 47 enrolled and a 240-day post-dose-2 safety window; the registered end date looks slightly early versus the 29 April 2026 start, and the adaptive design could add enrolment, so a slip past early May is plausible.
rationale: Registered primary completion 2027-02-03 sits about 300 days after dose 1, which is earlier than 29 April 2026 plus 300 days (late February 2027); later-vaccinated participants push the true last visit to March-April 2027. Adaptive design could reopen recruitment. Academic collaborators and a small sponsor make early CT.gov results posting unlikely. Six safety primaries invite some edits.

reason: Rocuronium sets a ceiling of roughly 95% good/excellent conditions, so non-inferiority is likely unless the unknown margin is tight or HRS-9190 onset is slower at the assessed time.
rationale: Phase 3 following dose-finding; rocuronium yields excellent/good intubation conditions in about 90-100% of patients, so both arms sit near the ceiling and non-inferiority is easy to show unless the margin is very tight. Hengrui rarely press-releases anesthesia trials, so public timing is slow; NDA acceptance may appear in 2027 but may not name the trial.
evidence: Rocuronium intubation conditions Cooper score trials (Perry Cochrane review 2008)

assumptions.claim: Rocuronium 0.6 mg/kg gives good or excellent intubation conditions in roughly 90-100% of patients.
assumptions.source: Cochrane review Perry et al. 2008, rocuronium vs succinylcholine

reason: Only 15 per arm with two co-primary endpoints that must both be significant; vehicle response in dry-eye type endpoints is large and an unproven agent needs a big effect on both staining and OSDI.
rationale: Co-primary corneal staining and OSDI both must reach p<0.05 with 15 per arm. Vehicle arms in ocular surface disease trials show sizeable improvements, and OSDI is noisy. Little is known about d-MAPPS efficacy; small private sponsor, so success would need a very large effect. Enrolling 30 chronic oGVHD patients at 5 sites by early 2027 is also optimistic, making any readout before mid-2027 unlikely.
evidence: Dry eye vehicle-controlled trials corneal staining (OPUS-3 NCT02284516)

assumptions.claim: Vehicle arms in dry eye trials typically improve corneal staining by a few tenths of a grade and OSDI by 10-15 points.

reason: Placebo-controlled 12-week BP trials on top of two or more drugs show large placebo responses of 7-9 mmHg; the top dose must beat that by about 5-6 mmHg at n=64 per arm, which is likely for an active antihypertensive but not certain.
rationale: Completed dose-ranging trial, top dose vs placebo, n=64 per arm, SD about 14 mmHg. Standard-of-care background plus run-in gives placebo change near -8 mmHg; resistant-hypertension add-on agents with a validated mechanism typically give a further 8-10 mmHg at 12 weeks (e.g. aldosterone synthase inhibitors), enough for significance. Companies tend to report positive phase 2 only via annual report or congress.

assumptions.claim: In BaxHTN, 12-week placebo-adjusted seated SBP reductions were about 9-10 mmHg with placebo change near -9 mmHg.
Study is registered as completed with primary completion 2026-07-02.

reason: Top dose of an oral incretin-type agent over 20 weeks in about 50 per arm should clearly separate from placebo; residual risk is a weak molecule or the announcement not stating the primary was met.
rationale: Oral once-daily GLP-1-class agent, four dose arms, highest dose counts. Oral incretin phase 2 benchmarks (orforglipron 26 weeks: -8.6% to -12.6% vs -2.0% placebo) imply large separation; at 20 weeks with titration and SD about 4.5%, n=51 per arm gives huge power. Placebo in a Chinese cohort with diet advice about -1.5%. Uncertainty is mainly whether and when the sponsor reports.

assumptions.claim: Orforglipron produced -8.6% to -12.6% weight change at 26 weeks vs -2.0% on placebo in non-diabetic obesity.
The trial is registered as completed with primary completion 2026-07-09.

reason: With about 31 per arm and SD near 5.5%, only a very weak injectable would fail to beat placebo on 36-week weight change at the top dose.
rationale: Injectable incretin-type agent, three dose arms, top dose over 36 weeks. Peer injectable incretins (mazdutide, tirzepatide) give -9% to -15% placebo-adjusted at similar durations in Chinese cohorts; even half of that is significant at n=31 per arm (SE about 1.4). Placebo about -1.5%. Main uncertainty is whether the sponsor publishes by mid-2027 and states significance.

assumptions.claim: Mazdutide 6 mg gave about -14% weight loss at 48 weeks vs about -0.5% on placebo in Chinese adults with overweight/obesity.
Primary completion registered as 2026-10 with status active, not recruiting.

reason: A GLP-1-class agent at top dose in T2D with baseline HbA1c 7.5-11% reliably lowers HbA1c by more than 1 point vs placebo; the residual risk is mostly whether and when results are made public.
rationale: Oral incretin-class agent in metformin-treated T2D with high baseline HbA1c; orforglipron phase 2 T2D gave -1.2 to -2.1 vs -0.4 on placebo at 26 weeks. At 20 weeks with 40 per arm and SD about 0.8, a placebo-adjusted -1.3 is very significant. Primary completion registered March 2027 and the trial was still recruiting, so a readout before June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Orforglipron phase 2 T2D Rosenstock Lancet 2023 NCT05048719

assumptions.claim: Orforglipron lowered HbA1c by 1.2 to 2.1 points vs 0.4 on placebo at 26 weeks in T2D.
Primary completion registered as 2027-03 and status recruiting at snapshot.

reason: Small open-label weight-maintenance extension that has already passed its registered primary completion; a Chinese private sponsor rarely posts results or edits primary outcomes, and no stop is expected.
rationale: Extension study with 71 participants, registered primary completion September 2026 already passed, no efficacy goal to meet. Private Chinese sponsor with several concurrent MWN109 trials; results posting on CT.gov is unlikely and the primary outcome is simple and unlikely to be rewritten.

reason: Vehicle drops usually improve corneal staining a lot over 12 weeks, and with about 30 per arm in a single-site phase 2 a modest true effect is easily lost; two doses give one extra chance.
rationale: Small single-site Korean phase 2 (about 30 per arm), 12-week change in NEI corneal staining. Vehicle response in dry eye staining is typically 1 to 2 points, which shrinks the drug-vehicle gap. Two TJO-087 doses give some multiplicity benefit, and sponsors that publicise results are biased toward positive outcomes. Mechanism and drug class not known to me, so I stay near a coin flip, a little below.
evidence: Dry eye vehicle-controlled phase 2/3 programs with corneal staining primaries (e.g. OPUS-3 lifitegrast 2017, OPUS-2 2015)

assumptions.claim: Vehicle arms in dry eye trials show a mean improvement of about 1 to 2 NEI-scale points in corneal staining over 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: OPUS-2 and OPUS-3 lifitegrast trials (Tauber 2015; Holland 2017)

reason: Coartem already gives PCR-corrected ACPR near 97 to 99 percent in African children, so superiority with 60 per arm is nearly impossible; this open-label phase 2 platform cohort is estimation-oriented with no formal test.
rationale: Control artemether-lumefantrine has PCR-corrected Day 29 ACPR of about 95 to 99 percent in children, leaving no room for a statistically significant superiority win with 60 per arm. The record states no hypothesis and the cohort is open-label phase 2 platform work, so the report will likely be descriptive (ACPR with CI, parasite clearance), which counts as not met.

assumptions.claim: Artemether-lumefantrine PCR-corrected ACPR at Day 28/29 in African children is typically above 95 percent.
assumptions.source: WWARN meta-analyses of artemether-lumefantrine efficacy; KALUMA phase 3 2025

reason: A depot corticosteroid versus untreated sham should clear anterior chamber cells clearly, but both co-primaries must be met and the Day 8 no-pain endpoint has a high placebo rate and smaller expected gap.
rationale: Subconjunctival triamcinolone against no-treatment sham in cataract surgery should produce a large difference in grade 0 cells at Day 14 (control about 20 to 30 percent; steroid depots reach 50 to 65 percent in Dexycu and Dextenza trials). Both co-primaries must hit; the pain-free Day 8 endpoint has high control response and is the main risk. 125 per arm gives good power on cells.

assumptions.claim: In vehicle/placebo arms of postoperative steroid trials, only about 15 to 35 percent of patients have anterior chamber cell grade 0 at Day 14.
Active steroid depots roughly double the proportion with cleared cells at Day 8 to 14.
assumptions.source: Dexycu phase 3 (63 vs 31 percent at Day 8)

reason: A long-acting subcutaneous antihypertensive with a 6-month double-blind design in 319 patients is very likely to separate from placebo on week 12 office SBP; the main uncertainty is the effect size at the lower dose and the chance it is not reported.
rationale: Phase 2 antihypertensive with about 160 per arm, baseline SBP 140 to 180, so power for a 5 mmHg or larger placebo-adjusted drop is high. Subcutaneous injection with a 6-month Part A suggests a long-acting agent (possibly an AGT-lowering class), where 12-week office SBP drops of 10 to 15 mmHg were seen (KARDIA-1). Placebo response is about 5 to 8 mmHg.
evidence: Phase 2 antihypertensive placebo-controlled trials with office SBP primary

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in office-SBP hypertension trials show a mean fall of about 5 to 8 mmHg at 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: KARDIA-1 2023 and other phase 2 hypertension trials

reason: Stannous fluoride usually beats regular fluoride toothpaste on gingivitis, bleeding and plaque over 6 months, but about 40 per arm and three co-primaries that must all be met leave a real chance one misses.
rationale: Colgate stannous fluoride studies against a regular fluoride negative control typically report significant 6-month gains in modified gingival index, bleeding and plaque (MGI effect about 0.2 to 0.3 points, 10 to 15 percent). With 40 per arm and SD of change near 0.35, the MGI is likely significant, but all three primaries must be met. Results usually appear on ClinicalTrials.gov or in journals long after completion, and enrolment seems to run past January 2027.
evidence: Colgate 0.454% stannous fluoride six-month gingivitis studies (J Clin Dent / Int Dent J, 2010s to 2020s)

assumptions.claim: In six-month trials, stannous fluoride toothpaste lowers the modified gingival index about 0.2 to 0.3 points more than a regular sodium fluoride toothpaste.
assumptions.source: Colgate stannous fluoride six-month clinical studies, J Clin Dent

reason: Tiny phase 2 safety study in a rare disease at Taiwanese sites: slow recruitment of 24 adults with matched EB lesion pairs makes primary completion slippage likely, with some risk of early closure; a small sponsor is unlikely to post results by August 2027.
A full opioid agonist like cebranopadol should blunt precipitated withdrawal, but with 15 per arm and a noisy peak COWS the result is borderline-powered even for a sizeable effect.
rationale: Cebranopadol is a NOP/MOP full agonist, so it should suppress withdrawal when the prescribed opioid is withheld, as methadone or buprenorphine do. Placebo peak COWS likely 8 to 15 with SD near 5 to 6. A 4 to 5 point gap with 15 per arm gives roughly 60 to 75 percent power. Sponsors tend to announce positive phase 2 toplines, which lifts p_met given a public result.
evidence: Cebranopadol ALLEVIATE-1 and ALLEVIATE-2 phase 3 acute pain 2024
Buprenorphine and lofexidine COWS suppression trials

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated opioid-dependent patients under precipitated or spontaneous withdrawal reach a peak COWS in the moderate range of about 10 to 15.
assumptions.source: Lofexidine phase 3 trials (Gorodetzky 2017; Yu 2008) and COWS validation (Wesson 2003)
